Coachella festival emergency management organizers reported 3 separate dust devils under sunny skies and following the cold strong winds that occurred April 21-22. The most significant dust devil on April 23 occurred during the festival and tossed a tent 50 feet in the air. One dust devil knocked over 2 persons which was captured on security cameras.
Several cloud to ground lightning strikes occurred in the mountains and were associated with heavy precipitation and snow.

Report from associate meteorologist at San Diego County Flood Control District. ALERT rain gauge in Coyote Canyon recorded 0.58 inch in an hour (2-year return interval). Minor flooding reported around Montezuma Road in De Anza neighborhood of Borrego Springs.

Report of power outage to all of Borrego Springs around 4:05 pm, shortly after numerous lightning strikes in Palm Canyon and northwestern areas of Borrego Springs. Power remained off for 3+ hours and was restored between 7:00 pm and 7:30 pm. Several brief heavy downpours were also reported, with rainfall of 0.11 inch.

Observations from KRIV indicate that this tornado touched down at 4:30 PM approximately four miles southeast of the March ARB and was on the ground for six minutes. No reports of damage were received and this tornado was rated EF-0 tornado. The exact path of this tornado is not known.

Observations from KRIV indicate that this tornado touched down on March Field at 4:42 PM, traveled approximately three miles in a west-southwest direction for 21 minutes, and had a max width of 75 yards. As the tornado crossed Interstate 215, a semi-truck was lifted 30 to 40 feet into the air and nine empty BNSF railroad cars were derailed. The driver of the semi had to be extricated using the ���jaws of life��� and was hospitalized for over a month due to moderate head injuries. The tornado also damaged the roofs of several homes and a trailer on Kuder Ave. It should be noted that another tornado developed nearby while this tornado was in progress. Based on input from Dr. Kisho Mehta and Tim Marshall, damage to the rail cars was consistent with wind gusts up to 120 mph, or an EF-2 tornado. This is the first EF-2 tornado in California since the new scale was implemented in February 2007, and the first F2 tornado in California since the 1998 Sunnyvale tornado.

Photos and video of the EF-2 tornado all show a separate tornado occurring in its vicinity at the same time. Based on photographic evidence and eyewitness accounts, this separate tornado would be the third tornado produced by the storm. The exact path is not known, however several videos indicate that this tornado was just west of Interstate 215 in close proximity to the Riverside National Cemetery. No reports of damage were received and this tornado was rated EF-0.

A trained weather spotter from the Lake Elsinore area captured video of a tornado between 5:40 ��� 5:45 PM. This tornado occurred in an unpopulated area near the Gavilan Hills between Woodcrest and Lake Elsinore, however the exact path is unknown. This was the fourth and final tornado produced by the storm. No reports of damage were received and this tornado was rated EF-0.

Temperatures soared well above seasonal normals starting May 13th and lasting through the 15th. Yorba Linda reached a high of 94 degrees on the 13th while John Wayne International Airport reached 86 degrees. The hottest temperatures occurred on the 14th, when Yorba Linda recorded a high of 95 degrees, while John Wayne International recorded a high of 87 degrees. Temperatures were a bit lower on the 15th, when Yorba Linda topped out at 86 degrees and John Wayne International reached 77 degrees.

events.event_narrative: Temperatures soared well above seasonal normals starting May 13th and lasting through the 15th. Many locations in the Inland Empire reached the middle to upper 90s on the 13th, when Chino Airport hit 97 degrees, Riverside Airport (RAL) reached 95 degrees, and San Bernardino International Airport reached 95 degrees. Several locations reached the upper 90s to just over 100 degrees on the 14th. Chino reached 101 degrees, Riverside Airport reached 98 degrees, and San Bernardino International Airport reached 99 degrees. Slightly cooler temperatures were observed on the 15th, with all three of the aforementioned locations reaching 91 degrees.

High temperatures topped out in the middle 80s to lower 90s on the 13th, when the Ramona Airport reached 92 degrees and Gillespie Field reached 90 degrees. Temperatures reached the upper 80s to middle 90s across many inland valley areas on the 14th. The Ramona Airport reached 96 degrees, while Gillespie Field reached 93 degrees. Slightly cooler temperatures were observed on the 15th, with Ramona reaching 91 degrees and Gillespie Field reaching 84 degrees.

The hottest temperatures occurred on the 14th, when Hesperia reached 92 degrees while Apple Valley topped out near 94 degrees. Slightly cooler temperatures were observed on the 15th, with Hesperia reaching 86 degrees and Apple Valley reaching 90 degrees.

Heavy rain from a thunderstorm over the Santiago Burn Area triggered damaging debris flows in Modjeska Canyon. The lowest floor of a 2-story house was completely inundated with approximately 1000 cubic meters of debris flow material. Damage to this home was extensive. The yard of a nearby home was inundated with approximately 2500 cubic meters of debris flow material.

Heavy rain over the Santiago Burn Area triggered flash flooding and debris flows in Williams Canyon. The debris flows blocked a roadway and stranded the residents of two homes near the back of Williams Canyons. No major damage or injuries were reported.

Heavy rainfall from a thunderstorm over the Santiago Burn Area triggered flash flood and debris flows in Trabuco Canyon near O' Neill Regional Park. Live Oak Canyon Road was shut down after it was inundated with up to four feet of water. The mud and water rushed out of Trabuco Canyon and poured into Cook's Corner, a roadside biker bar at the intersection of Santiago Canyon and Live Oak Canyon roads. The bar was completely flooded and filled with mud.

A tornadic thunderstorm left a swath of hail up to several inches deep from north of Moreno Valley to Perris. Snow plows were called out to clear the hail from Interstate 10. While most of the hailstones were pea-size, several reports of marble to nickel size hail were received from Moreno Valley just prior to the tornadoes. The larger hailstones left holes in awnings and stripped leaves from trees.

Flash flooding caused serious damage to several residential neighborhoods in rural northeastern Moreno Valley between Moreno Beach Dr and Redlands Blvd. City building and safety inspectors declared one home unsafe to occupy and at least four others damaged near Locust Ave north of State Highway 60. A few miles south at the 29000 Block of Stevens Ave, several more homes were damaged by ���major��� flooding. Elsewhere, flash flooding forced the closure of San Timoteo Canyon Rd, Live Oak Canyon Rd, and portions of Alessandro Rd. Fire officials received a total of 28 reports of flooded residences due to the thunderstorm.

Mission Beach Lifeguards report the rescue of two swimmers struggling near a sand bar in elevated surf and strong rip currents. A third swimmer was swept away, resulting in a drowning fatality. The victim had reportedly saved his friend from a large wave and was swept away in a rip current.
LCDR Alex Edward with the United States Coast Guard reported dense fog off of San Clemente Island on June 22. Their ability to launch boats off of the island was inhibited by the dense fog.

Border 27 wildfire east of Otay Lake/Chula Vista (about 1.5 miles south of Otay Lake Road) burned 100 acres. Nearly 200 firefighters were involved in the firefighting effort. Contained by 5 pm on July 19.

Excessive heat occurred in the Coachella Valley on July 21st, when Palm Springs recorded a high temperature of 113 degrees and Thermal recorded a high of 108. Similar temperatures occurred on the 22nd, when Palm Springs recorded a high of 113 degrees and Thermal topped out at 111 degrees.

Excessive heat occurred in the San Diego County Dserts on July 21st, when Ocotillo Wells recorded a high temperature of 117 degrees and Borrego Springs recorded a high of 109. Similar temperatures occurred on the 22nd, when Ocotillo Wells recorded a high of 117 degrees and Borrego Springs topped out at 111 degrees.

Excessive heat impacted the lower deserts July 15-17. High temperatures ranged from 112-116 in the Coachella Valley including 116 at Ocotillo Wells on July 15; temperatures of 115 to 118 on July 16, which was also the hottest day of the event; temperatures of 111 to 117 on July 17.

The Border 32 fire started at 2:17 pm on August 31 at Barret Lake Road and Highway 94 near Barret Lake. Temperatures were as high as 108 degrees during firefighting efforts. Total acreage burned 4,456 acres, and many structures were destroyed, including three homes, three outbuildings, two sheds, two RVs, three barns and one commercial structure. Evacuation orders were issued.
Idyllwild reached a high temperature of 96 degrees on August 31, breaking the previous record of 94 set in 2017.

Anaheim broke their daily high temperature record, reaching 106 degrees, breaking the previous record of 102 set in 2007. This also breaks the all-time monthly high temperature for the month of August, breaking the previous record of 105 degrees set on August 18, 2020.
Campo tied the daily high temperature record, reaching 105 degrees, tying the previous record of 105 degrees set in 1998.

Numerous pre-hospital related calls and transports were recorded through the duration of the heatwave. Six calls were received on August 30, with age range of 7-79 years, with most seeing mild symptoms; many were outside recreating or working. On August 31, 13 calls were placed with the age range of 18-86 years, with 11 experiencing mild symptoms, 1 seeing moderate symptoms and 1 acute.

Heavy rain from thunderstorms caused several areas of flash flooding in the Witch Creek Burn Area. Flash flooding was reported at Black Canyon Road and Sutherland Dam Road northeast of Ramona. Several other flash floods were reported along Highway 78 between Ramona and Santa Ysabel. Water spilled over a small dam at Ramona Canyon Resort and flooded the creek that runs alongside Highway 78. No serious damage was reported.
Heavy rain from a thunderstorm caused flash flooding in the Witch Creek Burn Area along Highway 78 near Weekend Villa Road. No damage was reported.

The ASOS at San Diego International Airport observed daily highs reaching at least the middle to upper 80s through much of early September, with several days reaching the lower to middle 90s. The highest daily maximum temperature of 95 degrees occurred on the afternoon of Saturday September 3rd, with a high of 94 occurring on Thursday, September 8th. Highs on Saturday, September 10th were significantly cooler due to clouds and rain associated with the approach of Hurricane Kay, which ended the heat wave.

The ASOS at John Wayne International Airport observed daily highs reaching at least the lower to middle 90s through much of early September, with several days ranging from 97 to 106 degrees. The highest daily maximum temperature of 106 degrees occurred on the afternoon of Sunday September 4th, with a high of 102 occurring on Thursday, September 8th. Highs on Saturday, September 10th were significantly cooler due to clouds and rain associated with the approach of Hurricane Kay, which ended the heat wave.

The ASOS at Ramona Airport observed daily highs ranging from 100 to 107 degrees through much of early September. The highest daily maximum temperature of 107 degrees occurred on the afternoon of Wednesday September 7th, with a high of 104 degrees occurring on all of the September 1st, 4th, and 6th. Highs on Saturday, September 10th were significantly cooler due to clouds and rain associated with the approach of Hurricane Kay, which ended the heat wave.

Highs on Friday, September 9th were significantly cooler due to clouds and rain associated with the approach of Hurricane Kay, which ended the heat wave.

The Border 32 fire started at 2:17 pm on August 31 at Barret Lake Road and Highway 94 near Barret Lake. Temperatures were as high as 108 degrees during firefighting efforts. Total acreage burned 4,456 acres, and many structures were destroyed, including three homes, three outbuildings, two sheds, two RVs, three barns and one commercial structure. Evacuation orders were issued. The fire was 100% contained by 4:55 PM PDT on September 5th.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: The Fairview Fire began burning around 3:37 PM PDT on September 5th at the intersection of Fairview Avenue and Bautista Road in Hemet. Evacuation orders were quickly put in place and then expanded several hours later. The fire consumed 28,307 acres, destroyed 35 properties, and damaged 6 properties before full containment. Two fatalities were also attributed to the Fairview Fire. As of 7:38 AM PDT on September 17th, the fire was 98% contained with crews working to patrol and for and monitor any smoldering material.

Heavy rain from a thunderstorm over the Poomacha Burn Area caused flash flooding in the Pauma Valley. Highway 76 was temporarily closed due to the flash flooding. No reports of serious damage were received.
Water flowing across Old Highway 80 into Mexico, completely covering the roadway and making it impassable based on video. About 2 inches of widespread rain fell in the area.
Portions of Wildcat Canyon Rd on the Barona Reservation under 3-10 inches of running water due to heavy rainfall. Visibility reduced to 1/4 mile during rain.

Highway 18 between Waterman Canyon and Highway 138, heavy rain led to debris flows including boulders up to 1 foot in diameter across all lanes. Water several inches deep was also flowing across lanes.
CHP report of flooding on Highway 247, 3 vehicles possible submerged.
CHP report of a driver stuck in flash flooding with water coming into the vehicle.
Three feet of water over the road on Route 66 at Frontier Road. Side of the road is eroding.
Borrego Salton Seaway / Arroyo Salado-Truckhaven Trail completely flooded out. Signage and Road Closed signs were placed. About 1 inch of rain fell in this area in 4 hours.
Indio Road just south of Interstate 10 was closed due to flooding. A rain gauge in Indio Hills, 9 miles north of Indio, had 1.07 inches of rain in two hours on Saturday morning.
KTLA report of flooding near the 5200 block of Chicago Avenue in Riverside. Two vehicles were stranded in flood waters. Nearby UC Riverside reported 0.49 inch of rain in one hour.
Spotter report of flash flooding with ankle-deep water. Nearby March Air Reserve Base picked up 0.28 inch of rainfall in about 10 minutes, with a storm total of 0.42 inch.
Strong winds associated with Tropical Storm Kay blew down a newly planted tree on the campus of Sherman Indian High School in Riverside.
Mesonet Station LGMC1 Mt. Laguna at 6,000 Feet measured 0.98 inch of rainfall in one hour, and 3.23 inches total.
Mesonet station RCHC1 Ranchita measured 4.62 inches of storm total rainfall.
A strong thunderstorm in Murrieta produced 0.64 inches of rainfall.
Crestline maintenance yard reported 2.10 inches of storm total rainfall.
Mesonet station FW1313 Running Springs 1 measured 3.58 inches of storm total rainfall. Radar estimates were also near this amount.
Mesonet station LRAC1 Larson Ranch measured 2.83 inches of storm total rainfall.
CoCoRAHS station CA-RV-60 2.8 miles south-southwest of Lake Elsinore measured 2.09 inches of storm total rainfall.
CoCoRAHS station CA-RV-58 4.2 miles west of San Jacinto measured 1.33 inches of storm total rainfall.
CoCoRAHS station CA-SR-53 1.8 miles north-northeast of Upland measured 1.35 inches of rainfall.
Co-Op Observer EORC1 Lake Elsinore measured 0.99 inches of rainfall.
Mesonet station CMFC1 Campo measured 0.87 inch of rainfall.
CoCoRAHS station CA-SD-186 1.8 miles west-southwest of Ramona measured 0.95 inch of rainfall.
Mesonet station ANEC1 Alpine RAWS site measured 0.64 inch of rainfall.
Mesonet station TR120 Mt Laguna Portable measured 1.46 inches of storm total rainfall.

Seal Beach had surges come across the beach and into parking lots and Boardwalk 2100. High tide was around 6.6 FT on September 8. Berm was hastily erected, with pumps in place and sandbags ready for residents.

Heavy rain associated with residual moisture from post-tropical cyclone Kay occurred during the afternoon on September 12 in the San Bernardino County Mountains. Rain amounts of 1.5 to 3 inches occurred in the region. The Department of Highways reported a flash flood near Crestline, with multiple vehicles stuck in flood water on Lake Drive at Forest Shade Drive. The following are measured rain amounts from various Mesonet sites:||Mesonet Station FW1313, 1 WNW Running Springs: 3.58 inch.|Strawberry Peak, 3 WSW Lake Arrowhead: 2.88 inch.|Heaps Peak RAWS, 3 NW Running Springs: 2.68 inch.|Mesonet Station CRQC1, 1 SSW Lake Arrowhead: 1.74 inch.|Mesonet Station PPOC1 Panorama Point, 2 SSW Crestline: 1.66 inch.|Mesonet Station FW0025 Lake Arrowhead South, 1 SE Lake Arrowhead: 1.52 inch.

Heavy thunderstorms associated with remnant moisture from post-tropical cyclone Kay produced torrential rain over the Apple and El Dorado burn scars on the afternoon of September 12. Multiple debris flows occurred following torrential one-hour rainfall rates exceeding debris flow guidance from the USGS and CAGS. Two of the debris flows traveled several miles including the Banning Canyon wash showing debris logs and ash water. The most impactful debris flow occurred in Forest Falls and Oak Glen, where the flow traveled at least 3 miles down Oakland Road with 4 foot boulders, logs over-topping the road with several feet of mud, with several power poles destroyed. Another highly impactful debris flow formed in Forest Falls on Prospect Road, where large boulders, black water and logs took out trees and damaged several homes. Another debris flow occurred 0.5 mile away on Valley of the Falls Road, producing a 12-foot wall of dirt and rocks. An additional debris flow occurred on State Highway Route 38 just before Angeles Oaks. These flows are the most significant that have occurred since the fires in 2020. An estimated 30 homes were damaged and three vehicles were moved and damaged.||The following are recorded rain amounts from the same region:|Raywood Flats, 6 NNW Forest Falls: 2.44 inch in 1 hour and 2.75 inch for the day, resulting in the full closure of Highway 38.||Mesonet Station Yucc1 Little San Gorgonio Peak Yucaipa Ridge, 2 SE Forest Falls: 1.06 inch in 60 minutes.||Mesonet Station FFPC1, 1.5 W Forest Falls: 1.93 inch.

Heavy rain associated with residual moisture from post-tropical cyclone Kay occurred during the afternoon on September 12 in northern portions of the Inland Empire, particularly north of Rancho Cucamonga.||The following are measured rainfall:||Mesonet station LRAC1, 5.5 NE Rancho Cucamonga: 2.83 inch.||Mesonet station DECC1, 4.2 N Rancho Cucamonga: 2.75 inch.||Mesonet station DACC1, 3.9 NE Rancho Cucamonga: 1.97 inch.

Heavy rain associated with residual moisture from post-tropical cyclone Kay occurred during the afternoon on September 12 in southern portions of the Inland Empire. The Department of Highways reported a swift water rescue of a person seeking refuge on top of a vehicle. Local emergency managers also reported the southbound lane of I-15 was flooded at Dos Lagos.||The following are measured rain reports in the region:||Mesonet Station CW7445 Temescal Valley, 10 SE Corona: 1.78 inch.||Mesonet Station ECSC1 El Cariso RAWS, 5 WSW Lake Elsinore: 1.28 inch.

Very strong winds associated with Tropical Cyclone Kay impacted the San Diego County Mountains on September 9, with winds peaking in the morning hours. The following are the strongest wind reports in the region:||Mesonet station HP029 Cuyamaca Peak, 9 S Julian: 109 mph|Mesonet station HP016 Big Black Mountain, 9 WNW Santa Ysabel: 96 mph|Mesonet station HF002 Laguna Launch, 7 NW Mt Laguna: 93 mph|Mesonet Station SILSD Sill Hill, 9 SSW Julian: 91 mph|Mesonet station HP019 Mt Laguna Observatory, 1 S Mt Laguna: 80 mph|Mesonet station OTYC1 Otay Mountain RAWS, 5 WSW Dulzura: 79 mph|Mesonet station HP014 Boucher Hill, 3 WNW Palomar Mountain: 74 mph|Mesonet station SYRSD Santa Ysabel Ranch, 2 N Santa Ysabel: 72 mph|Mesonet station HF003 Pine Valley, 4 SSE Pine Valley: 71 mph|Mesonet station EWRSD East Willows, 4 E Alpine: 63 mph|Mesonet station WDCSD West Descanso, 7 WNW Pine Valley: 59 mph|Mesonet station VISSD Viejas, 3 ENE Alpine: 58 mph|Mesonet station ANEC1 Alpine RAWS, 5 E Alpine: 56 mph||Multiple reports of damage were received from the Department of Highways during this time in the San Diego County Mountains, with trees down reported on SR-79, I-8, Highway 78, powerlines down near Alpine, and a report of round barrels rolling across lanes of traffic along I-8.

Strong winds associated with Tropical Cyclone Kay impacted the San Diego County Valleys on September 9, with winds peaking in the morning hours. The following are reports of damage that morning:||2 W Rancho Bernardo: Downed tree limb (8-12 inches in diameter) partially blocking the road (NWS Employee).|4 ESE Valley Center: Downed power line and blocking the road (Public).|1 NE Valley Center: Downed tree blocking two lanes (Department of Highways).

Heavy rain associated with Tropical Cyclone Kay produced heavy rainfall across the San Diego County Mountains on September 9. The following are the heaviest rain reports from the day:||Mesonet station LGMC1 Mt. Laguna: 4.25 inch.|Mesonet Station MLGC1 Mt. Laguna Observatory RAWS, 2 NNW Mt. Laguna: 3.79 inch.|Mesonet Station AGUC1 Agua Caliente, 10 NE Mt. Laguna: 2.06 inch.|Mesonet Station TRRC1 Tierra Del Sol, 9 ENE Campo: 1.02 inch, 0.45 inch which occurred in one hour.

Heavy rain from residual moisture associated with Tropical Cyclone Kay occurred across northern portions of the Inland Empire, leading to multiple instances of flash flooding. Flash flooding was reported by a trained spotter on University Parkway and Kendall Drive near Devore, with one foot of water covering the roadway. Farther south toward Rialto, flooding occurred across all lanes on I-215 northbound. Flooding was also reported near San Bernardino across all lanes from University Parkway to Mount Vernon Ave.

Heavy rain occurred from residual moisture associated with Tropical Cyclone Kay on September 11 in southern portions of the Inland Empire. Local emergency managers reported a mud flow over roads in Avery Canyon, and California Highway Patrol reported flooding at State Street and Cactus Valley Road.

The Manzanita Fire was reported around 3:22 PM along Highway 330 near Middle Passing Lane in Running Springs. The wildfire topped out near 50 acres and significant fire running uphill before the fire department stopped the forward progress of the blaze.
Mesonet station VGRC1 Vista Grande reported 0.75 inch of rain in one hour.
Thunderstorms produced moderate rainfall southeast of Yucaipa. A trained spotter reported 0.56 inch of heavy rain, and Mesonet station CW1772 Yucaipa reported 1.06 inch of rain in one hour.
Flooding reported along Highway 243 in Pine Cove near Idyllwild, with small gravel and mud flows noted. Small hail (0.25 inch in diameter) was also reported.

Law enforcement reported roadway flooding on I-10 along the Riverside/San Bernardino County line. County and Bryant Road intersection closed due to flooding, with several inches of water over the roadway. Social media reports of flood damage to inside of garages and backside of two homes in the area. CWOP site in Yucaipa reported 0.84 inch of rain in 25 minutes.
Trained spotter reported penny size (0.75 inch) hail associated with a heavy thunderstorm.
Mesonet station on Toro Peak via HPWREN reported 0.52 inch of rain in one hour.

Morongo Indian reservation had extensive mud, rock and logs in a major debris flow off the 2020 Apple burn scar which traveled down the San Gorgonio River. This inundated the Banning Water Plant and pushed mud, rocks and logs onto roads.

A major flash flood debris flow occurred in Birch Creek through Potato Canyon. This area was affected by lesser debris flows October and December 2021 and August 2022 but this flood filled the entire channel in layers, overtopped and damage the Steakhouse restaurant in Oak Glen, took out power poles, pushed large boulder and layers of mud downstream onto Oak Glen Road and pushed up to windows on a couple homes. WCM Alex Tardy did a storm survey. Estimated 100,000 cubic yards of debris removed by San Bernardino Public Works. Video of the debris flow between 3 and 4 pm was recorded.

A large flash flood and debris flow occurred on Prospect street off of Valley of the Falls in Forest Falls, CA. The debris flow originated on the 2020 El Dorado burn scar after 1.1 inches of rain in an hour on Yucaipa Ridge. More than 1 debris flow occurred but the largest crossed Prospect street moving and damaging vehicles as well as damage homes. At least 2 homes had major damage. One fatality occurred when an older female was buried in debris, 3 days later found by search and rescue dogs. Residents took photos of debris flows and flash flooding including video and Ring security cameras. WCM visited the damage and SAR activity on September 13 and spoke with residents who shared additional photos and descriptions. A 20 foot boulder was lodged just above their home and their Jeep was washed down the hill (caught on Ring camera).

A storm survey by WCM found several debris flows on Valley of the Falls road in Forest Falls. The largest produced mud and rocks as high as 10 feet, completely covering the Valley of the Falls road. Other flash floods and debris occurred further into the canyon (deeper) affecting the roads and residences property. Homeowners discussed and described the flooding and impact. Most severe since August 2014.

A strong dust storm, originating in Yuma County (Arizona) and Imperial County moved into San Diego and Riverside Counties on October 6. Widespread reports of strong winds and severely reduced visibility were received across the deserts, mountains and inland valleys. The following are received reports:||Mesonet Station IKPSD (SDG&E) reported a dust storm 20 miles east of Campo.|A trained spotter reported 1/4 mile visibility in blowing dust 2 miles SSW of Mt Laguna.

A strong dust storm, originating in Yuma County (Arizona) and Imperial County moved into San Diego and Riverside Counties on October 6. Widespread reports of strong winds and severely reduced visibility were received across the deserts, mountains and inland valleys. AWOS station KL08 Borrego Springs Valley Airport reported visibility less than 1/4 mile.

A strong dust storm, originating in Yuma County (Arizona) and Imperial County moved into the Coachella Valley on October 6. Widespread reports of strong winds and severely reduced visibility were received across the deserts, mountains and inland valleys. The following are received reports:||ASOS station KTRM Thermal Airport reported visibility below 1/4 mile in blowing dust.|ASOS station KPSP Palm Springs Airport reported visibility of 3/4 mile in blowing dust.|Mesonet station WWAC1 Whitewater RAWS reported dust storm in the San Gorgonio Pass, with a 43 mph wind gust out of the southeast.

A strong dust storm, originating in Yuma County (Arizona) and Imperial County moved into San Diego and Riverside Counties on October 6. Widespread reports of strong winds and severely reduced visibility were received across the deserts, mountains and inland valleys. The following are received reports:||Mesonet station OTMSD Otay Mountain (SDG&E) reported a wind gust of 53 mph. Outflow from the dust storm produced a thunderstorm moving from the mountains into the valleys.|Mesonet station HP028 San Miguel reported a wind gust of 49 mph.

An EF-0 landspout occurred from Menifee to Southern Canyon Lake along Highway 78. The landspout tracked across mostly open space before dissipating near I-15. Minor damage reported. Half inch hail was also reported.
Several reports of a funnel cloud near Romoland and Menifee between 3-4 pm.
Four downed trees in Menifee from thunderstorm wind gusts (measured at 40-46 mph). Two trees were dead.
Heavy rain associated with thunderstorms occurred across northern San Diego County on October 11. Mesonet station AT107 recorded 0.7 inch, and a trained spotter reported 0.5 inch near Vista.

Department of Highways reported flooding at SR-74 E and Cranston Ranger Station at mile marker 49. Water covering the road, originating from the Fairview Fire burn scar. Mesonet station CNSC1 Cranston reported 1.03 inch of heavy rain within two hours.

Heavy rain from thunderstorms occurred across the San Bernardino County Mountains on October 11. The following are measured rainfall from the region:||Mesonet station YUCC1 Yucaipa Ridge measured rainfall of 1.62 inch.|Mesonet station CAGC1 measured rainfall of 0.87 inch.||In addition, a trained spotter reported 1.44 inch of rain as well as minor hail accumulation on roadways near Lake Arrowhead.
Three to four feet of water accumulated on Box Canyon Road at Coachella Canal Road. Boulders were also in the road, causing Box Canyon Road to close at 4:45 PM local time.
Mud, rocks, and debris covered all lanes near 33015 Bautista Canyon Road.
Coyote Canyon in Anza-Borrego State Park was closed off due to flooding.
Lake Cuyamaca received 1.59 inches of rain in hour, occurring between 1 and 2 PM local time. The storm total rainfall as of 7 AM local time on the 16th was 2.78 inches.
Dirt, debris, and rocks on Palowet Drive at Highway 74.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: A big rig was flipped on its left side about 3 miles southeast of Ontario, per a CalTrans report. Santa Ana winds were blowing from the northeast with a gust of 43 mph recorded at Jarupa Hills, though this may not be representative of the actual location of the flipped big rig.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: A big rig was flipped over about 3 miles northeast of Rancho Cucamonga, per a CalTrans report. An observation nearby (SE540 East Etiwanda Creek) reported northeast winds sustained at 16 mph with a peak gust of 38 mph, though this may not be representative of the actual location of the flipped big rig.
The Fremont Canyon RAWS site recorded a peak wind gust of 65 mph at 6:51 AM.
The Toro Peak HPWREN site measured a peak wind gust of 60 mph at 8:33 AM.

Home weather station reported Santa Ana winds, with a peak wind gust of 60 mph. At 3:50 PM, roof damage was reported: 1/3 of the roofing material was taken off of a home (heavy flat torch, 4x20 foot sheets), as well as removed a truck cover (aluminum poles and tarp cover 24x12 feet).

Estimated 50 mph winds in Spring Valley. Damage occurred at the Terrace Estates on Sweetwater Road, where at least five mobile homes were damaged. A roof was removed, a car port was destroyed, several roofs were damaged, and debris was lifted several hundred feet.
Mesonet station SE266 Lucerne Valley reported a peak wind gust of 64 mph.
CalTrans reports dust storm damaged a vehicle. Northwest winds of 20-24 mph with wind gusts of 40 mph were occurring across the region.
Mesonet station 015SE Whitewater reported a peak wind gust of 66 mph.
Mesonet station HP003 Toro Peak (HPWREN) reported a peak wind gust of 62 mph.
Mesonet station HP029 Cuyamaca Peak reported a peak wind gust of 62 mph.
Mesonet station SE269 Cushenbury Springs reported a peak wind gust of 60 mph.
Minor mudslides and rocks on the road on Highway 18 near Panorama Point. Rain of 0.43 inch reported in four hours.

Moderate to locally heavy snow fell across the San Bernardino Mountains on the morning of November 3. The Department of Highways reported 3 inches of snow in Big Bear City. Highway 38 was closed from Hatchery Drive (Big Bear City) to Frontage Road (Angelus Oaks) due to heavy snow. Several other reports were received from a trained spotter (3 inches in Baldwin Lake near Big Bear City with higher amounts to the west), and from broadcast media (4-8 inches at Snow Summit Big Mountain Resort, and 3 inches at Snow Valley Resort at 7000 feet).
The Department of Highways reports a debris flow with large rocks in the roadway at SR-18 and Crestline Bridge; nearby observation reported rain of 0.45 inch in 8 hours.
Mesonet station HP029 Cuyamaca Peak reported a peak wind gust of 71 mph.
Mesonet station HP003 Toro Peak (HPWREN) reported a peak wind gust of 63 mph.

Periods of moderate rainfall fell across the San Diego metro area on the afternoon of November 8. Several reports of flooding were received:|The Department of Highways reported flooding on Highway 94 and Federal Blvd, where 0.50 inch fell in three hours.|The Department of Highways also reported flooding at SR 94 and College Ave.|A National Weather Service employee reported roadway flooding on University Ave where rainfall of 0.25-0.30 inch had been reported in one hour.

Periods of moderate rainfall fell across the San Diego metro area on the afternoon of November 8. The following are received reports of flooding:|The Department of Highways reported flooding along SR 67 and the off ramp towards Bradley Ave. Rainfall of 0.5 inch was reported in three hours.|The Department of Highways reported flooding across the on ramp to I-15 south at Rancho Bernardo Road, with one stalled vehicle.
A trained spotter reported 1.43 inch of storm total rainfall from November 8.
Mesonet station HP029 Cuyamaca Peak reported a peak wind gust of 73 mph.

Gusty onshore winds occurred through the afternoon and evening hours of November 8 across the San Diego County Valleys. The following are reports of damage:|The Department of Highways reported a downed, 20-foot palm tree, which was blocking traffic lanes near Rainbow.|The Department of Highways reported a tree limb blocking northbound Gird Road southeast of Fallbrook.|The Department of Highways reported a downed tree blocking eastbound lanes of W Lilac Road at the Highway 395 intersection.|The Department of Highways reported a few large tree branches downed on Circle Road east of Bonsall.|Also, a National Weather Service employee a downed, large eucalyptus tree off of Rancho Bernardo Road, with many small downed limbs as well.

Public report of a downed tree blocking lanes of the onramp of southbound I-5 at Carlsbad Village Drive. Reports of wind gusts between 40-45 mph were also observed at the San Clemente Buoy and the Scripps La Jolla Buoy.

Santa Ana winds impacted the Santa Ana Mountains and Foothills starting late on November 15th and lasting through the afternoon hours on the 16th. The strongest winds occurred during the early morning hours on the 16th. The Fremont Canyon RAWS site recorded a peak wind gust of 85 mph. The Upper Talega mesonet site also recorded a peak wind gust of 59 mph.

Santa Ana winds impacted the San Gorgonio Pass starting late on November 15th and lasting through the afternoon hours on the 16th. The strongest winds occurred during the early morning hours on the 16th. The Cabazon mesonet site recorded a peak wind gust of 62 mph. The Beaumont mesonet site also recorded a peak wind gust of 58 mph.

Santa Ana winds impacted the San Diego County Mountains starting late on November 15th and lasting through the afternoon hours on the 16th. The strongest winds occurred during the early morning hours on the 16th. The Sill Hill mesonet site recorded a peak wind gust of 83 mph. The Big Black Mountain mesonet site also recorded a peak wind gust of 73 mph.

Santa Ana winds impacted the San Diego County Valleys starting late on November 15th and lasting through the afternoon hours on the 16th. The strongest winds occurred during the early morning hours on the 16th. The Hauser Mountain mesonet site recorded a peak wind gust of 67 mph. The Palomar Mountain Launch mesonet site also recorded a peak wind gust of 66 mph.

The Marshall Peak mesonet site recorded a peak wind gust of 81 mph. The Arrowhead Springs SoCal-Edison mesonet site also recorded a peak wind gust of 69 mph.

Santa Ana winds occurred across portions of the Santa Ana Mountains and Foothills on November 24th and 25th. Winds remained strong during much of the 24th with high wind gusts occurring throughout the morning, afternoon, and into the evening hours. The Fremont Canyon RAWS site recorded a peak wind gust of 59 mph.

Santa Ana winds occurred across portions of the San Gorgonio Pass on November 24th and 25th. Winds remained strong during much of the 24th with high wind gusts occurring throughout the morning, afternoon, and into the evening hours. The Cabazon SoCal-Edison mesonet site recorded a peak wind gust of 65 mph. Another nearby SoCal-Edison site in Cabazon recorded a wind gust to 58 mph.

Santa Ana winds occurred across portions of the San Diego County Mountains on November 24th and 25th. Winds remained strong during much of the 24th with high wind gusts occurring throughout the morning, afternoon, and into the evening hours. The Sill Hill SDGE mesonet site recorded a peak wind gust of 88 mph. The Cuyamaca Peak mesonet site also recorded a peak wind gust to 77 mph. A report of a tree blown down was received from Campo.

Santa Ana winds occurred across portions of the San Diego County Valleys on November 24th and 25th. Winds remained strong during much of the 24th with high wind gusts occurring throughout the morning, afternoon, and into the evening hours. The East Willows SDGE mesonet site recorded a peak wind gust of 70 mph. The Hauser Mountain mesonet site also recorded a peak wind gust to 69 mph. Multiple reports of trees blown down were received from Poway and Rancho Bernardo.

The Homeland SoCal-Edison mesonet site recorded a peak wind gust of 67 mph. The Devil Canyon SoCal-Edison mesonet site also recorded a peak wind gust to 62 mph. A report of power lines blown down was observed near Winchester.

The Arrowhead Springs mesonet site recorded a peak wind gust of 73 mph. The Devil Canyon Marshall Peak mesonet site also recorded a peak wind gust to 73 mph.
