events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Strong wind gusts of 45-55 mph occurred across portions of the Inland Empire on the 15th and 16th. Several reports of semi-trucks blown over, wires, and trees blown down were observed near Fontana, Rancho Cucamonga, and Devore.  Another semi was overturned near Jurupa Hills in wind gusts of 50 to 55 mph. Another report of a tree blown over was observed near Murrieta.

Heavy rain fell across Orange County on November 8, leading to flooding. The Department of Highways reported flooding on the off ramp of I-5 at El Toro Rd near Lake Forest, and flooding on the onramp to I-5 from Oso Parkway.

Flooding was reported across the Inland Empire on November as widespread rain fell. The Department of Highways reported flooding at SR-60 West and the Phillips Ranch Road offramp in the morning, with an additional report of two vehicles stuck in flood waters after attempting to drive through a closed off ramp onto Euclid.
A fire at an abandoned large home spread into brus near Steele Canyon and Willow Glen Drive near golf course. The wildfire was kept at 10 acres.

Flooding was reported across the Inland Empire on November as widespread rain fell. The Department of Highways reported flooding at I-10 W/Euclid Ave, with three lanes experiencing water and debris. The offramp of Highway 91 to Adams street was also flooded.
Flooding was reported across the Inland Empire on November as widespread rain fell. The Department of Highways reported flooding in one lane on SR-79 at Garboni Road.

Heavy rain fell in and around the Apple/ El Dorado burn scar on November 8, resulting in debris flow and flash flooding. Roadway flooding was reported on Oak Glen Road and Potato Canyon Road, with the roadway washing out at 12099 Oak Glen Road.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: High winds impacted portions of the Inland Empire on the 8th and 9th of November. A peak wind gust of 59 mph occurred in Lake Elsinore. In Devore, winds were strong enough to blow a semi truck onto its side.

High winds impacted the San Gorgonio Pass on the 8th and 9th of November. Peak wind gusts of 60 mph occurred at the Snowcreek Canyon SoCal-Edison site, with a peak gust of 58 mph at the Whitewater SoCal-Edison site.
High winds impacted the Santa Ana Mountains and Foothills on the 8th and 9th of November. Peak wind gusts of 63 mph occurred at the Fremont Canyon RAWS site.
High winds impacted the Riverside County Mountains on the 8th and 9th of November. Peak wind gusts of 67 mph occurred at the Toro Peak HPWREN site.

High winds impacted the Apple and Lucerne Valleys on the 8th and 9th of November. Wind gusts of 50-60 mph were fairly common. Peak wind gusts of 72 mph occurred at the Oak Hills SoCal-Edison site, with gust to 71 mph occurring at the Burns Canyon Road SoCal-Edison site.

Strong wind gusts of 40-55 mph occurred across inland portions of Orange County on November 8th and 9th, strongest on the 8th. Multiple reports of tree limbs blown down and roof shingles blown off were received in both the Santa Ana and La Habra areas on the afternoon of November 8th.

Heavy rain fell across the San Bernardino County Mountains into the far northern portions of the Inland Empire on November 8. The Department of Highways reported that SR-18 was closed in both directions due to flooding from 48th street to SR-138/18 bridge, as well as water flowing over the roadway on Institution Road and Verdemont Ranch Road.

The Department of Highways reported flooding and debris on Highway 138 and Waters Drive, with 3 inches of water covering the roadway. Total rainfall of 3 to 4.5 inches at Crestline to Lake Arrowhead. Mud and debris also covered Cajon Blvd and Kenwood Ave.
Department of Highways reported washouts on Ice House Canyon Road and Mt Baldy Road, with vehicles stuck. Total rainfall of 3.7 inches at Mt Baldy.
Department of Highways reported flooding at the intersection of Arrowhead Lake Road and Havenhurst Road.

Heavy rain fell across the San Bernardino County Mountains on November 8. The following are rain reports from the region:|Mesonet station FW6602 Running Springs reported 5.11 inches of heavy rain.|Mesonet station SSVC1 San Sevaine Lookout reported 3.66 inch of heavy rain.|Mesonet station LTLC1 Lytle Creek RAWS reported 3.12 inch of heavy rain.

Swiftwater rescue along North Indain Canyon Drive in Whitewater Wash in Palm Springs around 12:30 PM. Multiple vehicles were trapped with three drivers and a dog rescued successfully. Multiple roads, including Gene Autry Trail, Indian Canyon Drive, Vista Chino Road and North Indian Canyon Drive remained closed through 6 AM the following day.

High winds impacted the San Bernardino County Mountains on the 8th and 9th of November. Wind gusts of 60 to 80 mph were common. Peak gusts of 101 mph at Burns Canyon and 89 mph at the Silverwood Lake SoCal-Edison site were observed. Several reports of trees down and trees falling on power lines were received. In Wrightwood, winds were strong enough to break a double pane window on a house.

High-elevation heavy snow impacted the San Bernardino County Mountains November 8-9, with snow levels starting above 8000 feet on November 8, falling as low as 5700 feet on November 9 after the cold frontal passage. Amounts of 1 to 4 inches were common, with locally higher amounts up to 8 inches at Bear Mountain Snow Summit, and up to 5 inches in Snow Valley. The Mount Baldy Notch Ski area reported extensive rime as a result of the snow and very strong winds that occurred with this system.

High-elevation snow impacted the San Diego County Mountains from the evening on December 11 through December 12. Snowfall of 1 to 5 inches was common, with a report of 8 inches reported at the Mt Laguna COOP. The Department of Highways implemented a chain control on SR-78 and SR-79 from Santa Ysabel to Pine Valley, with a snow level of 3500 feet.

Strong winds impacted the San Diego County Mountains from the morning on December 11 through that evening. The following are Mesonet observations from December 11:|Mesonet station HF001 Palomar Mountain Launch reported a peak wind gust of 89 mph.|Mesonet station HP029 Cuyamaca Peak reported a peak wind gust of 68 mph.|Mesonet station AT571 Palomar Mountain Lookout reported a peak wind gust of 61 mph.

Strong winds impacted the Riverside County Mountains from early in the morning on December 11 into the late morning. The following are notable Mesonet wind gust reports:|Mesonet station Toro Peak reported a peak wind gust of 65 mph.|Mesonet station 010SE Cabazon (SCE1010) reported a peak wind gust of 63 mph.

High-elevation snow impacted the Riverside County Mountains from the morning on December 11 through December 12. Snow accumulations of 2 to 4 inches were reported above 5000 feet. Light snow was reported as low as 2500 feet near Beaumont, but did not stick.

High-elevation snow impacted the San Bernardino County Mountains from the morning on December 11 through December 12. Snow accumulations of 2 to 8 inches were common at elevations above 4500 feet, with some notable amounts:|10 inches of snow near Running Springs|12-15 inches of snow at Snow Valley.|The Department of Highways reported three vehicles stuck in snow at 271 Fairway Drive, with as many as 80 vehicles stuck in snow on Highway 18, resulting in the closure of Highway 18 at Upper Waterman Canyon at 4000 feet.

Ontario Fire department reported 6 person in the swiftwater channel in John Galvin park where the channel begins near I-10. Rainfall rates of 0.50 to 0.75 inches per hour had occurred from 7 am to 9 am in Ontario and Rancho Cucamonga. 3 persons were rescued. 3 more person were later found drowned in a retaining pond which was filled 15 to 20 feet high with storm runoff water. The bodies were not found until several days later due the water being too deep and low visibility. Multiple agencies were involved in the week long recovery efforts. The channel runs south past Ontario airport to where it reached the storage collection ponds on East Philadelphia Street. Search and rescue in Cucamonga Channel reported by CalOES and Ontario Fire Department. As many as 10 people experiencing homelessness were swept away as a surge of water occurred following 2 hours of heavy rain. Five people were immediately rescued, one person immediately reported deceased, with two additional bodies recovered (one of November 14, the other on November 16).

Heavy rain fell in and around the Apple/ El Dorado burn scar on November 8, resulting in debris flow flooding. Roadway flooding was reported on Oak Glen Road and Potato Canyon Road at 12099 Oak Glen Road. El Dorado burn scar and flood prone area has had many prior flash floods and debris flows.
CalTrans report of rocks falling into both lanes of Highway 38 due to rainfall in the area. Storm total rainfall of 0.30-0.60 inch occurred across the region.
High winds occurred across the Riverside County Mountains mainly during the afternoon on December 27th. A peak wind gust of 77 mph occurred at the Toro Peak HPWREN site.

High winds impacted the San Bernardino County Mountains on December 11, with the peak winds occurring from midnight through the mid-morning hours. Widespread wind gusts of 60 to 70 mph were observed, with local wind gusts over 80 mph reported. The following are notable wind gust reports:|Mesonet station 424SCE Silverwood Lake reported a peak wind gust of 84 mph.|Mesonet station SCE338 Cajon Lookout reported a peak wind gust of 77 mph.|Mesonet station SCE269 Cushenbury Springs reported a peak wind gust of 74 mph.
Victorville Airport reported 1/4 mile - 1 mile visibility in blowing dust for about two hours. The peak wind gust of 50 kt was reported at 2:55 AM.
High winds occurred across the Apple and Lucerne Valleys on the afternoon of December 27th. A peak wind gust of 63 mph was observed at the Lucerne Valley SoCal-Edison site.

Swiftwater rescue of woman in Cucamonga Wash at Airport Drive. The Ontario Fire Department reported the woman received minor injuries. Rainfall rates of 0.5 to 0.7 inch from Fullerton to Rancho Cucamonga between 7-8 am. The main IVT frontal band moved through Southern California 7-10 AM.

Swiftwater rescue in the Santa Ana River at Garden Grove Blvd. The area received 0.5 to 1 inch of rain at the time of rescue. An adult male was successfully rescued but taken to the hospital. The main IVT frontal band moved through Southern California 7-10 AM.

Hail of pea size (0.25 inch) to 0.5 inch in diameter, with hail covering the road on Coronado. Accidents reported on Highway-75 between Nab Coronado and Leyte Road on the Silver Strand (Beach Highway). One vehicle flipped.

Public report of flooding across all lanes on SR-22 East at Main Street. Rainfall totals generally between 0.70 and 1.20 inch occurred across this area on New Year's Eve, with localized higher totals.

Orange County Fire Authority reported 2 vehicles stuck in water on the 4th Street off-ramp on SR-55 Northbound. Occupants were stuck inside and on top of their vehicles and required rescuing.  Rainfall totals generally between 1.10 and 1.75 inch occurred in this area on New Year's Eve.
High winds occurred across the Riverside County Mountains during the afternoon and evening on December 31st. A peak wind gust of 79 mph occurred at the Toro Peak HPWREN site.

High winds occurred across the San Bernardino County Mountains during the afternoon and evening on December 31st. A peak wind gust of 75 mph occurred at the Lytle Creek SoCal-Edison Site. Similar wind speeds occurred at the Cajon Lookout SoCal-Edison site.
High winds occurred across the Apple and Lucerne Valleys during the evening on December 31st. A peak wind gust of 62 mph occurred at the Lucerne Valley SoCal-Edison Site.

Palm Springs Police Department closed North Indian Canyon Drive through the Whitewater wash due to water over the road, with the closure reported at 4:26 PM and December 11, remaining closed through 1 PM on December 12. The Riverside County Mountains reported 1-2 inches of rain prior to the closure, and Palm Springs reported 0.23 inch.
High winds occurred across the San Gorgonio Pass on December 31st. A peak wind gust of 60 mph occurred at the Whitewater RAWS site.
High winds occurred across the San Diego County Mountains on December 31st. A peak wind gust of 60 mph occurred at an observation site on Cuyamaca Peak.

United States Coast Guard cancelled the Parade of Lights boating event (start time 5:30 pm). Wind was gusting to 40 mph with heavy rain reported at North Island at noon when the frontal system moved through.

High surf was reported at Orange County Beaches, with tide overflowing onto the Pacific Coast Highway. Elevated to high surf of 5 to 9 feet was reported by early afternoon on January 5, with sets of 8 to 12 feet reported on the afternoon on January 6. Surf slowly diminished through the day on January 7.

High surf was reported at San Diego County Beaches, with high tide resulting in the closure of the Ocean Beach Pier. Elevated to high surf of 4 to 8 feet was reported by early afternoon on January 5, with sets of 8 to 12 feet reported in the morning on January 6. Surf slowly diminished through the day on January 7.

Swiftwater rescue of two vehicles stuck in wash on North Indian Canyon Drive near Sunrise Parkway. Whitewater and Morongo Canyon (Whitewater Trout Farm) and Lower Snow Creek received 0.5-1 inch from 6am-12pm. Video of vehicles in lower water crossing submerged in flowing water.

Widespread moderate rainfall occurred across the San Bernardino County Mountains on January 5, from the early morning through the mid-afternoon hours. Multiple instances of debris flows were recorded, with mud and large rocks/boulders covering portions of Highway 330 and large boulders on Highway 38. Often, these were the result of the repeated freeze, snow, thaw and rain in the mountains this winter, with small amounts of rain then causing the movement of boulders.

High-elevation snowfall occurred across the San Bernardino County Mountains from early January 5-January 6. Snow levels generally remained above 7,000 feet, but several inches of accumulation were noted as low as 6,000 feet. Snow amounts of 2-8 inches were received above 7,000 feet, with accumulations of 2-4 inches as low as 6,000 feet.

Strong winds occurred across the San Bernardino County Mountains late January 4 through the morning of January 5. Widespread wind gusts of 35-55 mph were recorded, with several notable gusts listed below:|Mesonet station 424SCE Silverwood Lake reported a peak wind gust of 72 mph.|Burns Canyon reported a peak wind gust of 72 mph.|Mesonet station Cajon Lookout SCE338 reported a peak wind gust of 64 mph.

A series of storm systems in close succession brought very heavy snowfall to the San Bernardino County Mountains, with the first occurring along a cold front late on January 14 into the morning hours of January 15, with the second system close on its heels, producing additional snowfall late on January 15 to early on January 17. The first system produced light to locally moderate snowfall, with 4 inches of snow reported near Green Valley Lake, and up to 6 inches of snow near Big Bear with blowing snow also reported.||The second, colder, system produced very heavy snowfall, leading to impressive multi-day snow accumulations:|Broadcast media reported 20-28 inches of snow accumulation at 7,000-8,000 feet at Snow Valley.|Broadcast media reported 21 inches of snow accumulation at 7,100 feet at Bear Mountain Snow Summit.|The Department of Highways reported 16 inches of snow accumulation at 6,900 feet near Running Springs.|The Department of Highways reported 13 inches of snow accumulation at 6,900 feet at Barton Flats.|The Department of Highways reported 12 inches of snow accumulation at 6,800 feet at the Big Bear Yard.

A series of Pacific storm systems produced widespread heavy rainfall across the San Diego metro area, producing rainfall totals of 3-5 inches near Fashion Valley from January 14-17, with the heaviest occurring the morning of January 15- the morning of January 16. The San Diego River reached 12.4-12.7 feet at Fashion Valley.||Every cross street in Mission Valley along the San Diego River was flooded, including toward the San Diego Trolley. Three vehicles were abandoned and under 2-3 feet of flowing water on Camino Del Este, Qualcomm Way and Fashion Valley Road. The San Diego River overflowed, with over 1 foot of standing water into the nearby parking structure.||Numerous swiftwater rescues were conducted, including one rescue of a woman whose car was completely submerged into the flood waters at Camino De La Reina and Avenida del No; a helicopter search for two victims was conducted near 4700 Pacific Highway, with five victims having been rescued from the water.||Hotel guests at the Riverleaf Inn were evacuated and vehicles were submerged in flowing water.

Strong winds impacted the San Diego County coastal areas through the early morning hours on January 16. Numerous trees were reported downed across the metro area:||A large pine tree fell on apartments on Marathon Drive in Mission Valley; some units were tagged as residents were unable to return.||A tree fell at 4059 Newton Ave. No injuries were reported, but residents were evacuated from the building.||A tree was downed into the roadway at Fortuna Ave and Ingraham St in Pacific Beach.||A large tree was downed at Archer and Cass St. Power outages of 2000 reported by SDG&E for Bonita and Pacific Beach.||A large tree landed on a vehicle at Playa Del Sur off of La Jolla Blvd.||A tree was reported down and blocking the road at 16292 Rambla De Las Flores.||Downed trees onto powerlines resulted in a road closure in Vista.

Strong winds impacted the San Diego County Valleys the evening of January 14. The Department of Highways reported a downed tree, which took down cable wires and partially blocked vehicles on Eucalyptus Drive.
Strong winds resulted in a downed tree in Valley Center, blocking all lanes of traffic at the intersection of Valley Center Road and Mac Tan Road.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Trees were downed near Lake Elsinore, resulting in structure damage.

Very strong winds impacted the San Diego County Mountains from the morning on January 15 into early January 16. Two notable peaks in the winds occurred, with the first occurring near sunrise on January 15; the following are the peak gust reported from January 15:||Laguna Launch (SDHGPA) reported a peak wind gust of 75 mph.|Volcan Mountain reported a peak wind gust of 66 mph.||The second peak occurred before dawn on the 16th. The following are some of the top wind gust reports from the second surge event:||Palomar Mountain Lookout reported a peak wind gust of 74 mph.|Boucher Hill reported a peak wind gust of 62 mph.|Harrison Park reported a peak wind gust of 61 mph.

Widespread heavy rain fell from late morning on January 14 through much of the afternoon. Rain accumulations of 1.25 inch to 2 inches were common across inland Orange County, resulting in widespread flooding reports. The following are reports of flooding from the Department of Highways.||Both lanes of the I-5 north offramp was 4th Ave was flooded in Santa Ana. Four vehicles were stuck in the flood waters.||Farther south, three vehicles were stuck in the flooded onramp to northbound I-5 at Crown Valley Pkwy in Laguna Niguel.
Orange County Fire Authority reported a swiftwater rescue of a young adult clinging to a tree in a creek, with rapidly moving water below. The person was airlifted out with no injuries reported.
The Department of Highways reported a rockslide in the westbound lane of Highway 74 near Hot Springs Canyon Road. Over 1 inch of rain had fallen in the region.
Heavy rain resulted in the closure of North Indian Canyon Road between Garnet Ave and Sunrise Pkwy due to flooding from the Whitewater River.
Heavy rain resulted in the flooding of Huffstatler Creek flowing over Huffstatler Road at 2nd St and 5th St; roads were closed due to flooding.
Harmony Grove Rd flooded at Wilgren Drive near Elfin Forest with four feet of water flowing in both directions into Elfin Park. Rain of 1.25-1.50 inch was reported that afternoon.
Department of Highways reported two to three lanes of southbound I-5 bypass at Highway 56 was flooded. Vehicles were unable to drive in the slow lane.

Heavy rain of 0.50 to 1.00 inch was reported on the afternoon and evening of January 14. The right lane of southbound I-805 north of Clairemont Mesa Blvd was flooded, and at Murray Ridge Road was flooded. All lanes except the HOV were flooded and vehicles were unable to pass. 10 inches of water were reported in lanes 1 and 2.

Moderate to heavy rain occurred across the San Diego County metro area from 5-7 pm, resulting in flooding of major freeways. Highway 94 at Euclid Ave was flooded in Lanes 3 and 4; I-5 at Mile of Cars north was flooded, with a large amount of water in all lanes making it difficult for vehicles to drive; I-805 Bonita Rd offramp was flooded.
Heavy rain resulted in flooding at N Gene Autry Trail and at Vista Chino near the Whitewater Wash.

Four feet of flowing water was reported on Saturn Blvd from the Tijuana River. A stolen SUV was found in the water, though no one was seen near the vehicle; speculated that the vehicle had been stolen.

A series of storm systems in close succession brought very heavy snowfall to the Riverside County Mountains, with the first occurring along a cold front late on January 14 into the morning hours of January 15, with the second system close on its heels, producing additional snowfall late on January 15 to early on January 17. The first system produced up to 11 inches of snow neat Mt San Jacinto at 8400 feet at the Long Valley Ranger Station at the top of the Palm Springs Tram. The second system had lower snow levels, with 4 to 6 inches reported as low as 5700 feet.

Heavy rain occurred across northern San Diego County on January 15-16, resulting in flooding near Rainbow. County officials announced the closure of Pala Mission Road near Highway 76, and Pala Temecula Road. Rainfall of 1 to 1.5 inch had been reported leading up to the flooding.
The Department of Highways reported water flowing across Cole Grade Road from the San Luis Rey River. Rainfall of 8 to 11 inches had been received in the 72 hours prior to the flood report.

Harmony Grove Road closed due to flooding, with 1-2 feet of flowing water from the Escondido Creek. Rainfall of 2 to 3 inches had been reported in the prior 24 hours, with 4 to 5.5 inches in the 72 hours leading up to the flooding.
Escondido Creek overflowed, and flooded fields and parking areas alongside the river and Rancho Santa Fe Road.
The Department of Highways reported large boulders in the road on SR-78 and Wynola Road near Julian. That area had received 2 to 3 inches of rain in the preceeding 24 hours.
San Diego County official reported flooding at on Pine Creek Crossing, resulting in the closure of the road.

Flooding was reported early in the morning on January 16 due to heavy rain, with the area having received 1.5 to 2 inches in the prior 12 hours, and 2.5 to 4 inches in the preceding 24 hours. Alpine Blvd was closed due to flooding, with flooding also reported south of Alpine due to the local creek.
Flooding was reported at Honey Springs Road and Mother Grundy truck trail, with two feet of water over the road. Three inches of rainfall was reported in the 24 hours preceding the flooding.
Swift water rescue on Otay Lakes Road and milepost 8. Victim was rescued on top of the vehicle.

A woman was rescued by San Diego lifeguard after being stranded in her vehicle in four feet of water near the Tijuana River. 7 inches of rain had been reported at Otay Mountain in the preceding 3 days, with 4.2 inches of rain in Bonita.

A retaining wall collapsed in Corona around 4:30 AM on January 16 resulting in twenty-four residents who had to evacuate their homes in nearby areas. One home was damaged immediately below the wall, and cracked the foundation above. Broadcast media reported that concrete blocks crashed down into adjacent properties, burying backyards and patios, and smashing through glass doors. Corona has received 1.5 to 3 inches of rain in the preceding 48 hours before the collapse.
Mesonet station FRCC1 Fremont Canyon reported a wind gust of 72 mph.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Department of Highways reported a downed tree into lanes on Simpson Road at Rice Road in Winchester. Nearby site Domenigoni Pkwy reported north winds gusting to 41 mph.
Mesonet station FBZC1 Fallbrook RAWS reported a peak wind gust of 65 mph.
Public report of a 30-foot tall, 3-foot diameter tree downed, blocking a lane of Antonio Parkway at Oso Pkwy. Nearby mesonet station reported northeast wind gusts of 25-30 mph at the time.

Department of Highways reported a downed tree and powerline onto Valley of the Falls Drive near Redwood Drive in Forest Falls. Nearby mesonet site Mill Creek reported south-southeast winds gusting to 44 mph.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Department of Highways reported a downed tree blocking all lanes of Ortega Highway at South Main Divide Road. Nearby El Cariso RAWS reported northwest wind gusts to 63 mph.
Department of Highways reports a downed tree blocking the northbound lanes of the Pacific Coast Highway at Doheny Park Blvd. Nearby Capistrano mesonet station reported winds gusting to 37 mph.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Mesonet station SE268 Box Springs Mountain reported a peak wind gust of 69 mph.
Mesonet station E3131 Pleasants Peak reported a peak wind gust of 71 mph.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Social media post of three large, uprooted trees near Whiterood Road and Avenida Acacias in Murrieta. Estimated wind gusts of 45 to 55 mph.
Trained spotter reported downed trees and branches and blowing dust, with wind gusts to 50 mph.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Mesonet station 039SE Shandin Hills reported a peak wind gust of 71 mph.
Mesonet station 189SE Arrowhead Springs reported a peak wind gust of 75 mph.

King Tides impacted the Southern California coastline January 21 and 22. Official observed water levels at 9410230 at La Jolla reported a peak water level of 6.90 feet at 1554z on January 21 and 7.04 feet at 1642z on January 22. Coastal flooding was reported in low-lying areas in San Diego County. A drone video from CBS8 shows water and surf pounding the Marine Room Restaurant during high tide on January 20.

Strong onshore winds impacted the San Bernardino County Mountains from the evening on January 9 through the afternoon on January 10. Widespread wind gusts over 50 mph were reported, with gusts as high as 77 mph recorded in several locations. The strongest winds occurred from late on January 9 through the morning on January 10. The following are the highest wind gust reports in the San Bernardino County Mountains:||Mesonet station SE338 Cajon Lookout reported a peak wind gust of 77 mph.|Mesonet station 056SE Lytle Creek South reported a peak wind gust of 77 mph.|Mesonet station 424SE Silverwood Lake reported a peak wind gust of 76 mph.|Burns Canyon reported a peak wind gust of 71 mph.|Mesonet station 053SE Cajon Canyon reported a peak wind gust of 68 mph.|Mesonet station 590SCE reported a peak wind gust of 68 mph.|Mesonet station SCE257 Boneyard Canyon reported a peak wind gust of 68 mph.|Mesonet station SCE664 Valley of the Falls reported a peak wind gust of 68 mph.||The Department of Highways reported a downed powerline in the lane of Camp Rock Road at Cheshire Road.

Strong onshore winds impacted the San Gorgonio Pass through the afternoon and evening on January 10. Widespread wind gusts over 50 mph were reported, with gusts as high as 70 mph recorded at Whitewater. The following are the highest wind gust reports at the San Gorgonio Pass near Banning:||Mesonet station 015SCE Whitewater reported a peak wind gust of 70 mph.|Whitewater RAWS reported a peak wind gust of 67 mph.|Mesonet station SCE1010 Cabazon reported a peak wind gust of 62 mph.

Strong onshore winds impacted the San Diego County Mountains through the afternoon and evening on January 10. Widespread wind gusts over 50 mph were reported, with gusts as high as 71 mph recorded at Boucher Hill. The following are the highest wind gust reports in the San Diego County Mountains:||HPWREN site Boucher Hill reported a peak wind gust of 71 mph.|Cuyamaca Peak reported a peak wind gust of 66 mph.|SDGE site Lucky Five Ranch reported a peak wind gust of 61 mph.|Oak Grover reported a peak wind gust of 60 mph.
Orange County Public Works reported minor flooding on roadways at Silverado Canyon, with rapid water movement in creeks. Two to three inches of rain were observed in the upper canyons.
The Department of Highways reported flooding in 4 out of 5 lanes.
Public report of six inches of flowing water in the HOV lane on Highway 91.
The Department of Highways reported a road closure along Silver Rock Road to Colorado Road due to flooding.
Arrowbear Bridge submerged due to flood waters.
Arrowbear Drive at Music Camp Drive closed due to flooding. The area received 3.5 inches of rainfall.
The Department of Highways reported a road closure of Glendale Ave to Deep Creek Road due to flow in the Mojave River.
Public report of standing water in the backyard of a residence, and water several inches deep covering roadways.
The Department of Highways reported water flowing across Highway 173, making the road impassable. A vehicle was stuck in the floodwaters near the west fork of the Mojave River.

The Department of Highways reported water flowing over Highway 173 at Arrowhead Lake Road, with a vehicle stuck in the floodwaters. The area had received 4.99 inch of rain in the previous 24 hours, with rainfall totals of 5.83 inches for the event.

Heavy rainfall occurred across the San Bernardino County Mountains (west of the Cajon Pass) from January 9-10. Mesonet stations reported 4.6 inches (DVOC1 Devore) to 6.59 inches (MFLC1 Lytle Creek) in the previous 24 hours, with rain amounts as high as 9.50 inches at the top of Lytle Creek Canyon. Several flood reports were received:||The Department of Highways reported a road closure at Glen Helen Parkway due to flooding and debris. Broadcast media report of fast flowing water over Lytle Creek Road, flowing over the culvert.

The City of Palm Springs reported the closure of North Indian Canyon Drive at the wash due to flooding. The Palm Springs Fire Department conducted a swift water rescue, with at least one person rescued from the vehicle.

Strong winds impacted Balboa Park on January 26, with wind gusts of 30 to 48 mph measured in the region surrounding the park. At least 35 trees were downed in Balboa Park, prompting city and county officials to close the park through the remainder of the day. One person was injured when a tree fell on her, with her sustaining minor injuries. Another tree fell on a car and broke a wind shield. Authorities worked to removed tree limbs and branches that fell and blocked area streets.
Caltrans report of water flooding the HOV lanes at SR-55 and I-5 Northbound. Clogged drains likely played a part as observed rainfall amounts at the time were 0.18 inch over the previous 3 hours.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: A large branch was torn off from a pine tree in Hunt Park. Widespread wind gusts 30 to 35 mph occurred in this region between Corona and Riverside.

Snow fell across many of the mountain communities in the San Bernardino Mountains generally at elevations near or above 5000 feet. Areas from Crestline to Running Springs to Green Valley lake received 4-6 inches of snow by sunrise on the 30th. The Mt Baldy Ski Resort also received 5 inches of snow.
A trained spotter reported storm total snowfall of 5.5 inches at Birch Hill on Palomar Mountain.

Heavy rain with a few embedded thunderstorms occurred mainly over the San Diego County Valleys on January 30th, generally between the hours of 11 AM and 6 PM. Rainfall totals of 0.50-1.00 inch were common, with a few localized areas near San Marcos and Escondido receiving about 1.10 inches.

Very strong winds impacted the San Diego County Mountains through much of the morning on January 26. Widespread wind gusts in excess of 60 mph occurred, especially from 9 AM through noon. The following are the strongest wind gusts recorded that morning:||SDGE Sill Hill reported a peak wind gust of 93 mph.|SDHGPA Laguna Launch reported a peak wind gust of 88 mph.|SDGE Buckman Springs reported a peak wind gust of  of 86 mph.|SDGE Crestwood reported a peak wind gust of 86 mph.|Palomar Mountain Lookout reported a peak wind gust of 83 mph.|Pine Valley - Horse Launch reported a peak wind gust of 83 mph.|Morena Dam reported a peak wind gust of 79 mph.|HPWREN Boucher Hill reported a peak wind gust of 79 mph.|Mt Laguna Observatory reported a peak wind gust of 79 mph.|SDGE La Posta reported a peak wind gust of 79 mph.|SDGE Sunrise Highway reported a peak wind gust of 75 mph.||Damage was reported by late morning, with a telephone pole downed across SR-79, blocking the southbound lanes near Pine Valley. A large tree was downed near Julian and was leaning on power lines.

Very strong winds impacted the I-8 corridor in the San Diego County Mountains the morning of January 26. Numerous semi-trucks were overturned near Campo, resulting in the closure of I-8 at Crestwood to divert traffic. I-8 west was eventually closed to high-profile vehicles to additional overturned big rigs. Winds were gusting around 70 to 80 mph at the time of the overturned vehicles, with a peak gust of 86 mph reported at mesonet station CWDSD Crestwood.

Strong winds impacted the San Diego County Valleys the morning of January 26. The Department of Highways reported numerous trees down across the county and two powerlines downed near Ramona, blocking the westbound lane. A big rig tipped over near Rancho Bernardo with asphalt blocking the slow lane, causing substantial traffic delays. A trained spotter reported a downed, 80-foot Euclid tree near Escondido.

Gusty winds impacted San Diego County coastal areas through much of the morning on January 26. Numerous trees were downed near downtown and Balboa Park, with one tree blocking the onramp to northbound I-5. San Diego International Airport KSAN reported a peak wind gust of 40 mph.
Mesonet station 645SE Offroad Porter reported a peak wind gust of 92 mph in the San Gorgonio Pass.

Very strong winds impacted the Santa Ana Mountains through much of the morning on January 26. Widespread wind gusts in excess of 50 mph occurred, especially from 9 AM through noon. The following are the strongest wind gusts in the Santa Ana Mountains:||Fremont Canyon reported a peak wind gust of 81 mph.|Pleasants Peak reported a peak wind gust of 75 mph.|Chino Hills reported a peak wind gust of 68 mph.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Very strong winds impacted the Inland Empire on January 26, with peak winds occurring during the late morning hours. Widespread wind gusts of 40 to 60 mph were observed. The following are the highest wind gusts across the Inland Empire:||SCE125 Devil Canyon reported a peak wind gust of 71 mph.|Rancho Cucamonga reported a peak wind gust of 65 mph.|Highland Springs reported a peak wind gust of 65 mph.|Ontario Airport reported a peak wind gust of 63 mph.|SCE157 Fontana reported a peak wind gust of 63 mph.|SCE809 SCU San Bernardino reported a peak wind gust of 63 mph.|SCE218 Chino Hills reported a peak wind gust of 62 mph.|SCE722 Lytle Creek reported a peak wind gust of 62 mph.|SCE271 North Fontana reported a peak wind gust of 61 mph.|SCE536 Fontana reported a peak wind gust of 60 mph.|SCE603 Verdemont reported a peak wind gust of 60 mph.||Impacts were especially felt across northern portions of the Inland Empire near Ontario, where numerous semi trucks were blown over, one instance where portions of I-15 were blocked by an overturned semi at I-10.

Strong winds impacted the San Bernardino County Mountains through much of the morning on January 26. Wind gusts in excess of 50 mph occurred, especially from 7 AM through 11 AM. The following are the strongest wind gusts recorded that morning:||Arrowhead Springs recorded a peak wind gust of 83 mph.|Marshall Peak recorded a peak wind gust of 80 mph.|Running Springs recorded a peak wind gust of 72 mph.|Lytle Creek South recorded a peak wind gust of 64 mph.|San Sevaine Flats recorded a peak wind gust of 61 mph.||Multiple reports of damage were reported, including a downed tree that brought powerlines down blocking a roadway; an electric pole broken in half; a semi truck with a 53-foot trailer flipped, blocking northbound I-15 at the Devore offramp; and an overturned big rig blocking all northbound lanes of I-215, resulting in a complete shutdown.

Snow fell across the Riverside County Mountains early in the morning on February 13. The Mt San Jacinto Long Valley Ranger Station at the top of the Palm Springs Tram reported 3 inches of snow at 8400 feet.
Snow fell across the San Diego County Mountains in the afternoon on February 12 through mid-morning on February 13. Storm total snowfall of 3.5 inches was reported at Birch Hill.
CalTrans report of a mudslide leading to rocks and dirt blocking eastbound lanes on Via de Santa Fe near Rancho Santa Fe.
CalTrans report of a mudslide on Old Julian Highway by MM 4.5.
CalTrans report of a 4' X 5' boulder on Highway 78 by Wynola Road.

Various reports of heavy snow received from San Bernardino County Public Works, broadcast media, and trained spotters. Totals ranged from around 4 inches of snow near Arrowbear Lake to 7 inches near Big Bear Lake, and upwards of 10 inches near Running Springs.

Flash flooding on College Avenue near SR76 reported by CalTrans. Full highway closure with disabled vehicles due to water up to 2.5 feet deep. Rainfall rates of 0.84 inch per hour occurred in the area, per observations from KCRQ ASOS.
CalTrans report of rocks and debris in roadway on Seminole Drive at Main Street in Cabazon.
CalTrans report of basketball-sized boulders on Ortega Highway near the Ortega Oaks Candy Store.
Newspaper reported a palm tree fell and crushed a parked Toyota Tundra due to strong winds estimated about 40 mph. The truck was parked in the 900 block of 8th street in Coronado. Time estimated.
Newspaper report of multiple trees down along Carlsbad Village Drive and Highland Drive due to wind gusts estimated around 40 mph. Time estimated.
CalTrans report of flooding on the Palm Ave off-ramp lanes on I-5 in Imperial Beach.
Report received from CalTrans. Woods Valley Road near Valley Center was flooded in both lanes due to rainwater runoff and poor drainage.

Rainfall rates of 0.5 to 0.8 inches per hour were observed in this area between 4 and 5 PM. Total rainfall of 1.30 inches occurred just west of Cranston Station near Valle Vista at Blackburn Road and State Highway 74. Flooding occurred at this location around 2:30 PM as well.
CalTrans report of flooding in the right lane on I-5 South near Oceanside.
Public report of flooding on SR78 West on the on-ramp to I-5 North.
Public report of flooding on SR76 at I-5. Water was reported to be up to 2.5 feet deep.
Flooding reported in all lanes on SR94 West at College Ave. A vehicle was stuck and flooded out on the right shoulder.
CalTrans report of flooding on the Mount Soledad Freeway near the I-15 on-ramp.
CalTrans report of flooding on the Palm Ave off-ramp lanes on I-5 near Imperial Beach.

Per an NWS Storm Survey, levels on the San Diego River at Fashion Valley reached up to 10.2 feet. Fashion Valley Road had 1 foot of flowing water and was closed. Avenida Del Rio had 2 feet of flowing water and was closed. The entire lower parking structure at the Fashion Valley Mall was filled with 1 to 2 feet of water. Mission Center Road was closed but did not have flowing water. Riverwalk Golf Driving Range was filled with water. San Diego Mission Road had minor water flow debris at crossing, but was open.
CalTrans report - Woods Valley Road near Valley Center was flooded in both lanes due to rainwater runoff and poor drainage.

Heavy rain fell across much of San Diego County on January 1st. Per reports from NWS Employees and other trained spotters rainfall totals of 1-3 inches fell across much of the county through the evening hours on the 1st.
A trained spotter reported storm total rainfall of 1.4 inches through about 8 AM.
A trained spotter reported 1.78 inches of heavy rain occurring at their location through about 8 AM on the 1st.
High winds impacted the Santa Ana Mountains early on January 1st. The Fremont Canyon RAWS site recorded a peak wind gust of 71 mph.
High winds impacted the San Gorgonio Pass early on January 1st. The Cabazon SoCal-Edison site recorded a peak wind gust of 59 mph on the morning of January 1st.

High winds impacted the San Diego County Mountains during the morning and afternoon hours on January 1st. The Boulevard West SDG&E site recorded a peak wind gust of 67 mph, with gusts of 50-65 mph elsewhere.

High winds occurred across the San Gorgonio Pass mainly during the morning and early afternoon hours on February 14th. Gusts of 55-65 mph were common, along with some localized higher gusts. The Whitewater RAWS site recorded a peak wind gust to 77 mph, and the Snowcreek Canyon SoCal-Edison site recorded a peak wind gust of 72 mph.

High winds occurred across the San Diego County Mountains mainly during the morning and early afternoon hours on February 14th. Gusts of 55-70 mph were common, along with some localized higher gusts. The Laguna Launch site recorded a peak wind gust to 93 mph, and the Volcan Mountain SDG&E site recorded a peak wind gust of 74 mph.

High winds occurred across the San Bernardino County Mountains mainly during the morning and early afternoon hours on February 14th. Gusts of 50-60 mph were common, along with some localized higher gusts. The Burns Canyon mesonet site recorded a peak wind gust to 65 mph, and the Cajon Lookout SoCal-Edison site recorded a peak wind gust of 60 mph.

High winds occurred across the Apple and Lucerne Valleys mainly during the morning and early afternoon hours on February 14th. Multiple SoCal-Edison sites in the Lucerne Valley recorded peak wind gusts of 58 mph. In Phelan, a street sign was blown over in 40-50 mph winds per a report from CalTrans.

Snow levels fell to as low as around 3000 feet in portions of the Riverside County Mountains on the evening of February 14th, allowing for about 1-3 inches of accumulating snow at these elevations. In Anza, icy road conditions on SR-371 and SR-74 led to multiple trapped vehicles and tow trucks were unable to reach the vehicles, per CalTrans.

Snow levels fell to as low as around 3000 feet in portions of the San Bernardino County Mountans on the evening of February 14th, allowing for about 1-3 inches of accumulating snow at these elevations. Multiple CalTrans reports of vehicles spinning out and sliding off of Highway 189 were received from the Lake Arrowhead and Crestline areas.

Snow levels fell to as low as around 3000 feet in portions of the Inland Empire on the evening of February 14th, allowing for about 2-4 inches of accumulating snow at these elevations. Icy road conditions led to multiple vehicles being trapped near Pine Valley, Warner Springs, and in Julian near S2 and S22 off of Highway 78. A semi truck also jackknifed near Warner Springs. CalTrans issued a Sigalert on San Felipe Road due to the treacherous travel conditions in the area.

Widespread rainfall occurred on the afternoon and evening of February 12, developing across the coastal mountain slopes and moving westward towards the coast in San Diego County. Lightning was reported across coastal areas as well as the deserts. The heaviest rainfall occurred across the valleys where general 0.50-0.75 were reported, with the highest amount of 1.39 recorded at Harbison Canyon.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Snow levels fell to as low as around 3000 feet in portions of the Inland Empire on the evening of February 14th, allowing for about 0.50-1.00 inch of accumulating snow at these elevations. Reports of very difficult travel conditions were received from CalTrans.

Anomalously strong winds impacted the San Diego County coastline from the very early morning hours on February 22 through the afternoon, peaking during the overnight hours through sunrise.||The following are the strongest wind reports from the coast:|Mesonet station XZUN Silver Strand Beach reported a peak wind gust of 58 mph.|Mesonet station XOCJ Oceanside Jetty reported a peak wind gust of 57 mph.|AWOS Station KNXF Red Beach Airport reported a peak wind gust of 56 mph.||Tree damage was also reported during the early morning hours, with a toppled tree resulting in car damage in Mission Valley; a large Torrey Pine tree fell on a home in Del Mar Heights with a branch crashing through the roof in the living room; and a large Torrey Pine tree toppled over at the Torrey Pines Golf Course.

Very strong winds impacted the San Diego County Mountains from the evening on February 21 through the early morning hours on February 22, when widespread wind gusts in excess of 50 mph were observed.||The following are the highest wind gusts recorded across the San Diego County Mountains:|Mesonet station VCMSD Volcan Mountain (SDGE) reported a peak wind gust of 84 mph.|Mesonet station HRPSD Harrison Park (SDGE) reported a peak wind gust of 81 mph.|Mesonet station Boulevard West (SDGE) reported a peak wind gust of 80 mph.|Pine Valley - Horse Launch reported a peak wind gust of 77 mph.|Lucky Five Ranch (SDGE) reported a peak wind gust of 75 mph.|Mesonet station DVI00558 Julian reported a peak wind gust of 70 mph.|Palomar Mountain Lookout reported a peak wind gust of 70 mph.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Snow levels falling to between 1000-2000 feet on February 23rd and 25th allowed for accumulating snow at various locations in the Inland Empire. Most accumulations were around 1 inch or less, but were still enough to cause hazardous travel conditions. Accumulating snow was observed near Fontana and Devore, with rain and snow mixing in near Riverside, Moreno Valley, and Temecula. Total snowfall of 10.5 inches was observed near Devore, just below the Cajon Pass which led to the closing of the I-15 and I-215 interchange due to multiple disabled vehicles. A severe pile-up involving 20 vehicles occurred around 11 PM on February 22 in Yucaipa; officials said the crash was caused by winter conditions, including icy slush that was seen on the road.

Snow levels fell to between 1500-2000 feet in the Santa Ana Mountains on the morning of February 25th. Per a report from a trained spotter, rain changed over to snow in Silverado Canyon at elevations around 1800 feet.

Snow levels fell to between 2000-3000 feet in the Apple and Lucerne Valleys on the morning of February 25th. Spotters reported upwards of 6 to 12 inches of accumulating snow near Phelan. Per reports from San Bernardino County Public Works, roughly 1-5 of snow fell in locations including Victorville, Apple Valley, and lower elevations near Hesperia.

Snow levels fell to between 3000-3500 feet in the Riverside County Mountains on February 25th. Areas along the San Diego-Riverside County border near Aguanga received roughly 3 to 6 inches of accumulating snowfall.

Snow levels fell to between 2700-3500 feet in the San Diego County Mountains on February 25th. Areas along the San Diego-Riverside County border near Aguanga received roughly 3 to 6 inches of accumulating snowfall, with up to 2 inches of snow reported as low as 2700 feet in Oak Grove. Areas near Santa Ysabel at elevations around 3000 feet received 3 inches of accumulating snowfall.
San Bernardino County Fire conducted a swift water rescue of one occupant from a truck. Report of rushing water enveloping the lower half of the truck.
CalTrans report of flooding across both lanes of Foothill Drive due to heavy rain.
Public report of flooding at Country Club Dip south of Harmony Grove Road, resulting in its closure.
Department of Highways reported a 3-4 foot boulder came off the mountain and fell into the road following heavy rainfall.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Strong winds impacted western and southern portions of the Inland Empire late evening on February 24 through the early morning hours on February 25 ahead of a cold front. The following are the strongest wind reports:||Mesonet station Corona RAWS reported a peak wind gust of 63 mph.|Temescal Valley reported a peak wind gust of 59 mph.|Temecula reported wind gusts of 40 to 55 mph.||The Department of Highways reported a downed tree blocking te right land of Campbell Ranch Road at Mayhew Canyon Road in Temescal.
The Department of Highways reported a downed tree blocking the slow lanes of Highway 55 north of the Highway 73 transition.

Heavy rain led to flooding early in the morning on February 25 across inland Orange County, centered around the community of Costa Mesa. The Department of Highways reported flooding at the Bristol Street on-ramp on I-405 with vehicles stuck in the floodwaters; street flooding leading to road closures and stranded vehicles; and SR-173 and Campus Drive had 1-2 feet of water in two lanes.
The Department of Highways reported flooding and mud along the Duncan Canyon Road offramp, with two vehicles stopped and on vehicle in two feet of mud.
The Department of Highways reported a vehicle stuck in mud on Cleghorn Road off of SR-1138. Search and rescue in place at midnight.

A historic blizzard impacted the San Bernardino County Mountains February 23-26, prompting the first-ever Blizzard Warning issued by NWS San Diego. The heaviest snowfall occurred on February 24-25. Snow accumulations on the order of FEET inundated mountain communities with 70-90+ inches recorded at ski resorts, and 2-3 feet occurred at mountain communities located at 5000-7000 feet.||This snowfall severely incapacitated communities, resulting in hard closures of Highway 2, Highway 18, Highway 138 and Highway 330 from Friday, February 24 through Monday, February 27. Prior to the road closures, multiple vehicles had been stuck or disabled.  Vehicles also became stuck on the heavily traveled I-15 through the Cajon Pass Saturday morning, which ended up being shut down due to snow and ice early Saturday afternoon. As of the evening on February 27, these highways partially reopened to escort residents back up the mountain and allow for food and fuel delivery to mountain communities. 500 6th and 7th grade students who were attending a Science Camp in the mountains were unable to return home as scheduled on Feb 24th.||The following are some of the highest recorded snow totals from this region:||Mountain High (6600-8000'): 93|Snow Valley (7000-8000'): 78-90|End of Mt Baldy Road (6360'): 77|Running Springs (6225'): 71|Green Valley Lake (6900'): 70|Lake Arrowhead (5200'): 68|Arrowbear Lake (6220'): 65|Big Bear Mountain Snow Summit (7100'): 63-75|Crestline Yard (4850'): 63|Long Valley Ranger Station (4850'): 60|Wrightwood Acorn Canyon (6600'): 50-55||Impacts extended well beyond the end time of this round of snow, especially as another storm system produced additional FEET of snowfall in the following days. Residents remained trapped, transportation remained halted and resources ran dry.

An extensive period of heavy snow impacted the San Diego County Mountains February 22-26. Chain controls were activated as early as the morning on February 22 ahead of the heavy snow. The following are some of the heaviest storm total snow reports from the San Diego County Mountains:||Palomar Mountain COOP (5600'): 36|Birch Hill Palomar Mountain (5700'): 32|Palomar Mountain (CalFire): 28|Julian North Peak (5100'): 25|Mt Laguna (6100'): 24.

An extensive period of heavy snow impacted the Riverside County Mountains February 22-26. The following are some of the heaviest storm total snow reports from the Riverside County Mountains:||Long Valley Ranger Station (8400'): 60|Idyllwild COOP (5400'): 36|Idyllwild (5600'): 17.

An avalanche on Mount San Jacinto was captured in photos and video by nearby travelers, which were then shared by the Riverside County Mountain Rescue Organization. No other specific impacts are known at this time.

High winds impacted the San Gorgonio Pass starting on the afternoon of February 28th and lasted overnight, with high winds continuing over into March 1st as well. A peak gust of 61 mph occurred at the Whitewater RAWS site on the 28th.

Additional rounds of light to moderate snow occurred in the San Bernardino County Mountains on February 27th, with more moderate to heavy snow occurring on February 28th. Numerous locations at elevations above 4000 feet received an additional 1 to 3 feet of snow during this time. Bear Mountain and Lake Arrowhead received upwards of 31 inches during the last two days of February. Crestline Yard and Mount Baldy received between 2 and 3 feet of snow during this time as well. Lower snow levels contributed to accumulating snow at elevations between 3000 and 4000 feet as well. A trained spotter reported moderate snow accumulating up to 1 inch at the top of the Cajon Pass. Accumulating snow was also reported near Devore during this time. Accumulating snow continued over into March 1st and 2nd, the totals and reports of which are reflected in a separate episode and event.

Additional rounds of light to moderate snow occurred in the Riverside County Mountains on February 27th, with more moderate to heavy snow occurring on February 28th. Numerous locations at elevations above 4000 feet received an additional 1 to 2 feet of snow during this time. A trained spotter in Idyllwild reported total snowfall of 17 inches on February 28th. Snow carried over into March 1st as well, with storm total reports reflected in a separate episode.

Additional rounds of light to moderate snow occurred in the San Diego County Mountains on February 27th, with more moderate to heavy snow occurring on February 28th. A COOP observer on Palomar Mountain observed upwards of 20 inches of snow falling on the 28th. A COOP observer near Mount Laguna reported upwards of 10 inches of snow falling on the 28th. Snow carried over into March 1st, with storm totals reflected in a different event/episode.

Very heavy rainfall occurred across the Inland Empire from the evening on March 14 through the morning on March 15. Rainfall of 2.00-3.50 fell, with local amounts up to 4 inches closer to the San Bernardino County Mountains. Flash flooding was reported early on the morning of March 15; firefighters responded to a vehicle in swift moving water, and the rescue was successful. Also, Grove Ave between Merrill Ave, Chino and Riverside Ave in Ontario saw 2 to 4 inches of running water covering the entire roadway. Kimball Ave in Chino between Quality Way and Euclid Ave were flooded with 2 to 4 inches of standing water.

Heavy rainfall fell across eastern portions of the Inland Empire the evening of March 14 through the afternoon on March 15. Rainfall of 1.00-2.25 was reported, and multiple reports of flooding were received via the Department of Highways: Cherry Valley Blvd at Roberts Road was flooded, as well as three lanes of Highway 60.

Very heavy rainfall occurred across inland Orange County from the evening on March 14 through the morning on March 15. Rainfall of 1.50-2.50 fell. An MPing report of street and road flooding resulting in road closures and stranded vehicles was reported near Santa Ana early in the morning on March 15.
The Department of Highways reported at leas three big boulders blocking SR-74.
Swiftwater rescue conducted by firefighters at Matthews Rd and Palomar Rd, with a vehicle submerged in one foot of water, with four occupants rescued.

A significant landslide occurred following heavy rain in San Clemente on the 1500 block of Buena Vista the morning of March 15. All buildings were immediately evacuated, with no injuries reported. At least four apartment buildings had been red-tagged by the afternoon (deemed too dangerous to enter).

Flooding occurred early in the morning on March 15 following very heavy rainfall over the previous 24 hours, with precipitation amounts of 2.5-3.5 inches. Huffstalter St between 5th and 2nd St was closed due to flooding, as well as Pala Temecula Road.
The Department of Highways reported a rockslide on the southbound lanes of SR-76 early in the morning on March 15. Rainfall of 2.50-3.50 inches occurred with the event.
The Department of Highways reported a large boulder blocking the southbound lanes of Highway 78.

Significant flooding was reported early in the morning on March 15 by the Department of Highways.||SR-78 near Carlsbad initially saw flooding around 3 AM on March 15, with flooding starting on the on-ramp, eventually expanding onto the eastbound lanes of SR-78, and into the westbound lanes nearly two hours later. A hard closure was announced around 5:30 AM for the eastbound lanes, with the westbound lanes closing around 7 AM.||Flooding was reported on Discovery St near San Pablo Ct, with a closure reported on Discovery St around 8 AM.||La Costa Ave was flooded at El Camino Real.||Widespread rainfall of 2.00-3.00 was reported in the 24 hours surrounding the flooding in coastal north county.

Mudslides, rockslides and debris flows were reported across western portions of the San Bernardino County Mountains on March 15 as widespread heavy rainfall of 1.00-3.50+ inches occurred. Rockslides occurred along the upper passing lanes on SR-330 near Running Springs; mud and rocks blocked the upbound lanes of Highway 18 at Old Waterman Canyon Road near Crestline; rocks were reported across the road on SR-18 near Crestline, and a vehicle reportedly hit the rocks.
The Department of Highways reported a rock slide on both the upbound and downbound lanes on SR-38.

An historic winter storm continued to produce very heavy snowfall in the San Bernardino County Mountains on March 1st. The final round of snow with this storm resulted in additional snowfall totals of anywhere from a few inches at some mountain communities between 5000-6000 feet in elevation, to upwards of 2-3 feet at many ski resorts. This resulted in storm total snowfall amounts ranging from 9-12 feet in many ski resorts, 5-9 feet of snow in many mountain communities at or above 6000 feet in elevation, 2-5 feet of snow at elevations between 5000-6000 feet, 1-3 feet of snow at elevations between 3000-5000 feet, and some reports of accumulating snow at elevations as low as 1000 feet. Some notable reports from February 22 to March 1 include 150 at Snow Valley, 134 at Snow Summit on Bear Mountain, 115 at Mountain High near Mount Baldy, 108 near Lake Arrowhead (32 inches in 24 hours), End of Baldy Road at 6400 feet with 103 inches (40 inches in 24 hours February 25-26), 100 in Crestline (35 inches in 24 hours February 25-26), 95 in Arrowbear, 82 in Big Bear Lake yard, 76 in Forest Falls, 64 at Top of the Tram Mt San Jacinto 8400 feet, 63 Angelus Oaks, 56-62 in Wrightwood 5800 to 6200 feet, and 58 inches at Baldwin Lake (east Big Bear city) and Palomar Mountain at 5700 feet.  Multiple reports of roofs collapsing due to snow load were received from the Lake Arrowhead and Crestline areas, resulting in several rescues. The Goodwin Grocery Store in Crestline had its entire roof collapse. Recovery efforts from this winter storm spanned several weeks after the storm itself. State highway closures lasted up to 3 weeks including Highways 18 and 330. Several hundred rescues occurred, some by snowcat, of residence from February 28 to March 10. Gas service was interrupted to thousands with up to 700 service calls. There were 12 homes burned by fires related to gas pressure damage from the heavy snowfall. Only emergency personnel (up to 1000 at peak) for rescue and snow removal were allowed into the mountains on state highways through mid March. Initially helicopters from CalDART and California National Guard delivered food and supplies. Later meals were provided at selected locations for the entire month of March for those displaced or not able to drive. Ski areas were closed from a few days (Mt Baldy) to 2 1/2 weeks (Snow Valley).

Flooding occurred near Big Bear City on March 15 following heavy rainfall of 0.50-1.50, with reports of 2.00-3.00+ inches nearby. Heavy rain combined with snow melt to lead to flooding in the San Bernardino County Mountains. The Department of Highways reported the closure of Gildart Drive and Division Drive; Irvine Way and Barrett Way were flooded; the riverbed broke through and resulted in flooding at SR-38, with 3 inches of standing water reported between Baldwin and State Lane.
Firefighters responded to a vehicle submerged in 1 foot of water at Matthews Road and Palomar Road. Four occupants were rescued from the vehicle.
The Department of Highways announced the closure of Highway 78 between Wynola Road and the Banner Store due to a mudslide in the eastbound lanes.
Flooding reported at Amarillo and Buckwheat Road, with rain of 0.50 inch reported.
Broadcast media reports Gene Autry Trail, North Indian Canyon Drive and Araby Drive in the Coachella Valley closed due to flooding.

An historic winter storm continued to produce heavy snowfall across the Riverside County Mountains on March 1st. Additional snowfall of 1-2 feet occurred across many mountain communities above 5,000 feet in elevation. Notable 7 day storm total snowfall amounts include 64 at the top of the Palm Springs tram on Mount San Jacinto, and 34 near Idyllwild.

An historic winter storm continued to impact the San Diego County Mountains on March 1st, producing heavy snowfall across the region. Additional snowfall of 1-2 feet occurred mainly near Palomar Mountain and Mount Laguna during this time. Storm total snowfall of around 58 was observed on Palomar Mountain.
Report from CalTrans: #3 and #5 lanes on I-10 East at Cherry Ave Exit were flooded due to heavy rainfall.
Flooded low lying areas at SR 55 and I-5. About 0.8 inch of rain fell in the area at the time.
Report from CalTrans: SR-74 at Blackburn Road was closed due to the road being completely covered with mud about 1 foot deep.
The intersection of I-210 and 5th street was flooded after 1.10 inches of rain had fallen in the area, over the course of 8 hours.
Gusty winds occurred early in the morning on March 15, and numerous large trees were reported downed, including one near Mt Soledad and one along Highway 163.
Report from CalTrans: Rocks fell into the road on the northbound lanes of Wildcat Canyon Road at Muth Valley Road.
Report from CalTrans: Mudslide blocking the entire #1 lane.
Report from CalTrans: Mud, small boulders, and rocks coming off the side of the hill and into the road.
Photo of a large tree landing on Descanso Elementary School Building shared by San Diego Office of Education. West winds gusted to 44 mph on a nearby RAWS site at 5 AM and 11 AM.
Public report of 1-inch tree limbs broken and roof shingles blown off.
A large mature pine tree was knocked down near the intersection of MacArthur and Main Street. Tree diameter was estimated to be around 3 feet, with lots of debris and branches also down.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: An historic winter storm brought snowfall down to lower elevations in the Inland Empire on March 1st. Areas near Riverside, Chino, Moreno Valley, Corona, and Perris observed rain changing to snow, though much of the snow in these areas melted on impact with the ground. Areas near Yucaipa, Banning, and Beaumont reported accumulations of up to 1 inch occur.

An historic winter storm brought snowfall down to inland portions of Orange County March 1st. Areas Yorba Linda reported accumulating snowfall of up to 0.5 inch occur. A mix of snow and snow pellets was also observed near Orange, Brea, and Los Alamitos, most of which melted upon reaching the ground.
A mix of snow and snow pellets was observed in San Juan Capistra on March 1st.
A trained spotter near Temesecal Valley reported storm total rainfall of 1.37 inches.
A trained spotter near Yucaipa reported storm total rainfall of 1.65 inches as of midday on March 1st.
A trained spotter near San Marcos reported 24hr rainfall totals of 0.95 inch.
A trained spotter near El Cajon reported storm total rainfall of 0.75 inch.
De Luz Road was closed due to flooding. About 0.50-0.70 inch of rain fell in this area in the 12hrs prior.
In the Rainbow area, Huffstatler St was closed from 5th St to 2nd St due to flooding. About 0.50-0.70 inch of rain fell in the 12 hours prior.
In Escondido, Country Club Drive was closed south of Harmony Grove Road due to flooding.
Flooding was reported in Lane 2 at the intersection of SR75 and Attu Avenue. Rainfall of 0.60 inch fell in the previous 6 hours.
The I-8 East on ramp at Texas Street was flooded, with water up to vehicle tires. Rainfall of 0.70 to 0.80 inches fell in the previous 6 hours.
Flooding on Vesper Road lead to multiple vehicle spinouts. About 0.90 to 1.10 inches of rain fell in this area in the previous 12 hours.
The off-ramp on I-5 North at La Jolla Village Drive was flooded. About 0.65 inch of rain fell in the previous 6 hours.
In Murrieta, the parking lot in front of the local Sam's Club was flooded with water about 1 foot deep.

A swiftwater rescue was needed near Cajon Boulevard and Swarthout Canyon Road after a vehicle tried to cross high water and got swept away in the current. The vehicle was swept approximately 100 yards down the river and was not recoverable.

Roads near the intersection of Anza Road and De Portola Road were shut down due to flowing water and a mud slide. A jeep vehicle required a rescue after it was stuck in 2 feet of flowing water and mud. About 1.4 inches of rain fell in this area in the previous 12 hours, with 1 inch falling in 6 hours.
The eastbound right-hand lane of Murrieta Hot Springs Road was flooded by a 3-foot waterfall from Warm Springs Creek. About 1.4 inches of rain fell in this area in the previous 12 hours.
Low-lying portions of Barona Road and Wildcat Canyon Road were flooded. Total rainfall of 1.6 inches occurred.
About 2 inches of rain fell at Palomar Mountain nearby, leading to the San Luis Rey River flowing over Cole Grade Road with water 1 to 2 feet deep.
A trained spotter reported fast-moving water over Via Montezuma at Murrieta Creek, prompting a road closure.
About 0.43 inch of rain fell in one hour between 7 and 8 PM, leading to flooding on Ocean View Blvd.
SR94 near College Grove Drive had all lanes flooded with standing water. About 0.35 inch of rain fell in 90 minutes prior to this report, with 1.27 inches falling in the previous 30 hours.
A large tree was downed near Weidners Garden.
A large tree was downed, resulting in a power outage.

Two rounds of precipitation impacted the San Bernardino County Mountains on March 29-30. The first round occurred during the day on March 29 had snow levels near 6000-7000 feet, before falling to 3500-4000 feet Wednesday night and Thursday with the second round of precipitation. The heaviest snow accumulations generally occurred above 6000 feet, where accumulations of 6-12 inches were observed. Lower elevations down to 4000 feet saw accumulations of 2-6 inches.

Snow developed across the San Diego County Mountains late in the evening on March 29, persisting through the afternoon on March 30. The heaviest snow accumulations generally occurred above 5500 feet, where accumulations of 8-12 inches were observed. Lower elevations down to 4000 feet saw accumulations of 1-7 inches.

Snow fell across the Riverside County Mountains in two rounds: the first occurring through the day on Wednesday with snow levels near 6500 feet, and the second late Wednesday night through Thursday afternoon, when snow levels fell to 3500-4500 feet. Snow accumulations of 1 to 4 inches were reported in the mountains.
Broadcast media reports potential wind damage near three homes, with downed powerlines and a damaged, though non-secure, tent. A small shower with weak rotation moved over the area.
The Department of Highways reported roadway flooding at SR-74W and College Grove Avenue, with 0.45-0.55 inch of rain reported in the previous 24 hours.
A wind gust of 66 mph was measured by the Burns Canyon RAWS.
A 59 mph wind gust was measured in Thousand Palms.
A 64 mph wind gust was measured at the Borrego Springs mesonet. Sustained winds of 49 mph were also measured.
A trained spotter in Temecula shared a photo of a flooded road crossing near Murrieta Creek.

A unseasonably cold, late-season storm dropped one to three inches of snow above 5,000 ft, and up to five inches of snow above 7,500 ft. Slick and icy conditions led to several accidents on mountain highways and roads, especially at resort level. Heavier snow may have occurred at the highest elevations in the San Gorgonio Wilderness, but no reports were received.

events.event_narrative: Caltrans reported 2 feet of water (photos included) on fast lane of state highway 60 at Jack Rabbit Trail, causing lane closures.  Between 400 and 418 pm local.

An avalanche occurred on Mount Baldy at approximately 5:30 AM PST. According to reports from local media, about 15 feet of snow came down off the mountain and blocked portions of Mount Baldy Road as well as the ski resort's parking lot. This caused closures of not just the road, but also at Mount Baldy Ski Resort which trapped residents above the avalanche area.

Mt Baldy ski resort was closed due to avalanche in Bowl Alley near the entrance to the ski area or the end of Mt Baldy road. The area received 110 inches of snow in the prior 7 days at 6500 feet and close to 150 inches at 8000 feet.
Report from CalTrans of Sig Alert, Closure due to flooding at transition of I-5 and Highway 55. About 0.8 inch of rain fell in the area at the time.

High wind impacted the San Gorgonio Pass near Banning on April 3rd. Wind gusts of 55 to 65 mph were common, with localized higher gusts. The Whitewater RAWS site recorded a peak wind gust of 73 mph, while the Desert Hot Springs SoCal-Edison mesonet site recorded a gust to 66 mph.

High wind impacted the San Diego County Mountains on April 3rd. Wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph were common, with localized higher gusts. The Volcan Mountain SDG&E site recorded a peak wind gust to 65 mph, while the Boulevard West SDG&E site recorded a gust to 64 mph.

High wind impacted the San Bernardino County Mountains on April 3rd. Wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph were common, with localized higher gusts. The Burns Canyon mesonet site recorded a peak wind gust to 67 mph.
High wind impacted the Coachella Valley on April 3rd. Wind gusts of 40 to 50 mph were common, with localized higher gusts. The ASOS at Palm Springs Airport recorded a peak wind gust of 61 mph.
Strong winds broke tree limbs about 1 inch in diameter as well as blew some roof shingles off of a house in Laguna Beach.
The Nob Fire ignited on April 26 and lasted through the end of the month. It burned roughly 227 acres, per the last update on Inciweb. The cause is currently unknown at this time.

Heavy rain from an early morning thunderstorm over the mountain slopes above Cathedral City caused a damaging flash flood that raced down Eagle Canyon, past Gilda���s Club, and onto East Palm Canyon Drive (Highway 111). At least 15-20 businesses were damaged as well as several homes at the Tramview Mobile Home Park. One home was lifted off its foundation and declared unsafe to live in. Debris consisting of rocks, a fence, mud, and tree limbs caused the closure of East Palm Canyon from Cathedral Canyon to Golf Club Drive. Several other intersection along and near East Palm Canyon were also closed. A trained weather spotter measured 1.25 inches of rain in 30 minutes with this storm.

events.event_narrative: High temperatures reached 108 at March Field, 109 at Chino, 110 at Elsinore, and 111 at Hemet. The relatively short duration of the heat in combination with the lack of humidity prevented temperatures from meeting excessive heat criteria.

High temperatures reached 104 at Rancho Bernardo, 105 at El Cajon, and 106 at Ramona. The relatively short duration of the heat in combination with the lack of humidity prevented temperatures from meeting excessive heat criteria.

High temperatures reached 115 at Indio, 117 at Palm Springs, and 118 at Thermal. The relatively short duration of the heat in combination with the lack of humidity prevented temperatures from meeting excessive heat criteria.

The high temperature reached 116 at the Anza Borrego Park Headquarters. The relatively short duration of the heat in combination with the lack of humidity prevented temperatures from meeting excessive heat criteria.

Snow fell at several communities in the San Bernardino County Mountains from the evening on May 3rd through the afternoon on the 4th. Communities at higher elevations near Mount Baldy and Running Springs received total snowfall of 7-8 inches. Numerous other communities including Big Bear Lake, Lake Arrowhead, and Forest Falls received anywhere from 1-5 inches of snow.
Snow fell at some communities in the Riverside County Mountains from the evening on May 3rd through the afternoon on the 4th. A trained spotter near Idyllwild measured storm total snowfall of 1 inch.

Local broadcast media observed and reported coastal flooding near Seal Beach Pier up to 18 inches deep from high tide and high surf. At least one car was swamped. No confirmed damage to homes or businesses.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: The Juniper Fire started near Perris, CA on June 27th and burned 68 acres. Four structures were destroyed as a result of the fire, including two homes. Evacuation orders were in place for about 6 hours due to the fire.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: A 350 acre vegetation fire burned in the San Jacinto Valley in Riverside County from the afternoon on May 22 through the evening on May 25. The ignition occurred in the Ramona Expressway and North Warren Road area. The fire approached residential area as well as dairy farms, prompting evacuation orders and warnings through the late evening on May 22 before being lifted. The fire was 100% contained by 8:00 PM on May 25.
The Wildcat Fire ignited around 3:45 PM PDT on June 20th and burned roughly 171 acres. Evacuation warnings were issued at San Diego Country Estates as a result.
Public report of traffic driving through several inches of moving water along Highway 395 at Desert Flower Road.
Public report (via Waze) of flooding along Highway 18 near Palmdale Road in Phelan. El Mirage Raws (9 miles north) received 1.23 inches of rain between 4:26-5:26 PM.

NWS storm survey conducted by WFO San Diego. Several sections of Mountain View Road were covered in mud as much as two feet deep with damage on the side pavement. El Mirage Raws recorded 1.23 inches of rain during the afternoon on May 21. Radar total estimates of 2-4 inches occurred in surrounding areas. Standing water along El Mirage Road with one home surrounded by water. A nearby dry lake bed was partially water logged.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: The Gavilan Fire started at 3:28 PM on July 15, and burned for six days before containment occurred by the evening of July 21. The fire burned 338 acres northwest of Perris, CA. Evacuation orders were issued during the height of the spread.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: The Reche Fire started at 12:58 AM on July 14, and burned for seven days before containment occurred by early morning on July 21. The fire burned 437 acres east of Riverside, CA. A hard road closure at Perris Blvd N and Heacock Ave at Reche Vista was issued, with communities east of Perris Blvd to Moreno Beach Drive were placed under evacuation warnings.

A heat wave impacted the Coachella Valley starting on July 1st and lasted through the 3rd. Highs each afternoon at Palm Springs International Airport topped out at 117 degrees each afternoon on the 1st through the 3rd, while Jacqueline Cochran Regional Airport (KTRM) reported highs of 115, 111, and 115 on the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd respectively. Excessive Heat Warnings were in effect during this time.

A heat wave impacted the San Diego County Deserts starting on July 1st and lasted through the 3rd. Highs each afternoon at Borrego Valley Airport topped out at 113 degrees on the 1st and 2nd, and hit 115 degrees on the 3rd. Excessive Heat Warnings were in effect during this time.

events.event_narrative: The Rabbit Fire started at 3:30 PM on July 14, and burned for eight days before containment occurred by the evening of July 22. The fire burned 8,283 acres northwest of San Jacinto, CA. Evacuation orders and warnings were issued.

A heat wave impacted the Apple and Lucerne Valleys starting on July 1st and lasting through the 3rd. Highs each afternoon at Southern California Logistics Airport (KVCV) topped out at 102, 106, and 102 degrees on the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd of July, respectively. Excessive Heat Warnings were in effect during this time.

events.event_narrative: The Highland Fire started the afternoon on July 14, and burned for three days before containment occurred by the evening of July 17. The fire burned 105 acres near Beaumont, California.

The pilot issued multiple IFR landings and were granted after the first effort resulted in a missed approach. The French Valley airport reported a 300 foot ceiling and visibility less than 3/4 mile visibility.
