Monsoonal thunderstorms produced heavy rainfall across the Riverside County Mountains on July 25. Mountain Center CWOP reported 0.51 inch of rain in 30 minutes, and the Anza SE gauge reported 0.62 inch in one hour.
Small fire detected on camera from an apparent lightning strike near 5364 feet, around 9 miles west-southwest of Borrego Springs.

Gusty outflow winds from a decaying thunderstorm produced strong winds and greatly reduced visibility across the San Diego County deserts early in the morning on July 31. AWOS station KL08 Borrego Valley Airport reported a wind gust of 40 mph, and the Borrego Springs AWOS reported 1/2 mile visibility in blowing dust for about 20 minutes.

Gusty outflow winds from a decaying thunderstorm produced strong winds and greatly reduced visibility across the Coachella Valley early in the morning on July 31. ASOS station KTRM Thermal Airport reported a peak wind gust of 51 mph, with gusts over 40 mph reported from 2:40 AM - 3:40 AM, and 1/2 mile visibility in blowing dust for 10 minutes; reduced visibility of 1 mile was reported for an hour at KTRM. Palm Springs ASOS reported 1.5 mi visibility in blowing dust from thunderstorm outflow between 330 and 415 am. Visibility briefly dropped to 1.25 mi at 405 am. Widespread wind gusts in excess of 45 mph were reported across the Coachella Valley. 1-inch tree limbs were broken and shingles were blown off near Anza.

events.event_narrative: The Sunset Fire ignited near the intersection of Mesa Street and Gilman Street in Banning just before 7 PM. An evacuation warning was issued that evening for a small portion of Banning. The fire burned 103 acres.

The Bonny Fire was reported the afternoon of July 27 near the 44000 block of Bonny Lane in Aguanga. The fire exhibited a critical rate of spread, reaching 225 across several hours after ignition, and up to 2,206 acres by the following evening. By the evening of July 31, the Bonny Fire was mapped at 2,305 acres and 30% containment. The fire burned until August 9, when 100% containment was achieved.
A roughly 30-mile stretch of I-10 between Bob Hope Drive and Indian Canyon Drive was closed due to inundation by mud, debris, and flooding. Flooding covered Gene Autry Road in Palm Springs.
The Mias Canyon Bridge near the Apple Burn Scar was washed out due to heavy rain and flowing debris.

Union Pacific rail tracks were undercut and washed out when the Whitewater River broke a division bern at the California and Colorado River Aqueduct. At least one train was confirmed to have derailed, with two other trains either observed off track after being forced off the rails by floodwaters, or buried on track. Water and debris was estimated to be 10-15 feet high, and also buckled/cracked the bridge footing at Whitewater. This also severed fiber cables in the area, leading to outages.
A swift water rescue was conducted on Box Canyon Road in Mecca.
Multiple reports of roadway flooding on I-10 in Cabazon.
Two vehicles were stuck in rushing water on Dillon Road and Landfill Road.
Video received from this area near Sheep Creek showing boulders, rocks, and high water over State Highway 2 after 6.23 inches of rain fell. Time is estimated.

Video received from Potato Canyon in Oak Glen of mud and rocks across the roadway. Mud and rocks surround a residence in Oak Glen following a debris flow. Widespread rocks and mud covers many roadways in the town.
Portions of State Highway 38 near the Heart Bar Campground were washed out.

Thirty residents in Seven Oaks were cut off from rescue after the Santa Ana River overflowed and Glass Road was damaged. One person was missing at the time of report, potentially washed into Barton Creek. Seven Oaks Road was closed for Emergency Crews.
Highway 78 was washed out at Yaqui Pass.

San Diego Swiftwater Rescue Lifeguard and Fire Department reported 14 rescues on Sunday 8/20. The San Diego River reached 9.8 feet with a very rapid rise after the watershed received 1.5 to 3.0 inches of rainfall.
Debris, rocks, and mud reported on In Ko Pah Road.

events.event_narrative: Very hot daytime temperatures occurred across the Inland Empire August 28-30th, when Excessive Heat Warnings were in effect. Highs between 100-107 occurred each afternoon, with the hottest temperatures occurring near Chino, Riverside, and San Bernardino.

Heavy rain associated with Tropical Cyclone Hilary impacted much of San Bernardino County starting late on August 19th. The heaviest rainfall occurred on August 20th which led to numerous reports of flash flooding and debris flows. Light rainfall continued through the 21st as well. The heaviest rainfall occurred in the San Bernardino County Mountains, where anywhere from about 2.00-6.00 of rain fell on average. Heavier amounts include 13.07 at Upper Mission Creek (UMCC1), 10.34 at Crestline (CA-SR-84), 9.71 at the Lytle Creek RAWS site, 8.23 at Running Springs, 6.92 at Wrightwood (CA-SR-69), and 6.44 at Forest Falls (FFPC1). Rainfall totals in the Apple and Lucerne Valleys generally ranged from 1.00-3.00. Notable higher totals in this area include Mojave Forks Dam southeast of Hesperia (MVDC1) receiving 6.43 of rain, and Phelan (CW6479) receiving 3.74. Rainfall totals farther south across the Inland Empire generally ranged from 1.50-3.50. The Devore Fire Station observed a localized higher rainfall total of 4.24.

Heavy rain associated with Tropical Cyclone Hilary impacted much of Riverside County starting late on August 19th. The heaviest rainfall occurred on August 20th which led to numerous reports of flash flooding and debris flows. Light rainfall continued through the 21st as well. The heaviest rainfall occurred in the Riverside County Mountains, where anywhere from about 2.00-6.00 of rain fell on average. Heavier amounts include 11.75 at Mount San Jacinto (MSJC1), 8.24 at Sky Valley (EW3393). ||Rainfall totals in the Coachella Valley generally ranged from 3.00-6.00. Notable rainfall totals where more extreme impacts occurred include 4.32 at Cathedral City (FW8322), 4.02 at Palm Desert (GW2765), and 3.23 at Palm Springs International Airport. ||Rainfall totals farther west across the Inland Empire generally ranged from 1.00-3.00. Notable higher totals in this area include 5.27 at Wildomar (1161D), 4.19 at Murrieta (FW8806), 3.59 at Lake Elsinore (FW0823), and 3.34 at Cabazon (BAZC1).

Heavy rain associated with Tropical Cyclone Hilary impacted much of Orange County starting late on August 19th. The heaviest rainfall occurred on August 20th which led to numerous reports of flash flooding and debris flows. Light rainfall continued through the 21st as well. The heaviest rainfall occurred in the Santa Ana Mountains, where anywhere from about 2.00-4.00 of rain fell on average. Heavier amounts include 4.53 of rain at Upper Harding Canyon (UHCC1), 4.17 at Santiago Peak (SAOC1), and 4.09 at both Horsethief Canyon (HTFC1) and Upper Silverado Canyon (SDOC1). Rainfall totals across inland Orange County as well as along the coast generally ranged from 1.00-3.00. Localized higher totals of 5.14 occurred in Huntington Beach (CW1521) and also north of Mission Viejo (MSTC1) where 3.42 of rain fell.

Heavy rain associated with Tropical Cyclone Hilary impacted much of San Diego County starting late on August 19th. The heaviest rainfall occurred on August 20th which led to numerous reports of flash flooding and debris flows. Light rainfall continued through the 21st as well. The heaviest rainfall occurred in the San Diego County Mountains, where anywhere from about 3.00-6.00 of rain fell on average. Heavier amounts include 6.67 of rain at Palomar Mountain (PRMC1), 6.64 at Mount Laguna Observatory (MLGC1), and 6.08 at Ranchita (RCHC1).||Rainfall totals across the San Diego County Deserts generally ranged from 1.00-2.30. Notable totals include 2.25 of rain at San Felipe (SFVC1), 2.20 of rain at Anza Borrego Desert Park (UCAB), and 1.55 of rain at Ocotillo Wells (OCWC1).||Rainfall totals across the San Diego County Valleys ranged from 1.50-3.60. Notable totals from this region include 3.56 of rain at Valley Center (CW9939), 3.51 at Lake Wohlford (WHLC1), 3.47 of rain in Fallbrook, 3.10 of rain in Escondido (EW6576), 2.42 in Poway (CA-SD-12), and 2.23 in Ramona (CA-SD-186).||Rainfall totals across the San Diego County coastal and beach areas generally ranged from 1.50-3.25. An observation near Carlsbad (CA-SD-86) received total rainfall of 3.16, Encinitas (3962D) received 3.12, San Marcos (AS654) recorded a rainfall total of 2.88, and San Diego International Airport received 1.84 of rain.

Local law enforcement reported debris flows in the Forest Falls and Angelus Oaks areas with rock debris in all lanes. The largest debris flow was estimated to be around 100 yards wide and 6 feet deep.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: The Highland Fire started at 12:37 PM on October 30 and burned for eight days before full containment. The fire started under very windy and dry conditions near Aguanga. The fire burned 2487 acres, destroyed 13 structures, damaged 7 further structures and injured two people. Evacuation orders and warnings were issued for surrounding areas. The fire was 100% contained by 1:18 PM on November 7.

The Escala Fire started in the mid-afternoon hours on October 30 at Battle Mountain Open Space east of I-15 near Rancho Bernardo. Evacuation warnings and orders were issued for nearby areas. The fire burned 5 acres and achieved 90% containment several hours after ignition. Two lanes of I-15 were closed due to close proximity of fire.

High temperatures across inland portions of Orange County on October 18th through the 20th were notably hotter than seasonal normal. Highs were routinely in the upper 80s to upper 90s during this time. The hottest day was October 20th when Anaheim hit 97 degrees for a high, Yorba Linda hit 95, while Fullerton hit 92.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE

The hottest day was October 20th when San Pasqual Valley hit 99 degrees for a high, Ramona hit 97 degrees, and Escondido hit 95.

High temperatures across portions of the Santa Ana Mountains on October 18th through the 20th were notably hotter than seasonal normal. Highs were routinely in the upper 80s to upper 90s during this time. El Cariso hit 97 degrees for a high temperature on both the 19th and 20th of October.

High temperatures across portions of the San Diego County Mountains at elevations generally below 5000ft on October 18th through the 20th were notably hotter than seasonal normal. Highs were routinely in the upper 80s to upper 90s during this time.  Campo hit 98 degrees for a high on both the 19th and 20th, while Alpine hit 95 degrees and Julian topped out at 87 degrees on the 19th.

High temperatures across portions of the San Diego County Deserts on October 18th through the 20th were notably hotter than seasonal normal. Highs at Borrego Springs ranged from 99 to 104 degrees during this time.

High temperatures across portions of the Coachella Valley on October 18th through the 20th were notably hotter than seasonal normal. Highs at Palm Springs International Airport ranged from 104 to 108 during this time, while Thermal Airport's highs ranged from 102 to 105.

The Elm Fire started at 9:21 AM on December 9 under gusty Santa Ana wind conditions. By the evening on December 10, the fire grew to 65 acres but was 80% contained. The fire reached full containment by 12:35 PM on December 11.
California Highway Patrol reported flooding at SR-62 and Yucca Park with water flowing down the Morongo Grade.
All lanes of I-10 Eastbound were flooded just west of Pepper Ave.
I-15 offramp to Main Street was closed due to flooding.
One of four crossings in Anza Borrego State Park had fast-flowing water, making it unpassable. Anza Borrego Research shared video of Coyote Creek flooding.
Coyote Creek overflowed a low water crossing along a dirt road in Anza-Borrego State Park. This occurred suddenly after the rain had ended. Time of event is estimated from radar.

Lightning snapped a large tree about two thirds of the way down near the base. Photo             received via Facebook of a tree near intersection of Douglas Dr and River Rd. This occurred during a line of storms moving through Oceanside around 11:30pm.

Thunderstorm microburst southwest (shift from the east) wind gust to 55 mph        recorded via the ASOS at KCRQ (Carlsbad-Palomar Airport) at 11:30 pm on December 21. Survey found a dozen trees downed, including a uprooted 3 foot wide eucalyptus tree, an uprooted 2 foot wide pine, and snapped 18 inch pepper tree. Many large branches and tops of trees were snapped off. Tree damage on both north and south sides of the CRQ airport which is on Palomar road, and most trees laying to the east. Yarrow, Kellogg, El Camino, Faraday, Camino Vida Roble and Corte Del Nogal roads affected. Airport reported a sign damaged near the tower.
Surfline reported 10 to 15 foot surf at Sunset Cliffs.
Surfline reported 10 to 15 foot surf at Imperial Beach Pier. Surf continued to increase through December 30th, when 15-18 foot surf was reported at Imperial Beach Pier.

Maximum surf heights of 15 to 18 feet were reported by Mission Beach Lifeguards. San Diego Fire-Rescue closed the Mission Bay Channel due to the surf conditions, but the Coast Guard Sector San Diego established a temporary safety zone for the navigable waters of Mission Bay Channel. Entry in/out of the bay was prohibited unless authorized by Captain of the Port.
Huntington Beach Lifeguards reported 10 to 12 foot surf with occasional very high sets of 15 to 18 feet.
Surfline reported 10 to 15 foot surf at Blacks Beach.

Social media photos and videos of missing piling on Ocean Beach pier, as well as damaged railings due to high surf on Dec 29. Time damage occurred is unknown, likely on Dec 28 when surf of 10-15 feet was reported.
Low-lying beach parking lots closed in Seal Beach due to coastal flooding.

Number 3 and 4 lanes of I-10W near and east of Date Palm Drive blocked with mud and debris. The nearby Thousand Palms mesonet recorded 0.83 inch of rain since 3 AM that morning, though no rain was occurring when the flooding was reported.

Trained spotter report of 6 inches of water flowing over a roadway 30 feet wide. Water was up to the bumpers of cars.

Rainfall rates in at the time of report were 1.30 inches per hour.||Northbound I-15 at Main Street was fully closed around 1:30 PM due to flooding, and drivers were at a standstill in the flooded roadways.
The off-ramp at SR-163 and Ash Street was closed due to major flooding. Rainfall rates in the area were measured between 0.80 and 1.30 inches in one hour.

CalTrans report of significant flooding near I-805 South and Imperial Avenue and Market Street in Encanto. Large debris and several vehicles were video taped moving downstream on Chollas Creek near Jacob Center and Chollas View, starting at the park. The light rail double train tracks were undercut and severely damaged. Concrete lining in the channel was completely removed and chain link fencing destroyed by debris and flash flooding. Numerous homes in Encanto were flooded out and damaged. FEMA estimated up to 600 homes in this area had major flood damage. This area had rainfall rates of 1 to 2 inches in 1 hour and 3 inches in around 90 minutes. Spring Valley ALERT recorded 1000 year rainfall return interval with 2.45 inches in 60 minutes and 3.15 inches in 2 hours. San Diego Fire and rescue reported just over 200 water rescues. There worse areas and were 1200 households were displaced from floods included Mountain View, Encanto, Valencia Park, Shelltown, Southcrest, and Lincoln Park.
CalTrans report of flooding across the entire freeway at SR-94 West and I-805. Rainfall of 2-3 inches in 60 to 90 minutes between 930 and 1100 am from heavy rainfall and thunderstorms.
All westbound lanes on SR-78 from College Blvd to El Camino Real were closed due to flooding.
All 4 lanes on I-805 North near El Cajon Blvd were flooded.
CalTrans report of flooding at I-5 South and Main Street.
Pictures received via social media of flooding on roads in Ocean Beach, specifically on Spray Street near the dog beach.
Report received via social media showing pictures of flooding from Chollas Creek which flooded downstream to Rigel Street. Cars were submerged up to their door handles in the photos.

San Diego River reached 11.3 feet at USGS Fashion Mall gauge. Flooding in the area was significant including full closure and barricades with flowing water over all crossings, Qualcomm Way, Mission Center road, Fashion Valley road, Camino del Este, Ward road, and Mission road. San Diego fire reported 25 water rescues in the region and tributaries. The Fashion Valley parking garage had 2 to 3 feet of water in the lowest level. The Ward and Fashion Valley trolly centers were surrounded by 1 to 3 feet of water. Water was flowing up to the Riverleaf Inn, mostly blocked by K-rail but was flowing into Hotel circle. Flooded areas were observed as early as 1 pm. Flash flooding along the river including Ward road.
CalTrans reported all lanes of Northbound SR-15 south of Ocean View Blvd were closed due to flooding.
CalTrans reported the Hawthorn Street off-ramp on I-5 was closed due to flooding.

Video received from social media of a flooded parking lot with water flowing along train tracks in Encanto. The fast flowing water in and around Chollas Creek was strong enough to carry vehicles downstream.

Two trees were down on the road at SR-163 South and the Washington Street offramp.
Lightning struck a palm tree and started a small fire in Banning.

Closure at El Camino Ave ramps on SR78. Rainfall of 1.2 to 1.4 inches fell in this region.

A rock slide led to rocks blocking traffic lanes of N Lake Wohlford Rd at Valley Center Rd.

Back-to-back atmospheric river events impacted Orange County starting early on February 4th, with weather impacts occurring through much of the week, and finally ending on February 9th. Much of Orange County received anywhere from 2-9 inches of rainfall. Some localized higher totals include 11.81 at Santiago Peak, numerous other locations in the Santa Ana Mountains including Holy Jim Canyon which received 8-10 inches of rain, and 8.94 of rain at the Coto De Caza (CTDC1) observation site. Coastal areas generally received 2-5 inches of rain, while inland areas generally received rainfall totals in the 5-8 range.

Back-to-back atmospheric river events impacted Riverside County starting early on February 4th, with weather impacts occurring through much of the week, and finally ending on February 9th. Much of Riverside County received anywhere from 2-5 inches of rainfall. Some localized higher totals include 5.55 at the North Elsinore (NELC1) observation site, 5.37 at Prado Dam (PDMC1), and 5.04 of rain at the Perris CDF (PRVC1) observation site. Areas in the Coachella Valley received notably less, generally on the order of 0.75 or less, with the exceptions of the San Gorgonio Pass, Whitewater, and Desert Hot Springs areas which received 1-4 of rain.

Back-to-back atmospheric river events impacted San Bernardino County starting early on February 4th, with weather impacts occurring through much of the week, and finally ending on February 9th. Some notable localized higher totals include 15.48 of rain at the Lytle Creek (MFLC1) observation site, 12.40 at the Deer Creek Dam (DECC1) site, 11.42 at the Glen Helen Reg Park (GLHC1) site, and 10.13 at the Devore Fire Station (DVEC1) site. Less rain fell in the Apple and Lucerne Valley regions, generally on the order of 1.50-4.00 inches. Localized higher totals of 5.44 occurred near Pioneertown (PWNC1).

He was swept away, and his body was later found near the Ramona Expressway by Cal Fire/Riverside County's Swift Water Rescue Team shortly before midnight, according to officials.

A hiker likely passed away from heat stroke off Nighthawk Trail on Black Mountain. Medical examiner is determining exact cause. At 700 am the temperature was 76F with a dewpoint 64F, wind southeast below 5 mph and relative humidity 67 percent at the base of Black Mountain and 93F at the summit of 1558 feet MSL. At 915 am the summit was 98F (SDHGPA site) and then the wind shifted to the west and gusted to 16 mph with a sea breeze lowering the temperature to 86F at the summit by 1100 am. At 1100 am, the base temperature was 84F and humidity at 58 percent. The highest temperature measured at the base was 86F at 1010 am per SDGE Rancho Penasquitos. Media reported a distress call to her family at 1008 am by the hiker saying she was very hot and she needed water. The hiker was separated from a large group of persons. The last contact to her sister was a photo from the top of Black Mountain summit. The hike is listed as moderate difficulty with 5.6 miles loop and roughly 3 hours to complete with a 850 feet elevation gain. Search and rescue consisted of 3 helicopters including infrared and drones as well as about 50 persons on foot. The search was called off at 1 am. Cell phone pings were not able to get an exact location. The search resumed at 730 am Monday. The 50 year old female was found at 915 am Monday just off the main trail and 1/4 mile from a population center. A heat advisory was in effect.

A strong thunderstorm developed over Baja during the early afternoon and then produced a damaging microburst as it drifted north into Campo. KNKX radar indicated a 50k ft echo top and reflectivity values greater than 70 dBZ with this storm. The Campo COOP observers reported tree damage on their property and the CHP log mentioned downed trees along Forest Gate Access Road. Although the Campo ASOS reported a wind gust of 52 mph, it is likely that local wind gusts met or exceeded 58 mph in that area.

Temperatures were extreme the first 10 days of July. On July 5, 2024, Palm Spring (PSP) recorded a high of 124F which is an all-time high temperature. From July 1 to July 12, the Palm Springs airport had high temperatures of 114 to to 124 including a high of 122F on July 8th.

Anza Borrego State Park recorded high temperatures of 110 to 121F between July 1 to 13, 2024. On July 8th, 2024, a high temperature of 121F was recorded. This severe heat is anomalous even for a desert region.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Excessive heat occurred in the Inland Empire July 1 to 11, 2024. On July 5, 2024, San Bernardino airport reached 117F. Other locations in the Inland Empire ranged from 103 to 118F, hottest on the east and south side. Other days during the heat wave recorded upper 90s to 105. The high temperatures again peaked on July 10 and 11 when highest temperatures in the Inland Empire reached 110F.
High temperatures in the High Desert reached 105 to 112F for several days including July 5 to 11 extended period of heat.

High temperatures in the mountains were in the 90s to around 100F between July 1 and July 12, 2024.  Highs reached as hot as 103 to 109F up to elevation 4000 feet, especially on July 5, 10 and 11, 2024. Big Bear Lake at 7000 feet had high temperatures in the lower 90s.
Very hot temperature in the mountains. Idyllwild recorded 104F on July 5 and 6. The all-time high at this location is 104F.

An extended period of excessive heat. On July 5, 2024, it was recorded as high as 106 to 108F at 3500 feet in the San Diego mountains including Descanso. Other days during the heat wave reached the mid 90s to 102F in the Cuyamaca, Laguna and Palomar mountains.
The inland San Diego county valleys had an extended period of high temperatures in the 90s with hottest days reached 99 to 102F. This included RNM airport in Ramona.

events.event_narrative: Hawarden wildfire started 130 pm on July 21, 2024. It burned and damaged up to 18 homes in City of Riverside. Fireworks were suspected to start the fire. Estimated 10 million in damages.

The Nixon wildfire started around 4 pm PDT on July 29. The fire burned up to 4000 acres and was just south of State Route 379 and east of Aguanga.  At the onset the humidity was 14 percent with gusts to 22 mph.

events.event_narrative: Brush fire called Beach in Santa Ana watershed burned very close to homes in Jurupa Valley. Limonite and Beach street affected. About 35 acres burned before containment.

Nixon fire that started at 130 pm local on July 29 burned 5,200 acres through August 7th, 2024. This was just south if SR 371. The wildfire was reported as human caused at Tule Valley Road and Richard Nixon Boulevard, Aguanga California.
Measured 1.06 inches of rain in 1 hour at Big Bear Lake. FW0665 weather station south of the lake near the mountains.

Thunderstorms over the Laguna mountains of  San Diego county near Pine Valley on August 1, 2024. 0.44 reported at Cameron Fire station and 0.48 at Japatul fire station. This is along and south of I-8.

High temperature reached a record 112 in Anaheim on September 6, 2024.  The heat wave lasted through September 9th with high temperatures of 104 to 113F across inland Orange County. A woman and a child were found in a locked vehicle on September 6th. The child died at the hospital. Authorities reported the air temperature at 104 when they arrived at 420 pm. Authorities reported that alcohol was involved and the mother of the child was later arrested. 112 exceeds the prior all-time high temperature at Anaheim which was 109 set in September 2020.

The Line fire began at 930 am September 5, 2024 at Baseline and Aplin Streets near Highland California.  High temperatures on September 5 were 107 to 112F where the fire began. The fire burned north into the Santa Ana drainage due to upslope wind flow. The wildfire grew to 36,000 acres over the next 2 weeks and was finally contained at 44,000 acres in early October. The fire was difficult to contain due to the activity in the remote and thick Bear Creek drainage. The wildfire burned a 98 year old Lookout tower on Keller Peak. The wildfire did severe damage to SR 330 including miles of guardrails and signs which was closed for repairs until November 24, 2024. The fire was contained at the ridge line at Snow Valley to Bear Mountain along SR 18.  Arson was determined to be the cause of the fire. The wildfire destroyed 5 structures in Running Springs and injured 4 firefighters. Estimated costs were 14.5 million. The Fire Management Assistance Grant (FMAG) was approved. Air quality index reached 1500 in Big Bear City causing the hospital to close and transport patients. The wildfire experienced a large flare up in Bear Creek on September 29th and burned an additional several thousand acres.

The Airport fire began at 120 pm PDT Monday September 9, 2024 in Trabuco Canyon, at a remote controlled airport facility, following an excessive heat wave where temperatures reached 100 to 112F. The wildfire burned the next 2 weeks across the Santa Ana mountains and SR 74 which was closed. The wildfire reached into western Riverside County, just west of Lake Elsinore. Total acreage was 23,500. Estimated cost of 95 million. There were a total of 160 structures destroyed in Riverside and Orange Counties with 89 of those structures in Orange County. 22 persons, 2 were civilians and the rest firefighters, suffered injuries. A Fire Management Assistance Grant was issued and approved by FEMA through the California.

The Bridge fire began at 215 pm PDT September 8th, 2024, suspected to have started by lightning. Excessive heat occurred leading up to the day of the wildfire.  The wildfire grew to 35,000 acres on Tuesday September 10th, burning along the ridgeline of the San Gabriel mountains up to 8000 feet MSL and destroying 20 homes in Mt Baldy and 3 in Wrightwood during the evening and night of September 9th. The wildfire created wind gusts up to 40 mph allowing it to become out of control in Wrightwood. There was a Red Flag warning in effect for onshore west winds in the San Gabriel mountains of LA County. The wildfire burned up to to 56,000 acres. 81 structures were destroyed. Defensible space was credited for minimizing the damages to homes. Mountain High ski  area recorded the wildfire on September 10th when it burned over the ridge and through the resort. Videos showed the snowmaking (water hydrants) were used to protect structures. 3 resort structures were destroyed along with powerlines but the main lodges were saved.
Caltrans reported flooding on I-10 causing closure of lanes.

California Highway Patrol reported numerous trees downed by wind along and near I-215 in Perris. A Socal Edison weather station recorded a gust to 71 mph on Ellis Avenue. Pea sized hail was also reported.

Heavy rainfall, up to 0.55 inch in 1 hour in Elder Gulch, was observed from thunderstorms across the Line fire. This caused minor debris flows and flooding on Greenspot road.

Several photos and videos of a long lived extended funnel cloud moving north to south along the San Jacinto ridgeline, viewed from La Quinta. Convective showers and thunderstorms occurred over the mountains and a few moved into the valleys. Video showed clear rotation of the funnel.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: The Airport fire began at 120 pm PDT Monday September 9, 2024 in Trabuco Canyon of Orange County (remote control airport facility) and then burned to the Santa Ana mountain crest and Santiago Peak and reached into western Riverside County on September 10th, 2024. The wildfire caused major damage in the small town of El Cariso village and prompted evacuations into Lake Elsinore. Riverside County reported 55 structures destroyed and 7 homes severe damaged. There were about 50 vehicles that were burned and damaged, which many were historical models and featured in movies.  Over 150 structures were destroyed in including 119 homes due to the Airport wildfire between Orange and Riverside counties. Fire Management Assistance Grant (FMAG) was awarded for the Airport wildfire with total damage estimated at 95 million. Reports indicated that up to 400 million in claims were filed.

events.event_narrative: Extreme heat started September 3 and continued through September 10, 2024. The hottest days were September 5 to 8, when high temperatures reached 105 to 114F across the entire Inland Empire. Despite scattered thunderstorms on September 7 and 8th, the high temperatures were still around 110F at many locations in the Inland Empire.
Public cameras showed a transition from hail to graupel (snow pellets) to dry snow over San Gorgonio mountain. This was also observed by dual pol radar algorithms.

High temperatures across inland San Diego county valleys reached 100 to 112F from September 4 to 9, 2024. The hottest days were September 6 and 8, when maximum temperatures reached 103 to 110F along I-15 corridor.

High temperatures were excessive in the Coachella Valley from September 4 to 9, 2024. The hottest day was observed on September 5th, when maximum temperatures were 115F at several locations including climate sites such as Palm Springs and Borrego Springs.
Dense fog was reported by Huntington Beach lifeguards as early as 5 pm October 5. Dense fog occurred through the morning of October 6.
Dense fog, as low as 0.06 visibility occurred at KSAN San Diego International Airport.
Dense fog reported at Oceanside Airport, KOKB. As low as 1/4 mile visibility.
Dense fog moved into Carlsbad McClellan Palomar airport around 6 pm October 7th and continued into the morning of October 8th.
Palm Springs airport reached 117F on October 1st. Hottest day recorded in October. Note that Phoenix also recorded record highs of 117F in late September 28-29, 2024.
The weekend of October 5 and 6th, 2024, Palm Springs airport recorded high temperatures of 115F both days. These are the 3rd and 4th hottest days measured at Palm Springs PSP airport.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: An unusual heat wave occurred October 5-6, 2024. High temperatures in the Inland Empire, in region known as the Lake Elsinore convergence zone (most protected by sea breeze from the south and another from the northwest) reached 104 to 108F each day. This was when air temperature monitoring was occurring at Galway Downs equestrian center and brought high concern about hosting events in Temecula in the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics.
Arrowhead Springs SCE had a gust to 66 mph at 140 pm.
Santiago Peak had wind gust of 65 mph at 11 am October 18th. Pleasants Peak gusted to 60 mph at 8 am.
Lower Lytle Creek ridge SCE mesonet (east of Mt Baldy) had measured gust of 70 pm at noon October 18, 2024.

Brush fire burned 40 acres near San Diego State University at Montezuma Road and Fairmount Avenue. The wildfire changed names so there was some confusion on the name initially, Montezuma or Fairmount. 6 homes reported damaged per media at Lila Drive and Lucille Drive. Evacuation orders (mandatory) were issued. 300 firefighters were involved in the suppression. Relative humidity was only as low as 40 percent and winds were normal daily sea breeze.

Lake Fire started around 4pm on June 28th on the western slopes of Silverwood Lake. As of 8pm on the 28th, fire is near 500 acres and has prompted evacuation warnings and orders in the area. The fire ended on July 6th at 10 PM with a total 489 acres burned according to CalFire website. Silverwood Lake State Recreational Area remains closed to the public.

A severe thunderstorm east of Idyllwild produced flash flooding in a line from Suicide and Tahquitz Rocks to the Fern Valley area. A search and rescue mission involving two injured rock climbers was ongoing prior to the storm. Several people involved in the SAR mission describe significant runoff and flash flooding 3 feet deep carrying rocks and debris down the mountain. Many roads in Fern Valley were littered with large rocks and mud.

A severe thunderstorm developed over the Fern Valley area and significantly interfered with an ongoing search and rescue operation involving two injured climbers at Suicide Rock. Several eyewitness accounts from climbers on Suicide and Tahquitz Rocks, as well as from people involved in the ongoing SAR mission, describe hailstones ranging in size from marbles to walnuts. A rescue helicopter was forced to abort a rescue attempt of the climbers and make an emergency landing after the thunderstorm moved into the area. One of the injured climbers suffered additional contusions from the hail while another person received cuts. Please note that the severe thunderstorm did not move into the area until nearly two hours after the initial (non-weather related) rock climbing accident.

Onshore flow and strong winds across the mountains caused very gusty downslope winds over the deserts. Wind gusts up to 72 MPH were measured by Burns Canyon RAWS. A trained weather spotter also measured a 62 MPH wind gust at Lucerne Valley.
Snow began in Lucerne Valley around 1000 PST. By 1130 PST 4 inches of snow had accumulated. Snowfall ended around 1900 PST, with a total accumulation of 9 inches.
Snow began to fall in Idyllwild around 0600 PST. By 1400 PST a total of 9 inches had accumulated and the snow had turned to rain.
Shortly after 0900 PST, the roof of a classroom partially collapsed due to heavy rain. Fourteen people, ages 17 to 50, were taken to the hospital with minor injuries.

Significant snowfall was observed above 3000 ft in the San Diego Mountains with 18 inches measured at Palomar Mountain and Julian. The heavy snow caused widespread tree damage between 3500-4000 ft. Live Oaks were especially hard hit due to their large growing habit and because they keep their leaves year-round. Some limbs and trees fell onto structures and roadways. A few tool sheds were also damaged by the weight of the snow.

The San Bernardino County Deserts received 6-20 inches of snow from a significant winter storm. The COOP observer in Hesperia measured 18 inches of snow. Elsewhere, trained weather spotters measured 20 inches of snow in Pinon Hills, 18 inches of snow in Lucerne Valley, 14 inches of snow in parts of Victorville, 12 inches of snow in Adelanto, and 7 inches of snow in Apple Valley. Interstate 15 through the Cajon Pass was shutdown for 24 hours due to heavy snow, the longest closure of that stretch of I-15 in more than 15 years.

The Riverside County Mountains received in excess of 16 inches of snow from a significant winter storm. The Idyllwild Fire Department measured 16 inches of new snow from this storm, however higher amounts probably fell in nearby areas where the flow was favorable for heavier snowfall. Tree damage resulted in power outages in Idyllwild and Fern Valley.

The San Bernardino County Mountains received 18-24 inches of new snow from a significant winter storm. The Big Bear Lake Fire Department measured 23 inches of new snow from this storm, bringing their 5 day total accumulation to an impressive 54 inches. Interstate 15 through the Cajon Pass was shutdown for 24 hours due to heavy snow, the longest closure of that stretch of I-15 in more than 15 years.

The first in a series of significant winter storms dumped 2-3 feet of new snow in the San Bernardino Mountains. Total snowfall accumulations measured 31 inches at Big Bear Lake, 30 inches at Running Springs, and 24 inches at Forest Falls. Most mountain highways were closed because of heavy snow and trapped motorists. Approximately 25 vehicles were stranded on Highway 330 near Running Springs and another 9 vehicles were stranded on Highway 38 near Cedar Falls.
Dense fog caused several injury accidents that led to significant traffic delays on Orange County freeways. The fog also caused numerous flight delays at John Wayne Airport.

Significant flooding in the Tijuana River Valley resulted in the deaths of a Tijuana man and numerous ranch and farm animals. At least 21 people had to be rescued, including 6 by helicopter. Three men were taken to a hospital and treated for hypothermia. An estimated 70 horses were also rescued. Three horses drowned before they could be rescued and another horse was later euthanized due to a leg injury. Fifteen goats and an unknown number of dogs also died in the flood. One farmer lost $600,000 dollars worth of his crop while another lost $10,000 dollars worth of watermelons. The one human death occurred outside the forecast area in Tijuana, Mexico. The flash flood occurred when both the Tijuana River and a nearby flood control channel became dammed with with sediment, trash, and other debris.
Onshore flow caused gusty downslope winds in the deserts. A peak wind gust of 59 MPH was measured by the Burns Canyon RAWS.
A peak wind gust of 89 MPH was measured by the Burns Canyon RAWS. Wind gusts greater than 58 MPH lasted for 5 hours, with sustained winds as high as 59 MPH.
A peak wind gust of 58 MPH was measured by the Ranger Peak RAWS.

Strong onshore flow brought gusty Northwest winds to the Coachella Valley. These winds ripped off part of the roof and a balcony at the Cambridge Inn in Palm Springs. Twenty-six out of 66 rooms in the hotel were closed due to damage. Several cars in a nearby parking lot suffered minor damage due to flying debris.

events.event_narrative: Wind gusts in excess of 58 MPH were measured at the Burns Canyon RAWS between 1651 and 1851 PST. A peak gust of 64 MPH was measured at 1651 PST.
At 245 PST, a trained spotter reported wind gusts up to 76 MPH in Lucerne Valley. The high winds caused some damage to a shed and blew down an antenna.

High winds began at the Whitewater RAWS at 550 PST and continued through 2050 PST. At 550 and 650 PST peak wind gusts of 69 MPH were measured. ||There were numerous reports of damage throughout the Coachella Valley. Several power lines and traffic signals were downed in the high winds, causing power outages to approximately 1,900 customers. Many trees suffered broken limbs, and about 40 trees were uprooted. Two tractor-trailers overturned on Interstate 10. Damage to structures included roofs being torn off buildings and damaged bleachers at the Palm Springs Stadium.
High winds occurred at the Burns Canyon Raws between 1751 and 1951 PST. At 1751 and 1951 PST, peak gusts of 64 MPH were measured.
A peak gust of 61 MPH was measured by the Pinyon RAWS at 1936 PST.
A peak wind gust of 58 MPH was measured by a personal weather station in Julian at 1749 PST.

A trained spotter reported sustained winds in excess of 40 MPH with gusts up to 78 MPH around 1700 PST. Two downed power poles, roof damage, window damage, and a shed ripped off its foundation were also reported. ||At 1452 PST, a mesonet station in Apple Valley reported a 59 MPH wind gust.

Wind gusts in excess of 58 MPH were measured by the Whitewater RAWS between 2050 PST and 0250 PST. Peak gusts of 72 MPH were measured at 2350 and 0050 PST. ||Downed power lines and an overturned tractor-trailer were reported in the Coachella Valley during this time.

The fire began in sparse desert brush near a residential neighborhood. Strong, gusty winds spread the fire towards the neighborhood, resulting in the damage of two homes and the evacuation of approximately 50 other homes. No major injuries were reported.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE

events.event_narrative: Winds from a possible microburst or gustnado damaged four horse shelter roofs near the intersection of Cottonwood Avenue and Joshua Street in Hesperia. One 10 foot by 10 foot metal and wood roof was completely removed from the shelter. Thunderstorm winds also knocked over power lines in Hesperia and Victorville earlier in the day.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Two separate vegetation fires were started by an arsonist around 1447 PST on May 27th. The fires spread over the next twenty-four hours, burning a total of 503 acres. The fires caused the evacuation of parts of the Lake Perris State Recreation Area and the closure of several roads. No damage or injuries were reported.

A four acre fire began around 1145 PST in Otay Mesa along Airway Road near Caliente Avenue. The fire spread through light grass and into a pile of tires. A shed and an abandoned house were destroyed by the blaze. The fire was contained by about 1245 PST. No injuries were reported.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE

events.event_narrative: Quarter-sized hail was reported in Del Mar Heights and Carmel Valley by the public in newspapers and on several websites. Exact locations and times were not reported, so storm track was based on radar data.

A was 40 year old female was struck and killed by lightning around 1530 PST while she was standing under a tree along the 8600 block of Bennett Avenue in Fontana. Some concrete nearby may have also been damaged due to the strike.||Six men were leaning against a metal fence near Electric Avenue and 40th Street in San Bernardino when lightning struck nearby. All six appeared to have suffered electrical burns. Four of the six were administered medical treatment by firefighters as a precaution.

A 31 year old male suffered serious injuries while doing landscape work at a home on Camden Place in San Marcos when lightning struck a palm tree nearby.  He was transported to the hospital in critical condition. His 48 year old brother was treated for minor injuries.
An apartment complex on Chicago Ave in Riverside caught fire when it was struck by lightning. The fire damaged four upstairs units.

A wind gust from a thunderstorm snapped a pine tree along the 400 block of Catalina Road near Avalon Drive in Big Bear Lake. The tree fell on a passing vehicle, crushing the car and killing the driver.

A chain reaction car accident occurred around 0630 PST when a tractor-trailer came around a bend along northbound Interstate 15 near Oak Hills Road and swerved to avoid slowed traffic ahead. A second pileup occurred shortly afterward about one-quarter mile south of the first accident as traffic slowed for the first accident. Approximately 30 vehicles were involved in the two pileups, resulting in 15 injuries, two of which were critical. ||A second set of accidents occurred along Highway 18 near mile marker 28. A 60 year old male was entering the highway when he collided with oncoming traffic. Less than 20 minutes later, a school bus was stopped just East of the first accident when it was hit by a truck. Another vehicle then ran into the truck. The 60 year old male suffered cardiac arrest when the accident occurred and died in the hospital two days later. No other injuries were reported.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE

events.event_narrative: Local broadcast media reported surf up to 20 feet at The Wedge in Newport Beach on Friday the 24th. Around 1300 PDT, a body surfer was killed when large waves and strong currents forced him into a nearby rock jetty. The cause of death was reported to be drowning. Further south, a Dana Point sheriff's deputy sustained a back injury when his patrol boat went airborne after it crested an unanticipated wave in the open water. In San Clemente, a portion of the fishing pier was closed after high surf tore off a wooden crossbeam. The pier reopened at 1100 PDT Saturday. Hundreds of rip current rescues were reported at various beaches in Orange County as well.
A trained spotter reported a 61 MPH wind gust around 1650 PST near the southern part of La Quinta Cove. The storm also produced brief heavy rain and frequent lightning.

events.event_narrative: A nearly stationary thunderstorm with heavy rain near the town of Ocotillo Wells caused flash flooding along the Fish Creek Wash and Split Mountain Road. Several power poles were down in the area, but this may have been attributed to high winds as well as the flooding.

Imperial Irrigation District Energy reported 16 broken power poles and associated equipment along Split Mountain Road in San Diego County due to strong winds from the thunderstorm near Ocotillo Wells.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: The fire broke out just after 1200 PDT in the hills between Norco and Riverside just East of the Interstate 15 between Fourth and Fifth streets. The Fire consumed 150 acres and destroyed a storage building.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: A second fire began around 1330 PDT in the Santa Ana River bottom near Norco. The fire burned 85 acres and caused minor damage to one home.

Riverside County Flood Control reported 0.55 inches of rain in 24 minutes near the intersection of Highway 60 and Moreno Beach Drive in Moreno Valley around 1530 PDT. A newspaper also reported flash flooding throughout Moreno Valley. No major damage was reported.

Four inches of mud and water was reported on Highway 78 near Witch Creek after a thunderstorm with heavy rain moved through. This storm produced over an inch of rain in San Diego Country Estates and Ramona.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE

events.event_narrative: A peak wind gust of 60 MPH was measured by the Burns Canyon RAWS between 0851 and 0951 PST.
A spotter measured gusts in excess of 58 MPH between 0100 and 0130 PST along Montezuma Grade Road in Ranchita. At 0109 PST, a peak gust of 60 MPH was measured.
High winds began in Whitewater between 0950 and 1050 PST, during which time a peak gust of 68 MPH was measured by the Whitewater RAWS. High winds ended between 1250 and 1350 PST.

Winds gusting around 30 MPH caused a eucalyptus tree to fall on a car driving along Rancheros Drive in San Marcos. The tree trapped the driver and one passenger in the car. The couple sustained only minor injuries.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE

events.event_narrative: A 25 foot fishing boat capsized around 0800 PST when returning to the San Diego Bay. Six people were on board and became trapped in the cabin. They managed to open the door and escape from the boat and were promptly rescued by the lifeguards. All six were admitted to the hospital, five of which were treated and released. The sixth person was kept and monitored overnight. A lifeguard boat flipped two hours later when trying to upright the overturned fishing boat. The two lifeguards on board were not injured.
High winds began at the Fremont Canyon RAWS around 2130 PST and ended between 0130 PST and 0230 PST on the 24th. A peak wind gust of 74 MPH was measured between 2231 and 2330 PST.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: A peak wind gust of 66.4 MPH was measured by the Palm Avenue Elementary School mesonet at 0123 PST. High winds occurred between approximately 0015 PST and 0200 PST.

events.event_narrative: Encinitas Lifeguards reported a waterspout off the coast of Moonlight Beach around 1642 PST and said that it had formed within the past 5 minutes. No damage or injuries were reported.

A peak wind gust of 59 MPH was measured by the Point Loma mesonet between 1730 and 1745 PST. High winds ended by 1815 PST.||In Encinitas, a eucalyptus tree fell on a condo causing minor damage to the roof.
A peak wind gust of 62 MPH was measured by the Burns Canyon RAWS between 0251 and 0351 PST.
High winds occurred in the Coachella Valley between 2350 and 0750 PST. The Whitewater RAWS measured a peak wind gust of 73 MPH between 0350 and 0450 PST.
High winds were measured by the Pinyon RAWS between 1936 and 0036 PST. Between 2336 and 0036 a peak wind gust of 62 MPH was measured.

High winds were measured by the Julian mesonet between 1507 and 0054 PST. At 2025 PST, a peak wind gust of 71 MPH was measured. A trained spotter also measured a peak gust of 74 MPH at Cuyamaca at 1523 PST.
Snow began in Big Bear around 0330 PST and continued through about 1845 PST. By 1600 PST, 13 inches of snow had accumulated.

Snow began at Pine Cove around 0400 PST and continued through about 1715 PST. A trained spotter reported a storm total of 14 inches. The nearby town of Idyllwild received 10 inches of snow from the storm.

Heavy snow and gusty winds were responsible for knocking down two trees in the San Bernardino County mountains. The first, in Big Bear Lake, fell onto a home on Cherry Lane, causing minor damage. The second incident was in Boulder Bay, where a tree fell and did damage to two homes, knocked down power lines, and destroyed a car and a trailer.
Gusty winds knocked over trees throughout Orange County, damaging buildings and cars. In Tustin, arcing power lines caused a power pole to catch fire. No injures were reported.

Gusty winds caused a large oak tree to fall on a car in Ramona around 1800 PST. In Scripps Ranch, a eucalyptus tree fell on a home, destroying a garage. No injuries were reported with either incident.

Two spotters in Lucerne Valley reported sustained winds near 50 MPH with frequent gusts around 70 MPH between 2215 and 0300 PST. Around 0030 PST a 100 MPH wind gust was measured. An 81 MPH gust was measured at 0142 PST. The winds blew shingles off roofs and damaged a trailer. Power lines were arcing and some were knocked down.
Two 4 foot by 8 foot signs fell over on cars in Wrightwood due to strong winds.

Excessive runoff from the heavy rain in the San Bernardino Mountains produced strong currents in the Whitewater River wash, which caused an earthen berm at a percolation basin in Palm Springs to collapse. The water then continued to flow through the wash and across several streets, bringing large amounts of mud and debris with it. Indian Canyon Road, Gene Autry Road, and Vista Chino road, all of which lie across the wash's natural path, were closed due to flooding. Three cars were swept off the road during the flood - two on Indian Canyon Drive and one on Vista Chino. One of the percolation ponds also sustained damage.
High winds were measured by the Julian CWOP between 0806 and 1107 PST. Between 0835 and 0848 PST multiple gusts of 65 MPH were measured.
Wind gusts in excess of 58 MPH were measured by the Burns Canyon RAWS between 1351 and 1651 PST. Between 1451 and 1551 PST, a peak wind gust of 68 MPH was measured.

Wind gusts in excess of 58 MPH were measured by the Whitewater RAWS between 1250 and 1650 PST. Multiple wind gusts of 66 MPH were measured during this period. At 1801 PST, the Palm Springs Airport ASOS measured a peak wind gust of 63 MPH. Blowing dust and downed palm fronds were also reported during this time.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE

events.event_narrative: Several trees fell on cars in Mission Viejo along Marguerite Parkway and Crown Valley Parkway. In Corona Del Mar, a large tree fell onto a house on Heliotrope Avenue.
Heavy rain and a blocked drains caused a portion of the roof to collapse at Westcliff Medical Laboratories in Santa Ana. The collapse happened around 1500 PST.
Rain-soaked soil combined with gusty winds caused a large Eucalyptus tree to fall down on North Torrey Pines Road, damaging two vehicles. The occupants of the vehicles were not injured.
Between 1251 and 1351 PST a peak wind gust of 65 MPH was measured by the Burns Canyon RAWS. During this event, approximately twenty road signs were blown down along Interstate 15 in the Cajon Pass.
Between 1330 and 1430 PST, a peak wind gust of 63 MPH was measured by the Fremont Canyon RAWS. The end time of the event is estimated due to the fact that the RAWS stopped reporting after 1430 PST.
Between 1216 and 1246 PST, high winds were measured by the Hesperia mesonet. At 1246 PST, a peak wind gust of 62 MPH was measured.

The California Highway Patrol reported flooding and mud across Highway 76 near Rincon Ranch Road in Pauma Valley. The flooding occurred after a narrow band of heavy rain moved over the area, which included the Poomacha Fire burn area. One vehicle became trapped in the mud.

A tornado formed off the coast of Sunset Beach in Orange County and moved Northeast. The tornado crossed Pacific Coast Highway just south of Anderson Street at 1257 PST and continued to move Northeast. A parked Ford Explorer was flipped on its side, and two 35 foot catamarans in the Huntington Harbour were lifted out of the water. One was lifted 50 feet in the air before landing on another vessel and a dock piling. The second was flipped over and landed 30 feet from its original position. There were multiple reports of roof damage, and a window in a residential building was blown in. A wind gust of 92 MPH was measured by a mesonet at the Huntington Beach Pier.

As a line of thunderstorms moved through Orange County, a peak wind gust of 93 MPH was measured by the weather station at the Newport Beach Pier. Several wind gusts in excess of 70 MPH were also reported. Several boats in the Newport Beach Harbor broke free. In Costa Mesa, just inland from Newport Beach, a building in an industrial park on 17th Ave sustained moderate damage. Approximately two-thirds of the top layer of the roof blew off. Pieces of the roof, some as large as 15 feet long, trees, and other debris littered the parking lot. Across the street at a mobile home park, metal awnings were ripped off by the wind and pieces of wood were seen flying through the air. A few blocks away near the intersection of Harbor Blvd and Victoria Street, the strong winds blew open the door to a business and shattered a window.

A narrow band of thunderstorms moved through San Diego county around 1500 PST. In Santee, winds tore off the roofs of three mobile homes, with some parts of the roof flying as much as 75 feet away. In Flinn Springs, a 10 foot diameter tree fell onto a mobile home, killing a woman. The San Miguel RAWS measured a peak wind gust of 59 MPH during this time.
The mesonet at the San Clemente Pier measured a peak wind gust of 60 MPH around 1400 PST.
High winds occurred between 1051 and 1251 PST. Between 1051 and 1151 PST, a peak wind gust of 73 MPH was measured by the Burns Canyon RAWS.

Gusty winds associated with the passage of the cold front combined with rain soaked soils caused a tree to collapse in Scripps Ranch. The tree crashed through a roof and into a bedroom of a house, causing major damage. No one was injured. A large tree branch fell in Ramona, damaging part of a chain link fence.

Heavy rain caused minor flooding in areas with poor drainage in Fontana and Redlands. In Fontana, a home was filled with several inches of water after sandbags surrounding the home failed. In Redlands, a clogged drain caused an apartment parking lot to flood, damaging several cars.
Strong winds associated with the passage of a cold front damaged the awnings of several mobile homes at the Calaveras Mobile Park in Oceanside.
Heavy rain caused a 20 foot by 20 foot section of roof to collapse at an industrial building on Valley View St in La Palma around 1645 PST.

A 40 inch diameter eucalyptus tree fell on the 400 block of Jasmine Street in Laguna Beach. The tree damaged a fence and gate opener between two houses.  At Doheny State Beach, a eucalyptus tree fell on a camper shell. No injuries were reported with either event.

Snow began in the San Bernardino County mountains around 1200 PST. Spotters in Wrightwood, Forest Falls, and Blue Jay reported blizzard conditions throughout the day, with visibility near zero at times. Wind gusts in the area were around 40 MPH. By 1700 PST, Wrightwood had received twelve inches of snow. The snow finally ended around 2130 PST.

Snow began in the Riverside County mountains around 1230 PST. A trained spotter in Pine Cove reported that approximately 8 inches fell by 1700 PST, with an additional 1.5 inches falling through about 2330 PST.
High winds were measured by the Burns Canyon RAWS between 1151 and 1451 PST. Between 1251 and 1351 PST, a peak gust of 85 MPH was measured.

High winds began around 1052 PST and continued through 1254 PST. At 1952 PST, the Victorville ASOS reported a peak wind gust of 62 MPH. A CWOP station in Hesperia reported a peak gust of 61 MPH at 1254 PST.

High winds were measured by the Julian mesonet between 1425 and 1325 PST. Wind gusts to 61 MPH were measured during that time. Patio furniture in Julian was picked up by the wind and ended up in a neighbors tree.

Several areas of the Coachella Valley experienced urban flooding on the 21st as another round of heavy rain moved through the region. A Ross store in Palm Springs sustained large amounts of damage as a 20 by 30 foot section of roof collapsed around 945 PST. The collapse also broke pipes for the fire sprinkler system. One store employee suffered minor injuries.

San Bernardino County Public Works reported debris and mud in several homes in Yucaipa beginning around 1236 PST and continuing through about 1400 PST. The flash flooding may have knocked over power lines along Wildwood Canyon Road near 2nd Street. The flash flood was a result of heavy rain in the region. Large amounts of water and mud flowed out of the hills to the east of Yucaipa and through the Wildwood Canyon Wash. It is likely that the majority of the flooding was due to the wash overflowing.

Snowfall began in the San Bernardino County Mountains around 0230 PST on January 21st and continued through about 2200 PST on the 22nd. Several spotters reported 24 hour snow accumulations of 24 to over 32 inches. Some areas received as much as 3 to 4 feet of snow within 36 hours. By the end of the storm, Snow Valley Ski Resort had a total of 80 to 92 inches of new snow for the week, Bear Mountain Ski Resort had 60 to 66 inches, and a spotter in Big Bear City reported 57 inches. Several mobile homes were damaged due to the heavy snow. A 30 foot tall cedar tree fell under the weight of the snow, damaging a fence and some outdoor tables at Broadway Cafe in Big Bear City.

San Bernardino County Works reported a debris flow on Pendleton Road in Yucaipa. The hills just above the road had been burned in the 2009 Pendleton Fire. The street was closed off due to flooding, but no other damage was reported. Mud was as deep as 4 feet in some locations.

San Diego County Flood Control relayed a report from the public of numerous locations of flooded roadways with mud, rocks, and debris along Highway 76 through the La Jolla Reservation. A newspaper reported two feet of mud in the garage of a home in Rincon. This occurred after heavy rain moved over the 2007 Poomacha Fire burn area.

The San Diego River crested just below the 11.3 foot flood stage on the afternoon of the 21st. There were reports of flooding along Ward Road and in the Qualcomm Stadium parking lot in Mission Valley. No damage was reported.

The Mount Woodson mesonet measured a peak wind gust of 62 MPH at 1230 PST as a line of thunderstorms moved over the area. A weather spotter estimated wind gusts in excess of 60 MPH in San Diego Country Estates around 1230 PST. Two large trees were blown down and blocking the road near San Diego Country Estates.

Snowfall began in the Riverside County mountains shortly after midnight on the 21st. Based on rainfall totals at lower elevations, snowfall in the San Bernardino County mountains, and spotter reports, approximately 12 inches of snow fell by 1530 PST. Snowfall finally ended by about 2000 PST on the 22nd. By the time snowfall ended, the Palm Springs Aerial Tramway reported a weekly total of 5 feet of snow.

Snowfall began in the San Diego County mountains around 1500 PST on the 21st. By a about 1300 PST on the 22nd, approximately 12 inches of snow had fallen at the Mount Laguna Lodge. The snow finally tapered off by the morning of the 23rd. A spotter also reported very icy road conditions and visibility down to 1/8 mile at times due to blowing snow and fog.

High winds were measured by several RAWS in the Riverside County Mountains between 1230 PST and 2330 PST. Strong Southwest winds ahead of a cold front peaked around 1300 PST. At that time, the Angelus Hill RAWS measured a peak gust of 67 MPH, while the Ranger Peak and Vista Grande RAWS both measured peak gusts of 63 MPH.

Heavy rain in the High Desert produced widespread flash flooding in the cities of Adelanto, Victorville, Hesperia, and Apple Valley. This area, on average, receives about 5 to 6 inches of rain per year. Most of these areas saw that amount of rain in just a few days. Runoff from the San Bernardino Mountains and a rapidly rising Mojave River may have contributed to some of the flooding. Numerous homes, schools, parks, and roads sustained minor to major damage. Some reports claimed as many as 124 homes in San Bernardino County were damaged. On January 28, the Governor of California declared a State of Emergency which included San Bernardino County.
A torrey pine tree fell on a home on Rimini Road in Del Mar. The time of the incident is unknown. No injuries were reported.

Wind gusts as high as 51 MPH were measured by the Ramona Airport ASOS. The strong gusty winds began around 0730 PST on the 21st and continued through about 2300 PST on the 22nd. During that time, an oak tree fell on a car driving on Mossey Grade Road in Ramona, trapping two teenagers. Neither were injured. Another large tree was uprooted and fell on a home on 11th Street in Ramona. Numerous other trees fell down around the city. On family on Highland Valley Road lost 17 avocado trees and a pole that powers their well.

High winds associated with a line of thunderstorms moved through south Orange County between 1330 and 1400 PST on the 19th. A spotter reported wind damage at his mother's condominium complex in Laguna Niguel, near Oso Parkway and Highway 73. A twelve foot tall tennis court enclosure with 4 inch aluminum posts was bent outwards at a 25 degree angle, two mature trees with a trunk diameter of greater than 12 inches were snapped off just above the ground level, and numerous 4 inch diameter tree branches from a pine tree broke off. The spotter was not at the location at the time, but observed the damage two months after it happened. The mother and another neighbor felt a suction and the windows of their condos shook violently. It is possible that a tornado briefly touched down in the complex, though no other reports of a tornado could be found.

A series of tsunami surges destroyed a section of dock on Shelter Island and damaged an underwater pipe. Several vessels in America's Cup Harbor also came loose from their moorings. Some concrete pilings were snapped after a couple commercial fishing boats that were tied to them were pulled away by the strong currents. At Oceanside Harbor, all but one of the channel buoys were lifted and dragged by the surges. The buoys later washed up on the beaches. Currents associated with the surges were estimated at 8 to 10 knots.

A bait barge at Dana Point Harbor was snapped in half by a series of tsunami surges. A 12 knot current was observed with a three inch wave in the main channel. The depth in the main channel fell to 6 feet as the water receded. The normal depth in the channel is 12 to 15 feet.
Snow began in Wrightwood around 1230 PST on Feb 9th. At 1822 PST, a trained spotter reported 8 inches of new snow. Snow showers continued until about 1030 PST on the 10th.

events.event_narrative: A waterspout south of Coronado was reported by the public at 0855 PST.

High winds began in the Riverside County mountains between 0720 and 0820 PST and continued through 0920 PST. Between 0820 and 0920 PST, a peak wind gust of 65 MPH was measured by the Indian Mountain RAWS.

High winds began in the Santa Ana Mountains between 0630 and 0730 PST and continued through 1130 PST. Between 0830 PST and 0930 PST, a peak wind gust of 70 MPH was measured by the Fremont Canyon RAWS.

The observer at John Wayne Airport (KSNA) spotted a funnel cloud about 3 miles south of the airport between 0947 PST and 0950 PST. A second funnel cloud was spotted over the water 10 minutes later. A police helicopter spotted 5 funnel clouds over the water about 0.5 to 2 miles off the coast of Crystal Cove around the same time.
Wind gusts in excess of 58 MPH were measured by the Julian mesonet between 1114 and 1334 PST. Multiple gusts of 61 MPH were measured 1313 and 1334 PST.
A trained spotter reported a measured gust of 76 MPH in Lucerne Valley around 1551 PST on April 4th. The same spotter also reported a gust of 67 MPH around 1030 PST on the 5th.
Wind gusts in excess of 58 MPH were measured by the Whitewater RAWS between 1150 and 1550 PST on April 5th. Between 1350 and 1450 PST a peak gust of 64 MPH was measured.
Wind gusts in excess of 58 MPH were measured by the Burns Canyon RAWS between 1551 and 1951 PST. Between 1751 and 1851 PST a peak wind gust of 62 MPH was measured.

Wind gusts in excess of 58 MPH were measured by the Whitewater RAWS between 1050 PST on the 28th and 0250 PST on the 29th. Between 2250 PST and 0050 PST multiple gusts of 71 MPH were measured. A trained spotter reported blowing dust with visibility down to 1/8 mile and some large tree branches down in Thousand Palms where gusts were as high as 55 MPH.

events.event_narrative: Heavy rain from a short-lived, intense thunderstorm caused frequent lightning, gusty winds, which downed a few trees, and dumped enough rain to cause minor street flooding. Smoke was also seen from spot fires started by lightning in the mountains near Murrieta.
A short, but intense thunderstorm near Borrego Springs caused runoff from heavy rain to enter some stores in town as well as a roof torn off due to gusty winds.

Around 1855 PDT, local law enforcement reported flooding on Shadow Mountain Road west of Highway 395 and on Highway 395 itself. Estimates of up to two feet of water on the flooded roadways was reported due to very heavy rainfall in the El Mirage, Phelan and Adelanto areas, north of Victorville.
Highway 74 closed due to flooding until 1600 PDT.
The East Hemet Mesonet site reported between 0.50 to 1.01 inches of rain fell between 1336 and 1349 PST.
The C4086 mesonet site located in Hemet, CA reported 0.50 inches of rain fell between 1336 and 1346 PST on August 25th.

A thunderstorm near Forest Falls, CA dumped rain for approximately 45 minutes over the western portion of the community. Trees, boulders and mud were reported flowing down Valley of the Falls Road, causing that portion of the road to be closed to traffic for several hours.
The Big Bear City South Mesonet site reported 1.02 inches of rain fell between 1045 and 1145 PST on August 25th. The storm total for that site was 1.54 inches, which fell between 0945 and 1245 PST.
The Mesonet site at Yucaipa Ridge reported that 0.51 inches of rain fell in 8 minutes between 1145 and 1153 PST on August 25th.
The Wrightwood Mesonet site reported 0.81 inches of rain fell within 35 minutes between 1400 and 1435 PST on August 25th.

A member of the public called to report mud, debris and four inch diameter rocks washing down the Sheep Creek Wash at the base of Heath Canyon near Wrightwood, CA on August 25th. Highway 2 was closed between Desert View and Summit Roads due to water, mud and debris washing across the roadway.
Spotter SDG173 reported 1.8 inches of rain measured between 1200 and 1256 PST. Mud, debris and rocks were reported flowing across side roads and blocking Highway 79 near Warner Springs.

A spotter reported 1.73 inches of rain fell between 1400 and 1530 PST on August 26th. The heavy rain flooded Highways 18 and 247 with 2 to 3 feet of water over the roadways.Two swift water rescues were performed, including three people in a car who got washed away, but were saved.
ALERT gauge 2801 at the Oak Glen Watershed measured 0.47 inches of rain between 1048 and 1119 PST on August 26th.

ALERT gauge 248 in Winchester, CA in Riverside County measured 0.49 inches of rain between 1340 and 1430 PST on August 26th. Instantaneous rainfall rates between 1400 and 1415 reached over an inch per hour.
Media reported downed power lines and trees of 1 to 2 feet in diameter near Hemet, CA on August 26th. Wind gusts estimated between 60-70 mph.

The Mataguaty SDGE anemometer, located at 6 meters above ground level, measured a peak wind at 1230 PST out of the NNW at 30 MPH with a gust of 60 MPH.  Downdrafts in excess of 40 MPH began shortly after 1220 and continued until 1250 PDT.
The Fawnskin ALERT gauge in San Bernardino County recorded 1.30 inches of rain in 31 minutes between 1358 and 1429 PST on August 26th.

A severe thunderstorm with estimated wind gusts of 60 MPH brought down ten power poles on Pottery Street in Lake Elsinore. Live power lines fell on a RTA bus around 1330 PST, trapping the driver and 11 passengers for two hours. Trampolines were also picked up and blown into adjacent yards. Street flooding was also reported in Lake Elsinore.

Spotter SDG173 observed a max hail size of 1 inch in Sunshine Summit (approximately 9 miles NW of Warner Springs), while the average hail size was more like 0.75 inch. Estimated duration for the hail and heaviest part of the thunderstorm was 10 to 15 minutes. Estimated wind gusts of 50 to 60 MPH also accompanied the rain and hail.

Seneca Road from Amargosa Road to El Evado Road was completely washed out due heavy rain on the afternoon of August 26th. Several other roads in Victor Valley, including Palmdale Road and portions of Highway 18 were flooded as well.
