events.event_narrative: Ninety-five hundredths of an inch of rain fell in the hour between 1700 and 1800PST. Heavy rain resulted in 3 inches of water flowing over roadway. Rainfall also produced 2 inches of water in garage.
Spotter SBD331 reported 0.62 inches of rain fell in 15 minutes, resulting in water flowing over roadways. Intense cloud-to ground lightning.
Spotter reported roadway flooding due to heavy rainfall with approximately 6 inches of water with debris at the junction of I-15 and Highway 18.

A single family residence received a direct lightning strike to the roof, creating a 3-inch diameter hole. No injuries or fire, but the American Red Cross was called to assist the 5 adults and one infant residents.
A two-story home was struck by lightning during a thunderstorm, creating a 6-inch hole in the roof. No fire or injuries.
High winds began in Whitewater between 2050 and 2150 PST, during which time a peak gust of 58 MPH was measured by the Whitewater RAWS. High winds ended between 2150 and 2250 PST.

High winds began in Lucerne Valley between 0900 and 1000 PST, during which time a peak gust of 78 MPH was measured by the spotter. High winds ended between 0400 and 0500 PST. Power was locally knocked out. Beginning and ending times are approximate, but spotter mentioned strong winds most of the night.
High winds began at Mt. Laguna between 0650 and 0750 PST. A peak gust of 77 MPH was measured by the Mt. Laguna Mesonet. High winds ended between 0950 and 1050 PST.
Spotter RIV256 in Yucaipa observed a white rotating funnel cloud at 1613 PST extending a quarter of the way down the distance between the storm cloud and the ground.

California Highway Patrol reported the ramp at D Street and southbound I-15, as well as D Street itself, was flooded with several inches of water. Bear Valley Road, along the freeway, also experienced some flooding. Businesses along Seventh Street also reported some flooding. No damage information was available.

A construction worker suffered minor burns when lightning struck a nearby crane at the Kaiser Permanente Fontana Medical Center at 0842 PST on October 1. The 50-year old man was thrown to the ground as a result of the strike. His injuries are non-life-threatening.
Lightning struck a trailer located in the 18000 block of Danbury Avenue around 0800 PST on October 19, setting it on fire. No injuries were reported.

Approximately 20 mudslides, due to rain and pre-loosened dirt, poured over Varner Road in Cathedral City in Riverside County on the morning of October 19. Thirty-eight hundredths of an inch of rain fell in the desert that day, resulting in the closure of Varner Road between Date Palm and Rio Del Sol due to an area of mud up to 60 feet wide and up to 18 inches deep. Two vehicles were trapped in the mud, which was cleared by 1000 PST October 20.

A band of convection moved through the San Diego County coastal areas between 1800 and 1900 PST. A clogged storm drain caused flooding at the intersection of Via de la Valle and Jimmy Durante Boulevard in Del Mar. Eight vehicles became trapped in the rapidly rising water, and eighteen people, including several children, had to be rescued by swift-water rescue teams and local lifeguards. There were no injuries.
In Mecca, eight homes had to be evacuated due to flooding. Some residents claimed that flooding has been a problem for years. An auto wrecking business in Indio was also flooded.

Moderate rain and saturated soil caused the ground beneath Highway 74 near Hemet to erode, taking with it a 30 foot by 40 foot section of the road. The highway was closed in both directions for several days for repairs. The incident occurred around 1340 PST in the Cottonwood Fire burn area, however, it was determined that a debris flow was not the cause. No other damage and no injuries were reported.

High winds began in the Santa Ana mountain foothills between 0530 and 0630 PST and continued to between 0930 and 1030 PST. Between 0820 and 0920 PST, multiple gusts above 58 MPH occurred. A peak wind gust of 61 MPH was measured by the Fremont Canyon RAWS.
High winds began in the Apple and Lucerne Valley area around 0150 PST and continued through 1600 PST. Between 1451 and 1551 PST, a peak wind gust of 78 MPH was measured by the Burns Canyon RAWS.
High winds began in the Coachella Valley between 0050 and 0150 PST and continued through 0350 PST. Between 0150 and 0350 PST, peak wind gusts of 60 and 61 MPH were measured by the Whitewater RAWS.

High winds began in the Coachella Valley between 0250 and 0350 PST and continued until approximately 0400 PST. Between 0250 and 0350 PST, a peak wind gust of 58 MPH was measured by the Whitewater RAWS.

San Bernardino County was the hardest hit county in California in terms of amount of damage due to the heavy rain at the end of December. County officials put the total damage amount (including public and private property of all types and labor to repair damage) at approximately $97 million. Both state and federal money will be available to help those affected.|Highway 395 at Highway 18 completely flooded with several stalled vehicles. Eastbound Highway 138 just west of LA County line has mud, debris and water across all lanes. Highway 18, west of Sheep Creek road is closed, as well as Koala Road between Rancho and El Mirage, due to flooding.

Orange County officials estimate the total damages to public and private property at $36 million, due the 10+ of rain received by many areas. The city of Laguna Beach was certainly the hardest hit, making up approximately $12 million of the county's damages. Twelve miles of beaches in the county also had to be closed due to massive amounts of debris and pollution in storm runoff.

Sheep Creek near Wrightwood had a sudden surge in flow to 4 feet at approximately 0745 PST that carried large boulders, several feet in diameter, as well as logs several feet long and over a foot diameter.|Another surge of debris flow occurred at Sheep Creek around 1715 PST. The crossing of Lone Pine Road and Sheep Creek had debris 6 to 8 feet deep.|Flash Flooding around 1630 PST along Lytle Creek running over Glen Helen Parkway, near Interstate 15 northeast of Fontana. Water was within one foot of a levee. Another round of flash flooding occurred along Lytle Creek around 1800 PST. One motorist had to be rescued when trapped in his car in high water.|Around 1500 PST, 8 feet of mud and debris covered Valley of the Falls Drive near the fire station. At 1730 PST, the mud moved into homes along this road.
A spotter in Hesperia measured a wind gust of 62 MPH at 0804 PST. Several fences were blown down in the local neighborhood.
Flash flood occurred in Mira Loma around 1800 PST, requiring two different swift-water rescues of four people in total.
Street flooding in Coronado. Both Northbound lanes on Orange Avenue have 3 to 4 inches of water on the roadway. There was 6 to 7 inches of water on 1st Street near the ferry landing as well.

The San Diego River at Fashion Valley has been above its flood stage of 11.3 feet since 1330 PST. A peak river stage of 14.01 feet was reported, making this a moderate flood event. The river flooding resulted in numerous closed roadways and portions of the Fashion Valley Mall parking facilities were under water. This river flooding also resulted in extensive flooding of the Qualcomm Stadium on Friars Road, including both the stadium itself and the surrounding parking lot. A total of about 1.5 million gallons of water had to be pumped out of that area, back into the river.|A flood channel overflowed, resulting in evacuations of 12 houses in Barrio Logan neighborhood in San Diego. Five people were evacuated from homes in Encanto due to stream flooding.

Highway 330, one of the main routes to Big Bear in the San Bernardino Mountains, collapsed near mile marker 35 on December 20. The force of the water coming down the mountain washed the hillside out from underneath the road itself, causing the collapse. Repairs to the road could take up to 2 years and $15 million.

Heavy rain caused extensive flooding in downtown Laguna Beach with up to 4 feet of water on Broadway Street. Stranded motorists were rescued. The water also swept mud through homes, businesses and streets in the city. Approximately 184 businesses, homes and structures were damaged by the flooding. Sewer pumps were also damaged, resulting in the closure of about 12 miles of Orange County beaches, due to the pollution and waste entered into the storm runoff.

A 39 year old Menifee woman was driving south on Goetz Road when the car was swept off the road by swift runoff from the Salt Creek, where it flows into Canyon Lake. She was found dead in her car at the bottom of the lake several hours later.

Numerous streets in the Chino area were flooded with several inches or more of water after nearly a week of intense rainfall. A 67 year old woman from Pasadena drove her car around a barricade near Chino on Christmas night. The water was deep enough that her car floated about 150 feet down the road, then sank in 10 feet of water. A 39 year old man, owner of a nearby business, jumped into the water and broke the car's sunroof to pull the woman out. He attempted CPR, but she later died at a local hospital.
High winds began at the Burns Canyon RAWS around 0700 PST and ended between 1900 PST and 2000 PST on the 20th. A peak wind gust of 70 MPH was measured between 1601 and 1700 PST.
The beginning and ending times of the high wind criteria are uncertain. The Mill Creek RAWS reported a gust of 63 MPH at 0223 PST on December 30.
The beginning and ending times for high wind criteria are uncertain. The Pinyon Pines RAWS reported a gust of 58 MPH at 0136 PST on December 20.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Also shown on National News. Numerous mud and landslides in Loma Linda and Highland. Cars buried up to 2 feet deep and roads impassable due to diverted water and mud.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Moderately high winds, estimated between 40 and 50 MPH, were blamed for downed power lines and a subsequent transformer explosion which killed three residents in the 5400 block of Acacia Avenue in San Bernardino, CA. The residents went outside to see what caused the explosion and a few small spot fires from sparks, and were electrocuted trying to extinguish the fires and help each other. A water line ruptured at the victims' house and 2700 customers also lost power because of the downed lines.
High winds began at the Fremont Canyon RAWS between 0830 and 0930 PST, during which time a peak gust of 74 MPH was measured. High winds ended between 1730 and 1830 PST.
High winds began at the Fremont Canyon RAWS between 0230 and 0330 PST, during which time a peak gust of 64 MPH was measured by the spotter. High winds ended between 0530 and 0630 PST.
High winds began in Boulder Creek between 0720 and 0730 PST, during which time a peak gust of 58 MPH was measured by the SDGE mesonet station. High winds ended between 0750 and 0800 PST.

Wind gusts estimated around 58 MPH were blamed for toppling a large Eucalyptus tree onto several parked vehicles in La Jolla. No one was injured. A semi was also blown over, blocking two lanes of eastbound Interstate 8 at Route 79. Again, no injuries. A downed power line near Ramona cause power outages to around 200 customers.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: High winds knocked over a 70-75' tree with a 30 diameter trunk that fell on three units of a multi-unit apartment community in Glen Avon, near Riverside. Power lines were also down. No injuries reported, but the three units were declared uninhabitable and the residents relocated.|Five big rigs went down due to winds in the early morning on the 3rd in the area near Interstates 10 and 15 interchange in Ontario. Another crashed on HIghway 60 near I-15. No injuries were reported.

Widespread urban flooding of highways and rural flooding of secondary streets in the Indio/La Quinta/Thermal area. Instantaneous rain rates were a quarter to a third of an inch per hour at times. There was also flash flooding of washes at the Whitewater River crossings (Dune Palms/Adams Street) in La Quinta.
High winds began at Heaps Peak between 1915 and 2015 PST, during which time a peak gust of 60 MPH was measured by the Heaps Peak RAWS. High winds ended between 2315 and 0015 (on the 19th) PST.
High winds began in Fremont Canyon between 1830 and 1930 PST, during which time a peak gust of 61 MPH was measured by the Fremont Canyon RAWS. High winds ended between 2030 and 2130 PST.
High winds began in Burns Canyon between 1351 and 1451 PST, during which time a peak gust of 64 MPH was measured by the Burns Canyon RAWS. High winds ended between 1451 and 1551 PST.

High winds began in Fremont Canyon between 1230 and 1330 PST, during which time a peak gust of 60 MPH was measured by the Fremont Canyon RAWS. High winds ended between 1530 and 1630 PST.|A tree, blown down by winds, blocked traffic for about 45 minutes on the westbound 22 connector to northbound I-5. No injuries reported.

A spotter in Forest Falls reported a storm total snowfall of 24 inches. A spotter in Wrightwood reported a storm total snowfall of 24.5 inches. A spotter in Lake Arrowhead reported a storm total snowfall of 21 inches.
A spotter in Idyllwild reported a storm total snowfall of 15 inches. A spotter in Pine Cove reported a storm total snowfall of 20.75 inches.

A spotter at the Palomar Observatory reported a storm total snowfall of 16 inches at 5600 feet. A spotter on Mt. Laguna reported a storm total snowfall of 23 inches. Spotters down to 3000 feet reported 3-6 inches of snow.
Heavy rain washed mud and debris onto sections of San Timoteo Canyon Road and Live Oak Canyon Roads. The roads were closed through the weekend to clean up. Cost of the cleanup is unknown.

High winds began in the Coachella Valley between 0750 and 0850 PST, during which time a peak gust of 72 MPH was measured by the Whitewater RAWS. High winds ended between 1350 and 1450 PST. A downed power pole closed a portion of Indian Canyon Road and a tractor trailer overturned near the intersection of Interstate 10 and Highway 111, but no injuries reported.

Mission Bay saw the first tsunami surge around 0915 PST and continued to experience surges every 1.5 to 2 hours. These surges broke apart a bait barge and sent 8 of its 26 bait boxes into the bay where they were lost.

Snowfall began in most locations between 1500 and 1600 PST Sunday the 20th. A spotter in Wrightwood reported a storm total of 28 inches, with strong winds blowing all afternoon. A spotter in Running Springs reported a storm total of 20 inches. A spotter in Big Bear City reported a storm total of 15 inches at 6800 feet elevation, with a few inches more at the resorts.

A spotter measured a gust of 115 MPH on an anemometer. The gust damaged the anemometer shortly after. Several power poles and trees were knocked down, causing a blackout that lasted nearly 24 hours. Numerous houses sustained roof damage and at lease one house had its roof destroyed. No related injuries were reported from the event.|Another spotter reported a measured wind gust of 59 MPH with sustained winds of 30 MPH, resulting in downed power lines, tiles blown off roof and power outages.|Yet another spotter measured sustained winds of 40 MPH with a gust of 65 MPH between 1300 and 1400 PST.
High winds began at the Hesperia South mesonet station between 1153 and 1253 PST. High winds ended between 1253 and 1353 PST. During this time, a wind gust of 62 MPH was recorded.

High winds began at the Burns Canyon RAWS around 0400 PST and ended around 1600 PST on the 20th. Numerous gusts over 80 MPH were recorded between 0500 and 1300 PST. A peak wind gust of 110 MPH was measured around 1030 PST.
A wind gust of 52 knots was measured by a Huntington Beach lifeguard between 1315 and 1415 PST on the 20th. He also reported the wind blowing sand and trash cans around the beach.

events.cz_name: SAN MATEO PT TO MEXICAN BDR OUT 30NM
events.event_narrative: One of these thunderstorms formed a waterspout approximately 4 miles northwest of San Diego, as seen by an airplane pilot. No damage or injuries were reported.

Gusty winds were responsible for moderate damage in the Coachella Valley on the 7th. A power line fell in an alley in the town of Coachella, causing six homes to be evacuated as a precaution while power was restored. Two trees fell in the Indian Springs area, one landing on the hood of an SUV and the other blocking traffic in Palm Desert. No injuries or fires were reported with any of the incidents. The Palm Springs Tramway closed its mountain station early due to high winds.

The Palm Springs Airport measured a wind gust of 45 mph on the 21st. The gusty winds were responsible for blowing over a single-engine, Cessna 172 aircraft after it landed Thursday afternoon around 1230 PST. The pilot, the only passenger, was not injured. Also, Indian Canyon Drive was closed due to large amounts of blowing sand near the Whitewater Wash around 1500 PST on the 21st. It had recently been reopened after being closed just a couple of days prior for blowing sand as well.

Strong winds took down 35-40 trees at the Rancho Mirage Public library between late Sunday (8th) and early Monday (9th). The trees were mature, 15 to 20 foot tall mesquites and palo verdes. Nearby Thousand Palms recorded a wind gust of 40 MPH at 0300 PST Monday, while Thermal airport recorded a gust of 53 MPH at 2300 PST Sunday. No other damage was done to the library and no one was injured.

Heavy winds knocked over a power pole around 1530 PST on the 9th near Stevens Road and Via Monte Vista, according to the Palm Springs Fire Department. Winds were gusting in the middle 50s at many nearby sensors during the day. The power pole fell into a vacant lot where it started a small brush fire, which was contained within a half hour and did not spread beyond that lot. Power was out for around 400 customers in the area for about a day. No injuries were reported.

Strong gusty winds damaged the main sign for the Hesperia Professional Building in the city of Hesperia during the early morning of the 29th. The nearby Hesperia South mesonet recorded a peak gust of 46 MPH around midnight that night, but higher gusts were possible between the recorded observations.

On each of the 17th and 18th, numerous record low temperatures (both max and min) were set in the Coachella Valley. Palm Springs and Thermal both broke records on May 18, previously set in 1994 with high temperatures of 76 and 77 respectively. The longest record broken was for Indio on the 18th with a high temperature of 74 breaking the previous record of 77 set back in 1948. The temperatures seen in this area during these few days were also about 25-20 degrees below normal for that time of year.

Strong winds began at the Whitewater RAWS between 1800 and 1900 PST on the 15th and ended between 0400 and 0500 PST on the 17th. A peak gust of 56 MPH was recorded between 0600 and 0700 PST on the 16th.||These strong winds were responsible for two overturned big rigs along Highway 111 just south of Overture Drive. No one was injured, but officers asked high profile vehicles to avoid the wind-prone area of Hwy 111 and even began turning them away from the area.|Hwy 111 was eventually shut down for a time from Interstate 10 past Overture Drive for about four hours.

Strong winds in Coachella had kicked up a cloud of dust on the evening of the 16th. The winds coupled with the dust were blamed for a pile-up involving 5 vehicles and 3 semi-trucks. Visibility was reported to be near zero at the time of the crash around 1610 PST. Several people were taken to the hospital for non-serious injuries. Highway 86 was shutdown between Avenues 50 and 52 for several hours, reopening around 2000 PST that night. The Thermal Airport was reporting sustained winds of 20 MPH with gusts to around 30 MPH around the time of the crash.

Strong winds began at the Palm Springs International Airport between 1000 and 1100 PST and ended between 1700 and 1800 PST on the 17th. During this time a peak gust of 28 MPH was recorded. ||During the gusty winds, a small experimental plane flipped up on its nose after landing at the Palm Springs Airport. It flipped while turning to taxi on the runway. The pilot was the only passenger and not injured.
Street flooding in numerous locations within Apple Valley due to heavy rain. Pea sized hail also reported.

Spotter SBD286 reported a very heavy downpour in the area of North Shore Drive and Greenway Drive in Big Bear City from approximately 1340-1355 PST. During this time, his rain gage showed just over a half inch of rain.
San Diego County Flood Control reported 0.80 inches of rain over 15 minutes and an additional 0.10 inches over the next 5 minutes, resulting in 0.90 inches of rain over 20 minutes.

Spotter SBD320 reported Phelan Road West closed at Beekley Road due to flooding from heavy rain of 0.26 inches of rain in one hour in Phelan. Highway 138 is also closed betweek Beekley Road and Green Road due to mud, water and debris on the roadway.|Another spotter reported 1.5 feet of water on the road at the intersection of Highway 18 and Sheep Creek Road, with cars stranded on the side of the road.

Power lines down due to wind in the vicinity of Perris and Romoland. Locations include Ethanac Road at Evans Road west of Romoland, South D and East 7th Streets in Perris, and the 27900 block of Washington Street. All lines reported down around 1400 PST on the 6th.
Three houses in Nuevo had minor flooding in the 500 block of West 10th, 28600 block of Central and the 28700 block of Reservoir. No one was forced out of their homes.
Spotter estimated a 60 mph wind gust from a thunderstorm in the area. Powerlines also reported down on 7th and D streets due to wind knocking down trees onto lines.
Spotter RIV116 reported numerous debris flows and arroyo flooding along Lone Pine Canyon Road near Wrightwood due to heavy rain from a thunderstorm.
A member of the public reported 0.76 inches of rain falling in a period of 45 minutes during a thunderstorm on the 30th. She also reported pea sized hail and substantial lightning.

Two trees in a backyard on Beekley in the Pinon Hills area, foothills below Wrightwood, lost limbs. The limbs that came down were the size of small trees. The wind also picked up their pool cover and threw it in to the pool.
The Whitewater River gage at Windy Point rose 1000 cfs in 30 minutes from 1830 TO 1900 PST. The source of the heavy rainfall was in the San Gorgonio Wilderness.
An employee of the Golden Acorn Casino along I-8 near Boulevard estimated penny-sized hail around 1200 PST.
Anza-Borrego State Park rangers reported three power poles down due to thudnerstorm wind gusts.

Parts of Ridgecrest Road flooded near railroad tracks. Many streets in Spring Valley have flowing water. Street flooding between Balsom and Mariposa. Outside lane flooding between Cottonwood and Nisqualli.

Parts of Ridgecrest Road flooded near railroad tracks. Many streets in Spring Valley have flowing water. Street flooding between Balsom and Mariposa. Outside lane flooding between Cottonwood and Nisqualli.

Local flooding at mile marker 15 of county road S-2, north of Scissors Crossing. Heavy rain from a thunderstorm moving north along S-2 caused low parts of the road to be covered with a few inches of running water.
Heavy rain from several hours caused street flooding on Palmdale Road at Del Gado.|1 inch rain in 12 hours.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE

events.event_narrative: Nickel sized hail was reported by a spotter, along with an estimated wind gust of 45 to 55 mph.
Spotter reported street flooding on Big Bear Boulevard from the Stanfield cutoff to Pine Knot Avenue, as well as Rathbun Creek at Catalina Road. Water 6-12 inches deep covered the roadway.

Chihuahua Valley Road was impassable due to fast-moving water over the roadway, up to 2 feet deep in places. Other roads were washed out nearby. Hail up to penny-sized (3/4) was also observed along Chihuahua Valley Road, with minor accumulation of the hail.

The SDGE Mesonet, CMCSD recorded a wind gust of 65 mph during a downburst from a thunderstorm at 1400 PST on the 28th. The Campo ASOS also recorded a gust of 61 mph at 1352 PST nearby. During the time of these gusts, 5 power poles were snapped on Buckman Springs Road near Highway 94 and several large tree branches fell onto the Campo COOP observer's property. Power was lost soon after these poles and branches came down. Lightning sparked several small fires on the observer's property, but all were contained quickly. The Campo ASOS also recorded 1.02 inches of rain in 30 minutes during this storm.
Spotter reported 1.05 inches of rainfall in 30 minutes, causing 1-2 inches of mud and water on SR-247 near Blandford Land and Larrea Road.

San Clemente Lifeguards reported damage to the San Clemente Pier when high surf caused two beams to break off in the middle section.|A female of unknown age was swept off a jetty in Dana Point, suffering significant scrapes and bruises.|Numerous beaches including Capistrano Beach were closed due to unsafe conditions and high surf. Significant beach erosion and flooding of nearby beach parking lots also occurred.
Lifeguards reported damage to the railings of the Ocean Beach Pier due to high surf.

Two reports of quarter-sized hail in Dana Point around 0600 PST. Quarter-sized hail was also reported in Costa Mesa and two others of one-inch hail in Anaheim between about 0900 and 0930 PST on the 10th.

Highway 18 was closed at Bear Valley Road just east of Apple Valley due to 1-2 feet of water  on the roadway between mile marker 80 and High Road. Numerous vehicles were stalled due to water intake. ||A spotter also reported 4 to 5 inches of standing water on highway 18 between Dead Man's Point and Highway 247. Multiple vehicles were also stalled here due to water intake.
Hail of dime size or 3/4 inch was reported with heavy rain in both Big Bear City and Highland from a cluster of thunderstorms.

A thunderstorm trained over the area dropping moderate rain for approximately three hours. As a result, a channel overflowed, pushing 8 inches of mud onto SR 111 between Highway 195 and Mecca Avenue. The Palm Ditch Bridge was was covered in this mud, but was declared undamaged. ||Numerous other roadways in the area were closed due to flooding and/or mud flows as well.

Heavy rain in the Pinion Hills/Antelope Valley Hills area caused flooding near Highway 138. Mud and rocks as large as oranges covered the roadway. In nearby Wrightwood, a spotter reported Sheep Creek crossing at Lone Pine Canyon Road was closed due to a flow of mud, rock and tree debris. The spotter reported a half of an inch of rainfall in 30 minutes.
Storm Chaser Will Wilkens captured a funnel cloud on video near Perris around 1440 PST. There was a strong thunderstorm in the area when the funnel was sighted.

High winds began at the Burns Canyon RAWS between 1000 and 1100 PST and ended between 2000 and 2100 PST. During this time, a wind gust of 65 mph was recorded between 1100 and 1200 PST and a gust of 68 mph was recorded between 1900 and 2000 PST.

Strong winds forced a big rig with an empty trailer into oncoming traffic on Highway 18 near Rabbit Springs Road in Lucerne Valley, causing an accident involving three vehicles. Three people were injured in the accident. Exact wind speed at the time of the incident is unknown.||Strong winds also downed power lines in Lucerne Valley during this time.
Strong winds began at the Harrison Park RAWS between 1400 and 1500 PST and ended between 1700 and 1800 PST. During this time, high winds were reached with a gust of 59 mph between 1610 and 1620 PST.

High winds began at the Fremont Canyon RAWS between 2230 and 2330 PST on the 1st and ended between 1030 and 1130 PST on the 2nd. During that time, a peak gust of 81 mph was measured between 0330 and 0430 PST on the 2nd.|Nearby, a large sign was blown down on the 91 freeway near Highway 55.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: High winds began at the Highland Springs RAWS between 0415 and 0515 PST and ended between 1015 and 1115 PST on the 2nd. Between 0815 and 0915 PST, a peak gust of 64 mph was measured.

High winds began at the Tonner Canyon RAWS between 0600 and 0700 PST on the 2nd and ended between 1100 and 1200 PST. During that time, winds gusted consistently above 50 mph with a peak gust of 60 mph measured between 1000 and 1100 PST.
CBS 8 via Twitter reported a large tree down on power lines leaving 1500 customers without power. There were no nearby wind reports, but nearby gusts were measured around 40 mph out of the east.

High winds began at the Otay Mountain SDGE mesonet site between 0910 and 0920 PST on the 10th and ended between 1030 and 1040 PST. During this time, several gusts over 58 mph were recorded with a peak gust of 63 mph measured between 0910 and 0920 PST.

This storm marked the first significant snow of the season for the San Bernardino County Mountains. A spotter in Running Springs reported 5 inches for the storm total, while another spotter in Forest Falls reported a storm total of 4 inches.
The Weather Currents station at Beaumont-Calimesa received 1.17 inches of rain in the hour between 1900 and 2000 PST on the 20th and a total of 1.61 inches for the day.

High winds began in the Coachella Valley between 0950 and 1050 PST and ended between 1250 and 1350 PST on the 19th. During that time, two gusts of 58 mph were measured at the Whitewater RAWS between 0950 and 1150 PST.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: The Palm Avenue Elementary weather station in the city of San Bernardino recorded sustained northeast winds of 49 mph around 0700 PST on the 1st. A max gust of 70 mph was also recorded at that station at 0551 PST. |The Cal State San Bernardino mesonet station reported high winds between 0350 and 0550 PST. During this time, sustained winds of 40 mph were recorded along with gusts of 47 and 53 mph.|Numerous occurrences of wind damage near these stations were reported. An overturned box truck was blocking the slow lane of I-15 near Glen Helen Parkway.  Power lines and trees were downed near the city of San Bernardino. Power poles and lines were also down across 3rd Avenue near the Crafton Reservoir in Mentone.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: The Ontario Airport ASOS measured a wind gust of 55 mph around 0300 PST on the 1st. Visibility was reduced to 3 SM in blowing dust due to the strong wind. |In nearby Rancho Cucamonga, the slow lane of Highway 210 at Day Creek Boulevard was closed to upright a semi truck. Fences and hundreds of trees were downed in that area, some blocking roadways. Another big rig overturned in the center divide of Highway 210 at Beech Avenue, blocking the HOV lane until it could be up-righted.

Snow began falling in the eastern sections of the San Bernardino County Mountains on the evening of November 30th, reached winter storm criteria sometime Thursday evening, December 1st and ceased later that night near midnight. Big Bear City received a storm total of 16 inches. Nearby Big Bear Lake received 18 inches, with some snow drifts reaching 2 to 3 feet. Onyx Peak received a storm total of 16 inches around 8200 feet.|Power lines were also downed in nearby Crestline on Crest Forest Drive at Scenic Drive.

High winds began at the Boulder Creek SDGE mesonet site around 2100 PST on the 5th and ended around midnight on the 6th. During that time, several gusts over 58 mph were recorded including a peak gust of 65 mph around 2130 PST and another of 62 mph around 2300 PST.
A spotter reported a funnel cloud southwest of the city of La Mesa around 1625 PST on the 12th.
Three waterspouts were spotted one mile off Windansea Beach, moving from southwest to northeast between 1130 and 1140 PST on the 12th. No landfall was noted.
Multiple funnel cloud reports from the KSNA ASOS at 10 and 15 miles east of John Wayne Airport.
Two funnel clouds estimated 10 miles to the north of the spotter, who is located in Riverside near Jarupa Avenue and Grand Avenue.

High winds began at the Fremont Canyon RAWS between 0351 and 0451 PST on the 16th and ended between 1351 and 1451 PST the same day. During that time a max gust of 65 mph was measured, along with several other gusts above 58 mph (including 2 of 61 mph and one of 60 mph).||During this time, power poles were reported down by Fox 11 News in nearby Yorba Linda. Around 240 customers were reported without power in nearby Tustin as well.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: High winds began at the Highland Springs RAWS between 1316 and 1416 PST on the 16th and ended between 1516 and 1616 PST. During this time a peak gust of 63 mph was recorded between 1416 and 1516.|Several trees and power lines were reported down in the Hemet area of Riverside County shortly after this report.
Strong winds damaged the patio roof on the property. Tree limbs as large as 4 inches in diameter have been breaking off trees. Property is located on Pala Mesa Road near SR 76 near Fallbrook.
The Bear Mountain Resort near Big Bear City reported a 24 hour snowfall total of 12 to 16 inches at 7500 feet elevation, approximately half of which fell between 0700 and 1300 PST on the 18th.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Winds began gusting over 40 mph at the Cal State San Bernardino mesonet station around 0350 PST on the 22nd and tapered off around 0850 PST the same morning. During that time a peak gust of 56 mph was recorded between 0700 and 0800 PST. |Several gusts between 45 and 55 mph occurred.  A sustained wind measurement of 43 mph was also reported for the hour between 0650 and 0750 PST. ||Damages included a semi overturned on Interstate 15 near Fontana and another big rig overturned in strong winds on Interstate 210 near Rancho Cucamonga. A third truck was overturned on Interstate 15 near Devore by a strong wind gust. The driver of this box truck suffered minor injuries as a result.

High winds began between 0551 and 0651 PST on the 22nd at the Fremont Canyon RAWS and ended between 1451 and 1551 PST the same day. During this time, wind gusts of 70 mph or greater were measured each hour for approximately 7 hours, with a peak gust of 75 mph between 0751 and 0851 PST. Sustained winds were 50 mph or greater during many of these hours as well.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Strong winds began at the Ontario International Airport between 0853 and 0953 PST on the 22nd and ended between 1153 and 1253 PST. During that time, several wind gusts between 44 and 46 mph were measured and a peak gust of 53 was recorded around 1120 PST. |A 50-foot empty semi tractor trailer overturned along Interstate 15 in nearby Mira Loma due to the strong winds.

High winds began at the Fremont Canyon RAWS between 0651 and 0751 PST on the 23rd and ended between 0751 and 0851 PST. During that time, a peak gust of 63 mph was measured between 0751 and 0851 PST. |The nearby Santiago Peak mesonet station recorded a peak gust of 60 mph earlier that morning around 0400 PST.

The John Wayne Airport ASOS reported visibility of less than one-quarter mile from 2318 PST on the 29th through 0439 PST on the morning of the 30th. Visibility of one-eighth of a mile was reported from 2229 to 2317 PST on the night of the 30th and again on the morning of the 31st from 0553 to 0652 PST and from 0721 to 0947 PST. Visibility of one-eighth of a mile was again reported the evening of the 31st from 1823 to 1852 PST and again from 2053 to 2352 PST.|The Newport Beach lifeguards also reported visibility of less than 100 yards on the morning of the 31st.

The San Diego Lindbergh Field ASOS reported visibility of one-eighth of a mile from 0351 to 0528 PST on the morning of the 30th and again on the morning of the 31st from 0201 to 0250 PST. |Zero visibility was reported at nearby Coronado Cays near Chula Vista.

John Wayne Airport ASOS reported less than 1/4 mile visibility from 0153 to 0352 PST on the 1st and 1/8 mile visibility from 0553 to 0652 PST and again from 0753 to 0836 PST. The following day, John Wayne reported less than 1/4 mile visibility from 0153 to 0452 PST and 1/16 mile visibility from 0753 to 0830 PST.|Newport and Huntington Beach lifeguards reported visibilities as low as 50 to 100 yards during these times.

Lindbergh Field ASOS reported 1/8 mile visibility from 0322 to 0550 PST, from 0624 to 0850 PST and again from 2025 to 2229 PST on the 1st. The following day, Carlsbad Palomar Airport ASOS reported less than 1/4 mile visibility from 2353 PST on the 1st to 0052 PST on the 2nd. During these mornings, Mission Beach lifeguards reported visibilities of 1/8 mile or less.
A San Clemente lifeguard reported that high surf caused a stringer to come off the San Clemente Pier around 1145 PST on the 6th.

During the swell increase on Monday the 2nd, a 26-year-old male and his friend were swept out past the surf zone in a strong rip current at Huntington Beach. The man's friend was pulled to safety by a nearby beach-goer, but did not want to come in himself. It took a helicopter two hours to recover his body, but by that time he had died.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: High winds began at the Ontario Airport ASOS around 1000 PST on the 7th and continued off and on until 0530 PST on the 8th. During this time, gusts of 60 mph were measured around 2209 PST (7th), 2217 PST (7th) and 0510 PST (8th).|California Highway Patrol reported an overturned big rig on the I-15 south/I-10 east elevated connector at 0329 PST on the 8th. The connector was closed until 1026 PST due to high winds. The Ontario Airport ASOS reported a gust of 53 mph at 0253 PST.|CHP reported another overturned big rig on I-10 east just west of the Valley Boulevard exit in Fontana around 0637 PST. KONT reported a wind gust of 49 mph at 0629 PST nearby.|Another big rig overturned on I-10 near the N. Vineyard Avenue exit in Ontario at 1024 PST. KONT recorded a wind gust between 36 and 38 mph during that time.

High winds began at the Fremont Canyon RAWS between 1900 and 2000 PST on the 7th and ended between 1100 and 1200 PST on the 8th. Several gusts over 60 mph were recorded during this time, with a peak gust of 82 mph between 0351 and 0451 PST on the 8th. |High winds began at the Santiago Peak mesonet station between 0030 and 0130 PST and ended between 0745 and 0945 PST on the 8th. During this time, a peak gust of 66 mph was recorded between 0119 and 0300 PST.

High winds began at the Crestline Ridge mesonet station between 0030 and 0130 PST and ended between 0845 and 0945 PST on the 8th. Several gusts over 60 mph were recorded during this time, with a peak gust of 74 mph between 0344 and 0500 PST on the 8th. At 1529 PST, the station reported sustained winds of 60 mph. |CHP reported power lines down in the road near the intersection of Rate Road and Lovers Lane. |CHP reported a medium sized tree down across Crest Forest Drive just west of N. Village Drive around 0530 PST and another tree down blocking Old Waterman Canyon Road just south of SR-18.

High winds occurred much of the early afternoon in the Borrego area of San Diego County, with plenty of blowing dust. At approximately 1415 PST, the spotter measured a wind gust of 74 mph on his home weather station.
A spotter 25 miles ENE of Victorville (northwest of Johnson Valley) recorded a peak wind gust of 78 mph around 1031 PST.

High winds began at the Burns Canyon RAWS between 0851 and 0951 PST and ended between 1851 and 1951 PST on the 21st. During this time, most wind gusts were above 60 mph and several above 80 mph. A peak gust of 99 mph was measured between 0951 and 1051 PST.
The Palm Springs Aerial Tramway was closed around 1115 PST due to estimated 80 to 90 mph wind gusts. Around 20 people were temporarily stranded at the top of the station, but no one was injured.

High winds began at the Palm Springs Airport between 1230 and 1300 PST and ended between 1853 and 1953 PST on the 21st. During this time, two gusts over 60 mph were recorded with a peak gust of 66 mph measured at 1348 PST. The other gust of 62 mph occurred at 1646 PST. Several reports of damage occurred during this period. Between 1600 and 1900 PST, the wind was sustained at 30 to 45 mph. |Three major roadways through Palm Springs were closed due to zero visibility caused by blowing dust and sand. They were Indian Avenue, Gene Autry Trail and Vista Chino. Reduced visibility from blowing sand is believed to have caused a crash between a bus, a truck and a sedan on I-10 westbound near the Gene Autry Train exit. Four people were taken to the hospital for injuries from the crash. Power poles were knocked down on Gene Autry Trail as well as Palm Canyon Drive at Linden Way (also closed). Carports were knocked over by winds, crushing cars, at an apartment complex at Highway 111 and Escoba. Numerous power lines and approximately 400 trees were also damaged or knocked down in the Palm Springs area.

The Thermal Regional Airport ASOS measured a gust of 60 mph at 1442 PST on the 21st, but had been reporting gusts 35 to 50 mph from approximately 1300 to 1700 PST. |Bridges and wash crossings were closed at Washington and Adams Streets due to blowing dust and sand reducing visibility. |The Humana Challenge Golf Tournament at the La Quinta Country Club was stopped at 1322 PST due to the high winds. The leader board at the 18th Hole was blown over into the lake on the Palmer Private course. The main tent in the Bob Hope Square fan area collapsed. There was also damage to the vendor and event tents. No injuries have been reported. Several trees were knocked over or uprooted on the La Quinta course, while a few other courses had only cosmetic damage and blowing debris.

High winds began at the Burns Canyon RAWS between 1051 and 1151 PST and ended between 1251 and 1351 PST on the 23rd. During that time two gusts over 60 mph were recorded, including the peak gust of 74 mph measured between 1151 and 1251 PST.

High winds occurred at the Harrison Park SDGE weather station between 1400 and 1600 PST on the 23rd. During that time two gusts of 58 mph were recorded, as well as the peak gust of 59 mph measured between 1310 and 1320 PST.

High winds occurred at the Crestline Ridge mesonet station on the 27th when sustained winds of 47 mph were recorded for the hour between 0443 and 0543 PST. High winds occurred again on the 28th beginning between 0243 and 0343 PST and ending between 1200 and 1243 PST on the 28th. During that time, wind gusts of 58 mph or higher were recorded between 0848 and 1043 PST, including the peak gust of 63 mph recorded 0913 and 1043 PST.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Sustained winds above 40 mph were recorded at 0550 PST, with gusts of 55 mph reported at 0610 PST. California State University San Bernardino closed on the 27th due to the high winds.

High winds began at the Fremont Canyon RAWS on the 27th 0651 and 0751 PST and ended between 1351 and 1451 PST. During that time, several gusts over 58 mph were recorded, including a peak gust of 61 mph measured twice (once at the beginning and once at the end) between the high wind interval. |High winds began again between 1751 and 1851 PST on the 27th and ended between 0751 and 0851 PST on the 28th. During that period, wind gusts were consistently above 60 mph and sustained winds were above 40 mph for the majority of the hours. A peak gust of 82 mph was measured between 0351 and 0451 PST on the 28th.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: A 911 call center reported large containers blown off of a semi-tractor trailer on eastbound Highway 210 at the overpass of Cherry Avenue. A peak wind gust from the northeast at 51 mph was observed at the Heritage School in Fontana.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: High winds occurred at the Highland Springs RAWS between 1100 and 1300 PST on the 27th. During that time a peak gust of 61 mph was measured between 1116 and 1216 PST.
Wind gusts over 50 mph were recorded at the Lucky Five Ranch mesonet station between 0840 and 1120 PST on the 28th. During that time, a peak gust of 59 mph was measured between 0920 and 0930 PST.
The Huntington Beach lifeguards reported wave sets to 10 feet for the majority of the day on the 9th.
The Solana Beach lifeguards reported wave sets to 7 feet during the morning and early afternoon on the 9th.

High winds began at the Sky Valley mesonet station between 1130 and 1230 PST and ended between 1600 and 1700 PST on the 11th. During this time, several gusts above 60 mph were recorded including a peak gust of 71 mph around 1300 PST. Sustained winds of 40 mph or greater occurred from 1000 to 1200 PST and from 1600 to 1800  PST.
A spotter in La Quinta, near Thermal, reported blowing dust reducing visibility to one tenth of a mile or less. Winds at the time were sustained 30 mph and gusting to 47 mph.
A Huntington Beach Lifeguard reported three funnel clouds approximately 4 miles offshore, sometime between 0800 and 0830 PST on the 14th. The funnel clouds dissipated without lowering to the water.

High winds began at the Fremont Canyon RAWS between 0651 and 0751 PST and ended between 1251 and 1351 PST on the 16th. During this time, winds consistently gusted above 60 mph and often above 65 mph. Two peak gust of 73 mph was recorded between 1851 and 2051 PST.
Two-day snow totals include: Snow Summit Resort near Big Bear (8200 ft)with 14; Onyx Summit (8200 ft) with 12; Running Springs (7200 ft) with 10 and Arrowbear Lake (6200 ft) with 10.
Two day snowfall totals include: Long Valley Resort (10,000 ft) with 20; Pine Cove/Idyllwild with 14 and San Jacinto (7000 ft) with 8.5.

San Diego lifeguards at Mission Bay reported visibility of one-eighth of a mile around 0930 PST on the 23rd. Solana Beach lifeguards reported visibility of one-eighth of a mile at Fletcher Cove around 1100 PST on the 23rd. Brown Field ASOS reported visibility less than one-quarter of a mile from 0453-0553 PST on the 24th. Montgomery Field ASOS reported less than one-quarter of a mile visibility at 0653 PST and one-sixteenth of a mile visibility at 0753 PST on the 24th.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Corona Airport ASOS reported visibility less than one-quarter of a mile from 0208 to 0256 PST on the 26th. Chino Airport ASOS reported less than one-quarter of a mile visibility from 0323 to 0353 PST on the 26th. Ontario Airport ASOS reported one-eighth of a mile visibility from 0453 to 0633 PST on the 26th. March Air Reserve Base ASOS reported three-sixteenths of a mile visibility at 0230 PST and one-eighth of a mile from 0248 through at least 0700 PST on the 26th.

A spotter 5 miles southwest of San Jacinto Peak reported storm total snowfall of 9.5 inches with a water equivalent of 1.33 inches. Idyllwild/Pine Cove reported 14 inches of snow at 5400 feet, which is their heaviest snow for the season.

Onyx Summit and Snow Summit between 8000 and 8500 feet near Big Bear received between 11 and 14 inches of storm-total snow.|Heavy snow of 4 to 8 inches in 6 hours led to CHP escorts on I-5 through the Cajon Pass (snow level 3000 feet).

A spotter on Mt. Laguna reported storm-total snowfall of 11 inches. Spotters at Palomar Mountain and Pine Valley each reported 7 inches.|Julian schools were closed, tree damage from heavy, wet snow, and the I-8 mountain pass saw issues with 2 to 4 inches of snowfall. Widespread chain control was mandated.
Heavy rain caused mud to cover Highway 78, 2 miles east of Scissors Crossing.

A mesonet station 5 miles ESE of Cuyamaca Peak measured a wind gust of 64 mph around 2250 PST on the 27th and a gust of 58 mph around 0330 PST on the 28th.|Another mesonet station 5 miles SW of Dulzura measured a wind gust of 60 mph around 2314 PST on the 27th.
Three to four inches of snow and icy roads caused California HIghway Patrol to close Interstate 8 near Pine Valley. Widespread chain control was enforced above 3500 feet.

High winds began at the Whitewater RAWS between 2350 PST on February 29 and 0050 PST on March 1 and ended between 0150 and 0250 PST on the 1st. During this time, a peak gust of 72 mph was measured between 2350 PST and 0050 PST. Winds continued to gust in the 50s during much of the rest of the day and evening.
A spotter in Lucerne Valley reported a wind gust of 68 mph which was responsible for knocking down a 35-foot tall ham radio antenna.

High winds began at the Crestline Ridge mesonet station between 0543 and 0648 PST on the 2nd and ended between 1043 and 1143 PST the same day. During that time, sustained winds over 50 mph were measured between 0630 and 0830 PST. A peak gust of 64 mph occurred around 0700 PST.

High winds began at the Fremont Canyon RAWS between 0651 and 0751 PST on the 2nd and ended between 1051 and 1151 PST. During that time, sustained winds over 40 mph were recorded for several hours as well as a peak gust of 65 mph between 0751 and 0851 PST.
The Sky Valley Mesonet station recorded a peak gust of 72 mph at 0704 PST on the 2nd.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: A Skywarn observer reported a mobile home roof being ripped off by winds. Winds at the nearby Jurupa Valley mesonet station were gusting in the 40s at the time.

High winds began at the Burns Canyon RAWS between 1051 and 1151 PST on the 6th and ended between 1851 and 1951 PST the same day. During that time, several hours of sustained winds over 45 mph occurred with many gusts above 70 mph. A peak gust of 85 mph was measured between 1251 and 1351 PST.

A spotter in Johnson Valley reported sustained winds between 38 and 63 mph during the afternoon of the 6th with visibility one-quarter mile or less in blowing dust. Sometime around 1300 PST, a peak gust of 105 mph was measured. No damage noted.

High winds began at the Sky Valley mesonet between 1044 and 1144 PST on the 6th and ended between 1844 and 1944 PST the same day. During that time, several wind gusts above 60 mph were measured including a peak gust of 75 mph recorded between 1400 and 1500 PST.

The Borrego State Park District office closed at 1530 PST due to flying debris. Wind had ripped apart a metal awning and a metal parking structure. Winds in Borrego Springs at 1545 PST were sustained at 41 mph and gusting to 47 mph. Visibility was less than 100 yards at times in blowing dust. ||A mobile home residence in Ocotillo Wells was blown over by winds around 1730 PST. NO injuries reported. At 1744 PST, winds were sustained 21 mph, gusting to 45 mph. At 1808 PST, winds were sustained  at 29 mph, gusting to 62 mph. Ocotillo Wells State Park lost many of its camping ramadas due to the wind. In Palm Canyon Campground at Anza Borrego, an electric golf cart was picked up by the wind and hurled into a visitors motor home.||At 2000 PST, Borrego Springs reported a wind gust of 63 mph. At 2045 PST, winds were sustained at 40 mph, gusting to 59 mph.

Strong winds in the Coachella Valley caused several instances of blowing dust as well as some traffic sign damage and trees down. A street sign was partially knocked down from its supporting pole on Sunrise Way, near Gene Autry Trail. Palm Springs police also closed Gene Autry Trail between Via Escuela and Interstate 10 for much of the day on the 6th to be reopened by 8am the following morning.

A spotter in Lucerne Valley estimated wind gusts of 75 mph with numerous power outages in the Lucerne Valley area. A nearby mesonet station reported wind gusts of 58 and 60 mph between 0800 and 0900 PST on the 17th.||At 0730 PST, the Victorville airport reported visibility of one quarter mile due to blowing dust. ||Around 0950 PST, another spotter reported sustained winds of 30 mph with gusts to 50 mph and blowing dusts causing visibility of less than 200 yards.

High winds began at the Sky Valley mesonet station between 0000 and 0044 PST and ended between 0200 and 0300 PST. During this time, a peak gust of 71 mph was recorded between 0200 and 0300 PST. High winds were again recorded between 1544 and 1744 PST with sustained winds of 42 mph and a gust to 60 mph.

High wind began at the Harrison Park mesonet station between 0530 and 0600 PST and ended between 1045 and 1100 PST on the 17th. During that time, a peak gust of 67 mph was measured between 0940 and 0950 PST. There were also several other gusts above 60 mph measured there that day.

Heavy rain of approximately 2.5 inches within 3-4 hours at Lytle Creek resulted in the creek running near bank-full. Upstream, the creek was 2-3 feet deep and 25 feet wide. The rise in the creek resulted in the partial wash-out of a dirt road leading to the Green Mountain Ranch Resort.

High winds began at the Burns Canyon RAWS between 0851 and 0951 PST and ended between 1651 and 1751 PST on the 17th. During that time, several gusts over 60 mph were recorded including a peak gust of 69 mph measured between 0951 and 1051 PST.
Heavy rain caused mud and rocks to cover part of Highway 74 near Ribbonwood Drive in Mountain Center.
Heavy rain caused a rock slide across Sunrise Highway (S1) near mile marker 18.
Several rock and mud slides on Highway 18 between Lake Gregory and Running Springs due to heavy rain throughout the afternoon and evening.

High winds began at the Burns Canyon RAWS between 2351 PST on the 17th and 0051 PST on the 18th and ended between 0251 and 0351 on the 18th. During that time,  a peak gust of 71 mph measured between 2351 and 0051 PST. Several gusts over 60 mph were also recorded that night along with sustained winds between 44 and 49 mph.||At the other end of the Morongo Valley in Beaumont (Riverside County), a large traffic sign was blown into the fast lane on west-bound Highway 60 near the summit.

Snowfall totals from late-night on the 17th through the 18th include: Arrowbear with 18 to 24 inches, Big Bear with 15 inches, Wrightwood with 7 to 13 inches, Onyx Summit with 11.5 inches, 9 to 10 inches at Forest Falls, Snow Summit and Bear Mountain ski resorts with 28 to 30 inches, and Mount Baldy/Mountain High ski resorts with 22 inches. Chains were required in all areas. Several periods of blizzard conditions and dense fog were reported as well.

Snowfall totals for the 18th include: Pine Cove with 11 inches, Idyllwild with 10 inches and traces of snow sticking down to 1500 feet in Hemet and up to 3 inches at 2600 feet in Cherry Valley. The Palm Springs Aerial Tramway received 24 inches of snow, which closed the tram for most of the day on the 18th, reopening the morning of the 19th. |Highway 74 was closed at Highway 371 on the evening of the 18th between Pinyon Pines and Anza due to heavy snow and blizzard conditions. Chains were required between San Jacinto and the Coachella Valley and in several other mountain locations. Several traffic collisions occurred as well due to cars sliding around on the icy and snowy roads.
Mission Beach lifeguards reported 8 foot surf for most of the day on the 18th, subsiding below 6 feet by the morning of the 19th.
Huntington Beach lifeguards reported 10-12 foot surf for most of the day on the 18th, subsiding below 6 feet by the morning of the 19th.

High winds began at the Burns Canyon RAWS between 2151 and 2251 PST on teh 24th and ended between 1400 and 1500 PST on the 25th. During this time, several gusts over 60 mph were recorded, including the peak gust of 75 mph measured between 1151 and 1251 PST on the 25th.

Snowfall totals from the Saturday 18th through the afternoon of the 19th include: Mt. Laguna with 14 inches, Cuyamaca State Park with 5+ inches (2-foot drifts), Julian with 12 inches, Warner Springs with 5 inches and Wynola with 4 inches. Strong winds caused many areas of blowing snow, blizzard conditions with very low visibility and large snow drifts. Many slide-outs and accidents occurred on area roadways including Highways 78 and 79. |Interstate 8 was closed in both directions from East Willows Road in Alpine to Ocotillo due to heavy snow, graupel and 100 foot visibility. The highway was closed around 0130 PST on the 19th and reopened at 0800 PST that morning. |The Boulevard West mesonet station reported sustained winds near 40 mph for several hours on the 18th between about 1600 and 1900 PST.

Huntington Beach Lifeguards reported average surf of 8 feet with sets of 10-12 feet. Newport Beach lifeguards reported 6 foot surf with sets to 8 feet. San Clemente lifeguards reported surf of 5-7 feet. Moderate to severe beach erosion also occurred near San Clemente producing a very steep sand escarpment and exposed cobblestones. |Minor coastal flooding also occurred near Seal Beach around the time of high tide on the evening of the 1st. Surf heights of 15 feet were reported then as well. The boardwalk was under 2.5 feet of water at times. Residents reported that water came within a foot of over-topping sand bags placed to protect dwellings.
Mission Beach lifeguards reported surf heights of 6 to 8 feet with sets of 10-12 feet at times. Ocean Beach lifeguards reported 8 foot surf with sets to 12 feet.

Winds from a thunderstorm in the Hemet area ripped off a 30-foot section of a mobile home carport awning and damaged part of the roof near the intersection of Gilbert and Chambers Streets. A piece of the awning landed roughly 150 yards away at Diamond Valley Middle School. A tree at the school was also damaged. Based on spotter reports and a survey of the area along with radar data, it was determined to be a possible gustnado with estimated gusts to 65 mph. Small debris was|found near McSweeny Elementary School. The extent of damage is unknown, but time was based on another report of a thunderstorm in the area.

High winds began at the Whitewater RAWS between 2150 and 2250 PST on the 10th and ended around 0050 PST on the 11th. During that time, sustained winds of 35-40 mph occurred with a peak gust of 64 mph between 2250 and 2350 PST on the 10th. ||The Sky Valley mesonet station also recorded sustained winds of 42-46 mph with a peak gust of 63 mph between 2144 and 2344 PST on the 10th.

High winds began at the Burns Canyon RAWS between 1051 and 1151 PST and ended between 1541 and1351 PST on the 13th. During that time, sustained winds were between 31 and 53 mph and gusts were consistently above 60 mph. A peak gust of 83 mph was measured between 1251 and 1351 PST with a secondary peak gust of 77 mph measured during the following hour.

A spotter 4 miles ESE of Yorba Linda reported trees down, bark peeled off trees and post office drop boxed flipped near Weir Canyon and the 91 freeway.||High winds were reported at the Fremont Canyon RAWS between 1251 and 1351 PST on the 13th with a peak gust of 63 mph.||The area was surveyed for possible tornado damage but only evidence of straight line wind was observed.

events.event_narrative: NBC San Diego reported a lightning strike to the Unified Port of San Diego building, resulting in part of the roof getting peeled back. The strike also took out power to the building, but no injuries were reported.
A 30-foot section of Slover Boulevard was covered with 5 inches of water due to heavy rain from a passing thunderstorm.
Heavy snowfall totals for the 13th-14th include 16 inches at Arrowbear Lake, 14 inches at Snow Summit, Onyx Summit and Forest Falls, and 10 inches at Wrightwood and Big Bear City.
Heavy snowfall totals for the 13th-14th include 12 inches at Mt. San Jacinto, 10 inches  in Idyllwild and 6 inches in Pine Cove.

High winds began at the Sky Valley mesonet station between 1445 and 1545 PST on the 23rd and occurred off and on through on the 26th. Several gusts over 58 mph were recorded between 1500 PST on the 23rd through 0000 PST on the 24th. A peak gust of 69 mph was measured between 2244 and 2344 PST on the 23rd. High winds occurred again late evening on the 25th with a peak gust of 73 mph around 2200 PST and early afternoon on the 26th with a peak gust of 66 mph around 1300 PST.||High winds also occurred at the Whitewater RAWS with a peak gust of 60 mph occurring between 2250 and 2350 PST on the 23rd as well as another gust to 59 mph between 0750 and 0850 PST on the 25th.

High winds occurred at the Sky Valley mesonet station from 2230 PST on the 1st through 0200 PST on the 2nd with a peak gust of 73 mph measured around 0000 PST on the 2nd. The station also recorded high winds between 1444 and 1800 PST on the 3rd with a peak gust of 62 mph. During these times, there were several instances of sustained winds over 40 mph. Sporadic gusts 55-60 mph occurred through around 1700 PST on the 4th. ||High winds occurred at the Whitewater RAWS between approximately 0100 and 0400 PST on the 2nd with a peak gust of 65 mph. Sustained winds 35-40 mph with gusts in the 50s continued through approximately 0200 PST on the 3rd.

Winds first gusted over 45 mph at the Sky Valley mesonet around 1600 PST on the 17th and continued through 1200 PST on the 18th. The peak gust of 74 mph occurred around 0000 PST on the 18th. ||Winds first gusted over 45 mph at the Whitewater RAWS around 1800 PST on the 17th and continued through 0800 PST on the 18th. The peak gust of 63 mph occurred around 2200 PST on the 17th.||Winds first gusted over 45 mph at the Edom Hill mesonet around 1800 PST on the 17th and continued through 0900 PST on the 18th. The peak gust of 55 mph occurred around 0800 PST on the 18th.
Winds first gusted over 45 mph at the Burns Canyon RAWS around 1300 PST on the 17th and continued through 0100 PST on the 18th. The peak gust of 76 mph occurred around 2100 PST on the 17th.

Winds first gusted over 45 mph at the Sky Valley mesonet station around 0930 PST on the 23rd and continued through around 2200 PST that day. The peak gust of 62+ mph occurred around 1800 PST. Winds again gusted over 50 mph from 0530 through 1800 PST on the 25th. During this time, several gusts over 65 mph were recorded including a peak gust of 75 mph around 0200 PST on the 25th. ||Winds first gusted over 45 mph at the Whitewater RAWS around 1800 PST on the 22nd and continued through the 24th. Several gusts 45-55 mph were recorded including a few gusts to 60 mph. Winds again gusted over 50 mph from 2300 on the 24th through 1200 PST on the 25th. During this time, several gusts over 50 mph were recorded including a peak gust of 62 mph around 1000 PST on the 25th.

An 86 year old male was hospitalized for a heat-related illness on May 12th near Mecca in the Salton Sea desert area of the Coachella Valley. The Riverside County Health Department confirmed his death on May 18 as heat-related. No mental issues were noted.

High winds occurred at the Sky Valley mesonet station between 1530 PST on the 4th and 0430 PST on the 5th. During this time, several gusts over 60 mph were measured including a peak gust of 74 mph around 1600 PST on the 4th. There were two periods of high winds, one from 1530 to 1900 PST on the 4th and the other from 0200-0430 PST on the 5th.||Peak wind gusts of 57 and 59 mph were also measured at the Edom Hill mesonet and the Whitewater RAWS, respectively, during this period.

High winds occurred at the Sky Valley mesonet between 1900 PST on the 8th and 2200 PST on the 9th. During this time, several gusts over 60 mph were recorded including a peak gust of 65 mph measured around 1900 PST on the 9th. ||During this time, the Edom Hill mesonet also recorded a peak gust of 58 mph around 2100 PST on the 9th.

Winds first gusted over 58 mph at the Whitewater RAWS between 1250 and 0150 PST on the 19th and stayed elevated through around 1700 PST the same day. During that time several gusts over 60 mph were measured, including a peak gust of 69 mph recorded between 0450 and 0550 PST on the 19th. ||A peak wind gust of 59 mph was also recorded at the Edom Hill mesonet station on this day around 0400 PST.
High winds occurred at the Burns Canyon RAWS between 0300 and 0600 PST on the 19th. During this time, a peak gust of 59 mph was measured between 0451 and 0551 PST.
