events.event_narrative: CHP reported large rocks as well as 4 to 6 inches of water across State Route 18 at Cactus Road.|A nearby rain gauge at Baldwin lake recorded 0.92 inches in one hour between 0400 and 0500 PST.
Marble to nickel sized hail reported from an intense thunderstorm near Ocotillo Wells. Heavy rain and a lot of cloud to ground lightning was also observed.
La Posta road flooded near Interstate 8. A nearby mesonet station recorded 1.66 inches of rain in the past hour from 1300 to 1400 PST.

Dillon Road and Fargo Canyon Road flooded due to heavy rain from a thunderstorm.||A local newspaper reported a wall of water flowing through a Thousand Palms Neighborhood causing minor flooding to several homes. ||Several roads were closed due to flooding in the Coachella Valley including: Box Canyon Road from mecca to Interstate 10, Highway 177 from Interstate 10 to Highway 62, and Highway 62 from Vidal Junction to Highway 177.

Heavy rain caused a 15-foot wall of water to rush through a slot canyon near the Silent Caves and Split Mountain Road. Two hikers, a man and his son, were caught in the canyon, but were able to get to higher ground in the caves and were unharmed. Their pickup truck, however, was washed 1.5 miles down the canyon and destroyed.
The Running Springs mesonet station recorded 2.69 inches of rain, the bulk of which fell between 1254 and 1354 PST.
California Highway Patrol reports roadway flooding along State Route 18 at the junction with Sheep Creek.

A thunderstorm with heavy rain and one-half inch hail began around 1230 PST. Although the spotter only measured 0.68 inches in approximately 2 hours, Swartout Creek is overflowing its banks. Cars are turning around due to flooded roadways, not wanting to cross.

Very heavy rainfall in the Big Bear area began around 1045 PST, resulting in minor street flooding in Big Bear City, as well as flash flooding along Highway 38 at mile marker 19. Cal Trans and CHP closed Highway 38 at this point due to a stream of water rushing down the road with embedded boulders. |A nearby spotter measured rainfall of 0.16 inches in 10 minutes and 0.95 inches in one hour, along with pea sized hail.

Heavy thunderstorm moving north toward Highway 94 and Interstate 8 with frequent lightning. Lightning hit the spotter's well in her yard.|Heavy rain also caused minor flooding on Buckman Springs Road.

Flooding observed on HIghway 395 as well as along Highway 18 and Phelan Road. Water was flowing on streets on both sides. Up to 4 inches of water was flowing at the intersection of Highway 395 and Mojave Road, with up to 8 inches of standing water at dips in the roads.

The Temescal RAWS near Lake Elsinore measured a wind gust of 88 mph between 1432 and 1532 PST, associated with a nearby warned thunderstorm. ||Winds were estimated at 60-65 mph from a microburst around 20 yards wide that caused damage in a residential neighborhood in northeast Temecula. It descended in a backyard and blew down the fences on the north and south ends of the yard. The fences were blown outward from the yard, indicative of a downward and outward thrust of winds.||Several large branches were broken and a few small trees downed in Trilogy at the Glen Ivy Resort and Spa. Estimated winds from the damage was 60 mph as determined by an NWS employee.

Rich Thompson, the IMET at the Chihuahua Fire heard reports of flooding on a few roads in and around the fire on the fire radios. A few crews were stranded temporarily, but no one was injured. He estimates approximately 0.26 to 0.50 inches of rain in less than one hour at the base camp and up to one inch in one hour over the fire itself.
The SDGE East Warners sensor recorded a 58 mph gust during a thunderstorm. A spotter also reported marble to penny sized hail (0.75 inch) 2 to 3 miles east of the San Felipe Road turnoff of SR 79.
CHP closed San Felipe Road (S2) between mile markers 2 and 3 due to mud and water that is 3 feet deep.

A land spout tornado was associated with and southwest of the parent (non-supercell) thunderstorm that was over Nuevo, on the east side of Perris. The land spout appeared to be over the fields just east of or near Interstate 215. Separate wind damage from the parent thunderstorm was observed to the northeast over Nuevo on Menifee Road. |There was no apparent damage from the land spout itself. A spotter also sent in video of the land spout.

On the west side of Perris, on Olive and Ellis Streets and just north of Highway 74, several small and large tree limbs down. Two power poles were broken by wind but remained leaning on Ellis Street just north of Highway 74. One rural street in that area was closed due to water about 12 inches deep. Estimated wind gusts were 50-55 mph for just this area. This damage was determined to be associated with a wet microburst from the severe storm in the area.

A severe thunderstorm caused significant straight-line wind damage from a wet microburst on the east side of Perris on Nuevo Road near Menifee Road. Several power poles were snapped completely and fell over like dominoes. Several vehicles were trapped in between the downed poles, though no one was injured. Law enforcement was called in to close off several roads in the area. The wind also tore up some roofing on a few homes in the area. This damage was likely caused by winds from a microburst and not the nearby landspout, though both were the result of the same parent thunderstorm cell.

A funnel cloud was observed just south of Perris from approximately 1525 to 1535 PST on the 12th. The funnel was observed by a spotter located near Albert Hill, north of Lake Elsinore as the severe thunderstorm moved east along Highway 74. The funnel was not determined to be associated with the landspout east of Perris.

A spotter heard on a police scanner that a 3-foot wall of water  came down near forest Falls and Angelus Oaks. Police evacuated people that were down at the bottom of the Santa Ana River/Mill Creek. The flooding was estimated to have occurred between 1330 and 1400 PST.

Rob Balfour reported strong winds at the Buck Fire base camp at Diamond Lake, with estimated max gusts of 60 mph. The winds destroyed two large tents, several camping tents and some awnings. A few port-a-potties overturned as well.

CHP is reporting a mud, dirt and rock slide along Deerhorn Valley Road. They also reported that heavy rain was causing flooding near Otay Lakes Road and that the bridge near the fire station was about to be washed out. No word was received if it actually did wash out.
Spotter SBD625 reported debris flows through canyons near Hesperia about one foot deep and 10 feet wide.

A spotter reported 2 to 3 inches of water flowing along part of Route 78 and County Road S3 (San Felipe Road). |A Borrego County Road Maintenance crew also reported water and debris flowing across San Felipe Road just north of Highway 78 between mile markers 12 and 14.
California Highway Patrol reported roadway flooding along county highway 22 (Borrego Salton Sea Way).
A spotter estimated 2 to 3 feet of water flowing across Highway 79 a mile west of Chihuahua Valley Road. In addition, trees and branches 3 to 5 inches in diameter were floating across the roadway.

Spotter reported 0.75 inches of rain in 20 minutes, leading to urban flooding near the intersection of Central and Waalew in Apple Valley with an estimated 6 inches of water in the low sections of roadways. |Another spotter in nearby Lucerne Valley reported 1 to 2 inches of standing water along Highway 247 on the north side of town.

Major flash flooding in Cathedral City with 1 to 2 feet of rapidly moving water, closing several roads including East Palm Canyon (Highway 111) and Araby Drive. Water forced mud and debris into several businesses in town, causing significant damage.
Spotter RIV230 reported heavy rain and lightning. Lightning struck a nearby palm tree, which then burst into flames. Winds also gusted to 25 mph.

The March AFB ASOS recorded a peak gust of 61 mph at 1347 PST. One of the planes at the museum was turned 180 degrees by the severe winds.||An Atmospheric Science teacher at nearby UC Riverside estimated wind gusts to 60 mph from a passing thunderstorm going through campus around the same time.
Heavy rain resulted in a debris flow on Highway 78 near Shelter Valley and Lizard Creek. A 2-foot boulder had to be removed from the roadway and one lane of the highway was closed.

Heavy rain caused flash flooding which closed San Timoteo Canyon Road. Six vehicles were stuck in the water. One person was rescued from a vehicle surrounded by a mud flow on San Timoteo Canyon Road and Live Oak Canyon Road. Rainfall of 1.53 inches fell in one hour at March AFB in Riverside. |Eastbound Highway 60 was closed at Redlands Boulevard due to flooding as well. |Mud and water also inundated a few homes in the Moreno Valley area.|At least 1 swift water rescue needed to be performed, including the one at Oliver Street and Cactus Avenue in Moreno Valley. Firefighters had to rescue persons trapped in their vehicle with water reported up to the windows.

Heavy rain from thunderstorms just north of Victorville resulted in flooding on National Trails Highway at Lynhaven Lane and a swift water rescue of a van caught in 4 feet of moving water. Barbosa Road was also washed out.
A spotter reported street flooding with water up to the curbs in some places at the north end of Lake Elsinore near Albert Hill.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE

events.event_narrative: Several mudslides were reported in the Forest Falls area, the first of which was reported at Valley of the Falls Drive and Lilac Road with mud over the roadway. Numerous side streets are also covered in mud, with up to 5 feet of mud and debris in Mill Creek. No rescues or injuries but people are stuck in their cars and houses because of mud in the roads. The Yucaipa Ridge rain gauge (owned San Bernardino County Flood Control and just south of Forest Falls) reported massive rainfall of 5.36 inches in 1 hour and 45 minutes, between 1200 and 1347 PST. A short time later, the Mill Creek tributary, Rattlesnake Creek, was reported at bank-full. A spotter sent in a video of the water and debris flow in the normally dry creek, which was up to the bridge at one time.
Spotter SDG437 reported mud and debris on the road at Japatul Valley and Lyons Roads as a result of a stationary and heavy thunderstorm over the area.

Spotter 625 reported 6 to 8 inches of water on the roadway near Bear Valley and Amethyst with the roadway completely covered with debris and water. There was also water flowing rapidly across the roadway approximately 1 to 2 feet deep, not allowing cars to pass. The same spotter also reported that the roadway at Corwin and Waalew Roads was covered with debris but still passable. The debris consisted of mostly dirt and rocks with an estimated 5 inches of water flow. A driver was stuck in widespread urban flooding at Topaz and Luna Roads in Victorville. Water was flowing very strong along Arrowhead Road at the Victorville Golf Course, resulting in a water rescue. Another spotter reported 2 to 4 inches of water over the intersection of Highway 395 and Highway 18, containing a lot of debris and stranding a few cars.
Four inches of water flowing over highway S2 near highway 78 in an area known as Scissors Crossing. Road remains passable.

A land spout was observed at 1330 PST along interstate 215 and highway 74 in Perris. No funnel was observed at the cloud base, and the land spout remained nearly stationary. Pictures and a video were submitted by spotters.
An NWS employee reported 3 to 5 inches of water flowing across the intersection of highway 74 and Lincoln in Lake Elsinore.
NWS employee reported 2 to 3 inch thick tree limbs down due to thunderstorms in Lake Elsinore around 1400 PST. Wind gust estimated around 55 MPH.

Law Enforcement reported an oak tree blown down across Lilac Rd near the intersection of San Luis Rey Drive. A newspaper article reported additional trees blown down across Lilac Road near the intersection of Couser Canyon Road. ||A NWS employee reported three large pine trees downed by wind along Highway 76 south of Palomar Mountain. The largest of the uprooted pine trees was 18 to 20 inches in diameter, and healthy. A weather spotter estimated a 40 MPH wind gust in the area. The SDGE weather station at Cuca Ranch reported a wind gust of 42 MPH just before 1630 PST.

Wind gusts at the Thermal ASOS gusted over 45 mph between 1916 and 1944 PST with a peak gust of 61 mph at 1928 PST. The ASOS reported visibility between three-quarters of a mile and 3 miles in blowing dust during that time frame.

Strong winds and low visibility in blowing dust forced several vehicles to pull over on Highway 86 in Mecca. The Department of Highways reported visibility of three-quarters of a mile at 1925 PST near Mecca. The ASOS reported visibility between three-quarters of a mile and 3 miles during that time frame. The Palm Springs ASOS also reported visibility between one-quarter and one-half mile with winds gusting to 47 mph between 1948 and 2053 PST. A spotter in Cathedral City also reported visibility down to one-eighth of a mile in blowing dust with wind gusts to 36 mph.

The SDGE station at Borrego Springs measured sustained winds of 34 mph with gusts to 60 mph at 1930 PST. Law enforcement reported visibility of less than one-sixteenth of a mile (300 feet) in blowing dust during that time.

A spotter reported four inches of water on Mountain Avenue in the city of San Jacinto near Hemet. The Riverside County sheriff closed the roadway. |A mesonet station in the Valle Vista/Hemet area recorded a one-hour rainfall amount of 0.81 inches.

A heavy downpour resulted in standing water on Interstate 8 between Boulevard and Inkopah, as well as along portions of Highways 80 and 94 in that area. |Small hail of one-quarter of an inch or less and reduced visibility in heavy rain also occurred with this storm.|The Border Patrol station in Boulevard suffered damages from the heavy rain as well when mud was forced through the doors into the garage.|Between 1050 and 1250 PST, the Boulevard mesonet station recorded 0.71 inches of rain.

Mill Creek in Forest Falls was running 100 feet wide  at one point with significant debris flowing with it. Police evacuated some people in the town of Forest Falls.|The Yucaipa Ridge mesonet station recorded approximately 3 inches of rain between 1130 and 1230 PST. The Heart Bar mesonet station, in the mountains upstream of Mill creek, recorded 2.84 inches of rain during that same hour.

The mesonet station of Eastern Tanks at La Jolla Amago recorded 1.46 inches of rain between 1311 and 1400 PST.|The mesonet station at the La Jolla Indian Reservation recorded 1.54 inches of rain between 1317 and 1405 PST.

A combination of debris and 6 inches of water flowing across National Trails Highway at Barbosa Road caused several vehicles to get stuck, resulting in CHP closing the highway for approximately 2 hours. |National Trails Highway was also closed at Hodge Road due to flooding.
Highway 76 east of Rincon was closed for one hour from 1430 to 1530 PST due to a flash flooding-induced debris flow 12-18 inches deep on the roadway.
Spotter SDG447 reported 0.84 inches of rain between 1430 and 1500 PST, which resulted in flooded roadways in the San Diego Country Estates area.
The ALERT rain gauge at Kent Sea Farms recorded 5.51 inches of rain in 24 hours, 4.18 inches of which was in the past 12 hours. The vast majority of the rain fell between 0000 and 0700 PST.

There were 11 heat-related injuries requiring hospitalization  between 0800 and 1000 PST at a 5K run in Balboa Park. Temperatures ranged between 92 and 99 degrees during that time. The ages of the injured ranged from 15 to 17 years old.
A 45 year old woman apparently suffered heat exhaustion and was airlifted from a hiking trail near Lake Hodges in Rancho Bernardo. Temperatures in the area were in the 90s at the time.

High temperatures resulted in heat exhaustion and dehydration of 8 runners participating in a cross country track meet at Fairview Park. Six were transported to hospitals; two were treated locally and released. Approximate ages of the injured were 17 to 20.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE

events.event_narrative: A stationary thunderstorm brought persistent heavy rain in Mecca between 0200 and 0800 PST, resulting in flash flooding of two mobile home parks. Approximately 15 to 20 mobile homes in the Duroville and Saint Anthony's mobile home parks were damaged. The American Red Cross set up an evacuation center at the Mecca Family and Farm Workers Services Facility for the approximately 1500 residents affected. A boil water message was issued for these locations as well. Saul Martinez Elementary School also reported water damage to 15 classrooms, the teachers' lounge and the administration building with 2 to 3 inches of water.

Heavy rain resulted in flooding along 66th Avenue east of Johnson Avenue. County Road Department was dispatched to barricade the roads. |A short distance upstream, the Thermal airport measured 1.42 inches of rain between 0019 and 0316 PST, over an inch of which fell between 0019 and 0236 PST.

Heavy rain resulted in flooding along State Highway 111, just east of the intersection with Colfax Street. The roadway there was covered with 3 feet of water. |A mesonet station, at Kent Sea Farms, just west of this location recorded 3.38 inches of rain between 0050 and 0419 PST.

Fire department and rescue officials in Riverside County reported residential flooding of approximately 4 homes on the 91000 block of 5th Street in Mecca due to heavy downpours. No injuries reported and depth of flood waters was unknown.

events.cz_name: SAN MATEO PT TO MEXICAN BDR OUT 30NM
events.event_narrative: A spotter reported a waterspout about 200 yards off the coast near the Carlsbad power plant. The waterspout was dissipating.

events.cz_name: SAN MATEO PT TO MEXICAN BDR OUT 30NM
events.event_narrative: Numerous pilot reports received of waterspouts off the coast in the vicinity of North Island and Imperial Beach.

A warehouse roof collapsed on the 11000 block of Mulberry Avenue in Fontana due to accumulation of over 1 foot of water. Drains were plugged allowing the water to accumulate. An alert gauge approximately 2 miles north of the location reported 1.02 inches of rain in 25 minutes between 1545 and 1610 PST.

Several streets were flooded due to heavy rain, stranding motorists in their vehicles. Streets affected included Wineville Avenue, Limonite Avenue, 50th Street, Ben Nevis Blvc, Quartz Canyon Road, Fircrest Lane, Agate Street, Mission Blvd, Hastings Blvd, Fleming Street, Glen Street and Villa Woods Drive in Jurupa Valley. No one was injured.

Two homes on Crestview Drive between Mount Shasta and Mount Rushmore Drives sustained damage to the insides of the residences. Eight additional homes on the block sustained damage on the external portion. No injuries and no residents displaced.
Street flooding occurred in Colton Valley between Hermosa and Grand Roads. Roadways were closed in that area.
City of San Diego reported the on ramp for highway 52 and from I -15 was closed in the morning for an hour due to flooded streets and multiple accidents.

The Sill Hill SDGE site, just northwest of Cuyamaca Peak, reported sustained winds of 40 to 46 mph with frequent gusts of 58 mph or greater between 0050 and 0420 PST. The peak gust of 66 mph occurred around 0320 PST.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: High winds began at the Highland Springs RAWS between 0116 and 0216 PST and ended between 0716 and 0816 PST on the 26th. During that time, winds were sustained 38 to 43 mph and gusting above 58 mph. The peak gust of 64 mph was measured between 0216 and 0316 PST.

High winds began at the Fremont Canyon RAWS between 0251 and 0351 PST and ended between 0751 and 0851 PST on the 26th. During that time, winds were sustained 38 to 46 mph with several gusts above 58 mph. The peak gust of 61 mph was measured twice between 0251 and 0451 PST.

High winds began at the Mt. Laguna North mesonet station between 0100 and 0200 PST on the 8th and ended between 0600 and 0700 PST the same day. During this time, winds were sustained 40-60 mph with several gusts over 65 mph. The peak gust of 70 mph was recorded between 0400 and 0500 PST. ||The Volcan Mountain SDGE mesonet station reported sustained winds above 40 mph between 0430 and 0600 PST. A peak gust of 60 mph was recorded between 0500 and 0510 PST.

High winds began at the Whitewater RAWS between 1150 and 1250 PST on the 8th and ended between 0650 and 0750 PST the same day. During this time, winds were sustained 35-48 mph with gusts over 59-80 mph. The peak gust of 80 mph was recorded between 0450 and 0550 PST.||The Sky Valley mesonet station reported sustained winds of 44 mph with gusts to 66 mph between 0443 and 0553 PST.

High winds began at the Mt. Laguna North mesonet station between 0200 and 0300 PST on the 9th and ended between 1200 and 1300 PST the same day. During this time, winds were sustained 55-68 mph with gusts over 67-76 mph. The peak gust of 76 mph was recorded between 0700 and 0800 PST.||High winds began at the Volcan Mountain mesonet station between 0130 and 0140 PST on the 9th and ended between 1420 and 1430 PST the same day. During this time, winds were sustained over 40 mph with frequent gusts 57-70 mph. The peak gust of 70 mph was recorded between 0720 and 0730 PST.||High winds began at the Harrison Park mesonet station between 0320 and 0330 PST on the 9th and ended between 0500 and 1730 PST the same day. During this time, winds were sustained 41-46 mph. The peak gust of 60 mph was recorded twice between 0440 and 0500 PST.

High winds began at the Sky Valley mesonet station between 0543 and 0643 PST on the 9th and ended between 0943 and 1043 PST the same day. During this time, winds were sustained 32-56 mph with gusts 56-79 mph. The peak gust of 79 mph was recorded between 0743 and 0843 PST. Another gust to 61 mph was measured later in the afternoon between 1443 and 1543 PST.||High winds began at the Whitewater RAWS between 0450 and 0550 PST on the 9th and ended between 1050 and 1150 PST the same day. During this time, winds were sustained 31-41 mph with gusts over 58-61 mph. The peak gust of 61 mph was recorded between 0650 and 0750 PST.
CHP reported boulders the size of beer kegs across both lanes of state route 18 near Upper Waterman Canyon.

Fullerton Airport ASOS reported one-quarter mile visibility from 0253 to 0944 PST. John Wayne Airport ASOS reported one-quarter mile visibility from 0142 to 0900 PST. CHP reported 100 foot visibility on Marine Way near Irvine.
Brown Field ASOS reported one-quarter mile visibility from 1253 to 0818 PST. Montgomery Field ASOS reported one-quarter mile visibility from 0253 to 0853 PST.
John Wayne Airport ASOS reported visibility of one-quarter mile from 0318 to 0949 PST. Fullerton Airport ASOS reported visibility of one-quarter mile or less from 0253 to 0927 PST.

Carlsbad-Palomar Airport ASOS reported visibility of one-quarter mile or less from 2141 PST on the 24th to 1000 PST on the 25th. Brown Field ASOS reported visibility of one-quarter mile or less from 2053 PST on the 24th to 0921 PST on the 25th, except between 0123 and 0153 when the visibility briefly improved. Miramar Airport ASOS reported visibility of one-quarter mile or less from 2355 PST on the 24th to 0855 PST on the 25th, down to one-sixteenth of a mile between 0055 and 0736 PST on the 25th. Montgomery Field ASOS reported visibility of one-quarter mile or less from 1253 to 0838 PST on the 25th. A spotter in Allied Gardens reported visibility less than one-quarter mile around 0212 PST.
Huntington Beach lifeguards reported surf up to 10 feet this day.

Lifeguards at Solana Beach reported surf of 7 feet with max sets to 10 feet. An NWS employee reported surf of 6 to 8 feet with occasional 12 foot sets at Sunset Cliffs. Surfline.com reported surf of 5 to 7 feet with occasional sets to 9 feet at Blacks Beach.

San Diego City lifeguards reported the Ocean Beach Pier was closed at 0830 PST on the 1st due to high surf. The Surfline web site reported 6 to 8 foot surf with occasional sets to 10 feet at Ocean Beach. Surfline also reported 5 to 8 foot surf with sets to 9 feet at Cardiff, Del Mar, Imperial Beach and Pacific Beach during this time. Surfline reported 8 foot surf with occasional sets to 13 feet at Sunset Cliffs. Some minor beach erosion occurred at Imperial Beach as well. Beach erosion was significant according to lifeguards after the recent sand replacement project completed in October. This type of project only occurs every 5 to 10 years and is important for beaches.
Huntington Beach lifeguards reported surf of 7 to 8 feet.

Media reports road closures and stalled cars at the intersection of Midway and Rosecrans. At least 5 motorists were trapped in their vehicles and had to be rescued by the lifeguard water rescue team. Roadway flooding was also reported along Sports Arena and West Mission Bay Drive, as well as northbound Interstate 5 and Garnet, where one vehicle was stuck in water. Lifeguard rescue crews retrieved a man trapped in his stalled vehicle along Ingraham just south of Sea World. CHP reported two highway ramp closures due to flooding: the I-5 northbound onramp at 28th Street and the off ramp at SR-163 and Washington. Flooding also reported on northbound I-5 at the Balboa off ramp. Several mudslides including one on south Interstate 5 at Balboa Avenue and another on Regents Road near SR 52, where mud was covering all lanes at 0500 PST.

CHP reported flooding along northbound I-215 at the intersection with SR 259. There was 12 inches of water in the number 3 lane as well as dirt from a nearby construction site running into the lanes. Number 3 lane was closed south of the incident at 5th Street.

An 8-ton boulder, measuring approximately 5 feet by 6 feet, was dislodged by rain-soaked ground and rolled down a hillside, through the garage of a house iin the 13000 block of Vian Road in Poway. The boulder ruptured a water line and a propane line.

Tide levels peaked around 0815 PST on the 13th around 8.4 feet. This was about 3 to 6 inches higher than the predicted astronomical high tide at La Jolla and likely due to the approaching low pressure area (not wind) at the same time of the high tide. This, along with runoff from moderate rain showers resulted in flooding along the Pacific Coast Highway near Huntington Beach. The water was all the way across the the highway at one point and was closed at Warner Avenue near Seal and Sunset Beaches. One foot of water was in some homes on the beach side of the highway. Flooding was also observed along Marcus Avenue in Newport Harbor, as well as at the intersection of Newport Boulevard and 26th Street. Flooding occurred again the next morning of the 14th in similar locations, inundating some homes along Huntington Harbor in Sunset Beach and a couple lanes of the Pacific Coast Highway with up to a foot of water. The tide was slightly lower on the 14th around 8 feet and occurred around 0900 PST.

A spotter in Arrowbear Lake reported 7 to 9 inches of snow. Another spotter reported total of 17 inches in Running Springs near Snow Valley Resort for the 13-14 storm total. Most of this occurred in a 12 hour period. A few branches were reported to be snapped and a couple trees completed toppled in Running Springs by the weight of the wet snow.

A peak gust of 64 mph was measured at the Sky Valley mesonet station around 1300 PST on the 24th. Winds were gusting over 50 mph between 0943 and 1342 PST.|High winds began at the Whitewater RAWS between 0250 and 0350 PST and ended between 0950 and 1050 PST on the 24th. Winds dropped below high wind for a time during this period, but a peak gust of 60 mph was measured between 0850 and 0950 PST.

High winds began at the Volcan Mountain SDGE mesonet between 0850 and 0900 PST on the 24th and ended between 1320 and 1330 PST the same day. During this time winds mostly gusted over 60 mph, with a peak gust of 70 mph between 1110 and 1120 PST.
High winds occurred at the Burns Canyon RAWS between 0651 and 1050 PST on the 24th. During this time, a peak gust of 62 mph was measured between 0651 and 0751 PST.
Winds gusted over 50 mph between 1200 and 1900 PST on the 26th. During this time, peak wind gusts of 59 mph and 64 mph occurred around 1700 and 1800 PST, respectively.
Public reported a funnel cloud over the city of Fallbrook from a thunderstorm nearby.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: A traffic collision involving 4 vehicles occurred on Interstate 15 near the Lake Street exit, north of Lake Elsinore on the 31st. CHP reported dense fog at the time of the accident. Two vehicles were involved in the initial accident and were blocking the #1 lane. Two additional vehicles struck these vehicles.

events.cz_name: SAN MATEO PT TO MEXICAN BDR OUT 30NM
events.event_narrative: A pilot reported a waterspout 19 miles WNW of Oceanside.

National coverage of the Chargers/Raiders football game showed heavy rain and pea sized hail during pre-game warmups and the beginning of the first quarter. The heavy rain resulted in the flooding of a few seating areas in the stadium.

High winds began at the Sill Hill mesonet station around 1830 PST on the 1st and lasted, off and on, until 0800 on the 2nd. During this time, several gusts over 60 mph were recorded, including the peak gust of 64 mph measured between 0720 and 0730 PST on the 2nd.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: High winds occurred at the Highland Springs RAWS between 2000 PST on the 1st and 0200 PST on the 2nd. During this time, a peak gust of 64 mph was recorded between 2316 and 0016 PST.

High winds began at the Volcan Mountain SDGE mesonet between 0800 and 0810 PST on the 10th and ended between 1550 and 1600 PST the same day. During this time, winds gusted above 60 mph almost the entire time. This included a few gusts above 70 mph and the peak gust of 73 mph, which was measured between 1300 and 1310 PST. |High winds also occurred at the Harrison Park mesonet, between 1030 and 1430 PST on the 10th. During this time, sustained winds were around 45 mph with gusts over 60 mph. This included the peak gust of 63 mph, which was measured between 1340 and 1350 PST.

The Sky Valley mesonet station recorded a peak gust of 76 mph around 1542 PST. During this afternoon, the  Thermal Airport ASOS measured a peak gust of 49 mph between 1251 and 1351 PST, with one-quarter mile visibility due to blowing dust.
NBC 7 reported waves flooding streets over Camino del Oro and Avenida de la Playa in La Jolla around 0730 PST, during the time of high tide. High tide that morning was just under 7 and a half feet.

San Bernardino County Skywarn reported 30 broken water lines both inside and outside buildings in the San Bernardino County High Desert and mountains due to freezing overnight temperatures. Another spotter in Lucerne Valley reported 15 to 20 water pipes that were broken or busted due to the freezing temperatures overnight. Lows there were in the low teens.

A wind gust of 65 mph occurred at the Sky Valley mesonet between 0044 and 0142 PST on the 14th and a peak gust of 65 mph between 0830 and 0845 PST. Sustained winds of 42 mph also occurred there around 0242 PST and 43 mph around 0843 PST.

High winds began at the Fremont Canyon RAWS between 0251 and 0351 PST on the 14th and ended between 0551 and 0651 PST the same morning. During this time, sustained winds were 45 to 48 mph with gusts over 60 mph, including the peak gust of 71 mph measured between 0351 and 0451 PST.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: CHP reported phone lines blown down in the vicinity of Highway 91 and West 14th Street. A large highway traffic sign and posts were also blown down along Highway 91 eastbound, just west of Arlington Avenue. Both of these reports were between 0400 and 0500 PST on the 14th. Later in the morning, around 0750 PST, another freeway sign was blown down near the Interstate 215 northbound off ramp at Baseline Street. Around 0930 PST that morning, a big rig trailer overturned on Interstate 15 southbound, near the Interstate 10 east connector.

Dense fog was intermittent at Montgomery Field between 0500 and 1600 PST on the 26th with visibilities of one-quarter mile or less. The lowest visibility was one-eighth of a mile around 1445 PST. Visibility at Lindbergh Field was one-quarter mile at 0725 PST that morning. The low ceilings and visibility resulted in numerous flight delays.

There were two periods of high winds at the Sill Hill SDGE mesonet station. The first was between 2050 and 2110 PST on the 15th, with a peak gust of 62 mph. The second was  between 1240 and 0110 PST pm the 16th, with a peak gust of 66 mph around 0100 PST.|The Lucky Five mesonet station gusted between 40 and 50 mph for several hours that night, but hit a peak gust of 58 mph between 0140 and 0150 PST on the 16th.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: March Air Base in Riverside reported visibility of one-quarter mile or less from 0222 to 0957 PST on the 7th. The lowest visibility reached was one-sixteenth of a mile and occurred from 0658 to 0957 PST.||Riverside ASOS reported visibility of one-quarter mile from 0701 to 0837 PST in dense fog on the 7th. Ontario ASOS also reported one-quarter mile visibility for 15 minutes from 0732 to 0747 PST.

High winds began at the Mt. Laguna North mesonet station between 2300 PST on the 7th and 0000 PST on the 8th and ended between 0100 and 0200 PST on the 8th. During this time, winds gusted to 68 mph between 2303 and 0102 PST on the 8th.|High sustained winds of 40 to 43 mph occurred at the Volcan Mountain mesonet station between 2310 and 0100 PST on the 7th-8th. A peak gust of 59 was measured between 2330 and 2340 PST.

High winds occurred at the Burns Canyon RAWS between 0500 and 0900 PST on the 8th. During this time, sustained winds of 40 mph were recorded at 0451 PST and a peak gust of 59 mph between 0651 and 0751 PST.
Strong winds, along with pea-sized hail damaged a biomedical firm's roof in Sorrento Valley. A 20 by 30 foot section of skylight paneling was torn off from the company's rooftop.
The Sky Valley Mesonet station recorded a peak gust of 71 mph around 1400 PST on the 8th. Occasional wind gusts of 58 mph or higher were recorded between 0300 and 1500 PST that day.

Two-day snowfall totals: 21 inches at Green Valley Lake, 20 inches at Onyx Peak, 18 inches at Snow Summit, 11 inches at Running Springs and 9-10 inches at Wrightwood and Lake Arrowhead. During this storm, a major manhunt was underway for an ex-LAPD officer who was on the run after a killing spree. All major national news outlets were covering the search.
Two-Day snowfall totals: 10 inches at Mt. Laguna, 6-8 inches at Cuyamaca, 8 inches at Palomar, 6 inches at Julian and 5 inches at Ranchita.
Accumulations of pea-sized hail resulted in multiple traffic collisions along Interstate 15 between University and El Cajon Blvd. Southbound Interstate 15 was closed for a few hours.

Two periods of high winds occurred at the Sill Hill SDGE mesonet station. The first occurred between 0130 and 1250 PST on the 15th with a peak gust of 91 mph between 1010 and 1020 PST. The second occurred between 2000 PST on the 15th and 0540 PST on the 16th with a peak gust of 81 mph between 0520 and 0530 PST on the 16th.

The Lucky Five Ranch mesonet station recorded gusts over 55 mph from 0420 to 1350 PST on the 15th with a peak gust of 61 mph between 0420 and 0430 PST. The site recorded a few other gusts 58-59 mph as well. |The Inaja Park mesonet station recorded high winds from 0920 to 1130 PST on the 15th with a peak gust of 63 mph between 0920 and 0930 PST. |The La Posta mesonet station recorded sustained winds 38-44 mph from 0830 to 1320 PST on the 15th with a peak gust of 59 mph between 1000 and 1010 PST. |The Santa Ysabel Ranch mesonet station recorded a peak gust of 59 mph between 1200 and 1210 PST. |The Buckman Springs mesonet station recorded a peak gust of 61 mph between 0110 and 0120 PST. |The Hellhole Canyon mesonet station recorded a peak gust of 61 mph between 0340 and 0350 PST.

A big rig overturned on Highway 111 at Overture Drive, near Windy Point. Northbound lanes were closed for more than two hours for a fuel spill cleanup. A highway department wind gauge 2.2 miles northwest of the accident measured gusts of 38-50 mph around the time of the incident. The truck was reportedly empty.

Big Bear ski resorts reported 16-17 inches of snow. A spotter in Big Bear Lake reported 16 inches of snow. A spotter in Big Bear City reported 11 inches of snow over 12 hours ending 0700 PST on the 20th. A spotter in Running Springs reported 12 inches of snow over the past 14 hours ending 0900 PST on the 20th. A spotter in Lucerne Valley reported 3-4 inches of snow, while another in Crestline reported 12 inches. Forest Falls and Garner Valley came in with 8 inches apiece.

Ten inches of snow was measured at the Crestwood Pass near Interstate 8 over 12 hours ending 0700 PST on the 20th. Temporary closures occurred on Interstate 8 due to snow and accidents. Seven inches of snow was also reported in Julian by a spotter.
Surfline website reported 8 foot surf at Ocean Beach, Mission Beach, Scripps Beach and Imperial Pier on the 20th.

High winds began at the Fremont Canyon RAWS between 0151 and 0251 PST on the 24th and ended around 1400 PST the same day. During this time several gusts over 60 mph were recorded, including the peak gust of 66 mph measured between 0751 and 0851 PST.
High winds occurred at the Sill Hill SDGE mesonet between 0800 and 1000 PST on the 24th. During this time, a peak gust of 60 mph was measured between 0840 and 0850 PST.
California Highway Patrol reported a power line down at the intersection of Twenty-nine Palms Highway and North Indian Canyon Drive, just south of Morongo Valley.

California Highway Patrol reported a tree blown down on two vehicles, a tree limb hanging on power lines and a power outage in the Lake Arrowhead area. Snow Valley ski area had wind hold on all lifts except the lower elevations on Sunday.

The Sill Hill SDGE mesonet station recorded wind gusts of 55 or greater between 0500 and 2000 PST on the 28th. During this time, several gusts of 59 mph or greater were measured, including the peak gust of 65 mph recorded between 0910 and 0920 PST.
Law enforcement reported flash flooding with rocks and mud over Highway S2 in Shelter Valley.
Flooding reported on Split Mountain Road near Highway 78 in Ocotillo Wells. Source unknown.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE

events.event_narrative: High winds began at the Sill Hill mesonet station between 0200 and 0210 PST on the 1st and ended between 1030 and 1040 PST the same day. During this period, winds gusted mostly in the 60s with a peak gust of 68 measured 3 times between 0720 and 0800 PST.

High winds began at the Sky Valley mesonet station between 1422 and 1522 PST on the 3rd, and ended between 2143 and 2243 PST the same day. During this period, a peak gust of 67 mph was measured between 1400 and 1500 PST.
A peak high wind gust at the Volcan Mountain mesonet station measured 58 mph between 1650 and 1700 PST on the 3rd.

In Oceanside, lots of small branches and pots were knocked over and a 12 foot shed was tossed approximately 100 feet, based on where it was located originally and the scrape marks where it landed on the street. At least two vehicles were damaged, one with a side mirror damaged by the shed and another had a large tree limb approximately 4 to 6 inches in diameter that broke the window. At least six screens were knocked off on the windows of the homes. And very unique damage done by pinecones from large trees just to the west which  left large scrape marks on the side of stucco. Based on the damage, winds are estimated to be 45 to 50 mph in the localized three or four block area.|Downed trees were blocking the roadway on Via de Santa Fe and large palm tree branches were in the number 4 lane of southbound Interstate 5 at Harbor Drive according to California Highway Patrol.

A spotter reported several locations of rocks, small vegetation and soil washed into the roadway north of Lake Wolford Road between Lake Wolford Cafe and Valley Center/East Valley Parkway. Law enforcement also reported rocks washed into the roadway on Del Dios Highway at Rancho Drive.

High winds began at the Sky Valley mesonet between 0343 and 0443 PST on the 8th and ended between 1343 and 1443 the same day. During this time, two periods of high winds were observed with a brief lull between. During those high wind periods, peak gusts of 68 and 80 mph were observed, the latter being around 0600 PST. California Highway Patrol reported an overturned big rig along Interstate 10 near Date Palm Drive. There were no injuries, but the number 3 and 4 eastbound lanes were closed for about two hours for the investigation. The Palm Springs airport reported a loss of utility power during this time as well, attributing it to the high winds nearby. A power pole was also downed by winds near Whitewater Wash and Vista Chino in Palm Springs, along with several downed palm trees across the valley. Vista Chino road was closed for a time while crews fixed the pole.

High winds began at the Volcan Mountain mesonet between 0900 and 0910 PST on the 8th and ended between 1500 and 1510 PST the same day. During this time, winds mostly gusted over 60 mph with a peak gust of 72 mph measured between 1200 and 1210 PST.|Between 1200 and 1400 PST, the Harrison Park mesonet also recorded several gusts to 58 mph and a peak gust of 59 mph.

High winds began at the Borrego Springs around 0700 PST on the 8th and ended around 1100 PST that morning. During this time, there were periods of high winds and lull periods. A peak gust of 73 mph was measured around 0840 PST. A spotter reported sustained winds of 53 mph with a gust to 83 mph around 1000 PST. This gust was blamed for downing the major power line running through the town. Several branches were also downed, with at least one road blocked. Another spotter reported a downed power pole and trees, as well as shingles blown off a roof, damaging a car. Visibility reported 2 miles in blowing dust for a time. Blowing sand pitted several vehicle windshields in the area as well, causing some windows to shatter. Significant damage was reported at the Anza-Borrego State Park, with Ranger HQ parking structures damaged, along with three Mongolian ger tents used by campers and 800 square feet of roof from the Stout Paleontology Laboratory.

High winds began at the Ocotillo Wells mesonet around 0700 PST on the 8th and ended around 1000 PST that morning. During this time, several gusts over 60 mph were recorded, including the peak gust of 73 mph, measured between 0815 and 0820 PST. A spotter in the area reported trees down with damage to a few buildings. Power outages also reported from residents at the Desert Ironwoods Resort.
A COOP observer in Johnson Valley reported sustained winds 32-42 mph with gusts as high as 87 mph.

Very windy conditions existed along the Interstate 10 corridor in the Coachella Valley on the evening of the 14th, with blowing dust bringing visibility down to under one-eighth of a mile. KESQ news reported a sand storm impacting the Coachella Music Festival with winds gusting up to 40 mph at the Coachella mesonet. California Highway Patrol reported a large quantity of sand  in the roadway near Vamer Road and Monterey Avenue the following morning. The Desert Sun newspaper reported police closed Gene Autry Trail between Interstate 10 and Via Escuela and Indian Canyon Road from Palm Springs Train Road to Tramway Road due to blowing sand and reduced visibility of less than one-quarter mile. These major roads remained closed until the 16th due to blowing sand and downed trees.

The Sky Valley Mesonet gusted over 58 mph off and on from around 0500 PST on the 14th to around 1000 PST on the 16th. The Whitewater RAWS also reported sustained winds 42-44 mph between 2150 PST on the 15th and 0150 PST on the 16th with gusts 58 to 68 mph.

The Volcan Mountain SDGE mesonet reported a peak gust of 75 mph between 0100 and 0110 PST on the 16th. Sustained winds of 40-50 mph occurred from 2000 PST on the 15th through 0450 PST on the 16th, with gusts above 58 mph from 2200 PST on the 15th through 0400 PST on the 16th. |The Harrison Park SDGE mesonet reported sustained winds 40-48 mph between 2200 PST on the 15th through 0330 PST on the 16th, with gusts 58-61 mph between 0130 and 0310 PST on the 16th. The peak gust was 61 mph on the 16th.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: A mesonet in Anza recorded a 1 minute gust to 58 mph at 1320 PST on the 9th, corresponding to a reported strong dust devil that tracked through a mobile home park in Jurupa Valley, near Riverside, damaging carports, several metal awnings and roofs. At least 6 metal awnings were lifted high in the air, some weighing over 100 pounds. No injuries were reported despite the flying debris. Skies were clear at the time.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE

events.event_narrative: High winds began at the Fremont Canyon RAWS between 0451 and 0551 PST on the 2nd and ended between 0951 and 1051 PST the same day. During this time, winds were sustained 30 to 45 mph with gusts mostly above 60 mph, including the peak gust of 70 mph measured between 0651 and 0751 PST.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Winds gusted 35-40 mph with gusts above 55 mph between 0500 and 1000 PST on the 2nd. During this time, a peak gust of 62 mph was measured between 0816 and 0916 PST.

At the 0700 observation, Huntington Beach reported 6 to 10 feet, Newport Beach reported 10 to 15 feet at the Wedge, and Trestles beach reported 5 to 8 feet. Huntington Beach reported 6 to 10 foot surf at the 1000 observation.

At the 0700 observation, Oceanside Harbor reported 6 to 8 foot surf, San Onofre State Beach reported 5 to 7 feet, Sunset Cliffs reported 4 to 7 feet with occasional 9 foot sets, and Pacific Beach reported 4 to 7 feet.
The El Mirage mesonet station reached a high of 110 degrees.
The Mormon Rock RAWS reached a high of 101 degrees. The Mill Creek RAWS reached a high of 100 degrees.
The Cathedral Canyon RAWS reached a high of 115 degrees. The Indian Wells mesonet reached a high of 122 degrees.
The Cameron RAWS reached a high of 100 degrees. The Buckman Springs mesonet reached a high of 103 degrees. The Campo ASOS reached a high of 102 degrees.
The Ocotillo Wells COOP observer recorded a high temperature of 115 degrees.
The Pinyon RAWS reached a high of 103 degrees.

The Palm Springs ASOS reached a high of 115 degrees. The Kent Sea Farms mesonet reached a high of 116 degrees. The Palm Desert mesonet reached a high of 116 degrees. The Mecca mesonet reached a high of 118 degrees.

Two Borrego Springs mesonets (BORYO and DW1021) reached a high of 118 degrees. Another Borrego Springs mesonet reached a high of 121 degrees. The Ocotillo Wells mesonet at Split Mountain Road reached a high of 116. The Borrego Springs Alert gauge recorded a high of 123 degrees.
The stream gauge at Palm Canyon Creek reported a water rise of 1.5 feet in a normally dry creek bed around 315 PST. This gauge later measured a peak flow of 211 cfs at 1430 PST.
Fire Dispatch for the Mountain Fire reported 1 foot of water crossing Morris Ranch Road near the fire. Dispatch also reported a rockslide and debris flow across Highway 74.

Crews on the Mountain Fire reported 0.5 inches of rain in 30 minutes between 1258 and 1328 PST. A debris flow from the fire moved through a pond, displacing the water and killing the fish. Other crews reported 18 inches of water and mud across Apple Canyon Road near Highway 74.
Around 1315 PST, a spotter reported 6 inches of water flowing across Interstate 8 at the Pine Valley Road exit.

A Cleveland National Forest Battalion Chief reported 6 inches of mud and rocks flowing across Sunrise Highway (S1), just north of Shrine Camp. The Shrine Camp area was recently burned during the Chariot Fire. The nearby Volcan Mountain Alert gauge reported 0.78 inches of rain in 10 minutes and 1.14 inches of rain over 20 minutes.

At 1129 PST, law enforcement reported 2 and a half feet of mud and water washing across Larsen Lane near the cross-section with Dillon road in Sky Valley. At 1350 PST, an 80-ft swath of dirt and rocks was in the roadway, The dirt was 3 feet thick with most rocks bigger than bowling balls. The road was closed due to it being impassable.

Highway 78 was flooded in two locations through Yaqui Pass with many large rocks in the roadway. Thirty vehicles were trapped between the two flooded locations, due to the road being impassable there. A weather service employee observed one of the flows was about 12 inches deep and another was about 6 inches deep.
A Big Bear resident reported that 0.5-inch hail had accumulated up to 1.5 inches deep in her yard. Plants and flowers in the yard were completely shredded by the hail.
The Palm Springs ASOS recorded a high temperature of 118 degrees, which tied the previous record set on the 28th in 1979. The Indio mesonet station also tied their old record at 118, set in 2003.

The Palm Springs and Thermal ASOS stations both recorded a high temperature of 122 degrees, which broke their old records of 121 and 118, respectively, in 1994. The Indio mesonet station set a record high of 121, breaking their old record of 117, set also in 1994.
The Campo COOP station recorded a high temperature of 106 degrees, which broke their previous record of 103, set in 1972.
The Borrego Desert State Park COOP station recorded a high temperature of 120 degrees, which broke their previous record of 118, set in 1973.
The Campo COOP observer recorded a high temperature of 107 degrees, which broke the previous record of 101, set in 2006.

Big Bear City Fire Department responded to three flooded homes within city limits. Other homeowners were able to divert the water from entering their homes. A spotter reported 2 to 3 inches of water running across Big Bear Boulevard near Greenway Drive. A Big Bear City resident reported a gauge total of 2.25 inches of rain.
California Highway Patrol closed Montezuma Valley Road at Mile Marker 14 because debris has made it impassable.

Heavy rain was concentrated west of the Tecate Divide, along and a quarter mile on either side of Interstate 8. The rains were so heavy, they turned the rocky terrain in the distance into hundreds of small waterfalls and turned a local dirt road on an adjacent ranch site into a muddy flow.
Law enforcement reports a hard closure of the intersection of Tyler Street and 64th Street in Mecca, due to roadway flooding. Intersection closed due to roads being impassable.

Heavy rain over the Anza Borrego State Park, including the headwaters of Fish Creek and Vallecito Creek, caused severe flash flooding with debris in those creeks. Flood waters washed 3 vehicles far down the drainage of each of the creeks, destroying the vehicles. The Fish Creek drainage is actually an unmaintained state road, part of the State Park, with free public travel allowed, so this drainage is especially dangerous during heavy rain.

A spotter called to report street flooding near the intersection of Old Woman Springs Road (Highway 247) and Locust Street. Locust Street was impassable with 1 foot of water estimated to be flowing over the road.  California Highway Patrol reported flooding with debris on the road along highway 247 at Midway Avenue.
A land-spout tornado on the west side of the storm near Helendale, was reported to the office twitter account with a photo.
Two and a half miles of Highway 247 required mud and debris removal by heavy equipment. Residual mud was as deep as 4 inches. Water was reported flowing over the roadway.
The USGS stream gage at Palm Canyon Creek reported a 2.7 ft. rise between 1500 and 1600 PST, with an estimated flow of 363 cfs.
Araby Road was closed at Palm Canyon Wash due to moving water and mud covering the roadway.
The intersection of Paisano Road and Cholla Way was washed out and impassable with flash flooding occurring.

Significant water flow on Whitewater storm channel through la quinta was reported by the Coachella Valley Water District. The water was contained in channel, but flowed through some golf courses. Waist deep water was reported along some roadways, stalling and nearly submerging several vehicles. A driver noted that the flooding came on quickly, in about 20-20 minutes.

Widespread flooding was reported in the areas of Indio, Indian Wells and Palm Desert due to very heavy rain. The storm channels in Palm Desert, many of which flow through the middle of golf courses, were running swiftly. Large rocks up to soccer ball size and water up to 2 feet deep covered Fred Waring Drive in Indian Wells, stranding one vehicle. The intersections of Avenues 48 and 49 with Monroe and Madison Streets were both covered with a foot or more of water, stalling at least 3 vehicles.

A spotter reported 1.24 inches of rain fell in 35 minutes near the intersection of Highway 111 and Indian Trail Road in Rancho Mirage, resulting in 1 foot of water in the roadway at the gutters. The Century Theatre at The River in Rancho Mirage also evacuated movie-goers due to flooding.
Water, debris and boulders were flowing across Highway 62 just north of North Indian Canyon Drive. The area flowing across the highway is 40 feet wide and 6 feet deep.

Borrego Springs Valley Road from Rango Way to Tilting T Road, Borrego Springs Road (S-33) from San Pablo to Yaqui Pass, and S-22 (Montezuma grade) were closed all of Sunday night due to debris and flooding. Mobile homes were flooded in the DeAnza Mobile Home Park. A spotter reported 18 inches of water over Highway S-2 at Vallecito Creek. Several low water crossings were also flooded with swiftly moving water over Highway S-22 between Borrego Springs and Ranchita, including Yukie Road. Numerous large boulders blocked the roadway, with other debris and running water in the roadway. Around this time, 3.35 inches of rain fell in two hours near Ranchita.

Significant mud and debris was reported at the Agua Caliente Springs airport...and the Agua Caliente county park. A spotter reported 18 inches of water over highway S-2, near Canebrake. Shortly before, an NWS rain gauge near Agua Caliente Springs recorded 2.05 inches of rain in 30 minutes.

A spotter reported major flooding in dry washes and debris removal required on Highway 18 towards Big Bear at intersection of Camp Rock Road. The water was as deep as 2 feet in places. Another spotter reported water over another spot along Highway 18, estimated to be 50ft wide and more than 2 feet deep, with flow carrying boulders across the road. Up the mountain west of these locations, a spotter recorded a little over one inch of rain in 20 minutes and approximately 3 inches of water over some roadways.

Fire rescue officials reported that portions of Valley of the Falls Drive were closed due to water flowing over the road from Clarks Creek and Prospect Creek. Less than an hour later, fire officials reported that Prospect and Clarks Creeks were out of their banks. The intersection of Valley of the Falls Drive and Canyon Lane was also closed to all vehicles due to a mud slide.

An employee at UC Riverside estimated wind gusts up to 70 mph with very heavy rain and reduced visibility. Nearby, a large tree fell on the Rubidoux Boulevard off-ramp along Highway 60. Several other locations reported branches down, including a large tree that was uprooted and fell on a house along Chapman Street west of Magnolia Avenue.

Law enforcement reported that the 60 freeway was flooded, with 4 or 5 vehicles stuck in flood waters under the Market Street overpass. One motorist reported that the flood waters were moving his vehicle. Lanes 2, 3, and 4 of Highway 91 were flooded, with vehicles flooded out and sliding, including a school bus. Riverside City College cancelled classes due to flooding at the Landis Performing Arts Center and the campus quadrangle. Several other cars were flooded in parking lots near 14th Street, as well as basement flooding at a business there.

California Highway Patrol reported Orange Avenue from Murrieta Road to Evans Road, just northeast of Perris, was completely flooded and vehicles were not able to make it through. A nearby mesonet station recorded 0.69 inches of rain in 20 minutes.

CHP reports flooded roadway and debris including rocks on Highway 243 south of Banning. Northbound traffic was closed. Further up the mountain off of 243, the Silent Valley RV Park had stranded residents due debris flows and flooding.
CHP reported minor roadway flooding on Gavilan Road and Esperanza Drive, west of Perris.

Radar estimates of rainfall were as high as 6 inches, resulting in damage along and east of the LA County boundary. A dirt road in this area was not usable for 18 hours, which stranded a few home owners until San Bernardino County heavy equipment could repair it. The road is very rural, but there was sign warning of torrential rain and runoff. Locals reported that nearby Lake El Mirage, which is normally totally dry, was filled during this event.

The spotter was in Idyllwild traveling on Highway 243 to Pine Cove. There was 2 deep of 0.5 hail and 1-3 of water flowing across Highway243. Broken tree branches were all over the roadway from hail damage. A nearby COOP observer reported that the roads turned white, all covered with accumulating hail.

The USGS stream gauge on Palm Canyon Creek reported a 3.19 ft. rise. The gauge peaked at 1400 PST. Downstream from the gauge, broadcast media reported Araby Drive in Palm Springs was shut down due to a wall of water that passed through the area. CHP reported Golf Club Drive was closed at the wash due to flooding. Media also reported a flash flood and debris flow 2 feet deep and 20 feet wide flowing across Golf Club Drive. Cathedral Canyon Drive was closed at Whitewater Wash due to flooding and debris flows. The public also reported a flash flood and debris flow down Tahquitz Creek through the Tahquitz Creek Golf Resort.
CHP reported water flowing across the roadway along state route 74 E / state route 371 in Mountain Center. The road is impassable.

The Sky Valley mesonet station recorded sustained winds greater than 40 mph from 1030 to 1200 PST. During this time, two gusts of 61 mph were measured between 1030 and 1040 PST. Two gusts of 58 mph were also recorded between 1050 and 1100 PST.

The Barrett RAWS measured a gust of 70 mph between 1350 and 1450 PST from a collapsing nearby thunderstorm. These winds were responsible for one small tree down, as well as branches and debris on Barrett Lake Road.

The Guatay mesonet station reported peak wind gusts of 38 and 44 mph between 1230 and 1250 PST due to a nearby thunderstorm. County representatives reported several trees down blocking roadways in nearby Pine Valley. San Diego Gas and Electric also reported a few power poles down, leading to outages.

The Warners mesonet station reported wind gusts of 52 and 59 mph between 1240 and 1310 PST due to a thunderstorm. Nearby, the Mataguay mesonet station recorded wind gusts of 56 and 58 mph between 1240 and 1300 PST. A san diego county official reported trees down on Valley View and Deer Creek Trail Roads.

California Highway Patrol reported a debris flow on Highway 74 at McCall Park Road. The water cleared out soon after and left behind debris on the road...such as rocks and sticks. The nearby Keenwild mesonet recorded 0.47 inches of rain during this time.

The public reported pea to quarter sized hail near Lake Morena on Facebook. The COOP observer a little further south in Campo reported heavy rain with a thunderstorm and 0.5 inch hail reducing visibility to 1/8 mile. Further north in Pine Valley, the public reported pea to dime size hail and 1 to 2 inches of water flowing over the road.

CHP reported Highway S2 was covered with mud, water and large boulders 3 miles southeast of the SR79 and S2 juncture. The mud was 2+ feet deep in places. A spotter reported on Facebook that he had seen 6-8 inches of water flowing through the same area. The S2 was closed from SR79 to S22. There were multiple reports of vehicles stuck in mud, including a fire truck that was en route to a lightning ignited fire. Pictures were submitted on Facebook. Further down Highway S22, the public reported up to quarter size hail. CHP also reported Borrego Springs Road was closed from San Pablo to Yaqui Pass due to flooding.

A storm spotter reported flooding of roads in Pine Valley with two homeowners shoveling to divert waters from their homes. Further south in Lake Morena, a resident reported minor road flooding at Buckman Springs Road and Lake Morena Dr. His rain gauge measured 0.81 inches of rainfall in 1 hour. The nearby Campo COOP observer reported 0.94 inches of rain in 45 minutes during this time.

A Borrego Springs mesonet station recorded a peak wind gust of 64 mph during a thunderstorm. California Highway Patrol reported power lines down on Borrego Valley Road and Rango Way, blocking both directions of traffic.

Significant heavy rain on the 3rd through 5th resulted in devastating flooding and debris flows in the canyon of the Riverside Mountains where the Zen Mountain Center is located. The Center sustained heavy damage from debris flows on the 4th and 5th and it is unclear which particular day was worse. On the 4th, approximately 3 to 5 feet of mud and rocks flowed through the retreat, half-burying cars and cabins. On the 5th, the second flow brought several more feet of mud and debris, fully burying a few cars. The flows broke plumbing pipes and uncovered buried phone lines. The various buildings sustained significant damage as well, with several feet of mud inside and water damage. Much of the walkways and common areas were unrecognizable due to the washouts.
Roadway flooding 1/2 mile south of the SR79 and SR371 juncture. Several washes were flowing over the roadway with mud in the roadway.
California Highway Patrol reported water quickly running across Bessemer Mine Road and Highway 247 about 50 feet wide.
The Mataguay mesonet station recorded a peak wind gust of 56 mph between 1230 and 1250 PST. Nearby, a large tree limb was broken off and laying by Highway 79.
A ham radio operator reported 2 funnel clouds over Lake Perris.
Water was flowing over Highway 78 near Banner with waves of water up to 8 inches deep. Mud and debris required removal by Caltrans.
CHP reported Golf Club Drive closed at the wash due to flooding.

An NWS employee reported water 4 to 8 inches deep flowing across Highway 78. The flow was estimated at 75 yards wide. The entire airport runway strip in Ocotillo was covered in areas of 1 to 3 inches of water. On the other side of Highway 78, water was flowing over Split Mountain Road in 2 locations. The water was draining from heavy rain over the entrance to Fish Creek and flowing 4 inches deep with mud 2 inches deep.
CHP reported rocks and mud going across Lambs Canyon near SR79 and Gilman Springs Road. CHP also reported a mud slide and flooding in the #1 lane of Highway 60.
Thunderstorm wind gusts downed nine power poles in Bermuda Dunes. Estimated wind gusts 50 to 55 mph.

High winds began at the Sky Valley mesonet station around 1400 PST on the 21st and gusted at or above 58 mph  off and on through 0200 PST on the 22nd. During this time, winds gusted over 60 mph several times, including the peak gust of 65 mph measured consistently between 0145 and 0200 PST on the 22nd.

Fire fighters on the Sierra wildfire observed strong winds during the morning of the 27th. Winds across the fire perimeter were gusting to 35 mph,while above the fire line and along the interstate 15 corridor near 3500 ft elevation, winds were estimated at 60 mph.
Mill Creek was running 2 feet deep and 50 feet wide. Campers were stranded on the north side of the creek.
The Sky Valley mesonet station reported winds gusts over 58 mph off and on from 0500-0700 PST on the 4th. During this time, a peak wind gust of 60 mph was measured twice between 0652 and 0702 PST.

The Fremont Canyon RAWS reported winds gusts over 60 mph between 0600-1100 PST on the 4th. During this time, a peak wind gust of 66 mph was measured 0651 and 0751 PST. The Pleasants Peak mesonet station reported winds gusts over 58 mph between 0700-1130 PST on the 4th. During this time, a peak wind gust of 61 mph was measured between 0901 and 0931 PST.

The Pleasants Peak mesonet station reported winds gusts over 58 mph between 0100 and 1030 PST on the 5th. During this time, a peak wind gust of 62 mph was measured between 0830 and 0900 PST.|The Sky Valley mesonet station reported winds gusts over 58 mph between midnight and 0200 PST on the 5th. During this time, a peak wind gust of 59 mph was measured between 0652 and 0702 PST.

The Sill Hill mesonet station reported wind gusts over 58 mph between 0100-0830 PST, with most gusts over 60 mph. During this time, a peak gust of 70 mph was recorded between 0700-0710 PST. The Big Black Mountain mesonet station reported wind gusts over 58 mph off and on between 0620-1120 PST, with sustained winds mostly 45 mph or greater. During this time, a peak gust of 66 mph was recorded between 0800 and 0810 PST. The Boulder Creek mesonet station also recorded a peak wind gust of 58 mph between 0640 and 0650 PST.
The Hellhole Canyon mesonet station reported wind gusts over 58 mph between 0630-0730 PST. During this time, a peak gust of 59 mph was recorded between 0710 and 0720 PST.

The Sill Hill mesonet station reported wind gusts over 58 mph from 2330 PST on the 5th to 0130 PST on the 6th, with most gusts over 60 mph. During this time, a peak gust of 70 mph was recorded between 0050 and 0100 PST on the 6th.

The Sky Valley mesonet station reported wind gusts over 58 mph off and on from 2000 PST on the 8th to 0400 PST on the 9th, with several gusts over 60 mph. During this time, a peak gust of 78 mph was recorded twice between 0222 and 0232 PST on the 9th. The Whitewater RAWS station reported a peak gust of 60 mph between 0150 and 0250 PST on the 9th.

The observer at the Los Pinos fire lookout reported a peak wind gust of 66 mph, measured at 1308 PST on the 9th. The Volcan Mountain mesonet station reported wind gusts over 58 mph between 0200-0300 PST, with a peak gust of 64 mph recorded between 0230 and 0240 PST.

San Bernardino County Fire is reporting a levee failure along Sheep Creek near the intersection of Buckwheat Road and Manzanita Road in Pinon Hills. Eight homes were threatened and those eight families were evacuated due to the flooding threat. County fire department set up sandbags around all the homes and all were spared from flood damage. Consistent heavy rain over the area throughout the day, resulted in Sheep Creek running over the road at the intersection of Sheep Creek Road and Lone Pine Canyon Road. This intersection was closed and 8-hour rainfall  total was 5 inches.

A spotter in Seal Beach reported street flooding around 6 inches deep at the intersection of Anderson and Pacific Coast Highway. Skywarn also relayed a report of street flooding along Tustin Avenue. Riverside County OES reported Ortega Highway (Hwy 74) closed due to debris flow of mud around the Falls Fire burn scar. A sink hole was also reported on Grand Avenue.

This area drains from the Tijuana River.

California Highway Patrol reported flash flooding along Highway 78 at Yaqui Pass with several boulders in the roadway. A road alert was issued and the road closed for a time.

CHP reported a mudslide over Borrego Springs Road at San Pablo Road, with equipment needed to scrape the roadway. Rocks, sand, and standing water also extended to near Tilting T Drive and Christmas Circle. Flash flooding was also reported in Borrego Springs with 6 inches of flowing water, and one home with water entering it.

Lifeguards started a mass rescue when seven people got caught in a rip current at the northern end of Moonlight Beach around 1310 PST on the 29th, according to Encinitas Fire officials. Five students found a Guatemalan man and his nephew unconscious and kept them afloat until lifeguards arrived to pull them to shore where they were taken to a local hospital. Both eventually died, the man on June 2 and the nephew June 14. The five students were unharmed.

The Bernardo Fire started on May 13, at 10:00 AM PDT, just south of Del Norte High School, in a construction trench off Nighthawk Lane and Camino San Bernardo. Over the next few hours the wildfire intensified due to the strong Santa Ana winds driving it southward. This prompted the evacuation of several schools (with the exception of Del Norte High School), in addition to at least 20,000 homes. Within several hours, the fire covered at least 800 acres. The rapid southward spread of the fire caused mandatory evacuation orders to be issued for portions of 4S Ranch, Del Sur, Black Mountain Ranch, Rancho Santa Fe, and other residential communities. Late on May 13, the Bernardo Fire reached a size of 1,600 acres. By 2300 PST on the 13th, the portion of the fire within 4S Ranch and Del Sur had been completely extinguished. Later on the 14, all of the evacuation orders were lifted for that area. By the morning of the 15th, the fire was 75% contained and no longer expanding. On the 16th, the Bernardo Fire was reported to be 90% contained, but some structures were still threatened by the fire. The Bernardo Fire was reported 100% contained on the 17th at 1915 PST, burning a total of 1548 acres. The San Diego Unified School District closed all its schools citywide on May 15, but reopened most of them on May 16. The cause of the Bernardo Fire was ruled accidental; starting in a small trench being dug by a construction crew and spread rapidly through the dry brush at the site. In all, 50 structures were threatened, and 3 unknown injuries per Cal Fire.

The River Fire broke out at 1112 PST on the 14th, in Oceanside, starting in the San Luis Rey River riverbed. Homes and an elementary school in the area were evacuated. The Oceanside Unified School District closed all schools on the 15th. On the evening of the 16th, the fire was 100% contained, after it had burned 105 acres of land, confined to the river bed. A man was arrested on the 15th and charged with arson, after witnesses saw him adding brush to the flames, but authorities do not believe he started the fire. Official cause is still unknown.

The Highway Fire, near Bonsall and Fallbrook, started at 1200 PST on the 14th near Interstate 15 and California State Route 76, near Old Highway 395 in the Deer Springs area. Several schools and about 600 residents were evacuated. Olive Hill Road was closed from Mission to Highway 76 due to wildfire, evacuating the Olive Hill area.  Highway 15 was also closed in both directions, along with old 395/Highway 76. By 1700 PST on the 15th, the fire was 100% contained, after burning 441 acres. No homes were damages or destroyed and no injuries reported. The heavy fuels in this area had not burned since the Gopher Canyon Fire in 1970. The cause of the fire is still under investigation.

The Pulgas Fire broke out around 1345 PST on the 15th at Camp Pendleton near Interstate 5 at Las Pulgas Road, to the north of Oceanside. Las Pulgas Area personnel were ordered to evacuate to the School of Infantry Parade deck behind the mess hall. The fire burned 500 acres acres within the next couple of hours. It became the largest of the fires, burning a total of 15,000 acres before being fully contained on the afternoon of the 21st. Road closures included the Las Pulgas gate closed to all traffic except emergency vehicles, Stuart Mesa Road north of Assault Craft Unit-5, Basilone Road from Marine Corps Air Station Camp Pendleton to Camp Horno, as well as Las Pulgas Road.

The Combat or San Mateo Fire (previously known as the Talega Fire), started around 1024 PST on the 16th near the Camp Talega area of the base, near Basilone Road. By the mid-afternoon, the fire had burned about 25 acres. All non-essential personnel were ordered to be sent home. Evacuation orders were given to personnel in nearby areas of the base including some housing facilities and a school. By the 17th, the fire had grown to 800 acres and was 25% contained. Very late at night on the 20th, the San Mateo Fire was reported 100% contained after burning a total of 1500 acres. The cause of the wildfire is still under investigation. No injuries reported.

The Tomahawk Fire started on the 14th around 0845 PST on the Naval Weapons Station Seal Beach Detachment Fallbrook (also known as Fallbrook Naval Weapons Station). The Tomahawk Fire was the second largest of the San Diego County fires in terms of size, behind the Pulgas Fire. Evacuation orders were issued for several schools and housing areas, as well as the Fallbrook Naval Weapons Station and the closed San Onofre Nuclear Generating Station. During the evening of the 18th, the fire was reported to be 100% contained after burning a total of 5400 acres. No injuries reported.

The Cocos Fire, previously known as the Twin Oaks Fire and later the Washingtonia Fire, was a wildfire that ignited around 1730 PST on the 14th in the hills south of California State University, San Marcos and burned 400 acres by later in the evening. Flames were reported near homes, and the southeastern part of the city was ordered evacuated. By the morning of the 15th, the Cocos Fire was the top priority for county firefighters. The Cocos Fire quickly spread into western Escondido with a big flare up near noon that day; then the sea breeze took replaced the Santa Ana, pushing the fire back toward the east with thick smoke on I-15 and additional evacuations in Escondido. It grew overnight to 800 acres and was only 5% contained. |Road closures/evacuations included:  Del Dios highway from Via Rancho Parkway to Rancho Drive, evacuating the Del Dios community; Mt. Israel Road, Harmony Grove Road from Elfin Forest to Kauana Loa Drive, Country Club Road to Kauana Loa Drive, Twin Oaks Road in San Marcos; San Elijo Hills evacuated as well. All schools in the San Marcos Unified School District were closed on the 15th and 16th. California State University, San Marcos, was evacuated on the 14th, along with the surrounding neighborhoods, in the midst of administering spring finals, and remained closed for the rest of the week. Additionally, commencement exercises scheduled for the weekend were also cancelled. Palomar College also closed the 15th and 16th, and postponed its commencement ceremonies until the following week.  At 1730 PST on the 22, the Cocos Fire was reported to be 100% contained after torching 1.995 acres. The fire destroyed more than 40 buildings, including 12 single family homes, and damaging at least 2 other homes. The Harmony Grove Spiritualist Association, a 13-acre spiritualist retreat founded in 1896, was particularly hard hit with most of the buildings and residences (22 structures) on the property destroyed. Property damage from the fire is estimated at more than $5.7 million. Three minor injuries have been reported. On July 9, the San Diego County Sheriff's Department said that they believe the Cocos Fire was intentionally set by a juvenile, who is now scheduled to appear in juvenile court.

The Poinsettia Fire started on the 14th, around 0930 PST, in the city of Carlsbad,  near the intersection of Poinsettia Lane and Alicante. After the fire burned through dry brush and crossed El Camino Real, evacuation orders were issued to 11,600 homes and businesses in Carlsbad, as well as two elementary schools and a middle school. By the end of the day on the 14th, the fire had destroyed eight homes, an 18-unit condominium complex, and two commercial buildings. Three other homes sustained minor damage. The Carlsbad Unified School District closed all schools May 15th and 16th. The Encinitas school district, which straddles Carlsbad, was closed both days as well. At 1600 PST on the 14th, the fire covered more than 400 acres, threatening additional structures. Early on the 16th, the fire had burned 400 acres and was 85% contained. As a result, all of the evacuation orders were lifted. The fire was reported to be 100% contained by 1600 PST on the 17th, after reaching a size of 600 acres. The Poinsettia Fire was the most destructive of the San Diego County wildfires. It caused property damage estimated at $22.5 million. As of July 10, 2014, the cause of the fire is still listed as undetermined. A body was also discovered in the fire damage near a transient encampment, but the cause of death has not been attributed to the fire.
