Water, 4 to 6 inches deep in places, along Indian Canyon Drive near Palm Springs Station Road.
CHP reports roadway flooding on Danbury Street in Cabazon. Flood water, rocks, mud, and debris flowing down the street. The roadway is impassable due to boulders and mud blocking the street.
Dinah Shore Drive between Date Palm Drive and Cathedral Canyon Drive was flooded...with at least one car abandoned.
Roadway washed out near the intersection of Box Canyon Road / 66th ave. Road closure required.

USGS gage in the Perris Valley storm drain at Nuevo Road showed a spike from 8.68 ft to 14.94 ft. by 2100 PST. The initial rise of 3 ft. occurred in less than 30 minutes. Flash flood duration was 2 hours 15 minutes. Another USGS gage on the Santa Ana River at Arlington jumped from 5.66 ft to 10.31 ft over 2 hours.
CHP reported mud/dirt/rock on Campo Road/State Route 94 just west of Forest Gate Road due to heavy rainfall.
Water up to 2 feet deep reported at the intersection of Aqua and 4th Streets.

CHP reported a rock slide at the intersection of Yaqui Pass Road and Borrego Springs Road. The road needed to be shut down and plowed. Not far down Borrego Springs Road, a spotter reported flooding of streets...dry lakes and nearby areas flooded. CHP also reported Highway 78 being closed due to flooding at the intersection of Split Mountain Road, east of Borrego Springs.

CHP reports Montezuma Valley Road being completely flooded with debris everywhere. The eastbound lane of that road completely collapsed. A spotter just south of this location reported heavy rain and debris flows on highway S-2.

CHP reports roadway flooded near the intersection of Oak Glen Road and Glen Road east of Yucaipa, with debris and water covering the road making it impassable. An NWS employee reported similar conditions along Oak Glen Road further west toward Yucaipa.

Cal OES San Bernardino reported flash flooding and debris flow in Mill Creek with people being evacuated from the creek basin. A spotter added that county fire was shutting down Valley of the Falls Drive at Highway 38. Shelter in place protocols were given by the county fire department. Multiple vehicles were reported in flooded wash and propane tanks were dislodged. Swift water rescues in progress. The area was closed to non-residents.

California Highway Patrol reported a rock slide on Mount Baldy Road and requested the road be closed. This appears to have occurred just east of the LA county line. Damage from flooding and a propane tank rupture at the Mount Baldy visitor center. Many roads were washed out in the area. The direct cause and extent of the damage is unknown. The Mt. Baldy fire station alert gage reported a total of 4.4 inches of rain beginning at 1430 PST and ending at 1630 PST. The majority of that rain, 3.98 inches, fell in 60 minutes from 1445-1545 PST.

CHP reported the east and west bound lanes of Interstate 210 were flooded. CHP also reported Marshall Boulevard flooded between Sterling and Arden Avenues, with vehicles stuck in the roadway. A couple hours later, the California Department of Forestry reported significant flooding in the city of Highland in the area of Baseline Road. Everyone was advised to shelter in place while they check for people stuck in water/mud.
CHP reported a vehicle almost under water at the intersection of Reche Canyon Road and Prado Lane.
CHP reported a side road of Lytle Creek Road was washed out due to heavy rainfall.

CHP reported a flooded wash with multiple cars stuck in the area.  4 inches of rain recorded in gauge within 2 hours on the steep slope of big Mt Baldy. A hiker parked their car in the small town of Mt Baldy and hiked to the top. Hail and lightning caused them to go back down the mountain early. They used the dry creek to go back|down and were swept away in a flash flood over 10 feet, per NWS Storm Survey of high water marks on trees. The hiker's car was found the next|day during the NWS Storm Survey. The car was destroyed and the person drowned somewhere along the middle or bottom of the creek, just on the San Bernardino County side. LA County Fire department led the search and rescue. Since Mt Baldy|town, where the car was parked, is in San Bernardino County they ended up having a unified command with Los Angeles County, San Bernardino Fire, and Town of|Mt Baldy.  At least 2 vehicles were towed out of the creek. We were told at the survey that the cars were on the Los Angeles County side of the mountain but washed downstream, and across the San Bernardino County side of the mountain, where the one fatality of a 48-yr old man from El Segundo, occurred.

A debris flow was observed with 18 to 24 inches of mud being removed from Highway 78 by Caltrans. A culvert had overflowed onto road, directly below a recent wildfire scare on the Banner Grade. The road was closed east of Julian and clean up was ongoing on the following day.
A trained spotter reported nickel size hail and heavy rain along Highway 247 just east of Lucerne Valley near Camp Rock Road.
The public reported 1-inch hail in Menifee from an early morning thunderstorm. Local news media reported large hail cracked a vehicle windshield in Menifee from the same storm.
A spotter reported hail up to one inch in Nuevo from a thunderstorm.

A spotter reported lightning struck and ignited fires in two palm trees near the community college. The fires were put out. Lightning also struck the technology building on campus, knocking out power.
One inch plus hail reported by the observers at the Mt. Laguna Observatory.
A spotter in Campo reported flash flooding and pea size hail at CA Highway 94 and Shookey road.
A ham radio spotter is reporting up to 6 inches of water on the road in the 35000 block of Highway 79 near Warner Springs.

A spotter reports a dust storm producing quarter mile visibility in Cathedral City, with winds estimated at 15-20 mph. A haboob in Palm Springs felled a tree onto a pickup truck containing a man who was injured and taken to the hospital. Peak wind speeds at the nearby Palm Springs ASOS were 40 mph at that time. The dust storm then proceeded down the Coachella Valley, reaching the Thermal Airport, whose ASOS reported one-quarter mile visibility in dust and 40 knot wind gusts.
Surfline reported 4 to 7 foot surf at Huntington Beach and Newport Beach. Higher surf of 5 to 10 feet was reported at the Wedge, near Newport Beach.
Surf of 4 to 7 feet reported by Surfline at Trestles Beach in northern San Diego County.

Huntington Beach lifeguards reported surf of 10 to 15 feet and large, powerful rip currents, along with 10 foot surf at nearby Seal Beach. Newport Beach lifeguards reported surf up to 18 feet, with higher surf to 25 feet at the Wedge. San Clemente lifeguards reported surf of 7 to 9 feet, while Laguna Beach lifeguards reported 10 feet.

Local TV media reported significant coastal flooding of Seal Beach, specifically along East Seal Way, where many homes experienced a few inches to 1 foot of water rushing into them after 12 to 14 foot waves cleared the 2 and a half foot protective sea wall.
Oceanside Beach lifeguards reported 6 to 10 foot surf and strong rip currents.

Newport Beach lifeguards reported 10 to 15 foot surf. Huntington and Seal Beach lifeguards reported 6 to 9 foot surf and strong rip currents. San Clemete City lifeguards reported 4 to 7 foot surf with strong rip currents.
California Highway Patrol reported a river of flood waters washing across the road at the intersection of Highway 79 and Chihuahua Valley Road. They shut down the road at that spot.
CHP reported rocks 2 feet in diameter blocking lanes. CHP also reported a boulder hitting the windshield of a black Toyota Prius on Highway 330.
CHP reported water breaking through the right-side berm, flooding all southbound lanes of Interstate 215, blocking the 2nd Street exit.

CHP reported a power line down in the dirt and National Trails Highway starting to flood just south of Helendale at Bryman Road. Some vehicles are stopped and others moving slowly. Six vehicles are stuck due to the flood waters.

CHP reported road washing out at Cedar Avenue in Hemet, as well as flooding along Highway 74 at 1st Street across all lanes of 74. Also flooding was reported at Palm and 1st, with knee-deep water. The Hemet Valle Vista alert gage recorded 2.06 inches of rain over the past hour. A few miles east on Highway 74, an off-road vehicle was stuck in a flash flood, as well as another party of 2 were stuck in a house and couldn't cross the road due to water. County Roads closed Highway 74 1.5 miles from the ranger station at Doe Canyon Road.

CHP reported the slow lane of Highway 60 at Main Street under at least 2 feet of water with several vehicles stuck in the water. CHP also reported one lane of the northbound University on-ramp to Interstate 215 is flooded. Also, all lanes of northbound Interstate 215 are flooded, except the HOV lane. Spotter 217 reported several locations flooded along Iowa Avenue in Riverside, near UC Riverside. Iowa Avenue at Center Street, Marlborough Street, and several other spots were under a foot or more of water, running up over the gutters and curbs. CHP also reported a woman stuck in her vehicle on the 14th Street on-ramp to eastbound SR 91. Several vehicles were also stuck in approximately 4 feet of water at the railroad crossing on 14th Street. CHP shut down both sides of the road there.
California Highway Patrol reported the canal at 66th Avenue and Harrison Street ruptured and completely flooded the intersection. The intersection was closed.
CHP reports flooding and debris in all lanes on Dillon road and North Indian Canyon Drive. Starting at 0345 PST, the road started to flood with mud and water up to 4 inches deep.

CHP reported 3 vehicles stuck in water, one of which has water up over the tires. Varner Road and Bob Hope Drive are closed. Two other vehicles stuck in water at Varner Road and Date Palm Drive. CHP reported heavy flooding in the center divide and #1 lane of Interstate 10 westbound. CHP reported 6 vehicles stuck in water on Ramon Road at Chimayo Road, with water covering the tires of at least one of the vehicles. CHP reported a stalled vehicle partially in the roadway and stuck in water on Ramon Road at Thousand Palms Canyon Road. As of 0830 PST, numerous vehicles were getting stuck and blocking Thousand Palms Canyon Road, so the wash was shut down at Frances, just east of Thousand Palms Canyon Road. The ALERT gage at Thousand Palms NE recorded 1.54 inches of rain between 0530-0630 PST.

CHP reported Country Club Drive at Starlight Lane flooded. Avenue 42 was also completely flooded between Adams and County Club drive and was closed at this location. CHP reported a vehicle flooded out and blocking the Washington Street on-ramp to westbound Interstate 10. CHP also reported flooding of the #1 and #2 lanes of Interstate 10 westbound at Washington and Monterrey streets. Flooding signs were placed at both locations. Water 3 to 4 feet deep submerged 4 to 5 vehicles at the intersection of Washington Street and Country Club Drive. Southbound Indian Canyon Road was also closed at I-10.

Several trees and a light pole fell on two parked trucks in a shopping center near the intersection of Calle Verde and Avocado Blvd in La Mesa. The tree also damaged the awnings and door of the McDonalds.
CHP reported a tree down blocking the right lane near the intersection of Jamacha Boulevard and Doubletree Road. They also reported a school bus hit by a tree.
A spotter in Murrieta reported 50 mph winds with a wooden fence blown down and lawn furniture thrown across the yard.
Lightning struck a home near Crestline, resulting in a fire.
Heavy rain resulted in 2 inches of flowing water across Bundy Canyon Road and Harvest Way east.

The El Cariso mesonet station recorded a wind gust of 48 mph from a thunderstorm in the area. Downwind of this station, CHP reported a tree falling onto a power line on Grand Avenue in Lake Elsinore, blocking traffic. Wind damage was also reported at Elsinore High School, with power lines down and some minor flooding.
The Lake Matthews mesonet station reported a gust of 50 mph due to a thunderstorm, which knocked down a tree, blocking all lanes of Glen Ivy Road a few miles north of the mesonet.
Multiple public photos show a funnel cloud just north of Big Bear Lake.
Montgomery Field ASOS recorded 0.80 inches of rain in less than one hour. Media reported 6 or more inches of water over a nearby roadway a short time later.
ASOS reported a gust of 56 mph around 1600 PST. Strong winds around this time flipped multiple small planes at the airfield.
The Mission Valley mesonet recorded a wind gust of 52 mph due to a thunderstorm. Media reported a tree falling on a car in Mission Valley nearby.
Multiple trees down and broken tree limbs throughout the neighborhood in Tierrasanta. Widespread minor damage to patio furniture, pop-up tents, and trampolines.
Two palm trees caught fire after a lightning strike.
The Whitewater RAWS measured a peak gust of 59 mph between 0050 and 0150 PST on the 27th. Winds had gusted in the mid to upper 50s for the past 2 hours.

High winds occurred at the Burns Canyon RAWS between 2300 PST on the 26th and 0200 PST on the 27th, with southwest winds sustained between 30 and 40 mph and gusting to over 60 mph. The peak gust of 66 mph was recorded between 0000 and 0100 PST on the 27th.

NWS survey found numerous trees downed by high winds from wet microburst. Most trees were snapped and a couple were uprooted. Trees blocked a couple roadways in residence just east of Chicago avenue. A couple trees were 2 to 3 feet in diameter. The same area had considerable flood damage to a sidewalk and concrete drainage ditch.
One of the local television stations and San Diego County Health Department reported 50-75 people were treated for heat-related injuries at the Miramar air show.

On the 6th, Newport Beach lifeguards reported 6 foot surf with max sets to 8 feet, while Surfline reported 10 to 15 foot surf at The Wedge. On the 7th, Huntington Beach lifeguards reported 6 to 8 foot surf, and later 8 foot surf with max sets to 10 feet.
Minor tidal overflow resulted in flooding along the Pacific Coast Highway at Anderson in Sunset Beach. The curb lane on the beach side was under a few inches of water.
High winds occurred at the Volcan Mountain mesonet station between 2200-2300 PST. During this time, winds were sustained out of the west-southwest between 35 -45 mph, with a peak gust of 63 mph.

High winds occurred at the Sill Hill SDGE mesonet site between 0440-0510 PST on the 4th, with a peak gust of 63 mph. High winds occurred at the Crestwood SDGE mesonet site between 0750-0830 PST on the 4th, with a peak gust of 61 mph. High winds occurred at the Lucky Five Ranch SDGE mesonet site between 0600-0630 PST on the 4th, with a peak gust of 61 mph.
High winds occurred at the Sill Hill SDGE mesonet site between 0330-0830 PST on the 4th, with a several gusts over 60 mph. The peak gust of 69 mph was recorded between 0625-0655 PST.

John Wayne Airport reported one-quarter mile visibility from 0031 to 0101 PST on the 9th. Fullerton Municipal Airport reported one-quarter mile visibility from 0400 to 0743 PST on the 9th. Los Alamitos U.S. Army Airfield reported one-quarter mile or less visibility from 0216 am to 0858 PST on the 9th.

Montgomery Field reported one-quarter mile visibility from 2249 PST on the 8th to 0253 PST on the 9th. Lindbergh Field reported intermittent one-quarter mile visibility between 0102 and 0315 PST on the 9th. McClellan-Palomar Airport reported one-quarter mile visibility from 2111 PST on the 8th to 0038 PST on the 9th, and again from 0223 to 0351 PST on the 9th.  Imperial Beach Naval Auxiliary Landing Field reported one-quarter mile of visibility from 1956 to 2248 PST on the 8th, and again from 0024 to 0356 PST on the 9th. MCOLF Camp Pendleton at Red Beach reported one-quarter mile visibility from 1802 PST on the 8th to 0021 PST on the 9th, and again from 0256 to 0751 PST on the 9th. North Island NAS reported one-quarter mile visibility between 2108 and 2135 PST on the 8th, and again from 0522 to 0752 PST on the 9th.

High winds began at the Whitewater RAWS between 1650-1750 PST and ended between 2250-2350 PST on the evening of the 15th. During this time, winds were sustained out of the west-northwest at 35-45 mph with gusts near 60, including the peak gust of 60 mph recorded between 2150-2250 PST.

High winds began at the Pleasants Peak SDGE mesonet between 0425-0455 PST and ended between 1059-1129 PST on the morning of the 16th. During this time, winds were sustained out of the east-northeast at 35-55 mph with gusts over 60 mph. The peak gust of 76 mph recorded between 1029-1059 PST. High winds also occurred at the Fremont Canyon RAWS between 0651-0951 PST on the 16th, with sustained winds out of the northeast at 35-40 mph, including the peak gust of 62 mph recorded between 0851-0951 PST.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Strong easterly winds caused damage to a roof in Eastvale, near the city of Riverside. Wind gusts were estimated around 52 mph, based on nearby observations. The Press Enterprise newspaper cited 1400 customers without power in central San Bernardino at 1022 PST on the 16th. CHP also reported power lines down northeast of Perris at 1347 PST and east of Moreno Valley at 2355 PST on the 16th.

Strong winds occurred at the Sill Hill and Crestwood SDGE mesonet stations from the evening of the 16th through the early morning of the 17th. During this period, winds were gusting 45 to 55 mph out of the east to northeast. Crestwood recorded a peak gust of 59 mph as well, between 1200-1210 PST on the 16th. Sill Hill recorded a peak gust of 59 mph between 0230-0240 PST on the 17th.
Surfline reported 5 to 8 foot surf on the 19th and 20th at Huntington Beach, Newport Beach, and Salt Creek Beach.
Lightning from the 17th eventually ignited the North Face Fire on the 21st, with the aid of offshore winds.
Lightning on the 17th eventually ignited the Strawberry Fire just southwest of Lake Arrowhead, with the aid of offshore winds.

High winds occurred at the Whitewater RAWS between 2100 PST and 0000 PST on the 23rd, with sustained winds out of the west-northwest at 35-45 mph and gusting over 60 mph. The peak gust of 63 mph was recorded between 2050-2150 PST on the 22nd.

High winds began at the Pleasants Peak SDGE mesonet between 0629-0659 PST on the 23rd and ended between 1151-1251 PST the same day. During this time, winds were sustained out of the east-northeast at 35-45 mph with several gusts over 60 mph, including the peak gust of 68 mph recorded between 0629-0659 PST. High winds began at the Fremont RAWS between 0651-0751 PST on the 23rd and ended between 1151-1251 PST the same day. During this time, winds were sustained out of the east-northeast at 35-45 mph with gusts over 60 mph, including the peak gust of 67 mph recorded between 0851-0951 PST.

High winds began at the Sill Hill SDGE mesonet between 2100-2110 PST on the 24th and ended between 0340-0350 PST on the 25th. During this time, winds were sustained out of the east at 40-60 mph with several gusts over 75 mph, including the peak gust of 87 mph recorded between 2300-2310 PST. High winds occurred at the Big Black Mountain mesonet between 2330 PST on the 24th and 0330 PST on the 25th. During this time, winds were sustained out of the east at 50-60 mph with gusts over 60 mph, including the peak gust of 78 mph recorded between 0007-0027 PST on the 25th. High winds occurred off and on at the Boulder Creek SDGE mesonet station between 2050 PST on the 24th and 0030 PST on the 25th with winds out of the east-northeast around 35 mph, gusting around 60, including a peak gust of 66 mph recorded near the beginning of the high wind period. High winds occurred at the Lucky Five Ranch SDGE mesonet between 2300 PST on the 24th and 0000 PST on the 25th, with ENE winds around 40 knots, gusting around 60 mph with a peak gust of 64 mph. Crestwood mesonet also had a peak gust of 58 mph between 2300 PST on the 24th and 0000 PST on the 25th.
The Otay Mountain and Lyons Peak mesonet sites each had a peak gust of 59 mph between 0215-0400 PST on the 25th.
CHP reported the right lanes of Van Buren closed due to flooding.

The Desert Sun reports that Gene Autry trail...Indian Canyon Drive...Araby Drive...and Vista Chino were closed due to flooding from water rushing down the Whitewater basin from heavy rains over Yucaipa. At the Snow Creek stream gage in Whitewater at 1830 PST the 2nd, the flow peaked at 157 cfs.

CHP reported vehicles stuck in mud with debris 10 feet high on both sides of Soboba Road, which was made a hard closure. A spotter reported a swift water rescue on Soboba Road west of Lake Park in San Jacinto. Three people were rescued and all were unharmed. CHP also reported flooding and a mudslide near Gilman Springs Road and Sublette Road, as well as a BMW sedan stuck in water at Cornell Street and Thornton Ave.
CHP reported that the road needs to be closed due to flooding at Rancho California Road and Anza Road.
CHP and ABC 7 news reported Highway 74 between Dartmouth and Columbia closed due to flooding.
CHP reported Glen Helen Parkway closed due to flooding from heavy rain.
CHP reported Duncan road in Phelan closed due to flooding between Sheepcreek and Buckwheat roads and minor street flooding at Main St. and I Ave near Hesperia.
CHP reported flooding and mud at San Timoteo Canyon Road and Live Oak Canyon Road.

CHP reported 5 to 6 vehicles stuck in flood waters near I-805 and Highway 54, multiple vehicles stranded in flood waters near I-805 and 47th Avenue, and lanes 3 and 4 at the intersection of Highland Avenue and Highway 54 East completely flooded.
CHP reported the closure of Quarry Road between Lakeview Avenue and Elkelton Drive due to flooding.
CHP reported a mudslide covering all lanes for 50 yards along Sloan Canyon Road, mud was approximately 18 inches deep.

CHP reported multiple vehicles stuck in flood waters near Highway 163 South and I-5, and heavy flooding at the India Street on-ramp to I-5 north, but cars were able to make it through. NBC 7 also reported a flooded underground parking lot in Mission Hills, with several vehicles underwater.
A swift water rescue was conducted to retrieve an adult male from the San Diego River near the Fashion Valley Mall.  No injury report available.
CHP reported 6 to 10 inches of water on the off ramp for Balboa Avenue from Highway 163.
CHP reported mud too deep to drive through at the intersection of Harmony Grove Road and Wilgen Drive. The roadway was closed for roughly 1 hour.

The Burns Canyon RAWS reported high winds between 0151-0451 PST on the 12th. During this time, winds were sustained out of the southwest at 40-50 mph. The peak gust of 76 mph was recorded between 0151-0251 PST.

Streets just south of Garden Grove were closed due to flooding, as reported by the Orange County Skywarn coordinator. The nearby Anaheim Barber City mesonet station reported a 3-hour rainfall total of 1.22 inches.

A spotter reported flooding on Bastanchury Road with streets under up to a foot of standing water.  Flooding was also reported by a spotter at the Miraloma and Lakeview Avenue low water crossing with 6 inches of water on the roadway. A nearby mesonet station in Yorba Linda recorded a 3-hour rain total of 1.06 inches.
Surfline reports surf of 5 to 8 feet at Huntington Beach.

Solana Beach lifeguards reported 5 to 8 foot surf.  Oceanside Beach lifeguards reported 5 to 7 foot surf. Mission Beach lifeguards reported 6 to 8 foot surf. Moonlight Beach lifeguards reported 6 to 8 foot surf.
KOGO radio reported flooding along Highway 78 and El Camino Real. An NWS employee reported around an inch of standing water on Interstate 5 stretching from Camp Pendleton, south to Highway 78.
KOGO radio reported a flooded ramp onto Interstate 5 near National City.

News10 reported a levee breech along the San Diego River near Qualcomm stadium, releasing large amounts of water into the parking area. At the time, the San Diego River stage was at 4.1 feet at the nearby Fashion Valley gage.
The Country Club Road webcam shows the road closed and water flowing over roadway at the Escondido Creek crossing.
Quarry Road was flooded with several inches of flowing water per a county flood control webcam. The road was closed as a result.
The March AFB AOS observer reported a cold air funnel cloud between 1153-1158 PST.
A debris flow of rocks and mud several inches deep covered Highway 91 in Corona. All east-bound lanes were closed at 0200 PST.
Surfline reported 5 to 8 foot surf at Blacks Beach and 5 to 7 foot surf at Ocean Beach.

CHP reported the roadway completely flooded at the I-805 and Highway 94 interchange where a vehicle hydroplaned and overturned. Nearby stations reported instantaneous rainfall rates of 0.25 to 0.40 per hour.

Road closed due to flowing water in Escondido Creek over Country Club Drive on low lying crossing. Webcams from SD county flood control confirmed flooding. News 10 reported roadway flooding Along Bent Avenue at Discover Street in San Marcos.
Minor tidal overflow was observed along the strand south from Oceanside Pier to Wisconsin Street between 0700-0800 PST on the 20th.

High winds occurred at the Fremont Canyon RAWS between 0051-0551 PST on the 23rd. During this time, winds were sustained out of the ENE at 30-40 mph with gusts in the 60s, including the peak gust of 67 mph, recorded between 0151-0251 PST. High winds occurred at the Pleasants Peak mesonet station between 0059-0229 PST on the 23rd. During this time, winds were sustained out of the east at 45-50 mph with gusts in the 60s, with a peak gust of 70 mph, recorded between 0129-0159 PST.

Winds at the Sill Hill SDGE mesonet were sustained 35-45 mph out of the east with gusts in the low to mid-50s mph between about 0600-1000 PST on the 23rd. During this time, a peak gust of 60 mph was recorded between 0630-0640 PST.

High winds occurred at the Whitewater RAWS between 2200 PST on the 24th and 0400 PST on the 25th. During this time, winds were sustained out of the WNW at 30-40 mph with gusts in the upper 50s, with a peak gust of 61 mph, recorded between 2150-2250 PST.

High winds occurred at the Burns Canyon RAWS between 1751 PST on the 24th and 0051 PST on the 25th. During this time, winds were sustained out of the WSW at 35-50 mph with gusts 60-75 mph. A peak gust of 90 mph, recorded between 2151-2251 PST.

High winds occurred at the Mount Laguna HPWREN mesonet between 2015 PST on the 24th and 0535 PST on the 25th. During this time, winds were sustained out of the southwest at 55-70 mph with gusts in the 70s, with a peak gust of 80 mph, recorded between 0305-0315 PST on the 25th. High winds occurred off and on at the Volcan Mountain SDGE mesonet between 2110 PST on the 24th and 0240 PST on the 25th. During this time, winds were sustained out of the WSW at 35-40 mph with gusts 50-60 mph, including the peak gust of 60 mph, recorded between 0230-0240 PST on the 25th.
Valley of the Falls Road reported open, but minor flooding as Mill Creek was running full. Yucaipa Ridge reported 4 inches of rain in 6 hours.

High winds occurred at the Fremont Canyon RAWS between 2051 PST on the 30th and 1051 PST on the 31st. During this time, winds were sustained out of the ENE at 35-55 mph with gusts in the 60s and 70s mph. A peak gust of 79 mph was recorded between 0451-0551 PST on the 31st.

High winds occurred at the Whitewater RAWS between 0150-0350 PST on the 30th. During this time, winds were sustained out of the west-northwest at 35-40 mph with gusts in the upper 50s, including the peak gust of 59 mph recorded between 0250-0350 PST.

CHP reported several inches of snow on Highway 74 in the Santa Ana Mountains resulted in closing both directions of the roadway between San Juan Capistrano and Lake Elsinore due to the heavy snow. An estimated 100 vehicles were stuck in the closure zone. There were also downed trees in roadway. A member of the public reported 6 inches of snow in 24 hours near Horsethief Canyon.

High winds occurred at the Mt. Laguna HPWREN mesonet between 0315-0515 PST on the 30th. During this time, winds were sustained out of the west-southwest at 45-55 mph with gusts in the low 60s. The peak gust of 63 mph was recorded between 0505-0515 PST.
A spotter in the city of Orange recorded a wind gust of 58 mph. Another spotter in that area reported a wind gust of 46 mph with shingles blown off the neighbors roof.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: A spotter just northwest of Lake Elsinore reported 6 inches of snow at 1400 feet causing widespread damage to trees with many limbs broken. CHP reported Interstate 15 impacted by snow with 1-2 at the Clinton Keith Road exit. The Baxter Road off-ramp was closed due to snow accumulations where cars are stuck in snow. Bundy Canyon Road off-ramp Was completely snowed in with several vehicles stuck in the snow. A spotter reported Interstate 15 shutdown at Wildomar with 8-10 inches estimated at elevation of 1400 ft. A member of the public reported a 24 hour snowfall of 5 inches reported near Lake Matthews.

A spotter in El Cariso Village reported 10 inches of snow as of 0800 PST with tree damage and power outages. The nearby El Cariso mesonet station recorded a wind gust of 44 mph between 1100-1115 PST on the 31st.
A 24 hour snowfall of 2-8 inches was reported by the public near Idyllwild.

Between 2000 PST on the 30th and 0200 PST on the 31st, heavy snow combined with wind and cold stranding over 100 motorists along Highway 138 between Pilot Rock Road and Old Mill Road along the south side of Silverwood Lake and around Crestline. No major injuries were reported, but a huge impact on resources for the county and risk to the people while they were stranded. The highway was closed in this area as a result.

The public reported 24 hour snowfall totals as follows: 9-12 inches at Big Bear Mountain and Snow Summit, 8 inches at Green Valley Lake and Running Springs, 6 inches at Lake Arrowhead and Forrest Falls, and 5 inches in Crestline.

The Mt. Laguna Observatory reported a 24 hour snow total of 12 inches. The COOP observer at Mt. Laguna reported a 24-hour snow total of 8 inches. The COOP observer at the Palomar Mountain Observatory reported a 24-hour snow total of 14 inches. Multiple public reports of 7 to 9 inches of snow in Julian.
The Red Mountain HPWREN mesonet recorded high winds between 0606-0626 PST on the 31st with a peak gust of 62 mph.

Brown Field municipal airport ASOS reported one-quarter mile visibility from 2153 PST on the 19th through 0616 PST on the 20th. Montgomery Field ASOS reported mostly one-quarter mile visibility from 2317 PST on the 19th through 0620 PST on the 20th. Carlsbad McClellan-Palomar airport ASOS reported mostly one-quarter mile visibility between 0010-0620 PST on the 20th. Camp Pendleton MCAS ASOS reported mostly one-quarter mile visibility between 0154-0803 PST on the 20th. A spotter in San Marcos reported visibility of only 100 feet with a fog depth of around 50 feet around 0730 PST on the 20th.

High winds occurred at the Fremont Canyon RAWS between 0000-2200 PST on the 24th. During this time, winds were sustained out of the ENE at 35-40 mph with gusts in the 60s and 70s. A peak gust of 77 mph was recorded between 0651-0751 PST. High winds occurred at the Pleasants Peak mesonet between 0222-1352 PST on the 24th. During this time, winds were sustained out of the ENE at 40-50 mph with gusts in the upper 50s and 60s. A peak gust of 63 mph was recorded twice between 0852-0952 PST.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: High winds occurred at the Highland Springs RAWS between 0516-0716 PST on the 24th. During this time, winds were sustained out of the ENE at 40-50 mph with gusts in the 60s. A peak gust of 69 mph was recorded between 0616-0716 PST. The Ontario Airport ASOS recorded a peak gust of 64 mph around 0405 PST on the 24th. ABC7 news reported several trees down due to wind in Rancho Cucamonga and Alta Loma, as well as power lines down and customers without electricity in Fontana. One large tree fell on a car, completely crushing it, in Rancho Cucamonga. CHP also reported a big rig flipped over into a ditch along Highway 210 near the Interstate 15 junction, likely wind-related.

High winds occurred at the Sill Hill Mesonet between 2110 PST on the 23rd and 2330 PST on the 24th. During this time, winds were sustained out of the E at 35-55 mph with most gusts in the high 50s to mid 70s. However, a peak gust of 89 mph was recorded between 0720-0730 PST on the 24th. Strong winds also occurred at the Big Black Mountain (peak gust of 81 mph between 0737 and 0747 on the 24th), West Santa Ysabel (peak gust of 58 mph between 0830 and 0840 on the 24th), Viejas Grade (peak gust of 67 mph between 0830 and 0840 on the 24th), and KG6SIB Descanso (peak gust of 59 mph between 1014 and 1024 on the 24th) mesonet sites. The California Highway Patrol also reported a semi truck knocked on its side near the intersection of Interstate 8 and State Highway 79 due to strong winds at 0937 PST.

High winds occurred at the Alpine RAWS site between 0152 to 2352 PST on the 24th. During this time, sustained winds out of the NE reached 35-45 mph with gusts in the high 50s to low 70s. A peak gust of 72 mph was recorded between 0952 and 1052 PST on the 24th. A wind gust of 73 mph was also measured an 0921 PST near the city of Poway by a trained weather spotter using a vortex anemometer. An additional wind gust of 62 mph was recorded at the Hellhole Canyon Mesonet station between 0610 and 0620 PST. Finally, California Highway Patrol reported power lines and a pole down across both lanes on Sutherland Dam Road at 1328 PST.

From 2030PST on the 2nd to 0600PST on the 3rd, periods of dense fog with visibility below 1/4 mi occurred at the MCAS Miramar Airport ASOS, McClellan-Palomar Airport ASOS, and Brown Field Municipal Airport ASOS. Visibilities below 1/4 mi also occurred at the MCOLF Camp Pendleton ASOS between 0500 and 0700PST on the 3rd, and at the Montgomery Field ASOS between 0100 and 0430PST on the 3rd. USBP Imperial Beach activated their Fog Cutter staffing program due to impact.

The Brown Field Municipal Airport ASOS reported a 1/4 mi visibility from 2253PST on the 3rd to 0807PST on the 4th. Periods of 1/4 mi visibility were also reported between 0200 and 0830PST on the 4th at the Oceanside Municipal Airport, MSAS Miramar Airport, Montgomery Field, and McClellan-Palomar Airport ASOS stations.
The ASOS station at the Gillespie Field Airport in El Cajon reported 1/4 mi visibility from 0155 to 0815PST of February 4th.
The ASOS station at John Wayne Airport reported visibility at or below 1/4 mi between 0304 and 0925PST on February 5th.
A brief period of 1/4 mi visibility occurred at the Fullerton Airport ASOS between 0425 and 0453PST.

The MCAS Miramar Airport ASOS reported visibility at or below than 1/4 mi between 2255 PST on the 4th and 0820 PST on the 5th. The Montgomery Field ASOS reported visibility at or below that 1/4 mi between 2301 PST on the 4th and 0853 PST on the 5th. Periods of fog with 1/4 mi or less visibility were also reported between 0000 and 0800 PST on the 5th at the McClellan-Palomar Airport, Camp Pendleton MCAS Airport,  MCOLF Camp Pendleton (Red Beach) Airport, Oceanside Airport, Lindbergh Field, and Brown Field ASOS stations.

The Fullerton Municipal Airport ASOS reported two periods of fog with 1/4 mi visibility  on February 3rd, with the first period being between 0102 to 0437PST and second period occurring from 0553 to 0800PST.

On the 8th at 1225PST surf of 5 to 8 ft was reported by Surfline at Blacks Beach. Surf fell into the 4 to 6 ft range on the 9th. Increases in surf occurred on the 10th with  Surfline reporting 5 to 8 ft surf at Oceanside, Pacific, Ocean, Imperial, and Salt Creek Beaches at 0700PST. Also on the 10th, a spotter reported 8 to 10 ft surf at Sunset Cliffs Beach and lifeguards reported 7 ft surf at Moonlight Beach, both at 0800PST.

At 1330PST on the 8th Laguna beach lifeguards reported an 18 year old male swept off the rocks and into a cave by 5 to 8 ft surf. Lifeguards were unable to locate the 18 year old, and he became a confirmed fatality on the 19th of February when his body was recovered near the south end of Shell Beach in Three Arch Bay. Surf of 8 to 10 ft with occasional sets to 15 ft was reported by the Huntington Beach lifeguards from 1300PST on the 8th until 1600PST on the 10th. At 0700PST on the 10th Surfline reported 5 to 7 ft surf at Salt Creek Beach.

Fog with visibility of 1/4 mi was reported at the Carlsbad, McClellan-Palomar Airport ASOS station between 0306 and 0653PST. Periods of fog with visibility of 1/4 mi were also reported at the Montgomery Field, Oceanside Municipal Airport, and MSAS Miramar Airport ASOS stations between 0100 and 0600PST.
The ASOS station at Gillespie Field reported fog with visibility below 1/4 mi between 0055 and 0455PST.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: The ASOS station at Corona Airport reported periods of fog with visibility below 1/4 mi between 0056 and 0756PST. Visibility below 1/4 mi was also reported at the Chino Airport ASOS station from 0526 and 0753PST.

A peak wind gust of 58 mph was reported at the Otay Mountain mesonet station between 0714 PST and 0814 PST on the 12th. Sustained winds in the 30s with gusts in the 40s and low 50s were reported between 2014 PST on the 11th and 1514 PST on the 12th. CBS 8 reported a 50 foot tree downed in El Cajon.

High winds occurred at the Sill Hill mesonet between 1950PST on the 11th and 1500PST on the 12th. During this time, winds were sustained out of the E at 35-50 mph with most gusts in the high 50s to mid 60s. However, a peak gust of 82 mph was recorded between 0750 and 0800PST on the 12th. Strong winds also occurred at the Big Black Mountain (peak gust of 66 mph between 1047 and 1057PST on the 12th) and Boulder Creek (peak gust of 60 mph between 0830 and 0840PST on the 12th) mesonet stations.
CBS 8 reported a large (approximately 75-foot tall) eucalyptus tree falling on a car in Encinitas due to strong easterly winds. The report also noted a large tree down in the Rancho Santa Fe area.
The Pleasants Peak mesonet station reported sustained ENE to ESE winds in the low to mid 40s (mph) from 0730 to 0830PST, with a peak gust of 66 mph between 0730 and 0800PST.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: For a period of 1 hour winds were sustained in the upper 30s with a peak gust of 63 mph.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: For a period of 1 hr winds were sustained in the mid 30s with a peak gust of 60 mph.

Multiple trained spotters and a CoCoRaHS observer reported 12 hour snowfall totals of 3 to 6 inches in the city of Big Bear as of 0900PST on the 23rd. Elsewhere in the San Bernardino Mountains spotters reported lighter 12 hour totals at 0900PST on the 23rd, with 1 to 4 inches reported by trained spotters in Wrightwood, 2 inches reported by a trained spotter in Running Springs, and 1 inch reported by a CoCoRaHS observer in Fawnskin.

As of 0900PST on the 23rd 12 hour snowfall totals of 6 inches in Green Valley Lake and Snow Summit, 8 inches at the end of Mt Baldy Road, 3 inches in Forest Falls and Arrowbear, and 2 inches at Onyx Peak and Crestline were reported.
The ski resorts of Mountain High and Snow Valley reported 10 to 14 inches of snow above 7000 feet in the 12 hours preceding 0900 PST on the 23rd.
A CoCoRaHS observer reported a 12 hour snowfall total of 2 inches at 0659 PST on the 23rd.

A trace to 5 inches of snow was reported from 0000 PST on the 1st through 0700 PST on the 2nd across the area. The heaviest total of 5 inches was reported by a spotter 2 mi ESE of Big Bear City. Additional snowfall amounts of 4 inches in Forest Falls, 3 inches in Angelus Oaks, and 2 inches in Green Valley Lake were also reported. Multiple traffic collisions were reported in the mountain top district, especially along Highway 38 between Angelus Oaks and Hatchery Drive (Big Bear). The aforementioned section of Highway 38 was closed.

Trained spotters in Idyllwild and Pine Cove both reported a 24 hour snowfall accumulation of 9.5 inches as of 0800 PST on the 2nd. A third spotter in Pine Cove reported 8 inches of snowfall in 12 hours, as of 2100 PST on the 1st.
At 2100PST on the 1st a trained spotter reported a 12 hour snowfall total of 7 inches at Palomar Mountain.

High winds occurred at the Sill Hill mesonet between 2000 PST on the 5th and 0500 PST on the 6th. During this time, winds were sustained out of the east at 35-45 mph with most gusts in the high 50s to mid 60s mph. However, a peak gust of 71 mph was recorded between 2130 and 2140 PST on the 5th. Strong winds were also reported at the Big Black Mountain mesonet station from 0627 to 0747 PST on the 6th, with a peak gust of 68 mph. Winds were more tame across the rest of the zone, with other mesonet stations reporting gusts from the 30s to low 50s mph.
The public reported a brief cold air funnel over Perris.

A band of rain and thunderstorms moved over the Silverado Burn scar between 1045 and 1200 PST on the 2nd, producing rain rates in excess of 0.5 inches per 30 minutes. As a result, a moderate mud flow occurred in the backyard of a local resident. Video was shared with NWS San Diego.

A series of thunderstorms dropped up to 1 inch depth accumulation of 0.5-in diameter hail on Huntington Beach. The hail covered the beach near Huntington Beach Pier and numerous roads within the city of Huntington Beach. The event received widespread attention from local and national media and extensive social media photos.
The public reported (via social media) 2 to 3 inches of snowfall in 12 hours in the Upper Moonridge area of Big Bear.
Funnel cloud reported near San Bernardino by a local resident.
CHP reported Country Club Drive closed due to water flowing over road at dip.
CalTrans and San Bernardino County Public Works reported power lines down due to 2-6 inches of heavy, wet snow.
CHP reported Quarry Road closed due to flooding in the low water crossing. The road had to be closed twice.
There were reports of San Diego fire and police responding to multiple (6 incidents) swift water rescues in the Midway and Mission Hills neighborhoods.

San Diego Lindbergh Field reported 1.30 inches of rain from 1900-2000 PST. The 6 hour period prior totaled 1.57 inches. The 9 minute period within that main hour, totaled 0.71 inches, which is near the 1/100 return interval.

San Diego Fire and San Diego city lifeguard swift rescue reported at least 3 vehicles under water and responded to high water rescues. The Midway area at the Marine Corps Recruit Depot was closed with a vehicle under 4 feet of water. A vehicle floated and damaged other vehicles. Trash cans were also reported floating. Homes on Torrance and Reynard were flooded with some resident evacuations and garage and minor home damage reported.
A resident reported flooding on El Cajon Boulevard in the North Park neighborhood of San Diego. Based on photos, the water appears to be around 6 to 8 inches deep.
CHP reported a mudslide and rock slide along Old Highway 395 at Dulin Road due to heavy rainfall.

CHP reported water build-up, north of Apple Valley, at the Dale Evans Parkway offramp from I-15 causing vehicles to slide. CHP also reported rock and mud slides into the slow lane, which was shut down near Phelan, as well as Highway 18 flooded west of Victorville with debris in the roadway. A resident near Baldy Mesa reported debris at the junction of Highways 138 and 2.

CHP reported several small fires started by lightning strikes. Vista: lightning struck the hillside and started a fire. Lightning started a fire at Poway Road near Community Road. Lightning also struck a hillside which started a fire near Bancroft Drive and Campo Road in La Mesa. CHP reported a power line and pole down across the roadway at Dye Road and Ramona Street due to lightning.
CHP reported lightning striking a wooden power pole with the pole catching on fire.

CHP reported a second-hand report of flash flood wash out with a depth of 1.5 feet of soil across the pavement at Highland Valley Road and Highway 67 near Ramona, as well as a mud slide across roadway at Highland Valley Road and Archie Moore Road in Poway.

Officials at the Lake Fire and CHP reported several debris flows; one consisting mostly of ash, 4 to 12 inches deep on Highway 38 at the South Fork of the Santa Ana River, as well as one 4 to 5 inches of mud and debris over another portion of the highway. The debris flow near the South Fork was located near one of the fire's highest impact areas, with an estimated 0.33 inches of rain falling on that basin, resulting in the debris flow.
A spotter in Lucerne Valley reported 6 inches of water at the intersection of Buena Vista Road and Buenos Aires Road.
CHP reported one foot of water flowing over Highway 395.
CHP reported a lightning strike that started a small fire near Interstate 8 and Kitchen Creek Road.
A spotter reported 4 to 6 inches of water flowing across Old Highway 80 in Guatay.

A spotter in Lucerne Valley reported a lightning strike onto power lines causing a power outage across a section of the Lucerne Valley area to the southeast of town. A transformer was burned out and tripped a number of circuit breakers on the nearby power grid causing the outage for over an hour in some locations.

A spotter in Phelan reported 4 inches of standing water at the intersection of Phelan Road and Johnson Road as well as ponding on other area roads. The spotter measured 0.23 inches of rain that fell in 20 minutes.
CHP reported power lines down and trees blocking the roadway on San Timoteo Canyon Road near Redlands Blvd.
Highway 18 flooded, with portions of roadway washing away. Several vehicles were stuck in mud.
CHP reported water and debris across the roadway at the intersection of Highway 138 and Evergreen Road. A spotter also reported 1/4 to 3/8 inch hail ongoing with heavy rainfall.

One person was stuck in vehicle that was stuck in flood waters near the railroad tracks at San Timoteo Canyon Road and Live Oak Canyon Road. The car was stuck in mud associated with the flash flooding.

A spotter reported torrential rains, marble sized hail, 2 of standing water in back yard, and 4-6 of water flowing in the road. Another spotter reported 1.00-1.25 of rain in 30 minutes and street flooding in Calimesa.

CHP reported boulders and a large amount of sand in roadway along Highway 74 from heavy rain. A nearby spotter reported 6 inches of water flowing across the road at the Highway 74 and Marshall Avenue cross-section in Valle Vista.
Strong winds from a thunderstorm downed power lines trapping individuals in their car at Oak Glen and Cherry Valley Road.

Photos shared by a local media outlet indicate a downburst/microburst was likely the cause of extensive wind damage in the northeast side of Indian Wells in the Palm Desert Country Club area. Based on damage, winds were estimated at 60 to 70 mph. Multiple large trees and power lines down, along with roofing material and other debris on the ground. Trees fell on an apartment on Elkhorn Trail and damaged the roof. A total of 5288 customers lost power due to downed lines. Fred Waring Drive between El Dorado and Warner Trail in Palm Desert was also closed due to flooding and debris.
The CHP reported a hard closure of roadways near the intersection of Jackson St. and 66th Ave. due to roadway flooding.
Thunderstorm winds knocked over and tree, which blocked the east bound lanes at 66th Ave. and Harrison St. in the town of Valerie.
An trained spotter estimated a 60 mph wind gust just southeast of Borrego Springs.
The CHP reported a vehicle almost submerged in water on one of the on-ramps at the intersection of Highway 163 and Interstate 8 near mission valley.
The CHP reported a stalled tour bus being struck by a rock slide. No injuries occurred but the bus was disabled.
Six large pine trees downed by strong winds near Porto Ct. The largest tree was close to 3 feet in diameter.
CHP reported multiple palm trees on fire due to a lightning strike near the intersection of Jackson St. and 61st Ave.
CHP reported a lightning fire near the intersection of Dillon Rd. and Fargo Canyon Rd. northeast of Indio.
CHP reported a lightning started brush fire at the intersection of Interstate 215 and Harley Knox Blvd.
Small brush fire from a lightning strike reported by CHP.
CHP reported a small brush fire started by a lightning strike.
CHP reported transformer struck by lightning.
CHP and local media reported a small brush fire started by lightning.
CHP reported traffic signals lights knocked out by a lightning strike.
CHP reported a small lightning ignited fire near Keller Peak.
A funnel cloud formed and dissipated in less than one minute.
A trained spotter reported a funnel cloud over Lake Elsinore.
CHP reported a downed palm tree blocking the roadway.
CHP reported a bent electrical pole with wires hanging across the roadway in Nuevo.
Spotter reported 1 to 2 feet of water across US-395 near Shadow Mountain Road.

CHP reported the roadway getting washed away at Lone Pine Canyon Rd. near East Canyon Dr. around 0345 PST. A spotter also reported significant flow through the normally dry Sheep Creek Wash, with lots of tree trunks going by.
CHP reported mud flowing across all lanes with lanes blocked on Interstate 15 near the Cajon Junction.
Spotter reported that Mt. Baldy Rd. was closed at Falls Rd. due to rock/mud slides.
Two swift water rescues were conducted along the Lytle Creek Wash.

CHP reported significant urban flooding in the Moreno Valley area due to a heavy line of thunderstorms. The most significant flooding was reported at the intersection of Interstate 215 and Van Buren Blvd, where 8 cars were stuck in high waters. In Reche Canyon residents were unable to leave their homes due to flooded roadways. Portions of State Highway 60 were also impassable.

CHP reported significant flooding along State Route 91. Vehicles were reported to be stuck in flood waters at the intersections of State Route 91 and Van Buren Blvd., and State Route 91 and Adams St. Mud covered all lanes at the the Central Ave. intersection.
CHP reported a vehicle stuck in flood waters on the interchange between State Routes 71 and 91.
CHP reported a roadway covered in mud at Cajalco Rd. and La Sierra Ave.
CHP reported Chihuahua Valley Rd. closed due to flooding.
The CHP reported a mud and rock slide at the intersection of State Route 78 near Wynola Rd. and a trained spotter reported a debris flow on Banner Grade at mile marker 61.

Training thunderstorms produce heavy rainfall over Ramona with 0.58 in falling between 1401 and 1419 PST.  The CHP reported significant flooding and road closures along 11th St. in Ramona, that the road was completely washed out at the intersection of State Route 78 and Ramona View Dr., and water washing fences and debris over Vista Ramona Rd. A trained spotter reported water 3 ft deep at Ramona Rd. and Lawrence St. with some residents unable to evacuate their homes.
CHP reported a mud and rock slide blocking both lanes of Old Julian Highway.
CHP reported vehicles stranded in water at the intersection of Interstate 5 and Genesee on-ramp.
The CHP reported multiple vehicles stalled in flooded waters on the off-ramp from Fletcher Parkway to Interstate 8. Multiple vehicles were also submerged in flood waters along Alvarado Road.
A large area of blowing dust from a thunderstorm downburst was reported over the Deserts of San Diego County.
Orange County Fire reported that a portion of Silverado Canyon Rd. was temporarily closed, with up to 3 ft of mud across the roadway.
Law enforcement reported two large palm trees fell onto the road at 77th and Harrison, as well as a power pole that fell onto a vehicle near 70th and Pierce Streets.

The damage was west of Highway 111 between 64th and 66th Avenues, paralleling Highway 86 towards the mountains, or approximately 3 1/2 miles. An emergency manager for the Imperial irrigation water district (IID) reported a total of 140 poles damaged, 30 of which were steel.
CHP reported mud and rocks on Highway 78 near Yaqui Pass, closing Highway 78. CHP also reported flash flooding Highway S2 from mile marker 36 to mile marker 44, blocking the southbound lanes.
A trained spotter reported quarter-sized hail and extremely heavy rain.
CHP reported a rock/mudslide blocking the roadway at Highway S-22 near San Felipe Road.
Public reported quarter-inch hail.

A flash flood at Mill Creek crossing...40 feet wide and 8 to 12 inches deep. The head of the flash flood was 3 to 4 feet deep. From Victor Valley news group: flood waters overtook a couple hiking. An off-duty sheriff's deputy heard the couple calling for help and was able to save the young woman, but the man was swept away. The body of the victim, a Rancho Cucamonga man in his 20s, was found shortly after 1800 PST.

Multiple swift water rescues along Bear Valley Road. Water flowed fast down the road with some areas of water around 5 feet deep. A spotter reported water 4-6 deep at the intersection of Bear Valley Road and Apple Valley Road.
Valley of the Falls Drive is washed out and the road was closed.
CHP reported a lightning-started brush fire along Highway 38 near Onyx Peak.
CHP reported a power pole down with live wires in the roadway near the intersection of Cowie Avenue and Lopez Road.
CHP reported vehicle stuck in flood waters at Marshall Street and Lopez Road.
An NWS employee reported a flash flood on Highway 79 in Aguanga leaving 1 foot of mud on the roads. Crews were still cleaning up mud the following day.
A male and a female were in a flood control channel and had to be rescued by the Orange County Fire Department when they were caught off guard by the quickly rising water.

An Orange County Emergency Manager reported a debris flow 2 feet deep over Silverado Canyon Road at Maple Springs Truck Trail. Further downstream, there was another debris flow at Silverado Canyon Road and Oak Lane, but the road was still passable.
A spotter reported the right lane of the Pacific Coast Highway flooded at the intersection with Main Street...road was nearly impassable.
CHP reported the #4 lane of the Avenida Pico southbound on-ramp to I-5 south was completely flooded.

The CBS affiliate in Los Angeles reported two westbound lanes on the 91 freeway at Green River Road in Corona experienced a 50-yard crack as water penetrated the soil underneath the pavement. An emergency repair of the road took place and multiple lanes were closed.

Several businesses in the Midway District were flooded...with water up to knee deep. Several vehicles were flooded in an underground parking garage in Ocean Beach, including a brand new Lamborghini luxury car flooded halfway deep.

One house had damage inside from flooding on the San Manuel Indian Reservation, while a second house had flooding on the outside, but did not sustain any damage inside. This was dubbed the Victoria Weather Incident by the San Bernardino County EOC.

TV media reported several vehicles stuck in flood waters at Grove Avenue and Francis Street in Ontario. Also, Peyton Drive in Chino Hills was shut down in both directions south of Eucalyptus Avenue due to flooding.
Valley Blvd. was flooded between Hermosa and Grand Avenues.
A debris flow along slide creek closed Valley of the Falls Drive, the main road going into Forest Falls. Also, Mill Creek experienced moderate flooding below Forest Falls.

An 8.3 magnitude earthquake that struck off the coast of Chile on the 16th led the National Tsunami Warning Center to issue a tsunami advisory at 1743 PST for a swath of California, from Orange County to north of San Luis Obispo. No action was necessary in San Diego County, the Center determined. All beaches, harbors, piers, and marinas in the Cities of Seal Beach, Huntington Beach, Newport Beach, Laguna Beach, Dana Point and San Clemente, including County and State beaches were closed through 0500 PST on the 17th. Tsunami wave heights were observed to be just under one foot along the Orange County coast. The Orange County EOC reported no significant coastal flooding occurred, but to be aware of the high likelihood of strong currents and waves dangerous to persons in or near the water. The advisory was lifted around 1100 PST on the 17th.
Minor street flooding was reported along Strand Way in Coronado.
Several low lying roads in south Mission Beach were inundated by minor tidal overflow. Minor sandbagging was required to keep water out of some structures.
Minor coastal flooding occurred at the end of Avenida de la Playa Street at the boat launch ramp in La Jolla Shores. Small waves were breaking against the windows of the Marine Room Restaurant.
Minor coastal flooding at the end of Agate Avenue, with several inches of water that flooded a deck at the end of the road.
Minor coastal flooding, with several inches of water in an alley off of Park Avenue in Sunset Beach.
The Santiago Peak mesonet station recorded a wind gust of 71 mph between 530PST and 600PST with sustained winds near or above 50 mph between 400PST and 730PST.
Numerous reports through the broadcast media and social media of a brief landspout near Menifee. The funnel was nearly stationary and occurred over open terrain, with no damage reported.

News media reports flooding near Federal Blvd. and San Miguel Ave in Lemon Grove, with debris also covering the road. Two blocks were impassable with water up to the doors of vehicles on College Ave. off of State Route 94.  Pacific Highway was closed from Juniper to Laurel Streets due to flooding. San Diego County officials reported that Quarry Dip Road was closed between Lakeview Road and State Route 125 in Spring Valley due to flooding.

Pine trees reported knocked down near Mcauliffe Middle School and damaged power lines by Los Alamitos High School. Power poles were knocked down in Seal Beach resulting in a power outage affecting 4242 customers.

A Carlsbad mesonet station (E0995) reported several wind gusts at or above 50 mph between 0000 and 1200 PST on the 16th, including two high wind gusts, 58 mph and 60 mph between 0000 and 0530 PST. The mesonet station at Point Loma Cabrillo reported sustained WNW winds around 40 mph between 0000 and 0430 PST on the 16th, including a peak gust of 58 mph measured twice between 0245-0315 PST.

Solana Beach lifeguards reported 6 foot surf with max sets to 8 feet. Mission Beach lifeguards reported 7 foot surf with max sets to 9 feet. Surfline reports 5 to 8 foot surf at Ocean Beach and 5 to 7 foot surf at Imperial Beach.

Power company reported flooding of patios on Park Avenue, just south of Seal Beach, as well as minor flooding on Pacific Coast Highway and 4 inches of water on Bayview Drive on Sunset Island in Huntington Beach.

Minor tidal flooding occurred in the Midway District in the area of Barnett Ave and Midway Dr., as well as Harbor Drive in Point Loma due to tides overwhelming the storm drains. An NWS employee reported minor tidal flooding of side streets between San Fernando place and San Gabriel place, east of Mission Blvd in south Mission Beach, as well as the curb on the east side of Mission Blvd in that area. The employee also reported minor coastal flooding of Avenida de la Playa in La Jolla,  water, seaweed and foam washing over the sidewalk past the beach barrier wall in La Jolla Shores, and the beach parking lot. The south end of Seacoast Drive in Imperial Beach also saw minor tidal flooding.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: AWOS station Corona Airport /Ajo/ temperature reached 29 to 32 degrees for a duration of 4 hours. Mesonet station Calimesa (4 s) /up331/. temperature reached 31 to 32 degrees for a duration of 4 hours.  AWOS station March AFB /RIV/ temperature reached 29 to 32 degrees for a duration of 5 hours. Mesonet station Hemet (2 n) /c3539/ temperature reached 32 degrees for a duration of 50 minutes.

The following stations' temperatures dropped to between 22-27 degrees for 3 to 6 hours the night of the 27th into the 28th: Lucerne Valley, Hesperia (mesonet and COOP), Pinon Hills, Apple Valley (mesonet and Airport), Mountain View Acres, and Helendale.

The Burns Canyon mesonet station reported a sustained wind of 57 mph and a peak wind gust of 80 mph between 1851 and 1951PST. Additional gusts in the 60 to 75 mph range were reported between 1751 and 2351PST.
The Volcan Mt. mesonet reported a wind gust of 71 mph.
The Anza Borrego Desert mesonet reported multiple wind gusts to 59 mph.
CHP reported roadway flooding with rocks and debris in the road. Water undermined power poles along the side of the road.
A strong burst of northwest winds produced near zero visibility and a 54 mph wind gust in Palm Springs.
The Los Alamitos U. S. Army Airfield ASOS reported predominately dense fog, with visibility of 1/4 mile or less for 10 hours.
The Fullerton Municipal Airport ASOS reported a prolonged period of dense fog, with visibility of 1/4 mile or less impacting the airport for just over 5 hours.
The John Wayne Airport ASOS reported a prolonged period of dense fog, with visibility of 1/4 mile or less, that impacted the airport for just over 7 hours.
The McClellan-Palomar Airport ASOS reported a prolonged period of dense fog, with visibility of 1/4 mile or less impacting the airport for nearly over 12 hours.
The Montgomery Field ASOS reported periods of dense fog, with visibility of 1/4 mile or less over a period of 13 hours.
The Brown Field Municipal Airport ASOS reported intermittent periods of dense fog, with visibility of 1/4 mile or less over a period of 13 hours.
The North Island Naval Air Station ASOS reported a 4 hour period of dense fog, with visibility of 1/4 mile or less.
The San Diego Lindbergh Field ASOS reported a brief 1 hour period of dense fog, with visibility of 1/4 mile or less.
Huntington Beach lifeguards reported 7 to 10 ft surf at the Huntington Beach Pier.
Newport Beach lifeguards reported 7 to 9 ft surf.
San Clemente City lifeguards reported 7 to 9 ft surf.
Solana Beach lifeguards reported 7 to 10 ft surf.
The Mission Beach lifeguards reported 7 to 10 ft surf.
Ocean Beach pier was closed for two days due to 12 to 13 ft sets. Minor damage to a pier railing and a flipped over a concrete bench were reported.
Three male surfers were rescued from the rocks at Sunset Cliffs. Two of the surfers suffered minor injuries, while the third suffered significant injuries to his head and neck.
Surf of 8 to 12 ft was reported at Blacks Beach.
Minor coastal flooding near the intersections of Ocean Front Rd. and 24th, 23rd, 19th, 18th, and 17th in Del Mar. Flooding was due to surf greater than 7 ft and astronomical high tide near 6.5 ft.
Minor coastal flooding of the south end of Seacoast Dr. in Imperial Beach, due to surf greater than 7 ft and an astronomical high tide near 6.5 ft.
Minor coastal flooding of the La Jolla Shores boardwalk. The surf was greater than 7 ft with a high tide near 6.5 feet.
Minor coastal flooding of the strand in Oceanside Beach. Surf in excess of 7 ft and a high tide near 6.5 ft were the primary causes.
Minor coastal flooding occurred along the boardwalk in Pacific Beach, from Pacific Beach Dr. to Santa Clara Place. Surf greater than 7 ft and a high tide near 6.5 ft were occurring at the time.
The Mission Beach lifeguards reported 7 to 10 ft surf.
The Mission Beach lifeguards reported 7 to 8 ft surf.
The Huntington Beach lifeguards reported 7 to 8 ft surf.
The Huntington Beach lifeguards reported 7 to 10 ft surf.
Occasional sets of 7 to 8 ft were reported at Blacks Beach.
Occasional sets of 7 to 8 ft were reported at Sunset Cliffs Beach.
High surf forced the precautionary closure of the Ocean Beach Pier.
Multiple gusts to 59 mph were reported at the Borrego Springs mesonet.
The Harrison Park mesonet station reported sustained winds to 51 mph and a wind gust of 70 mph.
The Otay Mountain mesonet station reported sustained winds in the low to mid 40s with a gust of 58 mph.
A girl and her father were injured by a falling tree at Big Rock Park. Near by mesonet stations were reported wind gusts of 25 to 30 mph.
The mesonet station at Sill Hill reported sustained winds over 50 mph for 30 min and a gust of 70 mph between 0410 and 0420PST.
Six utility poles were downed by strong winds.
A large tree was blown down by strong winds. The tree partially blocked Highway 189 near Blue Jay cutoff.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Strong winds flipped a semitrailer near the intersection of Interstate 10 and Cherry Ave.

events.event_narrative: Santa Ana winds surfaced at Ontario International Airport resulting in a wind gust of 62 mph and sustained winds in the upper 30s.

events.event_narrative: Winds toppled a tree onto a home in the 10700 Block of Holmes Ave., in Jurupa Valley.
The Pleasants Peak mesonet station recorded multiple gusts over 70 mph and sustained winds as high as 66 mph over a 6 hour period.
The Fremont Canyon mesonet recorded a wind gust of 70 mph and sustained winds to 48 mph.
Multiple trees downed and blocking lanes near the intersection of Vista Del Verde and Coto De Caza Dr.
The Santiago Peak mesonet reported multiple gusts into the mid and upper 70s with a max sustained wind of 69 mph.

Winds downed trees in Wrightwood and caused damage to multiple utility poles in the near Lake Arrowhead. The strongest measured winds were at the Heaps Peak mesonet station, where sustained winds in the upper 30s and a peak gust of 71 mph occurred from 1315 to 1515 PST.

A mesonet station 3 miles southwest of Hesperia reported a peak wind gust of 60 mph and sustianed winds in the low 30s. Strong wind gusts in the 40 to 50 mph range were reported elsewhere in the upper deserts.
Multiple mesonet stations reported wind gusts in the 50 to 70 mph range. Both the Serra Peak and Fremont Canyon mesonets reported peak wind gusts of 74 mph.
The Mateo Ridge mesonet reported wind gusts in excess of 58 mph for 5 hours, with a peak gust of 74 mph between 1922 and 2022 PST. Numerous large trees were downed in the surrounding valleys.

The San Clemente Ridge mesonet station reported a gust to 59 mph, with multiple additional gusts in excess of 50 mph between 1720 and 2320 PST. Tree damage was reported over other inland portions of the county.
The San Clemente Pier reported sustained winds in excess of 40 mph for a period of 8 hours, with a peak of 47 mph. Winds caused tree damage along the coast.
Thunderstorm wind gust estimated at 60 mph by a trained spotter.
CHP reported 1.5 ft diameter 100 ft tall eucalyptus tree downed by strong winds. The tree damaged a street sign.
The Oceanside Jetty reported a 60 mph thunderstorm wind gust.
The Silver Strand mesonet reported a thunderstorm wind gust of 59 mph.
The mesonet station at Mission Trails reported a 68 mph thunderstorm wind gust.
A 59 mph thunderstorm wind gust reported at the Anderson Valley mesonet.

Multiple mesonet stations at Otay Mountain reported wind gusts in excess of 58 mph between 1614 and 2359 PST, with a peak gust of 74 mph. Nearby Lyons Peak gusted to 60 mph between 2135 and 2145 PST. Numerous large trees were downed in the surrounding valleys.

The Otay Mountain mesonet reported wind gusts in excess of 58 mph with a peak gust of 67 mph from 0000 to 0314 PST. Widespread 40 to 55 mph gusts occurred over the rest of the San Diego County Valleys.

Multiple mesonet stations measured wind gusts in excess of 58 mph all along the San Diego County coast. The strongest gust occurred at Cabrillo National Monument where a 64 mph gust was reported. The winds caused extensive tree damage along the coast.

A pine tree 8 ft in diameter succumbed to strong winds, falling on 4 cars and killing a 48 year old woman who was driving down Ingraham Street. An additional tree fell during the cleanup operations, injuring 2 reporters.
The 20 ft light tower on the North Mission Bay Jetty was destroyed by high winds. Winds at surrounding coastal mesonet sites were gusting to 60 mph. The tower was a steel lattice structure.

Multiple mesonet stations reported winds in excess of 70 mph during this period. The strongest winds were reported at the Harrison Park and Luck Five Ranch mesonets, where respective 85 mph and 80 mph wind gusts occurred between 1520 and 1530 PST.
Multiple mesonet stations reported wind gusts in excess of 70 mph during this period, with a peak gust of 72 mph at the Harrison Park mesonet between 2150 and 2200 PST.
High winds blew out windows in a downtown skyscraper.
Multiple boats were pulled from their moorings by strong winds, they were blown up against a boardwalk and partially submerged.

San Bernardino Department of Public Works reported 14 inches of storm total snowfall in Fawnskin, elevation 6825 ft.

Sections of two stable roofs torn off by strong thunderstorm wind gusts at the San Luis Rey Equestrian Training Facility. An NWS employee went to survey and take pictures of the damage.
Strong thunderstorm winds damaged 8 buildings and downed power lines in Vista. A tornado is possible, but still under investigation.

An NWS employee reported 15 trees snapped or uprooted near Poway Road and Sabre Springs Road, with some being as large as 18 inches in diameter. Broadcast media reported strong winds in Poway toppled a tree, which fell onto a car.

Two-day snowfall totals for Riverside County mountain locations include: 14-16 inches at Pine Cove and Fern Valley near Idyllwild and 23 inches at the Long Valley Ranger Station in San Jacinto State Park.

CHP reported the Devore Road off-ramp from I-215 was closed due to flooding, as well as boulders blocking the down-bound lanes of Highway 18 south of Crestline. Broadcast media reported San Timoteo Canyon Road closed south of Redlands because of a mud and rock slide.

A funnel cloud was sighted by several people in south San Clemente near the Orange County and San Diego County border. One house was damaged, though most likely wet microburst damage, tornado not confirmed.

Orange County Public Works reported three moderate debris flows in the Silverado Canyon area between 1200-1400 PST on the 6th. The first was 40-50 cubic yards long and occurred at Silverado Canyon Road and Hafra Way blocking the road. The second was at the K-rail 100-200 feet past Smeisic Ranch, was 1-2 feet deep and 10 cubic yards long and blocked Silverado Canyon Road at that location. The third was at the Smeisic Ranch ravine about 20-30 cubic yards across but did not cross the road. The road was cleared and re-opened at 0100 on the 7th. As of 1330 PST, rainfall amounts over past 6 hours were 1.22 inches, 0.94 inches over past 3 hours and 0.39 inches over past hour at Silverado Motorway Gage. Rainfall of 2.2 inches over past 6 hours, 1.65 inches over past 3 hours, and 0.71 inches over past hour were observed at Upper Silverado Canyon.

CHP reported a mud and rock slide at La Cresta Road and Coyote Ridge Road in Granite Hills, just east of El Cajon.

A mudslide in the Rancho San Diego area of El Cajon on Willow Glen sent mud flowing into several homes and closed Dehesa Elementary School for at least 2 days. Nearby, the public reported 6 inches of mud across all lanes at Dehesa Road near Stallion Oaks Road.

CHP reported the northbound off-ramp from Interstate 5 to Grand Avenue was closed due to severe flooding, as well as the Genesee Avenue off-ramp from Interstate 5 was flooded with several cars stuck. TV media reported a sinkhole at the end of Avenida de la Playa in la Jolla as a result of the heavy rain. A little further south the public reported 6-12 of water flowing down Newport Avenue, over the sidewalks with minor flooding of local businesses in Ocean Beach. The public reported Ward Road in Mission Valley was flooded with several cars submerged. Nine high water rescues were performed in the greater San Diego area on January 6th.

An NWS San Diego employee reported flash flooding near Los Coches and Business 8 with between 6 inches and 2.5 feet of water flowing over the road, as well as flash flooding near El Cajon Blvd. and Main Street with 6-12 of water flowing over the road. A local spotter reported 1.5 feet of water on Johnson Ave. next to Parkway Plaza in El Cajon.

The San Diego River at Fashion Valley crested above action stage 4 times, and above flood stage once between the afternoon of the 5th and the afternoon of the 7th. The river remained above action stage for almost this entire time, except for a brief period below that level during the afternoon of the 6th. Flood stage was reached between 1930-2130 PST on the 5th, cresting at 11.9 feet around 2000 PST. This resulted in mostly minor flooding of surrounding areas in Mission Valley, including low water crossings and nearby parking lots.

The Border Fire began from unknown causes on the 19th of June. A local couple was killed on their property by the fire. Five structures and eleven outbuildings were destroyed, with one other home suffering damage. The fire also destroyed numerous power and phone lines. Firefighters acquired 100% containment on the fire June 30th, after 7,609 acres had been burned.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: The Checkpoint Fire was short lived but significant. It burned 12 acres and several small structures over 3.5 hours, caused 1 minor injury to a firefighter, and caused a partial closure of I-15 during rush hour.
The Roblar Fire began on the 21st and grew to over 1,000 acres in just 24 hours. The fire would consume a total of 1,245 acres before it was contained on the 30th.
Lifeguards at Huntington beach reported 6 to 8 ft surf with occasional sets to 9 ft on the 1st.

A spotter reported 6 inches of water about 50 feet wide flowing down Buena Vista Road with dirt and rock on the roads, including Highway 18 and Custer Road. Total rain of 1.5 inches reported. Another spotter reported 1 inch of rain in ten minutes nearby.
Lifeguards in Huntington Beach and Newport Beach reported sets to 8 ft.
Lifeguards in Huntington Beach and Newport Beach reported surf heights to 8 ft.

A band of convection formed along the leading edge of moisture from former Hurricane Paine as it moved northward. Numerous lightning strikes occurred in San Diego County setting palm trees on fire and causing power outages to 4000 customers.
A spotter reported minor urban flooding from a nearly stationary thunderstorm in Pine Valley.
Strong winds produced blowing dust and sand with visibility of 1/2 t 3/4 of a mile, impacting travel on highway 78 near Ocotillo Wells.
Strong winds produced blowing dust and sand with visibility of 1/2 t 3/4 of a mile, impacting travel in Hesperia.

A survey of 19 local hospitals indicated 20 heat related 911 calls over two days, with 3 heat related injuries and 1 death. These numbers do not include urgent care facilities and are therefore likely underdone.
CHP reported a fire due to power lines downed from a lightning strike.
Multiple utility poles down, likely caused by frequent cloud to ground lightning.
Multiple power lines and transformers damaged by lightning strikes.

Several power poles down across streets in Highland, with lines down across yards, likely due to a lightning strike. Lightning struck a power pole, pole and lines down on roadway southeast of Apple Valley.
The southbound lane on Highway 247 at Larrea Road was completely flooded.
Lightning struck a tree which caught on fire.
A teenage football player was sent to the emergency room after getting struck by lightning at Grossmont High School. The player survived the strike.

Multiple ASOS stations reported dense fog with a visibility of 1/4 mile or less along the San Diego County Coast. Mission Beach Lifeguards also reported visibility of 100 ft or less at 0700 PST. The fog slowed the morning commute, especially along the I-5 corridor.
Multiple trained spotters reported dense fog with visibility of 1/8-1/4 mile.
Dense fog with a visibility of 1/4 mile or less impacted KMYF, KSDM, and KCRQ for several hours.
A trained spotter reported dense fog with a visibility of 1/4 mile in Huntington Beach. Visibility was also reduced to 1/4 mile at KSNA for several hours.

Surf, with frequent sets to 8 ft, impacted primarily west facing beaches along the San Diego County coast. The highest sets were reported from La Jolla southward on the 9th and 10th, where the Children's Pool Walk, and Ocean Beach Piers were closed. A 24 ft private vessel fishing for Lobster capsized in the surf zone off Windansea Beach at 1800 PST on the 9th. The owner of the vessel drowned, and 4 other passengers were injured. One lifeguard was injured by surf during the rescue attempt.
Huntington Beach lifeguards reported frequent sets to 7 ft throughout the afternoon and evening of the 9th. Occasional sets to 7 ft persisted thereafter through the 11th.
Mission Beach lifeguards reported sets to 8 ft during the afternoon and evening hours on the 4th.
Mission Beach Lifeguards and several public sources reported sets to 8 ft south of Del Mar.
Surf, with sets of 5 to 8 ft, was reported at Huntington Beach.

Heavy snow fell on elevations above 5000 ft between 1400 and 2000 PST on the 26th. This was the first snow of the season and caught many holiday travelers off-guard, resulting in numerous accidents. Chain restrictions were implemented on Highways 18 and 38. Seven hour snowfall totals ranged from 6 inches at Green Valley Lake, Big Bear|and Forest Falls, to 2 inches in Crestline.

Heavy snow began shortly after 1500 PST and lasted through 2100 PST. Idyllwild reported 3-4 inches of snow, with up to 6 inches at the Long Valley Ranger Station. Chain restrictions were implemented on Highway 243.
Rangers at the Long Valley Ranger Station reported sustained winds of 50 mph with gusts to 70 mph. No significant impacts reported.

The Burns Canyon mesonet station reported a wind gust of 74 mph with sustained winds up to 50 mph between 1951 and 2151 PST on the 26th. Winds remained strong through the 27th with periodic gusts of 50-65 mph. An additional peak on the 28th brought a 76 mph gust between 0751 and 0851 PST. No significant impacts reported.

The Volcan Mountain mesonet station reported wind gusts of 60-80 mph with sustained winds of 35-55 mph. Winds peaked between 1550 and 1600 PST with sustained winds of 57 mph and a gust to 82. Winds were strong across the rest of the San Diego County mountains as well wind numerous 50-75 mph wind gust reports. No significant impacts were reported.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Northerly winds gusting to 70 mph downed numerous trees below the Cajon Pass. The fallen trees blocked roadways and caused at least 11,000 power outages. Planes were grounded at Ontario International Airport, where a peak wind gust of 68 mph broke terminal windows and fanned a small brush fire.
Strong northerly winds downed several trees in the vicinity of the Cajon Pass. One tree near Crestline fell, blocking a roadway.
Strong northeasterly winds downed numerous trees in the vicinity Irvine, Santa Ana and Orange. Approximately 85 customers lost power in the city of Santa Ana.
