Strong northeasterly winds developed in the northern Santa Ana Mountains. On the morning of the 3rd, Pleasants Peak reported and peak gust of 88 mph at 0630PST and Fremont Canyon gusted to 80 mph at 0651PST.

events.cz_name: SAN MATEO PT TO MEXICAN BDR 30 TO 60NM
events.event_narrative: The San Clemente Basin Buoy reported wind gusts of 40-42 mph between 1950 and 2250PST on the 16th. The buoy also reported seas of 9-11 ft.

The Volcan Mountain mesonet station reported a 70 mph wind gust between 0500 and 0510PST. Other stations reported westerly wind gusts in the 40-55 mph range along the desert slopes in San Diego County.
A mountain wave surfaced, downing large tree limbs in southern La Quinta. Several miles east the wave produced a gust of 56 mph at Jacqueline Cochran Regional Airport in Thermal.
A surfacing mountain wave produced a strong wind gust that lifted part of a roof from a home in southwestern Lucerne Valley.
A 71 mph westerly wind gust was reported by the Whitewater mesonet station. Strong wind gusts to 55 mph buffeted other eastern portions of the San Gorgonio Pass.

Strong winds over the San Bernardino County Mountains gusted in the 40-60 mph range, causing minor power line and tree damage in Big Bear City. East of Big Bear City, the mesonet station in Burns Canyon reported wind gusts in excess of 70 mph between 1351  and 1851PST, with a peak gust of 85 mph.

Winds briefly gusted to 59 mph out of the northeast at Hellhole Canyon. Numerous gusts of 45 to 55 mph were reported between 1800 and 2359PST on the 21st. Elsewhere in the San Diego County Valleys numerous 35 to 55 mph gusts form the northeast were reported during the same period.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: The RAWS station at Highland Springs reported multiple northeast wind gusts in excess of 58 mph with a peak of 67 mph between 2216 and 2316PST. Breezy northeast winds were reported over the rest of the Inland Empire, but the strongest winds were focused below the San Gorgonio Pass.

Multiple spotters reported 12 hour snowfall totals of 18 inches in Big Bear between 2100PST on the 23rd and 0900PST on the 24th. Other 12 hour totals in the San Bernardino County Mountains included 18 inches near Green Valley Lake, 12 inches in Forest Falls, 11 inches in Wrightwood, and 10 inches in Lake Arrowhead.

A spotter in Fern Valley reported an 11 hour snowfall total of 14 inches between 2200PST on the 23rd and 0900PST on the 24th. Another spotter reported 7 inches of snow in Idyllwild during this same period.

Spotters in Julian and at Mt. Laguna reported 10 hour snowfall totals of 6 inches between 2200PST on the 23rd and 0800PST on the 24th. During the same period 5 inches fell at Palomar Mountain, 2 inches in Guatay and 1 inch in Pine Valley.

Winds at Volcan Mountain gusted in excess of 70 mph for 2 hours, with peak gust of 73 mph. Numerous other stations in the San Diego County Mountains gusted between 55 and 70 mph between 0800 and 1800PST on the 24th. No damage was reported.

The RAWS station in Burns Canyon measured wind gusts in excess of 70 mph for 2 hours, with a peak of 80 mph during a surfacing mountain wave. Other stations in the area measured gusts between 35 mph and 50 mph during the same period.

CHP reported a tree down along Sweetwater Rd. in Lemon Grove. Peak gusts in the area were near 40 mph, with most gusts in the 25-35 mph range. This was the only significant damage report along the coast.
Several trees were downed near Orange Coast College in Costa Mesa. Winds in the area were predominantly gusting 25-35 mph with isolated gusts to 40 mph.

A large tree downed by winds blocked the road near the intersection of Rancho Bernardo Rd. and Alva Rd. Peak gusts in the area were near 40 mph, with most gusts in the 25-35 mph range. This was the only significant damage report in the valleys.
Swarthout Canyon Rd. was closed due to flooding, this is a re-occurring issue.

Dense fog and rain limited visibility along Interstate 8 through the San Diego County Mountains. One person was killed when her vehicle drove off a cliff. Weather was confirmed as in influencing factor.

Very strong mountain wave activity surfaced along the eastern slopes of the San Bernardino Mountains over an 8 hours period. A peak gust of 107 mph was reported between 2351PST on the 8th and 0051PST on the 9th. Numerous gusts in the 80-95 mph range were also reported during this period in Burns Canyon.
An 80 ft oak tree fell on a mini van killing the driver. Saturated soils were likely an influencing factor. Winds were light at the time.
Numerous reports of urban street flooding throughout the Inland Empire that produced significant impacts for the evening commute. The HOV lane along Interstate 60 was closed due to flooding.
Minor street flooding from Newport Beach to Fountain Valley. A tree was uprooted near the Orange County Fairgrounds, likely due to a combination of saturated soil and gusty winds.

A 24 hour snowfall of 10-18 inches was reported in Big Bear Lake, with 22 inches at the top of Big Bear resort as of 0900PST on the 13th. Other 24 hours snowfall reports from the area included 14-16 inches in Running Springs and Green Valley Lake, 15 inches in Arrorbear Lake, 10 inches at the end of Mt. Baldy Rd., and 7 inches in Forest Falls, Angelus Oaks and Blue Jay. Light snow continued after 0900PST on the 13th, but impacts and accumulations were minimal.

Spotters in Idyllwild reported 9-10 inches of snow in 21 hours, ending at 0900PST on the 13th. The majority of the snow fell between 1200 and 2200PST on the 12th. Some power outages were also reported.
A severe squall moved from Newport Beach to Santa Ana, downing multiple trees, knocking out power to 63 homes and causing minor roof damage.

A severe squall produced a swath of 60-70 mph winds from Imperial Beach to Lawson Creek. At least 6 mesonet stations reported peak wind gusts in excess of 58 mph including a 68 mph gust at Lawson Creek and 64 mph gust at Boarder Field. Hundreds of trees were downed. Roof damage was also reported. One person was injured when a tree fell on their car in Lakeside.
A squall produced a short burst of 50-65 mph winds between Cardiff by the Sea and Lake Hodges. The mesonet station at Elfin Forest reported a peak wind gust of 64 mph. Tree damage was also reported.
A severe squall produced 60-70 mph wind gusts over northern Camp Pendleton. A peak gust of 70 mph was measured at Mateo Ridge with an additional 64 mph gust recorded at Case Springs.
The CHP reported a vehicle in jeopardy of being washed off a bridge near Sandia Creek Dr. and Rock Mountain Rd.
Pala Temecula Rd. was closed due to flooding and rocks in the roadway.
Roadway closure due to flooding on Cole Grade Rd.

Rapid water rises after 1500PST flooded parts of Carroll Canyon Rd with 1-2 ft of rushing water. The flow carried dumpsters and debris. Three people were trapped in their vehicle that stalled as the water rose rapidly, resulting in multiple swift water rescues around 1530PST.
A swift water rescue to save 2 people and a dog was conducted at the intersection of University Ave. and Aragon Dr. in the neighborhood of Rolando.
Six feet of water inundated an apartment building in City Heights on 48th street. One family nearly drowned due to the flood.

Multiple low water crossings were closed due to rapid rises in the San Diego River, including Camino Del Rio and Ward Rd. Several cars were submerged by the rapidly rising waters. The Fashion Valley Transit Center was closed due to flooding. The river peaked at 0215PST on the 21st with a crest of 11.81 ft.
A mud slide blocked both lanes of Old Highway 80.

Heavy mountain rain produced flows in the Whitewater River and Palm Canyon Creek that lead to periodic closures of low water crossings in the Coachella Valley, including: Golf Club Dr., Gene Autry Trail., Indian Canyon Dr., Vista Chino Rd., Frank Sinatra Dr., Araby Dr. and Vista Chino.

Rapid water rises along Temecula Creek caused flooding in south Temecula. Firefighters rescued a woman stranded on a small island in Temecula Creek. The woman was transported to the hospital with minor injuries.
CHP reported 6 flooded roadways in Paloma Valley with one vehicle briefly stranded.
Swift water rescue conducted near North Golf Course in Sun City.
Widespread flooding occurred near Gilman Springs Rd. and Soboba Rd. in San Jacinto with multiple water rescues conducted.
CHP reported 3 vehicles submerged and stuck in water on Antonio Pkwy. in Las Flores.

Widespread heavy rain brought flash flooding to a large portion of Orange County. A water rescue occurred on Hamilton Ave. at the Santa Ana River in Huntington Beach. Numerous streets from Sunset Beach to Santa Ana to Newport Beach were also flooded with 1-3 ft of water. Numerous reports of vehicles stranded in flood waters were received, including half a dozen along Highway 55.

Cal Fire and Riverside County Firefighters conducted 2 water rescues along the Temescal Wash in Alberhill near the intersection of Hostettler Rd. and Temescal Canyon Rd. Four vehicles were stranded in 2-3 ft of water.
Cal Fire reported of a swift water rescue along the Pyrite Channel near Van Buren Blvd.
Highway 83 between Pine Ave. and Highway 71 closed due to flooding along Chino Creek.

Excessive rain induced flash flooding in the Cajon Wash. A swift water rescue was conducted to pull 2 people from the wash near Swarthout Canyon Road. Further south along the wash, San Bernardino County Public Works closed Glen Helen Pkwy. from Glen Helen Rd. to Cajon Blvd. for an extended period.
Roadway closure at the intersection of Highway 138 and 173 with a swift water rescue and 2 vehicles stranded in flood waters.
Heavy mountain rain drained into the deserts leading to flooding along several area roadways. A closure occurred along Highway 18 west of Victorville due to flooding across all lanes.
Heavy mountain rains produced flows from the Mojave Dam. Flow through the Mojave River lead to a closure of Rock Springs Rd. due to 6-8 inches of water flowing over the low water crossing.

Strong winds impacted the coast over a 22 hour period. Strongest winds, with gusts in the 40-50 mph range occurred between 1300 and 1800PST on the 20th. Outside of this period, peak gusts were in the 25-35 mph range along the coast. The winds combined with saturated grounds to down hundreds of trees that fell on cars and structures. Four students were hospitalized when a large tree fell on them at Chula Vista Middle School.

Local mesonets reported wind gusts in the 25-40 mph range between 1300PST on the 20th and 0400PST on the 21st. Highest gusts occurred between 1400 and 1800PST. The winds combined with saturated soils to down numerous trees.
The Lake Matthews Raws station reported a 67 mph gust between 1316 and 1416 PST. In Temescal Valley a large tree was blown down blocking the Knabe Rd. near Clay Canyon Dr.
Power lines downed in Hesperia and Phelan. Numerous gusts in the 50 mph range were reported, including a 53 mph gust at Victorville Airport.

The mesonet station in Burns Canyon reported wind gusts in excess of 70 mph between 1051 and 1351PST, with a peak of 99 mph between 1151 and 1251PST. Power lines were downed in Skyforest and Twin Peaks around 0930PST. A nearby mesonet station in Lake Arrowhead reported a peak gust of 50 mph between 0946 and 1001PST.
An avalanche on Mt. Baldy trapped 3 hikers. Two of the hikers were injured.

Periods of strong Santa Ana Winds blew through the passes and canyons of the Santa Ana Mountains between 2200PST on the 26th and 1200PST on the 28th. Strongest winds surfaced between 0700 and 1000PST on the 27th with a peak gust of 88 mph at Pleasants Peak and 87 mph in Fremont Canyon.
Several periods of gusty Santa Ana winds downed a tree near Peter's Canyon Regional Park and power lines in eastern Villa Park.
Santa Ana Winds with gusts of 40-45 mph surfaced briefly on the morning of the 27th in Santa Ana and Irvine. Winds downed a large tree that block 3 lanes along Interstate 405.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Periods of gusty Santa Ana winds developed between 0000PST on the 27th and 1200PST on the 28th. Strongest winds were reported in Devore with a peak gust of 71 mph between 0810 and 0910PST on the 27th. The winds downed power lines and trees in San Bernardino and Ontario. Two big rigs overturned, one near Mira Loma and another at the Interstate 10 and 15 inter-change.
The mesonet station at Sill Hill reported high winds with a peak gust of 75 mph between 0610 and 0620PST.

The Sill Hill mesonet reported a second period of high winds between 1730PST on the 27th and 1210PST on the 28th, with numerous gusts in excess of 70 mph and a peak gust of 99 mph between 0140 and 0150PST on the 28th. Other stations in the mountains reported wind gusts in the 40-60 mph range during the same period. Several big rigs were overturned along Interstate 8 and multiple trees were blown down along Highway 79.

The mesonet station in Potrero measured a 60 mph gust between 2240 and 2230PST, and the mesonet at Dye Mtn. measured a 58 mph gust between 2240 and 2250PST. Elsewhere, peak gusts were in the 35-55 mph range between 0700PST on the 27th and 1200PST on the 28th. A couple trees were downed near Fallbrook.

Locally gusty Santa Ana Winds briefly surfaced along the coast of San Diego County, including parts of the San Diego Metro. Peak gusts were in the 30-45 mph range. Winds combined with saturated soils to down at least 3 large trees in Downtown San Diego and Mission Valley. The trees crushed 2 cars.

events.cz_name: SAN MATEO PT TO MEXICAN BDR 30 TO 60NM
events.event_narrative: The San Clemente Basin Buoy reported wind gusts in excess of 34 knots for 5 hours, with a peak gust of 40 kt.
Lifeguards reported minor tidal overflow into low lying streets and parking lots in Imperial Beach and Oceanside (the Strand) with a high tide near 7 ft and 2-4 ft surf.
Numerous reports of urban street flooding throughout the Inland Empire that produced significant impacts for the evening commute.

Lifeguards along the San Diego County coast reported 7 to 10 ft surf between the 20th and 24th. Peak sets of 12-15 ft were reported on the 22nd and 21st south of Carlsbad. Two women were swept from the rocks in Sunset Cliffs by surf up to 15 ft between 1700 and 1800PST on the 21st. One woman was killed and the second suffered serious injuries. Two lifeguards were also injured during the rescue attempt. Significant beach erosion and minor coastal flooding occurred along the coast. The Imperial Beach Pier was closed for a time.

A swift water rescue team pulled a man from a submerged car in a small creek near Old Highway 395 and 5th St. in Rainbow. A young boy, also in the car, was swept down stream before rescuers arrived. The boys body was recovered on the 26th.
Lifeguards reported 7-8 ft surf between the 20th and 24th. Surf peaked on the the 21st and 22nd with 9-10 ft sets in Huntington Beach.

A bank of dense fog dropped visibility at San Diego International from 10 miles to 1/4 mile in just 15 minutes in between 1715 and 1730PST. The fog had a significant impact on the evening flight schedule, forcing 75 cancellations, 39 delays and 29 diversions to LAX. Fog remained dense with a visibility of 1/4 mile or less through 0845PST on the 1st of February.

The Santa Margarita River river gauge at Ysidora recorded a crest of 14.60 ft at 2345PST. This was the 6th highest crest on record and exceeded moderate flood stage by 1.3 ft. Impacts to Camp Pendleton Marine Corps Base are unknown.
Rangers at the Long Valley Ranger Station reported 12 inches of new snow at 8,400 ft over a 13 hour period.

A spotter in Moonridge reported 6-8 inches of new snow over a 7 hour period. Elsewhere,  3-5 inches was reported in Big Bear Lake and 3 inches at the end Mt. Baldy Rd., Arrowbear Lake, Green Valley Lake and Running Springs.

Very heavy snows were reported by San Bernardino County Public Works over a 24 hour period. Chain restrictions were widespread above 4,000 ft. Snow amounts ranged from a trace to 1 ft between 4,000 and 5,500 ft, while locations above 5,500 ft reported 1 to 2.5 ft of new snow. Some local totals included 31 inches in Green Valley Lake, 27 inches at Mt. Baldy, 20-27 inches in Big Bear Lake, 26 inches in Running Springs and Arrowbear Lake, 16 inches in Barton Flats, 15 inches in Angelus Oaks, and 11 inches in Wrightwood.
Rangers at the Long Valley Ranger Station reported 33 inches of new snow over a 24 hour period at 8,400 ft. Chain restrictions were required on local roadways.
The Long Valley Ranger Station reported 28 inches of new snow. The majority of the snow fell between 1200 and 1900PST on the 22nd. Chain restrictions were required on area highways.

CHP closed Interstate 8 for a short period due to a heavy burst of snow. The time of the closure was approximately 1500 to 1800 PST. Two big rigs jackknifed and subsequently crashed due to snow cover on the interstate.
Numerous trees were downed along the Orange County coast by a combination of strong winds and saturated soils. Peak wind gusts during the period were in the 35-50 mph range.
Numerous trees were downed in the Orange County valleys by a combination of strong winds and saturated soils. Peak wind gusts at local mesonet stations during the period were in the 35-50 mph range.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Numerous trees were downed in the Inland Empire by a combination of strong winds and saturated soils. Peak wind gusts reported by area mesonet stations during the period were in the 35-45 mph range.

Very heavy snow fellow over a 48 hour period, with the heaviest snow falling between 0700 and 1900PST on the 22nd. A trace-1 ft of snow was reported between 3,500 ft and 5,000 ft with 1 to 2.5 ft above 5,000 ft. Some local snow totals included: 18-30 inches in Big Bear Lake, 25 inches in Green Valley Lake, 24 end of Mt. Baldy Rd., 20 inches in Barton Flats, 18 inches in Running Springs, Arrowbear Lake, and Forest Falls, 16 inches in Angelus Oaks and Wrightwood, and 12 inches in Blue Jay.
Areas of dense fog developed around 0500PST and continued through 0700PST. Visibility of 1/4 mile or less was reported at John Wayne Airport and Los Alamitos U.S. Army Airfield.

Areas of dense fog with visibility of 1/4 mile or less were reported along the coast between 0000 and 0900PST. The greatest impacts were felt at San Diego International Airport, were numerous flights were delayed or canceled.

Lifeguards at Newport Beach reported visibility as low as 50 yards at 0700PST. Elsewhere near the coast the Los Alamitos U.S. Army Airfield reported periods of dense fog with a visibility of 1/4 mile or less between 2338PST on the 8th and 0803PST on the 9th. Dense fog was also reported at John Wayne Airport and by a trained spotter in Aliso Viejo.
Fullerton Municipal Airport reported periods of dense fog with a visibility of 1/4 mile or less between 2353PST on the 8th and 0553PST on the 9th.

Numerous ASOS stations near the coast reported periods of dense fog with a visibility of 1/4 mile or less between 2300PST on the 8th and 0830PST on the 9th. San Diego International reported dense fog between 0037 and 0603PST, but impacts were minimal. Lifeguards also reported dense fog with a visibility of 1/4 mile at Mission Beach at 0700PST.
Gillespie Field reported visibility of a 1/4 mile or less from 2315PST on the 8th to 0647PST on the 9th. Fog was limited to extreme western sections of the San Diego County Valleys.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Dense fog occurred over northwest sections of the Inland Empire. Chino Airport reported visibility of 1/4 mile or less from 0219PST to 0653PST.
A spotter in Aliso Viejo reported dense fog with a visibility of 200 yards at 0530PST.

Areas 2-10 miles inland from the coast reported periods of dense fog between 1830PST on the 9th and 0900PST on the 10th. Mcclellan-Palomar Airport, Montgomery Field, and Brown Field all reported periods of sub 1/4 mile visibility during this period. San Diego International reported 12 delays, 9 aircraft holding for 204 minutes, 1 divert.
John Wayne Airport and Los Alamitos Airfield reported persistent dense fog with a visibility of 1/4 mile or less.
A spotter reported dense fog with near zero visibility along Highway 55 near the cities of Orange and Villa Park.

Multiple ASOS stations along the coast reported a visibility of 1/4 mile or less over a 6 hour period. San Diego International reported fog with a visibility of 1/4 mile or less between 0324PST and 0627PST with 7 delays, 2 holds for 77 minutes, 3 diversions.

Multiple lifeguard reports of high surf along the San Diego County coast. Oceanside Beach reported 8-12 ft surf with peak sets near 16 ft on the afternoon of the 18th. Imperial Beach reported sets to 8 ft. Average sets of 7 ft were reported at Mission Beach and Solana Beach.
Lifeguards reported sets of 8-12 ft at Laguna Beach and 10-15 ft at San Clemente Beach. Sets near 10 ft were also reported in Newport Beach.
Three vehicles swept from Rodeo Dr. near Pebble Beach Park. Swift water rescues were conducted to rescue 3 people. One fatality was reported.
A jeep was submerged in a large sink hole at the intersection of Cedar St. and Chateau Rd. No water rescues required.

Flood waters and related erosion caused a collapse of lane number 5 along Interstate 15. A fire truck and big rig were caught up and destroyed in the collapse. No injuries were reported but damages to the Interstate reached into the millions.
Flood waters in the Cajon Pass submerged a vehicle along Keenbrook Rd. Three swift water rescues were conduced with no injuries reported.
Flood waters from the Wintersburg Channel exceeded the channels banks, producing flooding in a mobile home park.
Roughly 20 trees were downed by convective winds in Laguna Beach. The nearby Laguna Beach mesonet station measured a peak gust of 67 mph at 1737PST.

Mesonet stations along the coast reported wind gusts in the 30 to 45 mph range over a 6 hour period between 1300 and 1900PST. An isolated peak gust of 60 mph occurred at San Clemente Pier. Numerous trees were downed over the coastal areas.

Mesonet stations across inland Orange County reported wind gusts of 30 to 45 mph over a 6 hour period between 1300 and 1900PST.  Numerous trees and a few power lines were downed in Santa Ana and Tustin. The falling trees smashed cars blocked roadways.

Strong southerly winds downed hundreds of trees across coastal San Diego County. Many Cars were crushed by falling trees, power lines were downed, homes and business were damaged and one fatality was reported in East San Diego. The San Diego metro was hardest hit, with several mesonet/ASOS sites reporting wind gusts in the 50 to 60 mph range. A peak gust of 61 mph occurred at Imperial Beach. Storm damages reached the millions of dollars.

Numerous trees were downed across the western valleys of San Diego County. Peak wind gusts generally ranged between 35 and 50 mph, though a peak gust of 58 mph was reported at Otay Mountain between 1414 and 1514PST.

Numerous 70 mph or higher wind gusts were reported by the Palomar Mt. mesonet station over a 6 hour period. Peak gusts to 75 mph occurred between 1820 and 1830PST. No damage reports were received for the mountains areas.

The Burns Canyon mesonet reported frequent 70 to 80 mph gusts over a 9 hour period, with a peak gust of 84 mph between 1151 and 1251PST. A gust to 71 mph also occurred at Heaps Peak near Running Springs between 1015 and 1115PST. No damage reports were received.

Frequent wind gusts in the 55-65 mph range were measured by mesonet stations in Hesperia, with a peak gust of 72 mph between 1410 and 1420PST. Big rigs were blown over along Interstate 15 below the Cajon Pass and along Phelan Rd. west of Hesperia.
California Highway Patrol reported water across all lanes of Highway 138 near Summit Valley Rd.

Thirteen hour snow totals ranged from 12-24 inches above 6,500 ft, to a trace as low as 4,500 ft. Mt. Baldy and Mountain High ski resorts reported 16 to 24 inches of snow over a 13 hour period, while Green Valley Lake received 12 inches. Other snow totals included 8 inches in Wrightwood, 6 inches in Running Springs, and 3 inches in Big Bear.

Numerous large trees were reported down over the San Diego Metro. The downed trees blocked roadways and damaged several homes. Peak wind gusts in the region were near 35 mph. Saturated soils were likely a factor. Power outages to approximately 5,000 customers were also reported.

A few trees were downed in El Cajon and Rancho San Diego. The fallen trees damaged an apartment complex and blocked roadways. Peak wind gusts were near 35 mph and saturated soils were the likely causes.
Flooding from the Sweetwater River forced the closure of Plaza Bonita Rd due to water over topping the bridge.
California Highway Patrol reported 3 ft of water from Delzura Creek flowing over Highway 94.
The field a Petco Park was completely submerged under several inches of standing water.
Via Viejas road was flooded with a foot of water from Viejas Creek.
Flooding submerged two cars along Surrento Valley Rd. and Roselle St.
Heavy rain produced multiple reports of roadway flooding in Ramona.
A driver attempted and failed to cross a flooded roadway in a vehicle, resulting in water rescue.
Street flooding was reported in San Marcos with at least one car submerged.

Significant flooding occurred along the San Diego River in Mission Valley with the river cresting at 14.15 ft, the third highest stage all-time. Numerous roadways were closed, the Fashion Valley Mall parking structure was closed and the Fashion Valley Transit Center was closed to bus traffic. Numerous water rescues were conducted along the San Diego River including 20 people rescued from the Premier Inns Mission Valley. Many vehicles were also flooded and destroyed.
Flooding in the Tijuana River Valley impacted agricultural areas and led to roadway closures.
A big rig and car were caught in a mud flow near Highway 138 and Lone Pine Rd. Elsewhere along Highway 138 mud flows caused significant damage to area roadways.

events.cz_name: SAN MATEO PT TO MEXICAN BDR 30 TO 60NM
events.event_narrative: The San Clemente Basin Buoy reported wind gusts in excess of 34 kts for 4 hours with a peak gust of 37 kts.

events.cz_name: SAN MATEO PT TO MEXICAN BDR OUT 30NM
events.event_narrative: Southerly winds ahead of a cold front produced 34 to 52 kt wind gusts over the inshore waters. A peak gust of 52 kts occurred at San Clemente Pier.
John Wayne Airport reported dense fog with a visibility of 1/4 mile.
Los Alamitos Army Airfield reported a brief period of dense fog with a visibility of 1/4 mile.

Dense fog developed along the coast late on the 11th and pushed inland overnight. Carlsbad, McClellan-Palomar Airport reported 9 hours of dense fog with a visibility of 1/4 mile or less. Other airports up and down the coast also experienced visibility of 1/4 or less during this period, though San Diego International never dropped below 1/4 mile.
Dense fog briefly pushed into the western San Diego County Valleys, Gillespie Field Airport reported 1/4 mile or less visibility for about an hour.
Newport Beach lifeguards reported dense fog with a visibility of 200 ft.

Areas of dense fog were reported along the coast of San Diego County over a period of 12 hours at multiple ASOS/AWOS sites. Impacts were minimal at San Diego International where visibility only fell to 1/4 mile between 0615 and 0651PST.
John Wayne Airport reported reported dense fog with a visibility of 1/4 mile or less for more than 6 hours.
Los Alamitos Army Airfield reported periods of dense fog with a visibility of 1/4 mile or over a 9 hour period.

Areas of dense fog were reported by multiple ASOS/AWOS stations over a 11 hour period. No significant impacts were reported at San Diego International, though the visibility did drop to 1/4 mile for several hours.
John Wayne Airport reported 2 hours dense fog with a visibility of 1/4 mile or less. Newport Beach Lifeguards also reported a visibility of 200 ft at 0600PST.
Newport Beach Lifeguards reported dense fog with a visibility of 200 ft.
Numerous ASOS and AWOS stations along the San Diego County coast reported visibility of 1/4 mile or less over a 7 hour period. No impacts were reported at San Diego International.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: The Highland Springs RAWS station reported easterly wind gusts between 58 and 60 mph over a 7 hour period. The peak gust of 60 mph occurred between 0816 and 0916PST.
The RAWS station in Alpine reported a peak wind gust of 61 mph. Additional wind gusts in the 40-55 mph range were reported over other sections of the San Diego County Valleys.
The Burns Canyon mesonet station reported multiple wind gusts of 78 mph over a 5 hour period.
The Whitewater RAWS station reported multiple gusts in excess of 70 mph over a 3 hour period.
The CWOP station in Borrego Springs reported a peak gust of 62 mph.

The Means Lake mesonet station reported a 61 mph wind gust between 1526 and 1626PST. Victorville, Southern California Logistics Airport reported a wind gust of 60 mph between 1535 and 1555PST. The San Bernardino Sheriffs Office reported hundreds of tumbleweeds blocking all lanes of National Trails Highway near Mills Street a 1600PST.
The Burns Canyon mesonet station reported peak wind gusts in excess of 70 mph over a 4 hour period. The strongest gust of 94 mph occurred between 1351 and 1451PST.

The Anza Borrego Desert Research Center mesonet reported numerous wind gusts in excess of 58 mph over a 5 hour period. A peak gust of 69 mph occurred between 1820 and 1830PST. Roof and awning damage occurred at the Desert Research Center. In Borrego Springs power poles and street signs were blown over by wind along Borrego Valley Rd.
A mountain wave surfaced multiple times at Palm Springs Regional Airport producing multiple wind gusts in excess of 60 mph over a 6 hour period. The strongest wind gust was 66 mph at 1515PST.
California Highway Patrol reported a traffic light twisted due to high wind at the intersection of Monterey Ave. and Ramon Rd. in Thousand Palms.

Palm Springs Office of Emergency Management reported an injury from an awning blowing down at a mobile home park near Palm Canyon Dr. and Cherokee Way. A Large tree crushed a car at the Oasis Resort in Palm Springs and power lines were downed near the Horizon Mobile Park at 3575 E. Palm Canyon Dr.
A tree fell onto a golf cart at Tahquitz Creek Golf Resort, trapping two people and leaving one in critical condition.
California Highway Patrol reported high winds blowing rocks into lanes along Highway 74.
California Highway Patrol reported Varner Rd. in Bermuda Dunes closed due to blowing sand. A tree was uprooted on Fred Waring Dr. west of Adams St.
The Burns Canyon RAWS reported a peak gust of 70 mph. Elsewhere peak wind gusts were in the 40-55 mph range.
The Fremont Canyon mesonet reported a peak wind gust of 70 mph, along with multiple gusts into the 60 mph range between 0051 and 0851PST.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Low relative humidity and gusty winds helped the Opera Fire begin on the 30th. The fire consumed 1350 acres east of Riverside before being fully contained on May 2nd.
The Tower Fire occurred along Interstate 15 through the Cajon Pass. Approximately 150 acres of open country were consumed before the fire was contained on May 3rd.
The ANA Inspiration Golf Tournament at Mission Hills County Club in Rancho Mirage was suspended due to strong winds.
Two historic aircraft (1 plane and 1 helicopter) were damaged at the Palm Springs Air Museum after being lifted by strong winds.
VillageFest in Palm Springs was canceled due to strong winds.

A trained spotter reported a storm total snowfall of 10 inches at Birch Hill. The official coop site at Palomar Mountain reported 6 inches at 1500PST. Mount Laguna had a storm total snowfall of 4 inches.
Multiple spotters reported 2 to 5 inches of storm total snowfall. Lake Arrowhead received the most with 2 to 5 inches, Big Bear City reported 2 to 4 inches and 3 inches occurred in Twin Peaks.
A trained spotter in Idyllwild reported 2.5 inches of storm total snowfall.
A landspout tornado occured near Southern California Logistics Airport in Victorville.
A swift water rescue was conducted to rescue a man from a culvert. Urban and street flooding was reported in other portions of the San Diego metro.
Minor flooding of streets with some water creeping into houses near 36th and Finley Streets on Balboa Island due to 6.5 foot high tides. A protective sea wall had been recently demolished.
The Deluz Fire started on Camp Pendleton Marine Base on May 19th, it was extinguished on the 26th after burning 486 acres.

Dense fog rolled into coastal areas during the early morning hours and lingered through daybreak. Multiple ASOS stations, including Brown Field Municipal Airport, Miramar MCAS/Mitscher Field Airport, Imperial Beach Naval Outlying Field, and Mcclellan-Palomar Airport reported visibility of 1/4 mile or less.
Palm Springs recorded an afternoon high of 122 degrees, just on degree shy of the all time record.

Three Sister Hiking trail was closed on the 20th and 21st after 5 hikers suffering from heat related illnesses were rescued from the tail on the 20th. The high temperature in the nearby town of Ramona was 101 degrees.

Eight people suffered heat related illnesses hiking Three Sister Trail, 2 had to be airlifted to the hospital, and a third was transported to the hospital via ambulance. The high temperature in the nearby town of Ramona was 95 degrees.

A helicopter rescue and 3 vehicle rescues were conducted for heat related illnesses at El Capitan County Preserve. Park staff also had to do extra patrols of the area to share safety information and bottled water.
Anza Borrego State Park reported an afternoon high of 121 degrees, just one degree shy of the all-time record. Other nearby mesonets reported temperatures of 124-125 degrees.
An Elderly hiker died while hiking on a trail in La Quinta. Heat was suspected as a factor.
Palm Springs recorded an afternoon high of 122 degrees on both the 24th and 25th, just on degree shy of the all time record.
Huntington Beach Lifeguards rescued 200 plus people from rip currents over the weekend. Strong rip currents continued into the workweek, but rescue numbers are unavailable.

South facing beaches were impacted by elevated surf over a period of 5 days. Huntington Beach Lifeguards reported sets to 7 ft over the 5 day period.  Surf peaked on the 12th with 10 ft sets. Newport Beach also reported sets to 7 ft.
Northern San Diego County saw high surf along south facing beaches, sets to 8 ft were reported at Trestles.
Palm Springs recorded an afternoon high of 122 degrees, one degree shy of the cities all-time record. Thermal and Indio reported high temperatures of 121 and 119 degrees respectively.
The high temperature in Anza Borrego State Park reached 121 degrees, just one degree shy of the all-time record.

Three Sisters Trail in San Diego County was closed due to heat on the 7th and 8th. The trail reopened on the 9th, and four hikers with heat related illnesses were rescued. The high temperature in the nearby town of Ramona was 96 degrees on the 9th. EMS reported 8 calls for heat related illnesses on the 7th and 8th, with 4 hospitalizations.
Severe downburst winds knocked down branches that blocked roadways in Alpine and Harbison Canyon. A spotter estimated winds at 65 mph plus.
A severe downburst struck Temecula and Murrieta, winds overturned a big rig, downed trees, and damaged traffic signals.
Downburst winds toppled power lines and downed multiple large trees blocking several roadways in Perris.
Power lines downed by strong outflow winds.
A mud and debris flow from a recent fire flowed over Grand Ave. and Plumas St., both roads were closed.
High waters sent flows over the roadway near the intersection of State Routes 79 and 371. Vehicles were trapped in rocks and debris and the roadway was closed by CHP at 1320PST.
Heavy runoff through a normally dry wash flowed over Highway 78 two miles east of Yaqui Pass, forcing a closure of the highway.
A trained spotter reported a debris flow from Sheep Creek Wash flowing over Lone Pine Canyon Rd.
Video via social media of 4-6 inches of water flowing over the road near the intersection of Pipes Canyon Rd. and Gamma Gulch Rd.
A thunderstorm produced heavy rain with subsequent runoff that raised El Capitan Reservoir, a reservoir with a capacity of 112,800 acre feet, by 3 inches overnight.
Lightning strikes produced power outages in Palm Springs.
Lightning strikes produced power outages in Desert Hot Springs.
An intense thunderstorm produced widespread street flooding in Palm Springs. Flood water inundated Palm Spring High School with 1-1.5 inches of water, damaging 10 classrooms.

An intense thunderstorm produced intense street flooding in southern Corona. Flow pushed debris, branches, and trash cans down local streets. The flow along Colt Dr. was strong enough to damage and shift parked cars.
Severe winds downed a large tree (diameter > 2 ft) on a home in San Bernardino. A brief funnel cloud was also reported.
A trained spotter in Canebrake reported two car ports destroyed, numerous large tree limbs down and a roof folded over on a home.
Several roads were washed out in Canebrake, while rocks and debris covered a section of the S2. Plows were required to clear roads in Canebrake.

Rain rates exceeding 1 inch per hour produced major flooding in the Fish Creek Wash. Flow filled the slot canyon, and deposited several feet of mud and debris at the mouth of the canyon. Several hikers were stranded, but no injuries occurred.
Severe downburst winds toppled multiple large trees and downed seveal strings of power poles in Wildomar.
A downburst from a severe thunderstorm over Temescal Valley produced a 65 mph wind gust at a RAWS station.
Strong downburst winds damages roofs and a deck at a mobile home park in Home Gardens.

A lightning strike damaged a critical power transformer in Colton, cutting power to 95% of the city. An estimated 50,000 customers lost power. Area schools closed due to a lack of power that lingered into the following day.
Multiple vehicle stalled on Interstate 215 and Highway 60 due to flooding of lanes.
Lanes #3 and #4 of Highway 60 flooded with 1 foot of water.
Significant street flooding reported by CHP in the Temescal Valley. One vehicle stalled after trying to cross a flooded roadway.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Elsinore reported daily record high temperatures 3 days in a row from the 28th to the 30th. Afternoon highs were 111-112 degrees.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Excessive power needs from intense heat caused two transformers to fail in Yucaipa. Power was lost at Carriage Trade Manor (senior home center) and numerous residents spent the night outside trying to stay cool.
Three Sisters and Cedar Creek Falls hiking trails were closed due to heat from the 30th of August through the 1st of September. Temperatures in the area were between 105 and 110 degrees.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Riverside broke daily record highs on the 28th and 31st. The high of 112 degrees on the 31st was the 3rd hottest August temperature since records began in 1893.

Ramona recorded daily record high temperatures each day between the 28th and 31st. The high of 111 degrees on the 31st was the hottest August day on record, and the 108 degree reading on the 29th was the second hottest.
A state park ranger reported strong outflow winds from a thunderstorm with estimate peak gusts of 60 mph.

A state park ranger reported water up to 6 feet deep and 100 yards wide near the intersection of Salt Wash and Cutacross Trail. An additional photo from twitter showed minor road damage at Highway 78 and Fault Wash near Ocotillo Wells.

The ASOS at Jacqueline Cochran Regional Airport in Palm Springs reported a 62 mph wind gust between 1740 and 1746 PST. Multiple large trees and a fence were also toppled near the airport. Radar indicated the potential for additional severe gusts between 1730 and 1800 PST.

A mix of water and debris flowing through the normally dry Coyote Wash was reported around 1500 PST, by 1515 PST several inches of water and debris were flowing near Canyon Entrance dirt road and the Citrus Groves.
A lightning strike knocked out power to 1000 customers in Palm Springs.

The second intense thunderstorm of the day rolled over Palm Canyon and Palm Springs producing a daily rainfall record. Intense runoff through Palm Canyon Creek and the Whitewater River resulted in a closure of Cathedral Canyon Road and a swiftwater rescue and closure at Golf Club Drive. South Araby Drive was also closed. Other sections of the city were inundated with standing water and street flooding. Numerous homes suffered flood damage, cars were water logged and streets covered in debris.

The Canyon Fire began around 1300 PST, and spread rapidly near Highway 91, consuming 1700+ acres in the first 6 hours. The fire damaged 6 structures and forced hundreds of residents to evacuate in Corona. At least 8 schools were closed.
Lifeguards reported dense fog with a visibility of 100 yards or less at Newport Beach and Huntington Beach. The fog lingered into the afternoon with visibility still below 1/4 mile at 1300 PST.
A brief period of dense fog with 1/4 mile visibility or less impacted Brown Field.

The sea breeze brought dense fog with a visibility of 1/8 of a mile or less to the beaches of northern San Diego County during the late morning and early afternoon. Both Solana Beach and San Clemente Beach were impacted.

Dense fog with visibility of 1/4 mile or less hugged the beaches of Orange County for most of the day. Huntington Beach Lifeguards reported near zero visibility for the entire day.|The Huntington Beach Air Show training was cancelled.

Dense fog with a visibility of 1/4 mile or less impacted areas within 8 miles of the coast starting at 0200 PST. The fog retreated to the beaches after sunrise and lingered there into the afternoon. San Clemente was still reporting zero visibility at 1600 PST.
Flash flooding washed out the shoulder of the S22 (Borrego Salton Seaway) near Borrego Springs.

A 1-3 ft wall of water and debris surged through the Safari Mobile Home Park in Palm Springs. Multiple homes were damaged, Santa Monica Street was filled with debris and several residents were stranded in their homes.
Palm Springs High School suffered major flood damage for the second time in a month. A total of 31 classrooms were flooded.

Strong downburst winds from a thunderstorm produced a 55 mph wind gust at Palm Springs International Airport. Winds may have been stronger elsewhere in the city. Southern California Edison reported 1000 power outages.
A small plane crashed due to dense fog with a visibility of 1/4 mile or less at San Diego Brown Field around 0300 PST.
A 12 car pileup caused major traffic delays on Interstate 15 near the Interstate 8 interchange.
Afternoon high temperatures in the valleys ranged from 100-106 degrees.
More than 70 schools in the San Diego Unified School District closed early due to the excessive heat. Temperatures ranged from the upper 80 at the immediate coast to 105 several miles inland.
Afternoon highs in Inland Orange County ranged from 100-106 degrees.
Afternoon highs just inland from the coast ranged from 95-106 degrees.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Riverside was 109 degrees and Chino reached 108 degrees.
Ramona reached 109 degrees, the hottest September temperature on record. Other temperatures in the region included 108 in Valley Center and 106 in El Cajon.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Temperatures in the Inland Empire exceeded 110 degrees. Some sample high temperatures values include Ontario and Chino at 114 degrees and Corona at 110 degrees. Riverside reached 112 degrees, tying for the 5th highest September temperature on record.
Downburst winds from a thunderstorm toppled several trees at the Children's Discovery Museum in Rancho Mirage, CA, the irrigation system was also damaged.
A lightning strike struck a palm tree, catching the tree and a residence on fire.

Lifeguards reported 6-8 ft surf on the 7th and 8th in Newport Beach and Huntington Beach. Peak wave heights of 15 ft were reported at the Wedge. A local newspaper reported coastal flooding during high tide on the Balboa Peninsula in Newport Beach on the 7th. The beach parking lot was flooded, along with some nearby streets and homes. Several cars were also swamped while trying to drive through flood waters. In Capistrano Beach large breaking waves ran up against homes, shattering a window (most homes have shielding for waves).
Surf with sets of 7-8 ft were reported by lifeguards in San Clemente and Oceanside.
Lifeguards in San Clemente reported sets of 7-8 ft.
Lifeguards at Newport Beach and Huntington Beach reported sets to 7 ft.
A brief period of high surf was reported by lifeguards in Huntington Beach, with 7-10 ft sets.
A swimmer visiting from San Francisco was pulled out to sea and drowned by a strong rip current. Lifeguards reported peak wave heights of 8 ft. The body was found on Seal Beach a day later.

The Canyon 2 Fire began around 0900 PST on the 9th near the 91 Freeway and Gypsum Canyon Rd. in Anaheim Hills. The fire spread rapidly threatening numerous structures. In the first 24 hours the fire consumed more than 7,000 acres. In total 25 structures were destroyed, 55 were damaged and 9,217 acres burned. Four injuries were also reported. The cause of the fire was reported to be embers from the Canyon Fire which began September 25 and contained October 4th. Damage value is an estimate.
The mesonet station in Fremont Canyon reported a peak wind gust of 70 mph, sustained winds were 35-45 mph.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: The USFS RAWS station at Highland Springs (below the San Gorgonio Pass) reported peak wind gusts in the 58 to 61 mph range for 2 hours. Sustained winds were 30-40 mph. Winds in the rest of the Inland Empire remained below High Wind Criteria with peak gusts of 35-55 mph.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: CHP reported a big rig that jackknifed and flipped, blocking all lanes of the 210 north of Fontana.
Dense fog with a visibility of 1/4 mile or less impacted the beaches of Orange County, Huntington Beach Lifeguards reported 4 hours of dense fog.

Areas of dense fog with a visibility of 1/4 mile or less were reported all along the San Diego County Coast for 8 hours ending 0800 PST. San Diego International experienced periods of sub 1/4 mile visibility between 0230 PST and 750 PST. Impacts at the airport are unknown.

Afternoon high temperatures ranged from the upper 80s at the coast to the low 100s inland. The ASOS stations at Miramar MCAS/Mitscher Field and Montgomery Field reached 103 and 102 degrees respectively. The San Diego Unified School District resorted to early releases at 85 schools with insufficient/no air conditioning.

Afternoon high temperatures ranged from the mid 90s at the coast to the mid 100s inland. The ASOS stations at Miramar MCAS/Mitscher Field and Montgomery Field reached 107 and 106 degrees respectively. Vista was 105 degrees. The San Diego Unified School District resorted to early releases at 85 schools with insufficient/no air conditioning.

Afternoon high temperatures ranged from the low 90s at the coast to the low 100s inland. The ASOS stations at Miramar MCAS/Mitscher Field and Montgomery Field reached 105 and 104 degrees respectively. The San Diego Unified School District resorted to early releases at 85 schools with insufficient/no air conditioning.

High temperatures ranged from the upper 90s to low 100s across the valleys. A peak of 107 degrees occurred in Fallbrook. El Cajon set a daily record with a high of 104 degrees, the 4th warmest October day on record.

Afternoon high temperatures soared into the upper 90s and 100s, with a peak value of 110 degrees reported by a mesonet station in Poway. El Cajon recorded the cities 2nd warmest October day on record at 105 degrees.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Highs in the Inland Empire were in the upper 90s and mid 100s. Chino Airport reached 106 degrees and a mesonet in Montclair was 107 degrees.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: High temperatures were in the upper 90s and 100s for the second day in a row. Montclair was 106 degrees.
Temperatures spiked significantly with afternoon highs topping out in the 100-110 degree range. A station in Rancho Santa Margarita reported a high of 110 degrees.
Afternoon high temperatures were extreme for a 2nd day in a row, anywhere from 100-111 degrees. The peak value of 111 degrees occurred in Laguna Niguel.
Temperatures peaked in the upper 90s and low 100s. A mesonet in Fullerton was 104 degrees.
Valley highs were in the upper 90s and low 100s, with a peak of 104 degrees recorded in Pala. El Cajon and Escondido set daily records with readings of 102 and 100 degrees respectively.
Afternoon highs ranged from the upper 80s to upper 90s. Isolated areas several miles inland recorded values into the 100s, including 108 degrees at the Cattle Crest Trailhead mesonet station.

Afternoon highs at the beaches were in the mid 90s, while locations just a couple miles inland soared into the 100s. The highest value was at Cattle Crest Trailhead, with a high of 109 degrees. John Wayne Airport was 106 degrees, and Santa Ana was 104 degrees (tied for the 4th warmest October day on record).
Highs in most areas were in the mid 90s. A peak value of 103 degrees occurred at Cattle Crest Trailhead. A reading of 102 degrees was also reported at Lower Moro Campground.
A bank of dense fog moved across the coastal waters and up the coast, reducing visibility to 1/4 mile or less at the beaches.

Dense fog with a visibility of 1/4 mile or less formed along the coast. Fog with a visibility of 1/4 mile or less was reported continuously at Mcclellan Palomar Airport between 1920 PST on the 25th and 0910 PST on the 26th. Fog lingered through 1000 PST at Montgomery Field and Oceanside Municipal Airport. A period of visibility below 1/4 mile impacted San Diego International around 0700 PST, 20 flights were delayed.
A bank of dense fog with near zero visibility rolled up the Orange County coast, impacting mainly the beaches.
The mesonet station at Pleasants Peak reported a two and a half hour period with easterly wind gusts over 70 mph. A peak gust of 73 mph occurred between 0200 and 230 PST.
The mesonet station in Whitewater reported a peak westerly wind gust of 70 mph between 0050 PST and 0150 PST.
Temperatures ranged from the upper 80's at the beaches to the upper 90's several miles inland. San Diego reached 92 degrees, the latest 90 degree temperature on record for a calendar year.
Temperatures in the valleys were in the mid to upper 90's. El Cajon reported a high of 98 degrees. This is the cities second highest November temperature on record.
Temperatures in the Coachella Valley topped out in the mid 90's. Palm Springs reached 96 degrees, the highest temperatures on record for this late in the year.
Temperatures reached into the mid and upper 90's. Anaheim recorded the hottest temperature in the country on this day with a reading of 100 degrees.
Afternoon high temperatures topped out in the upper 80's and mid 90's.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Afternoon highs were in the mid 90's. Riverside set a daily record with an afternoon high of 95 degrees. This highest temperature on record for this late in the year.
Afternoon highs were in the upper 80s and mid 90s. All of the climate sites in the zone set daily record high temperatures.
High temperatures in the afternoon reached the low to upper 90s.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Afternoon high temperatures were in the low to mid 90s. Riverside reached 94 degrees, the hottest temperature this late in the year since 1958.
High temperatures were in the mid to upper 90s.

Fremont Canyon reported wind gusts over 70 mph for 13 hours, with sustained winds over 40 mph. A peak gust of 80 mph occurred 0751 PST and 0951 PST. Winds gusts over 70 mph were also reported at Pleasants Peak.
Report of a large tree downed by strong winds in Orange, CA. Tree damage, minor roof damage, and an exploding transformer were also occurred in Santa Ana.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Strong winds below the Cajon Pass downed numerous trees and power lines, toppled 8-12 big rigs and lofted debris onto highways. Most of the toppled big rigs occurred near the Interstate 15-210 interchange. Two small wildfires also occurred along the 215.
The Heaps Peak mesonet station reported wind gusts above 50 mph for 10 hours with a peak gust of 64 mph. A large tree fell along state route 38 near Barton Flats.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Peak wind gusts across the Inland Empire were mostly in the 30-40 mph range. Stronger gusts occurred below the Cajon Pass (with peak a gust of 55 mph at Ontario International) and the San Gorgonio Pass with a peak gust of 65 mph at Highland Springs Raws. The peak gust at Highland Springs occurred between 1316 and 1416 PST. Some tree damage occurred in Hemet. Small brush fires occurred near Murrieta and Mira Loma.
Fremont Canyon reported wind gusts above 70 mph for 3 hours. Sustained winds were as high as 63 mph.

Winds downed several large trees in Carlsbad, La Mesa and National City. A man was killed in Carlsbad when a large tree branch fell on him. Light poles were also knocked down in Carlsbad and Tierrasanta.

Three mesonet stations near the Pala Indian Reservation reported peak gusts between 64 and 69 mph, with the peak gust occurring at Palomar Launch between 1015 and 1030 PST. Similar gusts impacted southern San Diego County with a peak of 70 mph at an SDG&E gauge along East Willows Rd. Tree damage was reported in El Cajon, with both trees and power lines down in Ramona.

Winds gusts in the 50-70 mph range were reported throughout the San Diego County Mountains. The strongest winds were at Sill Hill where winds gusted over 70 mph for 12 hours (0600 to 1900 PST), with a peak gust of 88 mph. A section of Interstate 8 through the Cleveland National Forest was closed to High profile vehicles. A big rig and trailer were blown over near the intersection of Interstate 8 and Hwy 79.

The Lilac Fire began on the 7th near Interstate 15, and spread rapidly through the San Luis Rey River Basin near Bonsall. The fire consumed 4,100 acres, destroyed 157 structures and damaged 64. Over 100,000 residents were forced to or advised to evacuate and 20,000 people lost power. The fire was fanned by sub 10% relative humidity values and wind gusts over 50 mph. The fire was 100% contained on December 16th, but the majority of damage occurred in the first 48 hours. Damage value is an estimate.
The Paivika Ridge mesonet station reported wind gusts over 60 mph for 5 hours, with a peak gust of 66 mph. Heaps peak also reported a 56 mph gust.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Ontario International reported a 60 mph wind gust at 0753 PST, with additional gusts to 55 mph reported at Rialto.
The mesonet station in Fremont Canyon reported a peak gust of 79 mph, with additional gusts over 60 mph for 4 hours. Pleasants Peak also reported gusts over 60 mph during the same period.
The mesonet station at Sill Hill reported a gusts into the 60s, with a peak gust of 69 mph. Elsewhere peak gusts were in the 35 to 50 mph range.
Fremont Canyon reported wind gusts over 60 mph, with a peak gust of 67 mph. A 58 mph wind gust occurred a Pleasants Peak.
The mesonet station in Burns Canyon reported a 110 mph wind gust with sustained winds of 66 mph. Elsewhere wind gusts were much lower, in the 35-55 mph range. No damage was reported.

Strong winds gusting to 50 mph produced a dust storm down wind of Lucerne Valley Lake (dry lake bed) that reduce visibility to zero and lead to a closure of Highway 247 north of Lucerne Valley. Blowing dust also reduced visibility in Johnson Valley.
Strong winds surfaced below the San Gorgonio Pass with areas of blowing dust. The Whitewater mesonet station reported wind gusts over 70 mph for 3 hours.
Strong winds surfaced in the Palm Springs area causing power outages and blowing dust/sand. The Palm Spring Aerial Tramway briefly lost power.
The Volcan Mountain mesonet station reported wind gusts over 60 mph for about 3 hours. The Harrison Park mesonet also saw a few gusts over 60. Elsewhere winds were in the 25-50 mph range.

San Diego International and North Island Naval Air Station reported several hours of dense fog with a visibility of 1/4 mile or less. Approximately 20 flights into San Diego International were diverted/delayed or cancelled.

Mission Beach Lifeguards reported average sets to 8 ft and peak sets of 12 ft on the 16th, 8 ft surf lingered through the 17th. Surf in the 5-8 ft range was widespread along the coast via lifeguard and Surfline reports. Peak sets to 10 ft were reported at Black's Beach. The Ocean Beach Pier was closed due to the high surf. A surfer was pulled out to sea by a strong rip current at Ocean Beach.
Lifeguards at Huntington Beach reported 8-10 ft surf. Reported sets across the rest of the counties coastline were in the 4-8 ft range.
Mission Beach Lifeguards reported 8-10 ft surf on both the 19th and 20th, with most other sites reporting 5-9 ft surf. Windansea and Black's Beach both reported sets to 10 ft on the 20th.
Widespread 4-8 ft surf was reported along with occasional 9-10 ft sets at Huntington Beach and San Clemente.
A van drove into flood waters flowing through the normally dry Lytle Creek, resulting in a swift water rescue.

Three people and a dog were rescued by helicopter from the Santa Ana River Channel at Agua Mansa Rd. and Riverside Ave. in Colton. Several other individuals were swept down stream and rescued in Riverside.
Several vehicles were stuck in mud and flooded out. Additional urban flooding was reported elsewhere in the Inland Empire.
CHP reported large chunks of wood floating down Lemon Crest Dr., the intersection of Lake Jennings Park Rd. and Pino Dr. was completely flooded.

Multiple mesonets reported peak wind gusts in the 50-57 mph range between 0500 and 0700 PST, with the focus on southern San Diego. The historic Bay Theater lost it's sign and part of the front of the theater in National City.

A wind gust of 71 mph was reported a Palomar Lookout, with several other gusts into the 60s near Palomar Mountain. Peak wind gusts in the rest of the area were largely in the 35-50 mph range. No was damage reported.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: CHP reported two large trees down along Sage Road.
A 56 mph wind gust was reported at Otay Mountain. Around 6 large trees were reported down between San Marcos and Fallbrook. Peak winds gusts were in the 50-57 mph range.

Several rounds of snow impacted the area over roughly a 36 hour period. Peak snowfall amounts of 12 inches were reported above 7000 ft (12 inches at Green Valley Lake). Between 5,500 ft and 7,000 ft amounts were in the 2-8 inch range. Big Bear Lake and Wrightwood reported 2 inches, with 8 inches in Running Springs.
A light coating of snow required chain controls.
A quick burst of snow produced snow covered roads in Cuyamaca, at Mt. Laguna and along Sunrise Hwy and State Route 79.

The mesonet station at Sill Hill reported periodic gusts in the 60-80 mph range over a period of roughly 30 hours. A max gust of 89 mph was recorded. Winds were not as pronounced at other mountain mesonet stations with peak gust mostly in the 35-65 mph range. No major damage reported.
Multiple mesonet stations reported peak wind gusts in the 58-63 mph range. Winds were focused toward the eastern portion of the valleys. No major damage reported.
Multiple mesonet stations reported winds in the 50-65 mph range over the eastern valleys. A peak of 68 mph occurred at Alpine Raws between 0652 and 0752 PST. No significant impacts reported.
Winds gusted in the 60-74 mph range at Fremont Canyon. Other stations in the Santa Ana Mountains saw lighter winds, though Pleasants peak did have a peak gust of 65 mph.
The mesonet station in Fremont Canyon reported a brief period with wind gusts in excess of 70 mph. Pleasants Peak also gusted to 66 mph.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: The Highland Springs mesonet reported gusts in excess of 58 mph for 3 hours. Winds were significantly lower across the rest of the Inland Empire.
CalTrans reported mud and debris flowing onto Hwy 138, resulting in a closure of the highway.
Rains resulted is several rock falls along Hwy 330, that lead in a temporary road closure.
A minor debris flow was reported along Green River Rd. in Corona. The flow was associated with the Canyon 1 Fire.

Coastal flooding occurred in the parking lots of Aliso and Capistrano Beaches, and along the Strand in Oceanside during the morning high tide. A significant amount of sand was lost at Solana Beach, with 50 ft of sand erosion from the beach in Oceanside.
Huntington Beach Lifeguards reported mild to moderate beach erosion.

events.cz_name: SAN MATEO PT TO MEXICAN BDR OUT 30NM
events.event_narrative: Winds and seas resulted in 10 boats being beached near Zu��iga Point (entrance to San Diego Bay) after the boats pulled from their moorings. Multiple Coast Guard rescues were requested, but only one was conducted in the area.
Multiple reports of roadway flooding were reported, including a road closure at a low water crossing and street flooding near Muscoy.
Multiple rock slides occured along Highway 18 between Snow Valley and Big Bear Lake, the highway was closed for a brief period.
Flooding lead to a closure of Bear Valley Road at the intersection with Sheep Creek Road.
Burns Canyon reported a peak wind gust of 72 mph. Elsewhere Heaps Peak gusted to 64 mph, while other sites experienced peak gusts in the 30-45 mph range.
Southern California Logistics Airport in Victorville reported a peak wind gust of 58 mph. Peak gusts of 54 and 53 mph also occured at Apple Valley Airport and a mesonet station in Lucerne Valley.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Multiple locations in the San Bernardino County Mountains reported 1-3 inches of snow. Snow Valley had the highest total with 4-8 inches of new snow reported on the morning of the 4th. Chain controls were needed along Highways 18 and 38.
Several inches of snow resulted in chain controls along portions of Highways 74 and 243.
Several gusts in excess of 58 mph, including a peak wind gust of 66 mph, was measured by the Fremont Canyon RAWS.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Several vehicles were blown over on Interstate 15 near Devore and on Interstate 10 near Whitewater. Wind gusts in excess of 50 mph were observed by weather stations in the area, so it seems likely that local wind gusts greater than 58 mph were occurring.

A Ford F-250 with two occupants was swept away by flood waters while crossing Mill Creek at Chino Corona Rd. One male occupant was rescued after he was found hypothermic and clinging to a tree. The 25 year-old female driver was found dead about one mile downstream the following morning. Barricades had been placed across the road to prevent vehicles from crossing the creek, but an investigation later revealed that someone had illegally removed the barricades prior to the incident.
Winds gusted over 60 mph in Burns Canyon over a 3 hour period. Winds were lighter in the rest of the San Bernardino County Mountains.
Gusts of over 60 mph reported at the Whitewater Mesonet station for about 12 hours.

Heavy rain showers over Modjeska Canyon caused a debris flow at the Lost Canyon Ranch. The debris flow originated on a hillside about 500 feet in elevation above the ranch and destroyed several fences and horse stalls as it raced toward Santiago Creek. The owner estimates property damage at his ranch to be near $40K.

Palm Springs Airport ASOS reported a gust of 51 mph around 1800 PST on the 12th. Earlier that day, 4 planes were diverted from PSP due to wind shear on final approach. Numerous power outages were reported in Palm Springs, as well as downed trees and power lines.

Wind gusts of 69 mph were reported at Whitewater RAWS, with a gust of 59 mph also reported in Sky Valley between 0650 and 0850 PST. Indian Canyon Drive was closed to all traffic for 7 hours between Garnett Ave. and West Tramview Rd. due to high winds and blowing sand. High winds caused a tractor-trailer to flip on its side at San Rafael Drive and Indian Canyon Drive. All restaurants and gas stations were closed at Indian Canyon Drive and I-10 on the 12th. High winds downed 2 power poles in North Palm Springs. Numerous power outages occured in the vicinity of Indian Canyon.

Mountain wave activity resulted wind gusts over 70 mph for 5 hours with a peak gust of 84 mph in Burns Canyon. Winds were briefly sustained as high as 55 mph at the site. Winds were significantly lighter in the rest of the zone.
A 52 mph wind gust reported at Means Lake, along with minor tree damage in Lucerne Valley.
Mesonet stations in Borrego Springs and Ocotillo Wells reported wind gusts of 53 mph.

Wind gusts over 45 mph impacted the Coachella Mesonet from 1200 to 2300 PST, with a peak wind gust of 58 mph at 1800 PST. Visibility was down to 1/2 mile in some parts of the Coachella Valley. Workers at the Coachella Valley Festival were evacuated on the evening of the 16th due to high winds and blowing sand.

Wind gusts were over 50 mph from 0800 to 2300 PST, with a peak wind gust of 67 mph at Whitewater RAWS at 1600 PST. Surrounding areas had peak wind gusts of around 40 mph. A big rig was blown over at Palm Dr. and Varner Rd. High winds blew a trailer off of a vehicle on Highway 111.

Wind gusts at Big Bear City Airport were over 35 mph from 1000 to 1600 PST, with a peak wind gust of 48 mph at 1230 PST. Heaps Peak and Running Springs had peak wind gusts of 55 mph around 1400 PST. No significant impacts reported.

Wind gusts of over 40 mph occured at Apple Valley Airport between 1000 and 1800 PST, with a peak gust of 52 mph at 1300 PST. Lucerne Valley reported a peak wind gust of 53 mph around 1900 PST. Multiple power lines were downed in the area, resulting in power outages, 3 large trees were damaged in Hesperia.

Wind gusts at Volcan Mountain were over 60 mph from 1400 to 2300 PST, with a peak gust of 71 mph around 2030 PST. Harrison Park reported a peak gust of 68 mph at 2100 PST. Ranchita reported a peak gust of 61 mph at 2000 PST. Surrounding areas reported lighter winds. No significant impacts reported.

Wind gusts over 40 mph reported at Borrego Springs from 1900 to 2100 PST, with a peak gust of 55 mph at 2000 PST. Mason Valley reported a wind gust of 46 mph at 1900 PST. Surrounding areas reported lighter winds. No significant impacts reported.

Wind gusts for Palm Springs Airport were over 40 mph from 1800 to 2000 PST, with a peak gust of 56 mph and a sustained wind of 39 mph at 1815 PST. Surrounding areas reported wind gusts of around 30 mph. The campsite at the Coachella Valley Festival delayed opening until the 20th at 0200 PST due to high winds and blowing sand, leaving tourists stranded until the campsite opened.

Whitewater RAWS reported a maximum sustained wind of 49 mph at 1150 PST on the 19th. The maximum gust in that time period was 63 mph. California Highway Patrol reported issues using medical aircraft to respond to an auto accident in the area.
Victorville Airport reported a peak wind gust of 48 mph around 1500 PST on the 19th. No significant impacts reported.

Volcan Mountain reported a peak wind gust of 64 mph around 0600 PST. Harrison Park reported a peak wind gust of 63 mph around 0700 PST. Boulevard West Mesonet reported a peak gust of 62 mph. No significant impacts reported.
Wind gusts at Borrego Springs were greater than 40 mph from 1100 to 1500 PST, with a peak gust of 49 mph at 1330 PST. No significant impacts reported.

Snow fell in the San Bernardino Mountains in morning on May 2nd, producing 2 to 3 inches throughout the mountains, and up to 5 inches in Big Bear, Fawnskin and Snow Valley. Snowfall rates of up to 1 inch per hour occurred during some portions of the event. Chain controls were in effect in the San Bernardino Mountains.

Observed wind gusts at George AFB of over 28 mph were observed between 1300 PST and 1600 PST on May 12th, with a peak wind gust of 36 mph at 1456 PST. A child was injured in a residential neighborhood in Adelanto around 1400 PST due to a bounce house being blown away onto traffic lanes of 395.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: The Patterson Fire ignited around 1 pm PST on May 17th. Six homes were evacuated around 1500 PST on Hidden Falls Road and Vista Road, and one unoccupied structure was destroyed in the fire. The fire rapidly grew to approximately 1,200 acres by 1830 PST on the 17th. Evacuations were lifted around 2100 PST on the 17th. The fire was contained around 1800 PST on May 18th.
At Huntington Beach, high surf of 7-8 ft was reported. The Wedge reported 7-10 ft sets.
Mission Beach Lifeguards and Oceanside Pier reported 4-6 ft surf due to the south swell.

Foggy conditions attributed to a 30-vehicle crash on Interstate 15 near Oak Hill Road and Highway 138 interchange in the Cajon Pass. The crash occurred around 1030 PST when two vehicles became disabled in a collision south of Oak Hill Road. This resulted in a collision of crashes that stretched a mile long. The southbound lanes of Interstate 15 were closed until around 1330 PST. 20 people were injured in this incident.

Lifeguards reported 4-7 ft surf on Huntington and Newport beaches. 6-8 ft surf was reported at Laguna Beach. 8-12 ft surf reported at The Wedge. Orange County lifeguards stated they had hundreds of water rescues during this event.

Reports of 5-7 ft surf at Northern San Diego County Beaches and 3-5 ft surf reported at Southern San Diego County Beaches. Lower Trestles had surf of 5-8 ft. Two surfers rescued an unconscious swimmer off the coast of La Jolla. The swimmer had a pulse once rescued and was transported to a local hospital.

A brush fire broke out in Aliso Viejo around 1300 PST on June 2nd and spread to around 200 acres. Erratic winds and dry fuels helped to exasperate the fire. Thousands of homes were evacuated in Aliso Viejo and Laguna Beach due to the fire. The Top of the World neighborhood in Laguna Beach was evacuated as well. No structures were damaged in the fire. Five firefighters suffered non-life threatening injuries. Authorities determined that a young boy accidentally set the fire.

The Martinez Fire broke out around 1400 PST on June 23rd. Dry conditions and temperatures in the 120s helped exasperate the fire. Seven homes were destroyed. Approximately 30 tribal members were displaced from their homes and lost nearly all of their possessions. Three firefighters suffered minor injuries in the blaze.

High pressure aloft brought in dry conditions and extreme temperatures to the Coachella Valley on June 3-5. Temperatures reached 113 in Palm Springs and Thermal on the 3rd and 4th, and decreased to 104 on the 5th.

High pressure aloft brought in dry conditions and extreme temperatures to the San Diego County deserts from June 3-5. Ocotillo Wells reported temperatures of 111 on June 3 and 110 on June 4. One man died on June 4th from a heat-related illness.

The Coachella Valley experienced extreme high temperatures due to a high pressure aloft bringing dry and warm conditions to the region. Palm Springs recorded a temperature of 112 on June 13 and 14. Overnight lows were in the mid-80s in the Coachella Valley.

The San Diego County Deserts experienced extreme high temperatures on June 12 and 13 as high pressure aloft brought dry and hot temperatures to the region. Ocotillo Wells recorded a temperature of 109 on the 12th and 113 on the 13th.

Extreme temperatures were recorded in the Coachella Valley on June 21 and 22 as high pressure aloft brought dry and hot temperatures into the region. On June 22, Palm Springs recorded a high temperature of 116 and Thermal recorded a high temperature of 114.

Extreme temperatures were observed in the San Diego County deserts as high pressure aloft brought hot and dry conditions to the area. Borrego Springs recorded a high temperature of 114 and Ocotillo Wells reported a high temperature of 115 on June 22. An emergency official reported that one person died in Ocotillo Wells Recreational State Park due to a heat-related illness.

The West Fire started around 1015 PST on 07/06 and quickly spread to 400 acres by 1600 PST. The fire started for unknown reasons alongside eastbound I-8 at West Willows Road in Alpine.  Extreme temperatures and low relative humidity helped exasperate the fire. Most of the Alpine community was evacuated from their homes. The fast-moving brush fire destroyed or damaged approximately 50 structures. One firefighter was injured while battling the blaze. In total, the fire burned 505 acres and was fully contained 7/10 around 1600 PST.

A large thunderstorm cell progressed south off of the San Gorgonio Mountain into Banning on July 7th around 1100 PST.  It brought strong winds to the Banning area, in particular, Sylvan Park. Numerous trees were damaged from winds in the park. After a storm survey, the winds in Sylvan Park were estimated to be 56 knots from the thunderstorm.

Numerous thunderstorms formed in the San Bernardino Mountains due to enhanced monsoonal moisture on July 7th. Heavy rain from the thunderstorms resulted in multiple debris flows on State Route 38. The first debris flow was reported on State Route 38 near Valley of the Falls Drive in Forest Falls. This debris flow was approximately 11 feet deep and 25 feet wide. State Route 38 closed at Valley of the Falls Drive due to the debris flow. No injuries were reported, but at least one vehicle was stuck in the debris flow.  Another debris flow was reported on State Route 38 and Frustration Creek west of Mountain Home Village.  This debris flow was approximately 100 feet wide and 10 feet deep.

An intense line of thunderstorms across Arizona pushed to the west- northwest into Southern California around 0000 PST on July 9th. By 0100 PST, the thunderstorms began to collapse. The outflow boundary produced a gust front, which brought some gusty winds and kicked up a good bit of dust and dirt. The gust front pushed into the Coachella Valley around 0130-0200 PST and greatly reduced visibility through 15z. Visibility of �� of a mile was reported in Thermal. The intense winds downs a power pole and line onto a house, which caused it to catch fire. A wind gust of 40 knots was reported in Indio. Haze and dust were present in the Coachella Valley for a few hours in the morning of July 9th.

The Martinez Fire broke out around 1400 PST on July 23rd. Dry conditions and temperatures in the 120s helped exasperate the fire. Seven homes were destroyed. Approximately 30 tribal members were displaced from their homes and lost nearly all of their possessions. Three firefighters suffered minor injuries in the blaze.

A long-period southwest swell from Hurricane Fabio brought high surf to Orange County Beaches on July 5-6. Surf of 5-8 feet was reported at southern Orange County Beaches and surf of 6-8 feet, with local sets  10-12 feet, reported at northern Orange County beaches. The Wedge reported surf of 8-12 feet.

Heavy rain from monsoonal thunderstorms resulted in a rock slide in the San Bernardino Mountains. Highway 18 was closed for approximately 4 hours between Big Bear Lake and Snow Valley due to numerous rock slides in the Arctic Circle. One vehicle was reported to be stuck on the highway because of a large boulder stuck underneath their car.
A spotter reported lightning from numerous thunderstorms near Lucerne Valley.
A trained spotter measured 0.45 inches of rainfall in 20 minutes from a thunderstorm near Pine Valley.
Campo ASOS reported a thunderstorm wind gust of 43 knots.

The Cranston Fire started on 7/25 around 1100 PST in the Riverside County Mountains. By 1700 PST on 7/25, the fire had rapidly grown to 1,200 acres. In total, the Cranston Fire burned 13,000 acres, resulted in over 500 people being evacuated, and scorched 5 structures. The cause of the fire was determined to be arson. The Cranston Fire was fully contained on 8/13.
A spotter reported a flash flood on Fish Creek Wash near Split Creek Road. The dirt road had approximately 1 foot of water flowing across it.
The ASOS station at Palm Springs Airport recorded a 54 knot thunderstorm wind gust around 1753 PST.
Minor coastal flooding occurred during high tide between 26th street and 38th street in Newport Beach during late on July 11th. No damage to homes was reported.
Palm Springs ASOS reported 1.08 inches of rain from 1700 PST to 1900 PST on July 11th. This was a daily record amount of rainfall for that location.
California Highway Patrol reported that rocks and debris were blocking the roadway at Dillon Road and Bubbling Wells Road.

California Highway Patrol reported a mudslide along Highway 18 northeast of Big Bear City that was 6 feet deep and extending 20 feet across the highway. 12 vehicles were stranded in the mudslide. Highway 18 was closed between Big Bear and Lucerne Valley due to the debris flow.

Monsoonal moisture brought thunderstorms to the San Bernardino Mountains on July 12th. This resulted in flash flooding on Highway 18 near mile marker 65 (Mitsubishi Cement Corporation Plant). numerous vehicles stranded due to significant flow of water and debris. Highway 18 was closed in both directions through the afternoon on July 12th.

CalTrans and California Highway Patrol reported flash flooding on Valley of the Falls Drive near Highway 38. Concerns for debris flow movement and heavy rain forced the closure of Valley of the Falls Drive through the afternoon on July 12th.
One day total rainfall from Mesonet 7 mi NE of Cherry Valley (yucc1) of 1.84 inches.
Mesonet station (f2736) reported a 24-hour rainfall total of 1.56 inches.
