Two cloud-to-ground strikes occurred outside of a rain shaft. Highway Patrol reported brush fire start just west of Lake Arrowhead. Other strikes were detected just to the east and also outside of the main rain shaft near Big Bear Lake.
A spotter reported a tree engulfed in flames from a lightning strike on Delamar Mountain Road in Fawnskin.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: The Inland Empire experienced temperatures in excess of 100 degrees on August 6th and 7th. Most areas in the Inland Empire experienced temperatures of 100-105 degrees, with the highest values observed in San Bernardino (108 degrees) and Lake Elsinore (111 degrees). The heat began to subside slightly on the 8th, with warm conditions continuing throughout the week.

The Coachella Valley experienced the most extreme temperatures in Southern California during this heat event. Thermal hit 117 degrees and Palm Springs reach 115 degrees on August 6th. Similar temperatures were observed on August 7th as well. Heat began to subside on Thursday, August 9th, but it remained quite warm in the Coachella Valley through the entire week.

Apple and Lucerne Valleys experienced temperatures in excess of 100 degrees during this heat event. Apple Valley reached 106 degrees and Hesperia reached 107 degrees on August 6th. Temperatures dropped 3-4 degrees on August 7th, but still remained well above 100 degrees. Heat subsided slightly on August 8th and remained warm throughout the week.

Orange County Inland areas experienced hot temperatures during this heat event, with most areas experiencing temperatures over 95 degrees. The highest temperatures were observed on August 9th, with Anaheim reaching 100 degrees and Santa Ana reaching 97 degrees. August 6th-8th had temperatures slightly lower, but still remained above 95 degrees. Temperatures began to subside on Friday August 10th, but remained over 90 degrees through the weekend.

The San Diego County Deserts experience extreme temperatures on August 6th through 8th. Most areas experienced temperatures 100-105 degrees on August 6th, with similar temperatures observed on August 7th. Temperatures began to slowly subside on August 8th, but still remained over 95 degrees in most areas of the Lower Deserts. Heat slowly subsided throughout the week.

The San Diego County Valleys experienced temperatures in excess of 95 degrees in most areas from August 6th through August 9th. The warmest temperatures were observed on August 7th, with Valley Center reaching 103 degrees and Poway reaching 102 degrees. August 8th was not quite as hot, but still remained near 95 degrees in most areas. Hotter temperatures were observed on August 9th as well, with Ramona Airport reaching 103 degrees and Escondido reached 100 degrees. Heat began to subside on Friday, August 10th, but still remained quite warm throughout the weekend.

The San Diego County Mountains experienced temperatures in excess of 90 degrees on August 6th and 7th. Julian reached 91 degrees and Mount Laguna reached 89 degrees on August 6th. On August 7th, Julian reached 96 degrees and Mount Laguna reached 91 degrees. Heat subsided on Wednesday, August 8th, but still remained warm throughout the week.

California Department of Transportation reported that there were dozens of small debris flows in and around the Cranston Fire burn scar on August 15th  but highway 74 was proactively closed based on NWS warnings. On August 17th, there was a large debris flow up to 5 feet deep in the Lake Hemet Campground area from Hurkey Creek. Again highway 74 was closed about 2 hours in advanced based on NWS briefings and the actual Flash Flood Warning.  Very large boulders were reported to have traveled downstream on the upper Hurkey Creek near Fleming Ranch. Evacuations were in order at Hurkey Creek Campground and Sheriff was on site monitoring the potential based on NWS briefings. Video of the debris flow was captured. A storm survey was conducted by NWS following the debris flow. No injuries or major damages reported from this event. Rain gauges in the area reported 1-1.5 inches of rainfall near the Cranston Fire burn scar. Evacuations of the small communities near the Cranston Fire burn scar were put into place on August 15th in anticipation of the heavy rainfall and potential for flash flooding and debris flows.
Public reports of a landspout tornado northwest of Anza, CA. No injuries or damages were reported.
CHP reported that Brookside Avenue and Highland Springs Avenue was flooded out on both sides of the road from the heavy rain.
Public and Fire Radio reported that Valley of the Falls Drive was closed due to a debris flow.
CHP reported that water and mud flooded the entire roadway on Highway 247 at Locus Ave. No damages or injuries reported.

CHP reported that Highway 18 near Johnston Road was flooded. A vehicle went off the road in that area into a pothole and became flooded with water. Persons in the vehicle made it out okay, but some damage to the vehicle from the water.
Apple Valley mesonet (gntc1) reported a 40 knot thunderstorm wind gust at approximately 2:50 PM PST on August 16th.
Two spotters reported heavy rainfall in Wrightwood -- approximately 1 inch per hour rainfall rate. Moderate flooding was reported.
A trained spotter reported 1.14 inches of rainfall in 35 minutes.
Public reported a debris flow at the Sheep Creek Wash in Wrightwood on Lone Pine Canyon Road. The road was closed down for a few hours to clean up the debris flow.
Sheriff reported that a major debris flow occurred on Highway 74 near the Cranston Fire  burn scar. No injuries or damages were reported.
CHP reported boulders across the roadway on Highway 74 in Pinyon Pines near the fire station. No injuries or damages were reported.
CHP reported a rock/dirt/mud slide along Highway 38 between Onyx Peak and the town of Sugarloaf. Law enforcement indicated that the road was covered in rocks. No injuries or damages reported.

The Cranston Fire started on July 25th and continued to burn through August 13th when it was fully extinguished. It started on 7/25 around 1100 PST in the Riverside County Mountains. By 1700 PST on 7/25, the fire had rapidly grown to 1,200 acres. In total, the Cranston Fire burned 13,000 acres, resulted in over 500 people being evacuated, and scorched 5 structures. The cause of the fire was determined to be arson.

The Holy Fire began in the Santa Ana Mountains around 2:15 PM PST on August 6th. The hot and dry conditions helped to exasperate the fire further. By the morning of August 7, the fire had increased in size to 4,000 acres and by August 8, it had grown to 6,200 acres. By August 9, more than 21,400 people in 7,400 residences were placed under mandatory evacuation in south Corona, Lake Elsinore, and several communities in the Santa Ana Mountains. Ortega Highway was closed for an indefinite period of time, due to fire danger between Antonio Parkway in San Juan Capistrano and Grand Avenue in the Lake Elsinore. The fire size in total ended up growing to over 23,000 acres. Eighteen structures were destroyed in Orange and Riverside Counties. No major injuries or deaths were reported. The fire was fully contained on September 13th.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: On July 6, temperature at Chino ASOS reached 120F. This is the highest recorded reading for this location and possibly for an ASOS not in the desert. Ontario ASOS reached 117F, the prior highest reading was 114F. Riverside Airport hit 118F and Lake Elsinore reach 119F. On Saturday July 7, the temperatures cooled to 114 at Chino, 113 at Riverside and 112 at Ontario.

Intense heat on July 6 (and offshore flow) resulted in breezy east winds and a high of 117F at Ramona ASOS. The previous record high was 111F. At Escondido the high was 112 and Santee 110, these were just shy of all-time highs. San Diego Public Health and 211 services share statistic which showed a sharp jump in heat related 911 and 211 information calls. 211 San Diego can provide vouchers for those in need of cool shelter during heat waves. The destructive West Fire also occurred in Alpine, San Diego County on July 6. Alpine had highs of 109 and 104 for July 6 and 7th with wind gusts to 30 mph.
Santa Ana fire station climate site reached 114F on July 6, this was an all-time high. A scorching 115F was reported at Yorba Linda. On July 7, it still reached 109F at Yorba Linda.
Even the desert was hot on July 6, 120F reported at Thermal and 119F at Palm Springs. These were shy of the 123-124F all-time highs. Palm Springs managed to reach 115F the following day.
The Fremont Canyon RAWS measured an 82 mph wind gust.

Visibility of 1/4 SM or less was observed in the valley areas of San Diego County at NKX, SDM, and MYF on the morning of September 9th.  This dense fog was observed from 2 AM to 7 AM PST at those ASOS sites, and began clearing after sunrise.
Dense fog with visibility 1/4 mile or less was observed at Carlsbad Airport between 5 AM and 7 AM PST on the 8th. Fog began to clear after sunrise.
Carlsbad Airport ASOS reported less than 1/4 SM visibility between 3 AM and 5 AM PST. Also, Camp Pendleton reported visibility less than 1/4 SM between 4 AM and 6 AM PST.
An NWS employee reported dense fog and visibility around 500 feet between 6 AM and 7 AM PST on the 22nd.

Isolated thunderstorms formed over Forest Falls late on Sunday September 30th. About 2 inches was estimated on radar. The runoff towards Mill Creek was significant can caused hikers to be stranded after dark as the water flow was not safe to cross. First responders were called to aid in the recovery. There was video posted on Facebook.

A thunderstorms produced radar estimated 2 to 4 inches of rain in Box Canyon near I-10 within Box Canyon. The runoff destroyed a dike operated by Coachella Valley Water District. The moisture was associated with pre Tropical Cyclone Rosa. The thunderstorm produced prolific lightning in the area. Box Canyon had a flash flood which drains from the little San Bernardino mountains. The water eventually drains into the Salton Sea. A vehicle travelling on Box Canyon road was swept away in the flash flood and the driver drowned (within PHX area of responsibility).

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: A 65 mph wind gust was measured at Palm Avenue Elementary School. Elsewhere, the Ontario Airport ASOS measured sustained winds of 40 mph with a peak gust of 59 mph.
Lifeguards at Huntington Beach reported 8-10 ft surf on October 1, and 6-10 ft surf at Newport Beach.
CalTrans reported rocks and mud across Highway 78 near Buttes Pass Road. No injuries or damages were reported.
A 12 hour rainfall report from the public of 0.72 inches of rainfall in Palm Desert.
CalTrans reported road flooded at Monterey Ave and Ramon Road in Thousand Palms. Vehicles were unable to get through.
CalTrans reported flash flooding on Interstate-10. The flooding was 1.5 ft deep and 12 ft wide over the interstate.
CHP reported flash flooding at Varner Drive and Date Palm Drive and requested that the road be closed to traffic.
CalTrans reported Dillion Road at East Deception Road flooded out around 0030 PST on October 13th.
Broadcast media reported quarter sized (1 inch) hail in Indio. No damages or injuries were reported.
Mesonet recorded a wind gust of 71 knots in Fremont Canyon between 0751 and 0851 PST on October 15th.
Mesonet station se097, 8 miles SW of Corona, recorded a wind gust of 56 knots between 0600 and 0700 PST on October 15th.
Broadcast media reported high wind that resulted in a large tree falling over onto a vehicle and killing one person.
Mesonet station se081, 4 miles ENE of Tustin reported a 50 knot wind gust between 0640 and 0740 PST on October 15th.

Mesonet station se080, 5 ENE of Mission Viejo reported a 52 knot wind gust between 0910 and 1010 PST on October 15th.
Mesonet station hf001, 8 miles NNE of Valley Center reported a wind gust of 59 knots between 1030 and 1130 PST.
High wind resulted in a large tree down on Atherton Street in Irvine. No injuries or damages were reported.
CalTrans reported a tree down on Highway 330, south of Running Springs, blocking the downbound lane of the highway.

A winter storm brought heavy snow and gusty winds to the San Bernardino Mountains. Snowfall totals of one to three feet were reported at elevations above 6000 feet. Interstate 15 had to be shut down due to heavy snow and hazardous driving conditions in the Cajon Pass.
Public reported 100 ft estimated visibility at 800 ft elevation in the hills southeast of San Marcos between 0600 and 0900 PST on October 25th.
Brown Field ASOS reported 1/16th mile visibility between 0500 and 0800 PST on October 25th.
Public reported 1/2 mile visibility near University of San Diego between 0600 and 0900 PST on October 26th.
Spotter reported less than 1/4 mile visibility near Orange Coast College in Costa Mesa between 0500 and 0800 PST on October 27th.
Los Alamitos ASOS reported 1/8 mile visibility between 0500 and 0800 PST on October 27th.
John Wayne Airport ASOS reported less than 1/4 mile visibility between 0300 and 0800 PST on October 27th.
Imperial Beach ASOS reported 1/4 mile visibility between 0500 and 0800 PST on October 27th.
Spotter reported 1/4 mile visibility east of I-5 at 320 ft elevation from 0500 to 0800 PST on October 28th.
Montgomery Field ASOS reported 1/4 mile visibility or less between 0500 and 0800 PST on October 28th.
Fullerton Airport ASOS reported 1/4 mile visibility or less between 0500 and 0800 PST on October 28th.
San Diego Lindbergh Field ASOS reported 1/4 mile visibility between 0200 and 0400 PST on October 28th.
Carlsbad Palomar Airport ASOS reported less than 1/4 mile visibility between 0400 and 0700 PST on October 28th.
Los Alamitos ASOS reported less than 1/4 mile visibility between 0400 and 0700 PST on October 28th.
Public reported visibility of less than a mile in Brea between 0500 and 0800 PST on October 28th.
Carlsbad Palomar Airport reported less than 1/4 mile visibility between 0000 and 0500 PST on October 28th.
Fullerton Airport ASOS reported 1/4 mile visibility between 0100 and 0600 PST on October 28th.
Brown Field ASOS reported 1/4 mile visibility from 2300 on October 28th to 0500 on October 29th.
Heavy rain from Tropical Storm Sergio resulted in flash flooding in the Coachella Valley. The runoff destroyed a dike operated by the Coachella Valley Water District for a second time.
Sill Hill Mesonet reported a wind gust of 74 knots between 0800 and 0900 PST on November 12th.
Fremont Canyon Mesonet reported a wind gust of 64 knots between 1800 and 1900 PST on November 8th.

events.event_narrative: Highland Springs Mesonet reported a 54 knot wind gust between 1200 and 1300 PST on November 12th.
Fremont Canyon Mesonet reported a 50 knot wind gust between 0600 and 0700 PST on November 12th.

West Rancho Bernardo Mesonet reported a 35 knot wind gust between 1200 and 1300 PST on November 13th. Utility company preemptively shut off power in this area in anticipation of strong winds. Downed power lines were reported in the area on the morning of November 13th.

Rancho Santa Fe Mesonet reported a 22 knot wind gust between 1200 and 1300 PST on November 13th. The utility company reported downed power lines in the area where they preemptively shut off power due to forecast strong winds.
Alpine Mesonet reported a wind gust of 60 knots between 0700 and 0800 PST on November 13th.
Otay Mountain Mesonet reported a wind gust of 52 knots between 0500 and 0600 PST on November 13th.
Mesonet station povsd (Pamo Valley) reported a wind gust of 55 knots between 1000 to 1100 PST on November 13th.
Lifeguard reported persistent 10 ft surf at Mission Beach.
Lifeguard reported 8-10 ft surf at Ocean Beach, which forced the closure of the Ocean Beach Pier from November 30th through December 1st.
San Clemente Basin Buoy reported persistent 15 ft swell at a 15 second period.
Lifeguards at Huntington Beach reported 8 ft surf with sets to 9 ft on November 30th.

Media reported beach erosion during high surf causing damage to the boardwalk at Capistrano Beach in Dana Point. A walkway was severely damaged, palm trees were uprooted and old buried cars were exposed due to the beach erosion.
Media reported highway 60 (Pomona Ave.) at Etiwanda Ave. was flooded due to heavy rain with accidents reported in the area.
California Highway Patrol reported a vehicle stuck in approximately 1 foot of standing water along Highway 210. No injuries were reported.
Heaps Peak mesonet reported a peak wind gust of 57 knots between 0800 and 0900 PST on November 29th.
Whitewater raws mesonet reported a peak wind gust of 52 knots between 0700 and 0800 PST on November 30th.
Mesonet ssvc1 (8 mi nne of Rancho Cucamonga) reported a 24-hr rainfall total of 3.38 inches.
CoCoRaHS station ca-sr-63 in Crestline reported a 24-hr rainfall total of 3.6 inches.
A spotter reported a significant gray water flow in Horsethief Canyon within the canyon banks. No injuries or damages were reported.
Media reported major debris flow in Trabuco Canyon. The debris flow appeared to be mainly comprised of very little water and mostly mud/rocks.
Department of Highways reported a road closure due to flooding on Verdemont and Cajon Blvd.
CalFire reported water and debris from Coldwater Canyon flowing over into Glen Ivy Road.
Santiago Peak 2 mesonet reported a 24-hr rain total of 3.24 inches.
CalTrans reported an emergency closure of SR-38 at Valley of the Falls Drive due to a debris flow.
Riverside County Emergency Management reported water and rocks in the road near Temescal Canyon.
Burns Canyon mesonet reported a peak wind gust of 54 knots between 0900 and 1000 PST on November 29th.
Mormon Rock Mesonet reported a peak wind gust of 61 knots between 0100 and 0200 PST on November 29th.

John Wayne Airport reported 2.56 inches of rainfall in about 2 hours on December 6th. This is a 1 in 100 year return interval. Cars in nearby Costa Mesa were seen completely submerged completely or stalled in deep water up to the windows.
Public reported flash flooding along Highway 55 at Paularino Ave. in Costa Mesa. Reported that approximately 1 ft of water was along the right side of the road.
Spotter reported flash flooding on Orangethorpe Avenue at Raymond Street in Anaheim.
Victor Valley News Group reported that Del Gado Road between Anacapa Road and Palmdale Road was closed due to flash flooding. Three vehicles were stranded but no injuries were reported.

A debris flow was triggered by a burst of heavy rain over the Poomacha Burn Area just north of Adams Drive on the Pauma Indian Reservation. The debris flow rushed down an unnamed creek and towards Adams Drive. Once at the bottom of the hill, the debris flow crossed Adams Drive and continued down Pauma Reservation Road all the way to Highway 76. The portion of Adams Drive from the creeks intersection to Pauma Reservation Road was completely impassible due to very deep mud deposits. This area experienced a smaller flow on November 30, 2007.||Two smaller watersheds adjacent to and directly west of this watershed also released debris flows that impacted Adams Drive. Although these flows were not as large, up to one foot of mud was deposited on the roadway.

A burst of heavy rain over the Poomacha Burn Area triggered a couple debris flows on the southern slopes of Palomar Mountain. Two culverts were completely blocked and a fairly sizeable river was observed crossing Highway 76 just west of the South Grade Road.
Heavy rain triggered a debris flow in the Witch Creek Burn Area east of the San Pasqual Academy along Highway 78. The highway was completely covered in mud and had to be shut down for a couple days.
Broadcast media reported flooding in Sorrento Valley caused road closure on Carmel Valley Road.
San Diego International Airport reported 0.84 of rainfall betweem 1751 and 1851 PST on December 6th.
Oceanside Airport reported 0.50 of rainfall in 20 minutes between 1503 and 1533 PST on December 6th. This is a 1 in 20 year return interval.

The San Diego River at Fashion Valley went from 5 ft to 12 ft (minor flood stage) between 1700 and 2200 PST on December 6th. Avenida del Rio and Fashion Valley Road were both flooded out December 6th and 7th.
Mud and debris flowed right next to Rice Canyon Elementary School on December 6th due to heavy rain in the burn scar area.

Mud, water and debris impacted Grand Ave near Lakeshore Drive in Lake Elsinore due to heavy rain in the Holy fire burn area around 1400 PST on December 6th. Some areas of Grand Ave. reported mud 1 to 3 feet deep covering streets and yards.
Mud and debris in the road on Grand Ave. near Via Lakistas in Lake Elsinore due to heavy rain.
Mud and debris forced the closure of Temescal Canyon Road on December 6th due to heavy rain.

Notable heavy rainfall rates at the Holy Fire burn scar. Coldwater Canyon received 0.35 of rainfall in 30 minutes. McVicker Canyon received 0.35 in 15 minutes. USGS 30-minute burn scar rainfall thresholds were exceeded in 60 canyons, and the 1-hour thresholds were exceeded in 5 canyons.
Pacific Coast Highway (Route 1) was closed between 3rd and 9th street in South Laguna Beach due to flash flooding.
Broadcast media reported that the Alpha Project Bridge Shelter in East Village San Diego closed for a week due to flooding from the heavy rain.
Broadcast media reported a funnel cloud in Escondido around 1500 PST on December 6th.

Flash flooding was observed throughout downtown San Diego as a result of the heavy rain. Eight cars were seen floating on Laurel and Pacific Street in downtown requiring rescues with two cars having occupants.
A foot of water was reported in downtown Oceanside with multiple cars stalled. Oceanside reported 2.5 of rainfall in 2 hours.
Heavy rain resulted in flooding near the Shoppes at Carlsbad. Five businesses reported flooding damage. A roof collapsed at a childcare center in the shopping center.
Burns Canyon recorded a peak wind gust of 61 knots between 0251 and 0351 PST on December 25th.
Volcan Mountain recorded a peak wind gust of 55 knots between 0840 and 0940 PST on December 25th.
White Water RAWS recorded a peak wind gust of 50 knots between 2250 and 2350 on December 24th.
Quarry Road in Spring Valley closed around 1030 PST on December 25th due to flooding.
Lifeguards at Mission Beach and Solana Beach reported 6-8 ft surf on December 17th and 18th.
Lifeguards at Huntington Beach reported 6-8 ft surf December 17th and 18th.
Wind gusts in excess of 58 mph were measured by the Pinyon Raws for three consecutive hours.

Wind gusts in excess of 58 mph were measured by the Burns Canyon RAWS for 12 hours. A peak gust of 87 mph occurred at 1251 pm. One weather spotter in the Lucerne Valley reported several hours of wind gusts in excess of 60 mph with a peak wind gust of 85 mph. The spotter had numerous asphalt shingles and a satellite dish ripped off his roof. He also heard reports that other homes had incurred roof damage.
Carlsbad Airport reported visibility of 1/4 SM between 0400 and 0830 PST on December 22nd.
John Wayne Airport reported 1/16 SM visibility around 0500 PST on December 22nd.
John Wayne Airport ASOS reported visibility as low as 1/16 SM between 0700 and 0900 PST on December 24th.
Spotter reported dense fog with visibility around 1/4 SM at 0800 PST on December 24th.

A minor debris flow was triggered by heavy rain over the Witch Creek Burn Area near Witch Creek along Highway 78. Debris and mud that came down a nearby hillside clogged a drain and caused up to two feet of water to overtop the highway. At least one car became stuck in the mud and water.
Volcan Mountain reported a peak wind gust of 56 knots between 0300 and 0400 PST on December 31st.
Harrison Park ASOS reported a peak wind gust of 53 knots between 0200 and 0300 PST on December 31st.
White Water RAWS reported a peak wind gust of 54 knots between 2150 and 2250 PST on December 30th.
Burns Canyon ASOS reported a peak wind gust of 52 knots between 0251 and 0351 PST on December 31st.
NWS employee reported a funnel cloud near University Heights around 1330 PST on December 31st.
Multiple spotter reports of a waterspout/funnel cloud in Carlsbad around 1400 PST on December 31st.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE

events.event_narrative: A trained weather spotter reported a 65 mph wind gust in the Lucerne Valley.
Huntington Beach lifeguards reported 8 foot surf at 1 pm on January 6th.
Mission Beach lifeguards reported 8 foot surf at 1 pm on January 6th.

Total rainfall along the San Diego County coastline ranged from 0.50-1.0 from January 5-7. Max hourly rainfall rates along the coast were 0.25/hr. Warmer SSTs resulted in more instability along the coast, which likely contributed to higher rainfall rates along the coast during this event.
John Wayne Airport ASOS reported a funnel cloud near the airport moving to the southeast at 1712 PST on January 12th.
Dense fog reported at KSEE in El Cajon from 0200 to 0700 PST with visibility of 1/2 SM.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Dense fog reported at KRAL from 0300 to 0800 PST with visibility of 1/2 SM.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Dense fog reported at KRIV from 0100 to 0800 PST with visibility of 1/2 SM.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Dense fog reported at KONT from 0000 to 0800 PST with visibility of 1/2 SM or less.
Dense fog reported at KCRQ from 0400 to 0800 PST with visibility of 1/2 SM.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Dense fog reported at KAJO from 2000 PST on January 10th to 0800 PST on January 11th with visibility of 1/2 SM or less.
Dense fog reported at KMYF from 0100 to 0800 PST with visibility of 1/2 SM or less.
Garden Grove gage (GDNC1) reported 1.14 in 30 minutes from 1620 to 1650 PST on January 11th.
Huntington Beach lifeguards reported surf on 10ft at 1300 PST on January 9th.
Mission Beach lifeguards reported high surf of 10 ft at 1 pm on January 9th. A 64 year old man died trying to save his dogs from the high waves at nearby Ocean Beach around 1400 PST on January 9th.

Heavy rainfall began 7 pm on January 15th and inundated downtown Seal Beach. The heavy rain also affected parts of Huntington Beach and Fountain Valley. The flooding in Seal Beach old town affected homes with water entering garages and first levels. The Pacific Coast Highway was closed through the 16th due to the flooding and standing water. Radar estimated 2 inches of rain in about 2 hours with totals over 3 inches across northwest Orange County.
Highway 60 had lane closures due to heavy rain bands of 0.50 to 0.75 per hour. Multiple swift water rescues on the Santa Ana River including helicopter extractions along Fleetwood and Via Ricardo.
Flash flooding from heavy rainfall over Holy fire scar in Trilogy parkway and Glen Eden with water going around homes.

Huntington Beach received 1.25 inches of rainfall in one hour between 2000 and 2100 PST on January 15th. Local officials closed the Pacific Coast Highway (route 1) at approximately 9pm January 15th and kept it closed through the afternoon hours of January 16th.
Fountain Valley received 2 inches of rain in 2 hours between 2000 and 2200 PST on January 15th. An industrial roof collapsed due to water build up at approximately 2200 PST on Mt. Hermann Street.
Local media reported a 19 car pileup on southbound I-15 in the Cajon Pass due to dense fog in the morning hours of January 16th. 35 patients were treated  for minor to moderate injuries.
Burns Canyon Mesonet reported a peak wind gust of 65 knots between 1750 and 1850 PST on January 17th.
Harrison Park mesonet station reported a peak wind gust of 55 knots between 1800 and 1900 PST on January 17th.
CalTrans reported Temescal Canyon Road at I-15 south closed due to flooding.
CalTrans reported a mud/rock slide on Highway 18 at Live Oak Drive due to heavy rain.
CalTrans reported highway 76 at Adams Drive flooded due to heavy rain.
CalTrans reported 2 ft of water along Hwy 138 north of Cedarpines Park. A car stalled in the water, and 2 people had to be rescued.
Snow Peak mesonet reported a peak wind gust of 54 knots between 1730 and 1830 PST on January 17th.

San Diego lifeguards reported sets as high as 15 ft during this 3 day period of high surf. In Ocean Beach, sets were as high as 10 ft, and the pier sustained extensive damage. The railings were broken on both sides of the pier, and it had to be closed down for an extended period of time for repairs.
Spotter reported coastal flooding on 37th street in Newport Beach.
Spotter reported coastal flooding in La Jolla Shores the morning of January 18th.
Broadcast media reported 2 fatalities when a large Torrey Pine tree fell over onto a home due to strong wind. Wind gusts were around 45 mph at the time of the event.
Burns Canyon mesonet reported a peak wind gust of 84 knots between 0200 and 0300 PST on January 21st.
Spotter reported a large tree down on a home in Yorba Linda. No injuries or deaths were reported.
White Water RAWS reported a peak wind gust of 64 knots between 0600 and 0700 PST on January 21st.
Santiago Peak mesonet reported a peak gust of 58 knots between 0500 and 0600 PST on January 21st.
Borrego Air Ranch Airport mesonet reported a peak wind gust of 54 knots between 0600 and 0700 PST on January 21st.
Broadcast media reported that lightning struck a fence and caused damage to it. 40 cloud-to-ground lightning strikes were observed during this event.
CalTrans reported Pacific Coast Highway (highway 1) closed due to flooding. This area received around 0.5 inch of rainfall in 2 hours.

Horsethief Canyon recorded a peak hourly rainfall rate of 0.71 per hour between 1340 and 1440 PST on February 4th. This exceeded established flash flooding hourly rainfall thresholds of 0.50 per hour.
Water overtopped at Trabuco Canyon Road according to Orange County Fire Authority. Trabuco Canyon gauge reported 0.90 inches in 3 hours.

A quick hitting snowstorm dumped 8.5 inches at Cuyamaca, 8 inches at Sunshine Summit near Warner Springs, 7 inches at Warner Springs and Palomar Mountain, 6 to 8 inches at Julian, and 5 inches at Campo. Heavy snow was accompanied by lightning, poor visibility, and wind gusts of 30-50 mph. Four people were treated for hypothermia.

More than 4 inches of snow fell in the inland valleys at elevations between 2500-3000 feet. Other valleys at elevations between 1500-2500 feet generally received 1 to 3 inches of snow. Moderate to locally heavy snow was accompanied by lightning and gusty winds.

Heavy Rainfall of 5 to 9 inches in 24 hours caused devastating flash floods on Highway 243 north of Idyllwild. The state highway remains closed as of late April 2019. This was north of the Cranston Burn Scar.

Rainfall of 4 to 8 inches of occurred in less than 24 hours (heaviest during the morning and early afternoon hours on February 14). Debris flows and heavy runoff into the San Jacinto creek caused widespread damage to state highway 74 including complete wash outs at Strawberry Creek below the Cranston Burn Scar. Caltrans continues to complete repairs with only escorted vehicles allowed as of late April 2019.

Highway 18 received 5 to 10 inches of rain with snow levels at 10,000 feet. Runoff caused extensive damage to the state highway and it was closed to all traffic through March 2. This affected Snow Valley snow sports which was closed for 3 weeks. Emergency repairs were day and night to repair the road damage.

Heavy rainfall of 3 to 5 inches occurred on the desert slope of Mt San Jacinto and the Coachella Valley floor. This resulted in massive flooding and water flow into the Whitewater river (up to 10,000 CFS). Flooding severely damaged highway 111 causing a week long closure.

Flash flood on Palm Springs Tram Road completely destroyed the road. The tram and the road were closed through April 2. 3 to 5 inches of rain occurred in the dry side of Mt. San Jacinto. Security video on YouTube capture the major debris flow and flood.
A total of 5 to 10 inches of rain occurred on the  Palomar mountain coastal slopes in 12 hours. This lead to flash flooding in Pala with road damage and swift water rescues.
Multiple swift water rescues on Santa Margarita river reported by lifeguards. 4 to 8 inches of rainfall occurred over the river drainage.
Swift water rescue near Barona Indian Reservation on Wildcat Canyon road. Heavy rainfall of 4 to 6 inches occurred in about 12 hours.

Heavy rainfall of 3 to 6 inches occurred in 12 hours and up to 1 inch per hour rates. This was the most significant flash flooding and debris flows since the December 6, 2018 event. The Holy fire scar flooded and sent debris flows through Temescal Canyon road and into homes and over roadways. Riverside County reported up to 70 million dollars in flood control structure damage in the 8 canyons affected.

Flash flooding closed Mt. Baldy Road and caused debris flows. Rancho Cucamonga Creek recorded up to 8000 CFS. 4 to 8 inches of rain occurred in about 12 hours. Snow levels were as high as 10,000 feet resulting in excessive additional runoff.

Flash flooding in Big Bear City with up to 1 foot of moving water and 2 feet of standing water in the city streets. Water flows in to Lucerne Valley produced a large standing lake near Highway 18. Big Bear City received up 6 inches of rain in 24 hours.

Widespread flooding and flash flooding in Coachella Valley reported in Indian Canyon|and tributaries to the Whitewater River. Palm Springs airport set a daily record for rainfall with 3.6 inches, most of the rainfall in less than 6 hours. The City of Indio alone reported 1 million in roadway damages from flooding.

Heavy snowfall of 12 to 24 inches impacted the San Bernardino mountains. Highway 18 and 38 were closed February 21 to 23 leaving Big Bear city shut off from traffic (highway 18 was already closed west of Big Bear City). Several small avalanches and rockslides occurred on Highway 38 causing excessive snow removal. Motorists and those recreating in Big Bear did not have an exit route until Friday afternoon after 3 pm when highway 18 north of Big Bear city re-opened.

Heavy snowfall of 4 to 11 inches impacted the town of Julian and up to 22 inches along Sunrise Highway in the San Diego County mountains near Lake Cuyamaca. Snowfall caused accidents and road closures. Highways 78 and 79 were greatly affected. Snowfall of up to 1 inch occurred down to Alpine near 2500 feet elevation.

Black ice following low elevation snowfall during the morning of February 6th occurred causing numerous accidents on Interstate 8 and 2 fatalities in separate accidents. One motorist slid off the interstate over a cliff and into a creek near Boulevard and another died trying to avoid additional spin outs and fell off Pine Valley creek bridge. Interstate 8 was closed during the morning hours and vehicles had to turn around at about 2500 feet elevation near Alpine.
Peak wind gust at Wrightwood ASOS was 53 knots between 1200 and 1300 PST on February 14th. Extensive wind damage was reported at Mountain High Resort in Wrightwood.
Banning ASOS reported a peak wind gust of 52 knots between 1400 and 1500 on February 14th.
Coronado Cays reported a peak wind gust of 47 knots between 1000 and 1100 PST on February 14th. Damages were reported along the San Diego coast.
Intestate 8 was closed for 12 hours due to snow covered and icy roads. Numerous accidents including at Willows road at 2600 fee where video capture a school bus sliding into the hillside.
Snowfall of 3 to as much as 10 inches occurred in Landers (High Desert) during the morning hours associated with thundersnow. As much as 12 inches reported in Yucca Valley.
Snow was reported down to 1000 feet at the end of the storm. Highway 74 was closed to 2 hours due to a burst of heavy snow (Ortega Highway) across the Santa Ana mountains.
Storm channels were inundated by flash flooding with up to 2 inches of rain in 3 hours. Streets were closed and homes threatened by waters.

Flooding occurred in Ramona with up to 2 feet of standing water. Severe damage to portions of highway 78 and 79 along the shoulder of the road. Boulders and rocks fell on highways. 3 to 6 inches of rainfall in about 12 hours.

Extensive flooding on San Diego River in Mission Valley including Fashion Valley mall. Road closures due to flowing water and parking garage and golf course flooded. San Diego River reached 12.1 feet which is above flood stage.
Toro Peak mesonet recorded a peak wind gust of 59 mph between 0200 and 0300 PST on March 2nd.
Mt. Woodson mesonet recorded a peak wind gust of 67 mph between 0800 and 0900 PST on March 2nd.
Public reported a funnel cloud in Perris on March 3rd around 1245 PST.
Burns Canyon mesonet recorded a peak wind gust of 98 mph between 0600 and 0700 PST on March 6th.
Wrightwood mesonet recorded a peak wind gust of 76 mph between 0600 and 0700 PST on March 6th.
Toro Peak mesonet recorded a peak wind gust of 63 mph between 0900 and 1000 PST on March 6th.
CoCoRaHs observer reported 11 inches of storm total snow in Fawnskin.
Public reported 12.5 inches of storm total snow in Big Bear City.
CalTrans reported street flooding on Highway 60 and Rubidoux Blvd in Riverside due to heavy rain and clogged drains.
CalTrans reported HOV lane flooded on northbound 5 freeway due to heavy rain.
CalTrans reported flooding in the right hand lane of Highway 60 due to heavy rain.
Emergency Manager reported 3 inches storm total snow at Palomar Mountain.
CalTrans reported dense fog with visibility less than a mile in the Cajon Pass around 1100 PST on March 6th.
CalTrans reported mud/rock slide on Highway 18 east of Lakeview Point.
Spotter reported dime-sized hail in Yorba Linda around 1500 PST on March 20th.

Rainfall rates of 0.71/hr were reported at Temescal Canyon, which is the highest hourly rainfall rate of the winter season for that canyon. In 30 minutes, 0.59 fell over Temescal Canyon. Lanes were flooded and debris was on the roadway on Temescal Canyon Road near the intersection on I-15.
CalTrans reported roadway flooding and debris in the road on Grand Ave and Blackwell Blvd.
Spotters reported 1-2 inches storm total snow in Idyllwild between March 20th and 21st.
A CoCoRaHS observer reported 1.5 inches of snow at Lake Arrowhead, and another CoCoRaHS observer reported 1.2 inches of snow near Big Bear Lake.
In Orange County, lifeguards reported widespread 6 ft surf on the coast.
In San Diego County, lifeguards reported widespread 6 ft surf along the coast.
Spotter reported 4 inches of snow at Snow Valley (7800 ft elevation).
CalTrans reported accidents on Highway 241 northbound due to hail on the road.
Sill Hill mesonet recorded a peak wind gust of 75 mph on March 15th. Other locales in the San Diego County mountains recorded peak wind gusts of 50-60 mph.
SDG&E webcam captured a funnel cloud over Mount Laguna.
Lightning with these storms first reported over Julian in San Diego County a little after 2 PM PST.
Graupel/hail reported near Onyx Peak in the San Bernardino Mountains around 10 AM PST on April 29th.
Lightning over San Diego County and the waters totaled 69 cloud to ground lightning strikes on April 29th.

KUSI TV shared several photos of a waterspout over Lake Morena. Early a report and photo of a funnel cloud was capture on SDGE webcamera near Mt Laguna. No damage reported but water spray evident over the lake. Thunderstorms and cumulus clouds were in the vicinity.
Trained spotter reported dime sized hail in Wrightwood on May 6th.
CalTrans reported a rock slide on I-8 near Jacumba. Rocks were approximately the size of basketballs.
Spotter reported penny sized hail near town hall in Apple Valley.
Newspaper reported flooding on Dillion Road at Thousand Palms Canyon Road in Sky Valley.
Huntington Beach lifeguards reported 7-8 foot surf at 10am and 1pm on May 13th. Other Orange County beaches reported surf of 4-6 feet.
Huntington Beach and Newport Beach lifeguards reported 7-8 foot surf at 10am and 1pm on May 14th. Other Orange County beaches reported surf of 4-6 feet.
Huntington Beach reported 8 foot surf at 10am and 1pm on May 15th. Other Orange County beaches reported surf of 4-7 feet.
Power poles reported down in Desert Hot Springs. Wind gusts in nearby Sky Valley had peak gusts of 26 knots on May 16th.
Snow fell in the San Bernardino Mountains early in the morning on May 20th, dropping 1-5 inches. Chain controls were in effect for the morning hours of May 20th.
Mesonet Burns Canyon reported a peak wind gust of 68 knots between 1500 and 1600 PST on May 19th.
Mesonet Harrison Park reported a peak wind gust of 68 knots between 2200 and 2300 PST on May 20th.
Trained spotter reported power lines down in Lucerne Valley due to strong winds. Power was out for approximately 4-5 hours.
CalTrans reported numerous areas of highway 60 near Chino flooded out due to heavy rain.
CalTrans reported a car stuck on Monte Vista Ave and Phillips Ave north of Chino. Water got inside of the vehicle.
Spotter reported flash flooding and a swift water rescue just north of Upland. It was reported that the vehicle lost control, flipped over and was taking on water.
Spotter reported urban flooding and water going over curbs at the intersection of La Palma and Brookhurst in Anaheim on May 22nd.
Whitewater RAWS reported a peak wind gust of 54 knots between 1700 and 1800 PST on May 26th.
Harrison Park Mesonet reported a peak wind gust of 52 knots between 0000 and 0100 on May 27th.
Heaps Peak Mesonet reported a peak wind gust of 50 knots between 2100 and 2200 PST on May 26th.
Snow fell in the Riverside County Mountains on May 22nd, dropping 1-4 inches of snow.
Snow fell in the San Bernardino Mountains where 1-3 inches accumulated on May 27th.

Palm Springs ASOS reported high temperatures of 107-118 throughout the 4-day heatwave. The warmest day was June 12th when Thermal reached 118 (record) and Palm Springs recorded a high of 116 (1 shy of record). On June 9th and 10th Thermal broke records with a high of 113 and 116. On July 11, Palm Springs tied a record high of 114.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Inland Empire locations recorded temperatures ranging from 100 to 110 during this 4-day heatwave. June 9th, Riverside reached 104 which was a record.
Spotter reported dense fog along the Orange County coast with visibility between 1/8 and 1/2 of a mile. Fog lifted and visibility improved by 9 AM.
The San Diego County deserts observed high temperatures ranging from 105-115 during the 4-day heatwave. Campo and Borrego Springs broke their daily high temperature records on multiple days.

Ramona reached 102 on June 9th which was a record high. El Cajon had a record high of 94 on June 9th.  El Cajon reached 104 on June 10th and the prior record was 94.  Ramona had a record high of 103 on June 10th.
Anaheim reached 100 on June 10. Anaheim broke a record with a high of 91 on June 11.

Hurricance force wind gusts caused considerable damage in several high desert communities, especially between Lucerne Valley and Johnson Valley. Wind gusts in excess of 90 mph were measured by the Burns Canyon RAWS for three consecutive hours, with a peak wind gust of 96 mph occurring at 15:51 PST. The wind destroyed several outbuildings, damaged personal property, homes, and roofs, and snapped power poles in half. Blowing dust reduced visibility to near zero at times.
COOP Observer in Mount Laguna recorded 2.04 inches of rain in one hour between 1300 and 1400 PST. No flooding or damage was reported.

Strong wind gusts downed power lines, toppled trees, and caused areas of thick blowing dust. Homes and vehicles were damaged by falling trees and one small airplane at Palm Springs International Airport was blown over. A 61 mph wind gust was measured at Whitewater while a 55 mph wind gusts was measured by the Palm Springs ASOS. A weather spotter in the Coachella Valley estimated a wind gust in excess of 70 mph.

A peak wind gust of 68 mph was measured by the Pinyon RAWS. It is assumed that there was at least some minor damage to roof shingles, outbuildings, and possible power poles despite the lack of reports from the area.
Wind gusts estimated in excess of 60 mph caused considerable damage to outbuildings, snapped power poles in half, blew over fences and walls, and damaged homes.
Several stations in the San Diego Mountains measured wind gusts in excess of 50 mph. Only minor damage occurred.
A few stations recorded wind gusts in excess of 50 mph. Weather spotters reported downes trees and power lines.

A possible debris flow deposited 3 feet of mud across Soboba Road near State Street in Gilman Springs. Two vehicles were trapped and one person needed to be rescued. This event may have been triggered by heavy rain on the Sobaba Burn Area.
A 64 mph wind gust was measured by the Fremont Canyon RAWS.
A peak wind gust of 83 mph was measured by the Burns Canyon RAWS at 1:51 PST. Winds were sustained 50 mph or greater between 23:51 PST on the 23rd through 1:51 PST on the 24th.

Heavy rain over the steep slopes of the Witch Creek Burn Area triggered rapid runoff that resulted in significant erosion and undermined portions of Highway 78 near San Pasqual. It is not clear if this was a debris flow or a more traditional flash flood.
Spotter in Escondido reported near 0 visibility between 0530 and 0600 PST. Visibility improved slightly after 0600 PST to around 100 feet, then lifted shortly after 0700 PST.
Brown Field ASOS reported dense fog with visibility between 1/4 and 1 mile from 0000 to 0600 PST.
Palomar Airport reported dense fog with visibility of less than 1/4 mile to 1/4 mile from 0100 to 0600 PST.
NAS Coronado reported dense fog with visibility less than 1/4 mile to 1/2 mile between 0000 and 0600 PST.
Oceanside Airport reported dense fog with visibility between 1/2 and 1 mile from 0000 to 0600 PST.
Spotter reported flooding in their backyard from heavy rain.
Campo COOP observer reported 6 inches of standing water in backyard and runoff with mud/debris.
Spotter reported penny sized hail.
Upper Bear Creek gage reported 2.4 inches of rainfall in 3 hours.
CalTrans reported rocks and mud in the road due to heavy rain.
Mount Laguna mesonet recorded a peak wind gust of 53 knots.
CalTrans reported that roadway S2 was washed out near MM35 due to heavy rain and resultant flooding.
Hot weather impacted the Coachella Valley, where high temperatures ranged from 110-116 degrees. The hottest day was July 12th, where both Palm Springs and Thermal reached 116 degrees.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: The Inland Empire experienced excessive heat on July 11-12 with high temperatures ranging from 95-104. The hottest day was July 12th, where many locations in the Inland Empire reached 100 degrees or more.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: High temperatures in the Inland Empire ranged from 100 to 108 degrees.
High temperatures in the San Diego County valleys ranged from 95-101 degrees, especially in the eastern portion of the valleys.
High temperatures in inland Orange County ranged from 95-100 degrees on July 23rd and 24th.
High temperatures in the Coachella Valley ranged from 113-118 degrees both July 27th and 28th, with the highest temperature of 118 at Palm Springs Airport.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: High temperatures in the Inland Empire ranged from 97-111 degrees on both July 27th and 28th, with the highest temperature of 111 degrees in Rancho Cucamonga.

Estimated 8 million in damage reported from thunderstorms microburst. Up to 20 utility poles downed, snapped or damaged in Imperial Irrigation District. Thunderstorms collapsed on desert floor. Strong winds also brought down a large tree onto a vehicle, trapping a man inside.
A 75 mph wind gust was measured at the Fremont Canyon RAWS.

Numerous locations in the Coachella Valley experienced extreme high temperatures on August 14th and 15th. Thermal Airport recorded a high temperature of 120 degrees, and Palm Springs Airport recorded a high temperature of 119 degrees on August 15th.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Many locations throughout the Inland Empire reported temperatures in excess of 100 degrees on August 14th and 15th. The warmest temperatures were recorded at Lake Elsinore and San Jacinto (105 on the 14th and 104 on the 14th).

Many locations in the San Diego County deserts recorded extreme temperatures August 14th-15th. Borrego Springs recorded a high temperature of 115 degrees, and Ocotillo Wells recorded a high temperature of 119 degrees on August 15th.

Many locations in the San Diego County valleys experienced extreme temperatures on August 14th and 15th. Valley Center recorded a high temperature of 101 degrees, and Ramona and Alpine recorded a high temperature of 99 on August 15th.
Many locations throughout the Coachella Valley experienced excessive heat on August 21st. Thermal reached 117 degrees and Palm Springs reached 116 degrees.
Many locations throughout the San Diego desert experienced excessive heat on August 21st. The warmest location was Ocotillo Wells, where the high temperature was 117 degrees.
A few locations in the High Desert reached over 100 degrees on August 21st. Both Hesperia and Apple Valley reached 103 degrees.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Many locations throughout the Inland Empire reached over 100 degrees on August 21st. Hemet was the hottest location at 104 degrees. Lake Elsinore reached 103 degrees.
Many locations in the San Diego County valleys recorded high temperatures of 90-95 degrees on August 21st. The location with the highest temperature was Ramona at 100 degrees.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: A 5 acre vegetation fire broke out at Bay Ave. and Phyllis Ave. in Moreno Valley late on August 15th. 2 single family homes were destroyed, as well as 3 outbuildings and 9 vehicles.
Spotter reported dense fog on Hwy 78 west between Escondido and Vista. Visibility was between 1/4 and 1/3 of a mile from 0500 to 0700 PST.
Dense fog with visibility less than a mile along the 241 toll rd near Lake Forest.
Dense fog observed in Escondido on 8/20 at 6:30 am with visibility of 1/8 mile. Fog lifted and visibility improved by 0800 PST.

Many locations in the High Desert recorded high temperatures in excess of 100 degrees on August 14th and 15th. Hesperia reached a high of 103 degrees and Apple Valley reached a high of 104 degrees on August 15th.
Palm Springs reach 115F on August 2, 116F on August 4 and the hottest day of the summer at 121F on August 5. On August 5 Thermal and Ocotillo Wells reached 120F.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: The Inland Empire was 98 to 102F on August 2 and peaked to 103 to 107 on August 5 and 6th. On Tuesday, San Bernardino and Lake Elsinore (RTP) reached 106F and Riverside Airport topped out at 105F. Chino airport reached 104F and Ontario Airport 103F.
Ocotillo Wells hit 120F on August 5 after a couple days topping off around 115F.
Palm Springs Airport ASOS recorded 0.98 inches of precipitation between 0200 and 0600 PST on September 2nd. The heaviest rain was between 0300 and 0400 PST.
Flash flooding along Date Palm Drive at Los Gatos Road from heavy rain from 0400 through mid-morning on 9/2. At one point, there was roughly 12 inches of water on the road.
North Indian Canyon Drive was closed on the morning of 9/2 due to water over the roadway. Media reports that the road was still closed monday evening.
Over 1 inch of rain fell in Anza between 1400 and 1500 PST on 9/2.
An electrical cable was dislodged and was draped across the road. A wind gust of 40 mph was reported about 5 miles to the northwest of this location.

Wind gust of 53 knots reported in Pine Valley near I-8. A tree was down on the roadway near Pine Blvd. and Cedar Lane. USBP station on I-8 in Pine Valley reported hail and near zero visibility. Spotter John Grisafi reported wind damage at his home.
CHP reported several basketball-sized boulders blocking lanes on highway 78 near Banner.
Spotter reports branches down, dead tree down near Warner Springs. Estimated gusts to 35 mph at the time.
Spotter reports penny sized hail near Warner Springs.
Heavy rain for 20 minutes ending at 1515 PST with accumulations around 3/4 of an inch.  Road flooding in Chihuahua Valley.
Around 1 inch of precipitation fell in Pine Cove near the Cranston Burn Scar in 1 hour on 9/5.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: The Tenaja Fire started on September 4th in the town of La Cresta in Riverside County and quickly grew to over 1,900 acres over the course of two days. 1,200 people were evacuated, and many schools closed due to the poor air quality. Two structures were damaged and three firefighters suffered minor injuries. The cause of the fire is still under investigation, but lightning may be the cause. The fire was contained on September 14th.
The Coachella Valley experienced hot temperatures on September 13th and 14th. Palm Springs Airport and Thermal reached 110 degrees on September 13th. Similar temperatures were observed on the 14th.

events.event_narrative: Hillside fire erupted at 140 am along Highway 18. This wildfire destroyed 3 homes and damage 6 others. Up to 1300 persons were evacuated. Neighbors went door to door at 2 am to wake up people. The fire consumed about 250 acres near Muscoy in San Bernardino. The fire burned downhill due to 40-50 mph wind gusts (Santa Ana) in lower Waterman Canyon. This wildfire rescue made the A&E Network Rescue series as #1 in 2019. 1 fire fighter was hospitalized for smoke inhalation.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Hill fire broke out in Jurupa Valley at 10 am. The fire burned just 600 acres. 1 reported related injury. Evacuations were lifted by the end of the day. Santa Ana winds were occurring. The fire caused the closure of major Highway 60.

The Miller wildfire erupted in Valley Center and burned 37 acres. The brush fire was in heavy fuel but response was rapid. 3 buildings were destroyed. Evacuations occurred on Cole Grade and Miller Lanes.

Flash flooding at Cumbres Road, northwest of Valley Center. One inch in one hour was observed in one hour, and two inches of rain fell the day before. Some damage was reported in the area.

Many locations in the San Bernardino Mountains reported over 5 inches of snow over 48 hours. Green Valley Lake was the highest with 13 inches of snow. Arrowbear and Running Springs reported 9 inches of snow. Big Bear resorts and Mount Baldy reported 5 inches of snow.
Highway 243 was washed away from heavy rain and closed from Twin Pines to Banning.

On highway 38, over 20 vehicles were abandoned, making it nearly impossible for the road to be plowed.

Fawnskin, Arrowbear, and Running Springs reported 9 inches of snow. Big Bear and Mountain High reported 6-8 inches. Angelus Oaks and Crestline reported 3 inches. Chain controls were in place on March 1st and 2nd.

Fire department reported funnel clouds or waterspouts off the coast of Oceanside and Carlsbad. They confirmed that there were funnel clouds, and possibly waterspouts but it was too far offshore to tell.

Snow fell in the San Bernardino Mountains on March 18th and 19th. Snowfall totals were highest at Green Valley Lake, Running Springs and Lake Arrowhead where 5-6 inches of snow fell. Mt Baldy and Arrowbear Lake picked up 4 inches of snow. Lower elevations such as Forest Falls, Crestline and Wrightwood received 2 inches of snow.
