Between 6pm and 8pm on March 10th, heavy rain in El Cajon and Santee was observed. A vehicle was traveling on I-8 westbound when it crashed into the Forrester Creek canal near First street and Naranca Avenue in El Cajon. As they were trying to escape, one of the passengers got caught in the fast-moving canal (but still within its banks) and was swept miles away. The person was located about 5 miles down Forrester creek near Prospect Avenue in Santee. When pulled from the water, the individual was alive but unconscious, but was later pronounced dead at the hospital.
Report of a mudslide near mile marker 74 on Highway 74 near Pinyon Pines.
California Highway Patrol reports flooding along I-10 west near Coachella.
California Highway Patrol reports Highway 91 at the Adams Street off ramp completely flooded, with vehicles floating.
California Highway Patrol reports mud in the road on Dillion Road with cars stuck.
HOV lanes on Highway 60, just east of I-15, flooded with approximately 2 ft of water.
Riverside County Fire responded to a palm tree on fire next to a home. The tree was struck by lightning.
Road damage at Lugonia and Tennessee ave with severe erosion.
Rescue of 2 adults and a minor from a heavily flooded storm channel near Lincoln Avenue and Rincon Street in Corona. Unknown how they entered channel or if it was overflowing.
Roadway completely submerged under approximately 2 feet of water at Hansen Ave and Ramona Expressway.
Water rescue performed on two individuals stuck in their vehicle. 3 to 4 ft of water reported around the vehicle, at the intersection of Pedley rd and Jurupa rd.
Between one half and one foot of standing water across the intersection of Tonikan rd and Cholena rd in Apple Valley.
Between 7 and 12 inches of snow fell in the San Bernardino Mountains from Thursday afternoon (March 12) through Friday morning (March 13).

Encinitas Police Department is reporting 12 incidents of flooding and flash flooding in Encinitas. Several people have been evacuated from homes in the Encinitas Blvd/Quail Gardens Road area. Twenty persons evacuated from a nursing home. Debris flow also in flooded area up to window of structure at Sunshine Gardens Apartments.
Indian Canyon Drive temporarily closed at the Whitewater Wash due to flooding (1-5 inches of water over the road) caused from rain runoff down the mountains.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: High temperatures in the upper 90s to 101 degrees were observed in the Inland Empire on the 24th and 25th.
High temperatures in the upper 90s to 100 degrees were observed in Inland Orange County on the 24th and 25th.
High temperatures of 100 to 106 degrees were observed in the Coachella Valley from the 24th through the 30th.
High temperatures of 100 to 105 degrees were recorded in the San Diego County deserts from the 24th through the 30th.
High temperatures of 90 to 95 degrees were recorded in the High Desert on the 28th and 29th.
Mudslide under a home spilled onto Black Mountain Road in Rancho Penasquitos, closing part of the road and causing stress to owner's house and property.
Flooding on I-5 northbound offramp to Garnet/Grand Streets causing the ramp to temporarily close.
Southbound on-ramp for Route 125 from Paradise Valley Rd closed due to flooding.
Several boulders completely blocking southbound lane and partially blocking northbound lane. Area has seen just over an inch of rain over 6 hours.
Media reported and had video of water above vehicle tires and streets flooded. Flood prone area but they received 1.8 inches of rain in 24 hours on saturated grounds.

The Buena Vista Creek left its banks and flooded an entire golf driving range and 3 lanes of highway 78 eastbound. At 2 pm, despite efforts to pump water away, Caltrans and CHP closed all 3 lanes of westbound Highway 78. A sig alert was issued around 930 am. The highway was not fully reopen until 10 pm Friday.

Orange County Register reported a swift water rescue in Coyote Creek channel near Buena Park. Person was yelling for help and the fire department was called. 3 feet of moving water was reporting in the canal near 4600 Minorca avenue.
Widespread urban flooding reported throughout Costa Mesa with water on roadways and some fast moving shallow water.
Flooding in lanes 3 and 4 on Hwy 55 near Yorba Linda.
Near 1 inch of rain in 20 minutes in San Juan Capistrano.
In Silverado Canyon, 0.88 of rain was reported in 1 hour from 2 gages.
Lytle Creek reported 3 inches of rain in 6 hours between 0600 and 1200 PST on April 6th.
Rock slide at Highway 18 and Highway 138 near Crestline. Rocks were covering both sides of the road.
Large rocks in lane on Highway 38.
Westbound lanes of Highway 60 in Moreno Valley heavily flooded.

Reports of heavy snow throughout the San Bernardino Mountains starting the evening of April 6th and continuing through April 10th. In Arrowbear, 37 inches of snow was reported. Mountain High received 34 inches. Snow Valley received 30 inches. Snow Summit (Bear Mountain) received 28 inches. Green Valley Lake received 33 inches. Barton Flats received 29 inches.
Up to 12 inches of standing water was reported on Aero Drive in Kearny Mesa.
Gusty winds (estimated 40 mph) prevented the Coast Guard from towing in a 25-foot distressed boat to shore in Encinitas.
Turner Road was closed due to flooding.
Swift water rescue occurred in Seal Beach, near Westminister Blvd in a drainage canal.
A few inches of snow fell in the San Diego County mountains between April 6th and 10th. Palomar Mountain received 6.5 inches of snow. Mount Laguna received 4 inches of snow.
Around 6 AM, firefighters were dispatched to Harmony Grove Road, where 4 people, 3 dogs and 1 cat were trapped in the swiftly flowing Escondido Creek. Everyone was rescued and accounted for.
NWS Employee reports flooding at W San Marcos Blvd at Discovery Street.
Riverleaf Inn in Mission Valley was surrounded by flood waters as the San Diego River reached minor flood stage. 80 persons were displaced from the hotel as it was uninhabitable.
San Diego Fire and lifeguards rescued 2 people that drove their Jeep into a drainage ditch on Chollas Creek. Both people were rescued. The creek was within its banks.
A debris flow occurred on El Camino Real at Tennis Club Drive in Encinitas. The entire road was covered in mud and debris.
Flash flooding and debris on Encinitaas Blvd at Quail Gardens Road. Power lines fell into the water and were hazardous.
Brown Field reported 1/4 mile visibility from 0400 to 0800 PST.
Carlsbad Airport (CRQ) reported 1/4 mile visibility from 0400 to 0800 PST.
MCAS Miramar (NKX) reported 1/4 mile visibility from 0400 to 0800.
Brown Field reported 1/8 mile visibility from 2200 to 2300 PST.
Montgomery Field (MYF) reported dense fog with visibility of 1/4 mile from 0100 to 0300 PST.
San Diego Airport (SAN) reported dense fog with 1/4 mile visibility between 0500 and 0700 PST.

In addition to the 6 am to 11 am closures on Fashion Valley road and Avenida Del Rio further west on the San Diego River when it was exceeding 9.5 feet, from 1130 am to 2 pm, San Diego river rises to 12 feet as heavy rain showers continued. Upstream closures by police expanded to Qualcomm Way, Mission Center Road, along Camino De La Reina at the Highway 163 underpass, Camino Del Este crossing, as well as Ward road (Mission San Diego station) and Grantville trolly station (barricades set up) and north to the San Diego Mission road crossing gate closure - river reached a peak of 12.5 feet at 6 pm. Between noon and 2 pm swift water rescues were observed along the river east of Mission Center road. Storm survey conducted during this period.
Water rising and flooding on Sandia Creek into the Santa Margarita River. 1-2 feet of water reported flowing over Sandia Creek Drive via SDCFCD webcam.

Swift water rescue of a pregnant women and pets near or in Otay River. Rescue occurred in dark and may have been homeless camp. Heavy rainfall had ended but river was running fast and swift at bank full levels.
San Luis Rey River and tributaries caused flooding across Cole Grade Road, where the road was closed from the low water crossing to Route 76.
Heavy rainfall rates over 0.70 per hour caused 8 inches of swift moving water to flood Lakeview Ave, just north of Miraloma Ave.
Flash flooding and boulders reported on roads in Valley Center. Area received 4 inches of rain in about 12 hours.
A car sized boulder was reported on a road in Bonsall. This area had received 3 inches of rain in the past 12 hours and still heavy rainfall occurring at the time.
Interstate 8 landslide and debris on highway caused closure.
Orange County Register photo of large tree that crush a truck. Combination of winds and heavy rainfall appear to cause the tree to topple over.
City of Oceanside had significant damage to the wastewater treatment plant. Estimated up to 2 millions gallons spilled as the plant was inundated by the flash flooding of Buena Vista Creek.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: High temperatures reached the upper 90s to 102 degrees for areas across the Inland Empire May 5th through May 8th.
Areas of the Coachella Valley saw high temperatures in the low 100s to 110 degrees from May 5th through 10th.
High temperatures across the lower deserts of San Diego County ranged from the low 100s to near 110 degrees May 5th through 10th.
High temperatures in the low to upper 90s were recorded across parts of the San Diego County valleys May 5th through 7th.
Areas of inland Orange County saw high temperatures in the low to mid 90s May 5th through 7th.
Temperatures ranged from near 100 in Victorville up to 107 degrees in Lucerne Valley on the 26th to the 28th.
Temperatures generally ranged from 105 to 110 degrees across the Coachella Valley each day from the 26th to the 28th, though Palm Springs did hit 111 degrees on the 26th.
Temperatures ranged from 105 to 110 degrees in parts of the San Diego County deserts.

Areas of coastal San Diego County experienced patchy dense fog on the early mornings of May 7th and 8th. San Diego International Airport reported one quarter mile visibility on the 7th and Miramar MCAS reported a visibility near zero on the 8th.
High temperatures ranged from 100 to 113 degrees across the lower deserts of San Diego County. Ocotillo Wells reached 113 degrees and Borrego Springs reached 112 degrees both on June 3rd.
Temperatures ranged from 105 to 115 degrees across the Coachella Valley June 2nd-4th. Palm Springs and Thermal airports both recorded a temperature of 115 degrees on June 3rd.
Temperatures ranged from 95 to 105 degrees across the High Desert June 2nd through 4th.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Temperatures ranged from 95 to 106 degrees across the Inland Empire June 2nd through 4th. Chino Airport hit 106 degree and Ontario Airport reached 102 both on June 3rd.
Gusty westerly winds occurred, highest near the foothills of the San Bernardino Mountains. Winds 40-50 MPH reported, some sites as high as 67 MPH at Whitewater.
Whitewater RAWS reports 70 MPH wind gust.
Site SE586 reports 59 MPH wind gust.
Mesonet station HF002 Laguna Launch reports wind gust of 70 MPH at 7 PM on June 28th.
Mesonet station SE585 measures a wind gust of 59 MPH.
Hot temperatures ranging from 110 to 117 degrees reported in the Coachella Valley July 16th through 19th. ASOS sites at Palm Springs and Thermal both reached 117 degrees on July 19th.
Hot temperatures were recorded in areas of the High Desert July 17th-20th. Temperatures of 100 to 106 occurred with hottest temperature readings on July 20th.
San Bernardino National Forest reports 62.5 acre Mount R Fire, which closed a portion of California State Route 330 between Live Oak Drive to Highland Boulevard.
San Bernardino County Fire Department responded to the Easton Fire near the city of Highland on July 20th. The fire was put out the next afternoon with a total of 71 acres.

Minor coastal flooding occurred in Newport Beach because of high tide near 6.8 feet with high surf also reported at the time. Flooding of parking lots and streets happened up to three blocks inland and a sailboat was washed ashore and destroyed.
Stations at North Island and Imperial Beach reported intermittent dense fog with visibility as low as one quarter-mile.

One of the Navy's vessels in the San Diego Bay, the U.S.S. Bonhomme Richard, caught fire the morning of July 12th and lasted for four days. Copious amounts of smoke entered the atmosphere creating poor air quality in the greater San Diego metro, along with a total of 68 military and civilian firefighters injured during the blaze.

Police responded to a call around 3:30 p.m. about a infant left inside a car on the 400 block of West Wilshire Avenue, according to the Fullerton Police Department. When officers arrived, the infant was already outside of the car but was unresponsive. The boy was pronounced dead at the scene.

A hiker required medical rescue due to heat-related illness near doghouse Junction on Otay Mountain. Patient was airlifted to a waiting ambulance. Around 1:15 pm, temperature at Otay Mountain was 87 degrees.
Palm Springs ASOS reports highs 117-121 degrees during the 3 day period. High of 121 degrees occurred July 12th.
Anza Borrego State Park site reports highs 111-121 degrees during the 3 day period. High of 121 degrees occurred July 12th.
Temperatures spanned 100 to 110 degrees across areas of the High Desert during the period. Hottest day was on July 12th.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Many sites around the Inland Empire report temperatures between 100 and 110 degrees for the three day period. Hottest temperatures occurred July 11th and 12th.

Two hikers were rescued on the Three Sisters Trail near Julian, which was had been closed due to excessive heat. The temperature was around 91 degrees at the time of the rescue (based on station that is slightly higher than elevation of trail, so actual temperature was likely warmer).

Three distressed hikers were rescued from Cedar Creek Falls Trail in San Diego County Estates, which was closed due to excessive heat. All 3 hikers were released with no injuries reported. Rescue started around 11:30 AM and finished around 1:30 PM. Temperatures during that time were between 95 and 98 degrees.
USFS San Bernardino and CalFire worked on the Apple fire which began July 31st. The fire burned 33,424 acres into mid August 2020. 3 injuries on wildfire. 4 homes destroyed.
High temperatures of 100 to 110 degrees occurred across the region from July 30th through August 3rd.

Areas of the Coachella Valley heated up to 110 to 120 degrees during this July 30th through August 3rd heat wave, with some areas hitting over 120 degrees on July 30th and 31st. The 122 degree reading on July 31st at the Palm Springs ASOS was one degree shy of the all-time record high temperature at that location.
Areas of the lower deserts of San Diego County reached 110 to 122 degrees during this July 30th through August 3rd heat wave.

Areas of the San Diego County Mountains observed temperatures over 100 degrees during this July 30th through August 3rd heat wave. The COOP observer at Campo reported a high temperature of 105 degrees on both July 30th and 31st.
Parts of the San Diego County valleys reported high temperatures of 95 to 105 degrees on the July 30th through August 3rd heat wave. Hottest days were July 30th and 31st.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Parts of the Inland Empire recorded temperatures from 100 to 110 degrees from the July 30th to August 3rd heat wave.
Portions of the Coachella Valley recorded temperatures of 110 to 120 degrees during this heat wave. The 14th was the hottest day, where the Palm Springs ASOS reported a 120 degree reading.

A portion of the fire reached into parts of Riverside County. Portions of the Cherry Valley and Beaumont communities were under Evacuation Orders and Warnings, as well as partial road closures due to damages, including State Highway 38. The San Gorgonio Wilderness Area was shut down to the public starting August 2nd.

A portion of the fire reached into parts of San Bernardino County. The communities of Oak Glen were under an evacuation order, while Forest Falls, Pioneertown, and Rim Rock were all under an evacuation warning. The area also saw partial road closures and damages in areas of the fire, including State Highway 38. The San Gorgonio Wilderness was shut down to all starting August 2nd.
Carlsbad, San Diego, and North Island ASOS sites reported visibility of 1/4 mile at times throughout the night.

Portions of the San Diego deserts recorded temperatures of 110 to 120 degrees during this heat wave. Anza Borrego State Park recorded 118 degrees for three consecutive days from the 14th through the 16th.
Portions of the San Diego valleys recorded temperatures of 95 to 105 degrees during this heat wave. El Cajon reported a high of 102 degrees, breaking the record for the day.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Temperatures ranged from 105 to 115 degrees across the Inland Empire during this event. The Riverside Airport broke 2 daily records with this event.
Temperatures of 95 to 105 degrees were recorded during this heat event. The Laguna Hills CWOP recorded a high temperature of 107 degrees on August 14th.
Areas of the High Desert reported temperatures of 100 to 110 degrees during this heat wave.

Monsoon thunderstorms brought areas of light rainfall with some heavier spots along the Santa Ana River in the San Bernardino County Mountains, where automated gauges picked up over one inch in some spots.
CWOP in the eastern portion of Hemet reported 1.35 inches of rain from monsoon thunderstorms on the 18th.

Parts of the lower deserts reported highs above 110 degrees during this time period. The peak of the heat was on the 5th and 6th, where some areas hit close to the 120 degree mark. Anza Borrego State Park broke daily record highs on the 5th and 6th, reaching 117 degrees both days.

Very hot temperatures were experienced in parts of the Coachella Valley with temperatures 115 to over 120 degrees. The Palm Springs ASOS recorded 3 daily high temperatures records on the 4th, 5th and 6th of the month with the highest reaching 122 degrees, one degree shy of the all time record high.
Hot temperatures from 100 to 110 degrees were reported across areas of the high desert from the 4th to the 7th.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: High temperatures across the Inland Empire ranged from 110 to over 120 degrees for this event. The Riverside ASOS reported 117 degrees on the 5th and 6th, breaking two daily record highs. The Chino ASOS reported 121 degrees on the 6th, making it the hottest temperature ever recorded in the Inland Empire.

Parts of the area rose up to 110 to 115 degrees during this time period. The Ramona ASOS broke two daily record highs on the 5th and 6th, reaching 112 degrees each day.|Escondido had an all-time high of 115��F. On September 6th, an all-time high of 113 was recorded at Alpine on September 5th. San Diego county Public Health recorded significant (77) hospitalizations due to the excessive heat.

The Valley Fire started on September 5th at approximately 2:30 PM and burned approximately 16,390 acres across the southern portion of the San Diego County Mountains until being 100% contained on September 24th. Many resources were deployed with some parts of the area having evacuation orders issued.

The El Dorado wildfire started at approximately 10:40 AM on September 5th, scorching 22,680 acres over a 23 day period into parts of the San Bernardino and Riverside County Mountains. The fire forced road closures (including State Highway 38) and the evacuations of Oak Glen, north Yucaipa, Mountain Home Village, Forest Falls, and Angelus Oaks communities. There were 4 residences damaged, 5 residences destroyed along with 15 other structures destroyed. 13 firefighters were injured as well as one fatality while fighting the flames. The fire is expected to be fully contained by mid-December. CalTrans started repairing the road and surrounding areas in early October and expects the project to be completed by late Spring 2021.
Very hot temperatures ranging from 108 - 113 degrees occurred. The Palm Springs ASOS recorded 113 degrees on the 17th.
Temperatures soared close to 105 degrees in some spots during this heat wave. El Cajon tied its daily record of 104 degrees on the 18th.
Some areas reported highs in the triple digits during this heat wave. The Campo COOP reported a high of 100 degrees on the 18th, breaking a daily record.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Hot temperatures in upwards of 100 degrees were reported across the Inland Empire. The Chino ASOS reported a high temperature of 106 degrees on the 17th.
Temperatures climbed into the upper 90s and low 100s in some spots during this heat wave. Santa Ana reached 99 degrees on the 17th and Anaheim broke a daily record, reaching 96, on the 18th.
Temperatures soared into the upper 80s to low 90s in some coastal locations. Chula Vista tied a daily record high, reaching 91 degrees on the 17th.
Temperatures soared near 110 degrees in parts of the San Diego County Deserts, where Anza Borrego State Park tied their record daily high temperature of 110 degrees on the 17th.
Widespread 90s and low 100s were reported with this event. The San Diego Airport ASOS hit 96 degrees on September 30th and 97 degrees on October 1st, breaking the daily record highs both days.
High temperatures from the 90s at the beaches to just over 100 degree readings were reported a few miles inland during this heat wave. John Wayne Airport ASOS reached 100 degrees on September 30th.
Temperatures over 100 degrees occurred across the region during this heat wave. El Cajon reached 107 degrees on the 30th, breaking the daily record high temperature.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Temperatures rose over the century mark across the Inland Empire during this heat wave. The Riverside Airport ASOS reached 108 degrees on the 30th, tying the daily record high.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: The Candy Fire burned 227 acres of vegetation on the 29th and 30th in the hills just north of Lake Elsinore near the intersection of Gavilan Road and Lake Matthews Drive. The fire was 100% contained on the evening of the 30th with no reports of structural damage.
Some areas hit close to 100 degrees during this heat wave from the 12th to the 16th. Chula Vista recorded 93 degrees on the 13th, tying the daily record high.
Some areas recorded temperatures near 100 degrees during this heat wave from the 12th to the 16th. Santa Ana set a daily record high temperature on the 14th, hitting 96 degrees.

A strong dust devil caused 14 injuries at a church gathering at Montera Elementary School when several large tents were lofted into the air. Two people were taken to the hospital. Skies were clear at the time with temperatures in the 90s.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Hot temperatures of over 100 degrees were reported from the 12th through the 16th. The Riverside Municipal Airport (KRAL) ASOS tied a record daily high of 101 degrees on the 15th.
Prevalent 90s and near 100 degree readings were recorded during this heat wave from the 12th to the 16th. Escondido tied their daily record high of 101 degrees on the 16th.

The Blue Ridge fire started near the Green River Golf Club. The fire grew in strength rapidly over the next couple of days before being 100% contained on November 7th, burning approximately 13,964 acres. The blaze destroyed one structure and damaged ten others. Partial road closures included state routes 71, 91, 142 and 241.

The Silverado Fire burned 12,466 acres before being contained on November 7th around 7:08 AM. The fire burned into the city of Irvine, forcing evacuations of at least 60,000 people throughout the area. There were 5 destroyed structures along with 9 damaged. The fire also shut down State Highway 241, which burned across the road. 2 firefighters received second and third degree burns while battling the blaze.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Strong Santa Ana winds impacted areas of the Inland Empire. The Ontario Airport ASOS reported a gust of 70 MPH around 11:30 AM on the 26th. Many trees in the area uprooted and damage to power lines and some structures. The airport also had a ground stop as well as power shutoffs for to some of the region.

Strong Santa Ana winds occurred in this region resulting in an 88 MPH wind gust at the Fremont Canyon RAWS station. Other notable gusts that occurred are a 66 MPH wind gust at SCE station in Trabuco Canyon and 60 MPH wind gust in the Peters Canyon area in North Tustin. Local power shutoffs occurred across the area as well.
Areas of dense fog impacted the area with low visibility. The San Diego Airport ASOS reported dense fog at times from 10 pm Thursday to 9 am Friday, with lowest visibility of 1/8 mile.

Patchy dense fog occurred in the area. John Wayne Airport ASOS reported lowest visibility of 1/4 mile early morning on the 18th, and Los Alamitos Airfield AWOS reported lowest visibility of 1/8 mile early morning on the 17th.
Gusty Santa Ana winds occurred in the San Bernardino Mountains the evening of the 26th into the morning of the 27th. Heaps Peak RAWS reported a wind gust of 64 MPH at 2:15 AM on the 27th.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Gusty Santa Ana winds occurred the evening of the 26th into the morning of the 27th with some stations measuring gusts over 55 MPH.
Gusty Santa Ana winds occurred across the Orange County Mountains and foothills. The Fremont Canyon RAWS measured a wind gust of 79 MPH at 1:51 AM on the 27th.
Cal Fire reports firefighter injury during the Hawk Fire, which burned 10 acres near Japutal Valley Road and Hawk Ridge between 1 and 3 PM on the 27th.

Gusty Santa Ana winds impacted areas of the Riverside County Mountains from the evening of the 26th into the morning of the 27th. University of California San Diego HPWREN network observations measured a 68 MPH wind gust around 1 AM.
Portions of the San Diego County coast saw periods of dense fog. San Diego Airport ASOS observed periods of dense fog as low as 1/8 of a mile.
Portions of the Orange County coast saw periods of dense fog. John Wayne Airport ASOS reports dense fog with visibility as low as 1/8th of a mile.
Portions of the mountains in San Diego County received significant snowfall. Mt. Laguna measured a total of 7 inches, while Palomar Mountain measured 4 inches of snow.
Areas of heavy snow impacted the Riverside County Mountains, such as in Idyllwild, where the storm total snow observed was 6 inches.

Heavy snow fell in portions of the San Bernardino Mountains. Notable totals occurred at Big Bear Snow Summit Ski Resort, where 18 inches of snow fell at at 8,800 feet and 16 inches at Green Valley Lake. CalTrans closed a large portion of Route 38 on the 9th due to heavy snow, along with large power lines and trees down on the road.

Gusty winds occurred in the San Diego mountains. UC San Diego HPWREN Network observation station measured a 72 MPH wind gust. Gusty winds led to a tree, approximately 14 inches in diameter, blocking road completely at Highway 76 / Highway 79 interchange. Observations near Lake Henshaw report wind gusts of 38-39 mph with sustained winds of 28-29 mph out of the southwest from 1:10 pm until 1:30 pm on the 8th.
Areas of heavy rainfall occurred across the mountains and valleys of San Diego County. Notable totals occurred at Lake Cuyamaca with 3.98 inches of rain and Pine Valley with 3.31 inches of rain.
Lifeguards at Huntington Beach report high surf of 8 feet at 4 PM.

Gusty winds occurred across the Coachella Valley over this period. Earlier in the period, a trained spotter reported a 46 mph wind gust with uprooted trees and broken tree limbs in the city of Coachella. The Thermal ASOS recorded a wind gust 54 MPH as well.  In the late afternoon of the 8th, CHP report of downed light pole blocking Jackson St. just south of 58th Ave. where, Thermal ASOS had gusts to 33 mph at the time, however, a surfacing mountain wave may have produced higher gusts at this location.
Gusty winds occurred across the High Desert. Cushenbury Springs observation site reported a 68 MPH wind gust at 4:30 AM on the 7th.
Portions of the High Desert saw cold temperatures with patchy areas of frost. The low temperature in Apple Valley dropped to 19 degrees on the afternoon of the 10th.
Trained spotter reports roadway flooding is occurring on carbon canyon road in various locations in carbon canyon. flooding is ranging from 1/2 an inch to 2 inches.

San Bernardino County Public works reports a road closure of Brookside Road in Crestline due to downed trees. with heavy snow of 17 inches reported around 5,000 feet. Heavy snow of 15 inches also reported by a trained spotter in Lake Arrowhead and at SNow Valley ski resort of close to 20 inches in total.
CalTrans reports lane closures along Interstate 15 through the Cajon Pass due to snowfall down to 3,500 feet. The area experienced major traffic delays and multiple vehicle spinouts.
Public reports a swift water rescue in the channel near the intersection of Raitt Street and Edinger Avenue in Santa Ana. Reports of 2 people swept away in the channel.
Standing water of approximately 2.5 feet in lanes at Route 55 and Route 91 connector reported by CalTrans.
CalTrans reports flooding and standing water on Route 60 westbound at Rubidoux interchange.
CalTrans reports Interstate 15 South at Temecula Parkway/Highway 79 with mud and water in lanes 1 and 2. The area measured 1.5 to 1.9 inch rainfall in 24 hours.
CalTrans reports lanes flooded coming off the Coronado bridge onto the 5.
Flooding reported on road where lanes merge on I-805 northbound and El Cajon Boulevard interchange.

NBC 7 media reports large palm tree top snapped off and damage to the roof of an Amazon warehouse. A line of thunderstorms moved through this area 7 to 8 pm Monday the 28th. Heavy rain and wind microburst likely caused damage. photos provided on nbc7.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: SoCal Edison Site Thunder Ridge (SE851) reports wind gust of 63 MPH on December 31st at 3:30 PM in the Pedley Hills above Jurupa Valley.
Mesonet station HHCSD Hellhole Canyon (SDGE) measures wind gust of 81 MPH at approximately 6:30 PM on the 7th.
Mesonet station HP003 Toro Peak (HPWREN) measures wind gust of 69 MPH at approximately 10 PM on the 7th.
Mesonet station FRCC1 Fremont Canyon measures wind gust of 65 MPH at approximately 10:51 AM on the 8th.
Mesonet station SE700 Banning (SCE700) reports wind gust of 57 MPH at approximately 1:30 AM on the 8th.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Cal Fire reports 1,087 acre fire near Butterfield Drive and Aviation Drive near the Corona Airport from the 1st until the 12th. The fire prompted closures of Route 71 and the airport, along with evacuation of homes in the region.

Cal Fire reports the start of the Bond Fire from a house fire on the night of December 2nd. Gusty Santa Ana winds aided in the scorching of 6,686 acres in the Santa Ana foothills near Santiago and Silverado Canyons. The area experienced multiple evacuation warnings and road closures, 21 structures damaged and 31 structures destroyed, along with 2 firefighter injuries.

Local fire authorities responded to the 30 acre vegetation fire, known as the Willow fire, on the evening of the 2nd. The fire began near 10 pm and may have started from a structure near Willow Glen Drive and Hillsdale Road in Rancho San Diego. 1 home was destroyed and 6 damaged. Wind gusts to 20 mph occurred late Wednesday evening with humidity values in the teens.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: CalFire reports 300 acre Cerritos on the western side of Hemet near the 23900 block of California avenue. Wind gusts 25 to 30 mph at time of start and prompted evacuation orders and warnings.
Strong Santa Ana winds occurred across the region with a peak gust of 95 MPH at Big Black Mountain site.

events.cz_name: SAN BERNARDINO AND RIVERSIDE COUNTY VALLEYS - THE INLAND EMPIRE
events.event_narrative: Gusty Santa Ana winds occurred near and below the Cajon Pass generally 50-60 MPH. Marshall Peak observation hit 80 MPH around 12:45 AM on the 3rd.
Gusty Santa Ana winds occurred in the region with the Chino Hills RAWS hitting 79 MPH early morning on the 3rd. Most gusts in the region peaked around 50-60 MPH.
Gusty Santa Ana winds swept through the region with the highest gust occurring at the Highland Springs RAWS at 76 MPH.
Gusty Santa Ana winds occurred in this region, where SoCal Edison site Apple Canyon measures peak gust of 65 MPH.
Gusty Santa Ana winds occurred across the valleys with Rockwood peaking at 66 MPH and Black Mountain Ranch peaking at 56 MPH.

events.event_narrative: High temperatures reached the lower-100s on Saturday, September 4th. The heat peaked across the Inland Empire on Sunday, September 5th, when highs reached 108 degrees in Ontario, and 107 degrees in Riverside. The heat ramped back up the following weekend, with high temperatures reaching the low-100s September 11th through September 13th.

Much of the Coachella Valley saw excessive heat Labor Day Weekend through the following weekend. The first peak occurred on Sunday, September 5th, when highs ranged from the upper-100s to the mid-110s. The heat persisted through the following weekend, when the highest temperatures of event occurred. Several locations saw their highest temperatures of the heat event on Monday, September 13, after all heat products had expired, including Ocotillo Wells (116/91), Thermal (111) and Indio (112/87).||Several sites saw very warm overnight low temperatures, exacerbating the heat risk through the event. Indio set a record for the highest minimum temperature on September 13, with the overnight low falling to 87, breaking the previous record of 86 set in 2015.

High temperatures across the San Diego County Mountains and valleys consistently reaching the mid-90s from Saturday, September 4th through September 13th. Eight Preliminary Prehospital Heat Related Calls occurred from September 5 through September 10, seven of which were mild cases, and one that was a moderate case of heat-related illness.
The High Desert saw excessive heat the first full week of September, with heat peaking on Wednesday, September 8th, when highs reached the upper-100s.
